1001	In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
1002	Now the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters.
1003	And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
1004	And God saw that the light was good, and He separated the light from the darkness.
1005	God called the light “day,” and the darkness He called “night.” And there was evening, and there was morning—the first day.
1006	And God said, “Let there be an expanse between the waters, to separate the waters from the waters.”
1007	So God made the expanse and separated the waters beneath it from the waters above. And it was so.
1008	God called the expanse “sky.” And there was evening, and there was morning—the second day.
1009	And God said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear.” And it was so.
1010	God called the dry land “earth,” and the gathering of waters He called “seas.” And God saw that it was good.
1011	Then God said, “Let the earth bring forth vegetation: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed according to its kind.” And it was so.
1012	The earth produced vegetation: seed-bearing plants according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.
1013	And there was evening, and there was morning—the third day.
1014	And God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to distinguish between the day and the night, and let them be signs to mark the seasons and days and years.
1015	And let them serve as lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth.” And it was so.
1016	God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night. And He made the stars as well.
1017	God set these lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth,
1018	to preside over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
1019	And there was evening, and there was morning—the fourth day.
1020	And God said, “Let the waters teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”
1021	So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, with which the waters teemed according to their kinds, and every winged bird after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
1022	Then God blessed them and said, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”
1023	And there was evening, and there was morning—the fifth day.
1024	And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, land crawlers, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.
1025	God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that crawls upon the earth according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
1026	Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself and every creature that crawls upon it.”
1027	So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.
1028	God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth.”
1029	Then God said, “Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of all the earth, and every tree whose fruit contains seed. They will be yours for food.
1030	And to every beast of the earth and every bird of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth—everything that has the breath of life in it—I have given every green plant for food.” And it was so.
1031	And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.
2001	Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array.
2002	And by the seventh day God had finished the work He had been doing; so on that day He rested from all His work.
2003	Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on that day He rested from all the work of creation that He had accomplished.
2004	This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made them.
2005	Now no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, nor had any plant of the field sprouted, for the LORD God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.
2006	But springs welled up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.
2007	Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
2008	And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, where He placed the man He had formed.
2009	Out of the ground the LORD God gave growth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food. And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
2010	Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it branched into four headwaters:
2011	The name of the first river is the Pishon; it winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
2012	And the gold of that land is pure, and bdellium and onyx are found there.
2013	The name of the second river is the Gihon; it winds through the whole land of Cush.
2014	The name of the third river is the Tigris; it runs along the east side of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
2015	Then the LORD God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
2016	And the LORD God commanded him, “You may eat freely from every tree of the garden,
2017	but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”
2018	The LORD God also said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make for him a suitable helper.”
2019	And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and He brought them to the man to see what he would name each one. And whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.
2020	The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam no suitable helper was found.
2021	So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and while he slept, He took one of the man’s ribs and closed up the area with flesh.
2022	And from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman and brought her to him.
2023	And the man said: “This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called ‘woman,’ for out of man she was taken.”
2024	For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and they will become one flesh.
2025	And the man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.
3001	Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field that the LORD God had made. And he said to the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden?’”
3002	The woman answered the serpent, “We may eat the fruit of the trees of the garden,
3003	but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God has said, ‘You must not eat of it or touch it, or you will die.’”
3004	“You will not surely die,” the serpent told the woman.
3005	“For God knows that in the day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”
3006	When the woman saw that the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eyes, and that it was desirable for obtaining wisdom, she took the fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.
3007	And the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves.
3008	Then the man and his wife heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the breeze of the day, and they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
3009	But the LORD God called out to the man, “Where are you?”
3010	“I heard Your voice in the garden,” he replied, “and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself.”
3011	“Who told you that you were naked?” asked the LORD God. “Have you eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?”
3012	And the man answered, “The woman whom You gave me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”
3013	Then the LORD God said to the woman, “What is this you have done?” “The serpent deceived me,” she replied, “and I ate.”
3014	So the LORD God said to the serpent: “Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and every beast of the field! On your belly will you go, and dust you will eat, all the days of your life.
3015	And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.”
3016	To the woman He said: “I will sharply increase your pain in childbirth; in pain you will bring forth children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.”
3017	And to Adam He said: “Because you have listened to the voice of your wife and have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life.
3018	Both thorns and thistles it will yield for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
3019	By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread, until you return to the ground— because out of it were you taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.”
3020	And Adam named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living.
3021	And the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and He clothed them.
3022	Then the LORD God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...”
3023	Therefore the LORD God banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.
3024	So He drove out the man and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life.
4001	And Adam had relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. “With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man,” she said.
4002	Later she gave birth to Cain’s brother Abel. Now Abel was a keeper of sheep, while Cain was a tiller of the soil.
4003	So in the course of time, Cain brought some of the fruit of the soil as an offering to the LORD,
4004	while Abel brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock. And the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering,
4005	but He had no regard for Cain and his offering. So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.
4006	“Why are you angry,” said the LORD to Cain, “and why has your countenance fallen?
4007	If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you refuse to do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.”
4008	Then Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let us go out to the field.” And while they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
4009	And the LORD said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” “I do not know!” he answered. “Am I my brother’s keeper?”
4010	“What have you done?” replied the LORD. “The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.
4011	Now you are cursed and banished from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
4012	When you till the ground, it will no longer yield its produce to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”
4013	But Cain said to the LORD, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.
4014	Behold, this day You have driven me from the face of the earth, and from Your face I will be hidden; I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”
4015	“Not so!” replied the LORD. “If anyone slays Cain, then Cain will be avenged sevenfold.” And the LORD placed a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him.
4016	So Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
4017	And Cain had relations with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.
4018	Now to Enoch was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael was the father of Methusael, and Methusael was the father of Lamech.
4019	And Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.
4020	Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.
4021	And his brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the harp and flute.
4022	And Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain, a forger of every implement of bronze and iron. And the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.
4023	Then Lamech said to his wives: “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my speech. For I have slain a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.
4024	If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.”
4025	And Adam again had relations with his wife, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, “God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.”
4026	And to Seth also a son was born, and he called him Enosh. At that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD.
5001	This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, He made him in His own likeness.
5002	Male and female He created them, and He blessed them. And in the day they were created, He called them “man.”
5003	When Adam was 130 years old, he had a son in his own likeness, after his own image; and he named him Seth.
5004	And after he had become the father of Seth, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
5005	So Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died.
5006	When Seth was 105 years old, he became the father of Enosh.
5007	And after he had become the father of Enosh, Seth lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters.
5008	So Seth lived a total of 912 years, and then he died.
5009	When Enosh was 90 years old, he became the father of Kenan.
5010	And after he had become the father of Kenan, Enosh lived 815 years and had other sons and daughters.
5011	So Enosh lived a total of 905 years, and then he died.
5012	When Kenan was 70 years old, he became the father of Mahalalel.
5013	And after he had become the father of Mahalalel, Kenan lived 840 years and had other sons and daughters.
5014	So Kenan lived a total of 910 years, and then he died.
5015	When Mahalalel was 65 years old, he became the father of Jared.
5016	And after he had become the father of Jared, Mahalalel lived 830 years and had other sons and daughters.
5017	So Mahalalel lived a total of 895 years, and then he died.
5018	When Jared was 162 years old, he became the father of Enoch.
5019	And after he had become the father of Enoch, Jared lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
5020	So Jared lived a total of 962 years, and then he died.
5021	When Enoch was 65 years old, he became the father of Methuselah.
5022	And after he had become the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked with God 300 years and had other sons and daughters.
5023	So Enoch lived a total of 365 years.
5024	Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away.
5025	When Methuselah was 187 years old, he became the father of Lamech.
5026	And after he had become the father of Lamech, Methuselah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters.
5027	So Methuselah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died.
5028	When Lamech was 182 years old, he had a son.
5029	And he named him Noah, saying, “May this one comfort us in the labor and toil of our hands caused by the ground that the LORD has cursed.”
5030	And after he had become the father of Noah, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
5031	So Lamech lived a total of 777 years, and then he died.
5032	After Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
6001	Now when men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them,
6002	the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and they took as wives whomever they chose.
6003	So the LORD said, “My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days shall be 120 years.”
6004	The Nephilim were on the earth in those days—and afterward as well—when the sons of God had relations with the daughters of men. And they bore them children who became the mighty men of old, men of renown.
6005	Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time.
6006	And the LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart.
6007	So the LORD said, “I will blot out man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth—every man and beast and crawling creature and bird of the air—for I am grieved that I have made them.”
6008	Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
6009	This is the account of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah walked with God.
6010	And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
6011	Now the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence.
6012	And God looked upon the earth and saw that it was corrupt; for all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways.
6013	Then God said to Noah, “The end of all living creatures has come before Me, because through them the earth is full of violence. Now behold, I will destroy both them and the earth.
6014	Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms in the ark and coat it with pitch inside and out.
6015	And this is how you are to build it: The ark is to be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
6016	You are to make a roof for the ark, finish its walls a cubit from the top, place a door in the side of the ark, and build lower, middle, and upper decks.
6017	And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life. Everything on the earth will perish.
6018	But I will establish My covenant with you, and you will enter the ark—you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.
6019	And you are to bring two of every living creature into the ark—male and female—to keep them alive with you.
6020	Two of every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to you to be kept alive.
6021	You are also to take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten and gather it as food for yourselves and for the animals.”
6022	So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.
7001	Then the LORD said to Noah, “Go into the ark, you and all your family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.
7002	You are to take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate; a pair of every kind of unclean animal, a male and its mate;
7003	and seven pairs of every kind of bird of the air, male and female, to preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth.
7004	For seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe from the face of the earth every living thing I have made.”
7005	And Noah did all that the LORD had commanded him.
7006	Now Noah was 600 years old when the floodwaters came upon the earth.
7007	And Noah and his wife, with his sons and their wives, entered the ark to escape the waters of the flood.
7008	The clean and unclean animals, the birds, and everything that crawls along the ground
7009	came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.
7010	And after seven days the floodwaters came upon the earth.
7011	In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.
7012	And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
7013	On that very day Noah entered the ark, along with his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and his wife, and the three wives of his sons—
7014	they and every kind of wild animal, livestock, crawling creature, bird, and winged creature.
7015	They came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two of every creature with the breath of life.
7016	And they entered, the male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the LORD shut him in.
7017	For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth, and the waters rose and lifted the ark high above the earth.
7018	So the waters continued to surge and rise greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the waters.
7019	Finally, the waters completely prevailed upon the earth, so that all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered.
7020	The waters rose and covered the mountaintops to a depth of fifteen cubits.
7021	And every living thing that moved upon the earth perished—birds, livestock, animals, every creature that swarms upon the earth, and all mankind.
7022	Of all that was on dry land, everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.
7023	And every living thing on the face of the earth was destroyed—man and livestock, crawling creatures and birds of the air; they were blotted out from the earth, and only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.
7024	And the waters prevailed upon the earth for 150 days.
8001	But God remembered Noah and all the animals and livestock that were with him in the ark. And God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to subside.
8002	The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens were closed, and the rain from the sky was restrained.
8003	The waters receded steadily from the earth, and after 150 days the waters had gone down.
8004	On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
8005	And the waters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible.
8006	After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
8007	and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth.
8008	Then Noah sent out a dove to see if the waters had receded from the surface of the ground.
8009	But the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned to him in the ark, because the waters were still covering the surface of all the earth. So he reached out his hand and brought her back inside the ark.
8010	Noah waited seven more days and again sent out the dove from the ark.
8011	And behold, the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak. So Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth.
8012	And Noah waited seven more days and sent out the dove again, but this time she did not return to him.
8013	In Noah’s six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the waters had dried up from the earth. So Noah removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.
8014	By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was fully dry.
8015	Then God said to Noah,
8016	“Come out of the ark, you and your wife, along with your sons and their wives.
8017	Bring out all the living creatures that are with you—birds, livestock, and everything that crawls upon the ground—so that they can spread out over the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon it.”
8018	So Noah came out, along with his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives.
8019	Every living creature, every creeping thing, and every bird—everything that moves upon the earth—came out of the ark, kind by kind.
8020	Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. And taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar.
8021	When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma, He said in His heart, “Never again will I curse the ground because of man, even though every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth. And never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done.
8022	As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease.”
9001	And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.
9002	The fear and dread of you will fall on every living creature on the earth, every bird of the air, every creature that crawls on the ground, and all the fish of the sea. They are delivered into your hand.
9003	Everything that lives and moves will be food for you; just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you all things.
9004	But you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it.
9005	And surely I will require the life of any man or beast by whose hand your lifeblood is shed. I will demand an accounting from anyone who takes the life of his fellow man:
9006	Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood will be shed; for in His own image God has made mankind.
9007	But as for you, be fruitful and multiply; spread out across the earth and multiply upon it.”
9008	Then God said to Noah and his sons with him,
9009	“Behold, I now establish My covenant with you and your descendants after you,
9010	and with every living creature that was with you—the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth—every living thing that came out of the ark.
9011	And I establish My covenant with you: Never again will all life be cut off by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth.”
9012	And God said, “This is the sign of the covenant I am making between Me and you and every living creature with you, a covenant for all generations to come:
9013	I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth.
9014	Whenever I form clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds,
9015	I will remember My covenant between Me and you and every living creature of every kind. Never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all life.
9016	And whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of every kind that is on the earth.”
9017	So God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between Me and every creature on the earth.”
9018	The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. And Ham was the father of Canaan.
9019	These three were the sons of Noah, and from them the whole earth was populated.
9020	Now Noah, a man of the soil, proceeded to plant a vineyard.
9021	But when he drank some of its wine, he became drunk and uncovered himself inside his tent.
9022	And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father’s nakedness and told his two brothers outside.
9023	Then Shem and Japheth took a garment and placed it across their shoulders, and walking backward, they covered their father’s nakedness. Their faces were turned away so that they did not see their father’s nakedness.
9024	When Noah awoke from his drunkenness and learned what his youngest son had done to him,
9025	he said, “Cursed be Canaan! A servant of servants shall he be to his brothers.”
9026	He also declared: “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be the servant of Shem.
9027	May God expand the territory of Japheth; may he dwell in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be his servant.”
9028	After the flood, Noah lived 350 years.
9029	So Noah lived a total of 950 years, and then he died.
10001	This is the account of Noah’s sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, who also had sons after the flood.
10002	The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
10003	The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
10004	And the sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittites, and the Rodanites.
10005	From these, the maritime peoples separated into their territories, according to their languages, by clans within their nations.
10006	The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
10007	The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
10008	Cush was the father of Nimrod, who began to be a mighty one on the earth.
10009	He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; so it is said, “Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.”
10010	His kingdom began in Babylon, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
10011	From that land he went forth into Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,
10012	and Resen, which is between Nineveh and the great city of Calah.
10013	Mizraim was the father of the Ludites, the Anamites, the Lehabites, the Naphtuhites,
10014	the Pathrusites, the Casluhites (from whom the Philistines came), and the Caphtorites.
10015	And Canaan was the father of Sidon his firstborn, and of the Hittites,
10016	the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
10017	the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
10018	the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Later the Canaanite clans were scattered,
10019	and the borders of Canaan extended from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and then toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
10020	These are the sons of Ham according to their clans, languages, lands, and nations.
10021	And sons were also born to Shem, the older brother of Japheth; Shem was the forefather of all the sons of Eber.
10022	The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
10023	The sons of Aram: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
10024	Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.
10025	Two sons were born to Eber: One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother was named Joktan.
10026	And Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
10027	Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
10028	Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
10029	Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.
10030	Their territory extended from Mesha to Sephar, in the eastern hill country.
10031	These are the sons of Shem, according to their clans, languages, lands, and nations.
10032	All these are the clans of Noah’s sons, according to their generations and nations. From these the nations of the earth spread out after the flood.
11001	Now the whole world had one language and a common form of speech.
11002	And as people journeyed eastward, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
11003	And they said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks and bake them thoroughly.” So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.
11004	“Come,” they said, “let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens, that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.”
11005	Then the LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the sons of men were building.
11006	And the LORD said, “If they have begun to do this as one people speaking the same language, then nothing they devise will be beyond them.
11007	Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.”
11008	So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.
11009	That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world, and from that place the LORD scattered them over the face of all the earth.
11010	This is the account of Shem. Two years after the flood, when Shem was 100 years old, he became the father of Arphaxad.
11011	And after he had become the father of Arphaxad, Shem lived 500 years and had other sons and daughters.
11012	When Arphaxad was 35 years old, he became the father of Shelah.
11013	And after he had become the father of Shelah, Arphaxad lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
11014	When Shelah was 30 years old, he became the father of Eber.
11015	And after he had become the father of Eber, Shelah lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
11016	When Eber was 34 years old, he became the father of Peleg.
11017	And after he had become the father of Peleg, Eber lived 430 years and had other sons and daughters.
11018	When Peleg was 30 years old, he became the father of Reu.
11019	And after he had become the father of Reu, Peleg lived 209 years and had other sons and daughters.
11020	When Reu was 32 years old, he became the father of Serug.
11021	And after he had become the father of Serug, Reu lived 207 years and had other sons and daughters.
11022	When Serug was 30 years old, he became the father of Nahor.
11023	And after he had become the father of Nahor, Serug lived 200 years and had other sons and daughters.
11024	When Nahor was 29 years old, he became the father of Terah.
11025	And after he had become the father of Terah, Nahor lived 119 years and had other sons and daughters.
11026	When Terah was 70 years old, he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
11027	This is the account of Terah. Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. And Haran became the father of Lot.
11028	During his father Terah’s lifetime, Haran died in his native land, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
11029	And Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. Abram’s wife was named Sarai, and Nahor’s wife was named Milcah; she was the daughter of Haran, who was the father of both Milcah and Iscah.
11030	But Sarai was barren; she had no children.
11031	And Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai the wife of Abram, and they set out from Ur of the Chaldeans for the land of Canaan. But when they arrived in Haran, they settled there.
11032	Terah lived 205 years, and he died in Haran.
12001	Then the LORD said to Abram, “Leave your country, your kindred, and your father’s household, and go to the land I will show you.
12002	I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.
12003	I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you; and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”
12004	So Abram departed, as the LORD had directed him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
12005	And Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all the possessions and people they had acquired in Haran, and set out for the land of Canaan. When they came to the land of Canaan,
12006	Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the Oak of Moreh at Shechem. And at that time the Canaanites were in the land.
12007	Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring.” So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
12008	From there Abram moved on to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the LORD, and he called on the name of the LORD.
12009	And Abram journeyed on toward the Negev.
12010	Now there was a famine in the land. So Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while because the famine was severe.
12011	As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, “Look, I know that you are a beautiful woman,
12012	and when the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife.’ Then they will kill me but will let you live.
12013	Please say you are my sister, so that I will be treated well for your sake, and on account of you my life will be spared.”
12014	So when Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
12015	When Pharaoh’s officials saw Sarai, they commended her to him, and she was taken into the palace of Pharaoh.
12016	He treated Abram well on her account, and Abram acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels.
12017	The LORD, however, afflicted Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Abram’s wife Sarai.
12018	So Pharaoh summoned Abram and asked, “What have you done to me? Why didn’t you tell me she was your wife?
12019	Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? Now then, here is your wife. Take her and go!”
12020	Then Pharaoh gave his men orders concerning Abram, and they sent him away with his wife and all his possessions.
13001	So Abram went up out of Egypt into the Negev—he and his wife and all his possessions—and Lot was with him.
13002	And Abram had become extremely wealthy in livestock and silver and gold.
13003	From the Negev he journeyed from place to place toward Bethel, until he came to the place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had formerly been pitched,
13004	to the site where he had built the altar. And there Abram called on the name of the LORD.
13005	Now Lot, who was traveling with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents.
13006	But the land was unable to support both of them while they stayed together, for they had so many possessions that they were unable to coexist.
13007	And there was discord between the herdsmen of Abram and the herdsmen of Lot. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were also living in the land.
13008	So Abram said to Lot, “Please let there be no contention between you and me, or between your herdsmen and my herdsmen. After all, we are kinsmen.
13009	Is not the whole land before you? Now separate yourself from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right; if you go to the right, I will go to the left.”
13010	And Lot looked out and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan, all the way to Zoar, was well watered like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt. (This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)
13011	So Lot chose the whole plain of the Jordan for himself and set out toward the east. And Abram and Lot parted company.
13012	Abram lived in the land of Canaan, but Lot settled in the cities of the plain and pitched his tent toward Sodom.
13013	But the men of Sodom were wicked, sinning greatly against the LORD.
13014	After Lot had departed, the LORD said to Abram, “Now lift up your eyes from the place where you are, and look to the north and south and east and west,
13015	for all the land that you see, I will give to you and your offspring forever.
13016	I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if one could count the dust of the earth, then your offspring could be counted.
13017	Get up and walk around the land, through its length and breadth, for I will give it to you.”
13018	So Abram moved his tent and went to live near the Oaks of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar to the LORD.
14001	In those days Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim
14002	went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar).
14003	The latter five came as allies to the Valley of Siddim (that is, the Salt Sea).
14004	For twelve years they had been subject to Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
14005	In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him went out and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, the Emites in Shaveh-kiriathaim,
14006	and the Horites in the area of Mount Seir, as far as El-paran, which is near the desert.
14007	Then they turned back to invade En-mishpat (that is, Kadesh), and they conquered the whole territory of the Amalekites, as well as the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.
14008	Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar) marched out and arrayed themselves for battle in the Valley of Siddim
14009	against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar—four kings against five.
14010	Now the Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits, and as the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some men fell into the pits, but the survivors fled to the hill country.
14011	The four kings seized all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food, and they went on their way.
14012	They also carried off Abram’s nephew Lot and his possessions, since Lot was living in Sodom.
14013	Then an escapee came and reported this to Abram the Hebrew. Now Abram was living near the Oaks of Mamre the Amorite, a brother of Eshcol and Aner, all of whom were bound by treaty to Abram.
14014	And when Abram heard that his relative had been captured, he mobilized the 318 trained men born in his household, and they set out in pursuit as far as Dan.
14015	During the night, Abram divided his forces and routed Chedorlaomer’s army, pursuing them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.
14016	He retrieved all the goods, as well as his relative Lot and his possessions, together with the women and the rest of the people.
14017	After Abram returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh (that is, the King’s Valley).
14018	Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine—since he was priest of God Most High —
14019	and he blessed Abram and said: “Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
14020	and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
14021	The king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, but take the goods for yourself.”
14022	But Abram replied to the king of Sodom, “I have raised my hand to the LORD God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
14023	that I will not accept even a thread, or a strap of a sandal, or anything that belongs to you, lest you should say, ‘I have made Abram rich.’
14024	I will accept nothing but what my men have eaten and the share for the men who went with me—Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. They may take their portion.”
15001	After these events, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.”
15002	But Abram replied, “O Lord GOD, what can You give me, since I remain childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?”
15003	Abram continued, “Behold, You have given me no offspring, so a servant in my household will be my heir.”
15004	Then the word of the LORD came to Abram, saying, “This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own body will be your heir.”
15005	And the LORD took him outside and said, “Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.” Then He told him, “So shall your offspring be.”
15006	Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
15007	The LORD also told him, “I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess.”
15008	But Abram replied, “Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it?”
15009	And the LORD said to him, “Bring Me a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon.”
15010	So Abram brought all these to Him, split each of them down the middle, and laid the halves opposite each other. The birds, however, he did not cut in half.
15011	And the birds of prey descended on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
15012	As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and suddenly great terror and darkness overwhelmed him.
15013	Then the LORD said to Abram, “Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.
15014	But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves, and afterward they will depart with many possessions.
15015	You, however, will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a ripe old age.
15016	In the fourth generation your descendants will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.”
15017	When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, behold, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appeared and passed between the halves of the carcasses.
15018	On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your descendants I have given this land—from the river of Egypt to the great River Euphrates—
15019	the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites,
15020	Hittites, Perizzites, Rephaites,
15021	Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites.”
16001	Now Abram’s wife Sarai had borne him no children, but she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.
16002	So Sarai said to Abram, “Look now, the LORD has prevented me from bearing children. Please go to my maidservant; perhaps I can build a family by her.” And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
16003	So after he had lived in Canaan for ten years, his wife Sarai took her Egyptian maidservant Hagar and gave her to Abram to be his wife.
16004	And he slept with Hagar, and she conceived. But when Hagar realized that she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.
16005	Then Sarai said to Abram, “May the wrong done to me be upon you! I delivered my servant into your arms, and ever since she saw that she was pregnant, she has treated me with contempt. May the LORD judge between you and me.”
16006	“Here,” said Abram, “your servant is in your hands. Do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that she fled from her.
16007	Now the angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring of water in the desert—the spring along the road to Shur.
16008	“Hagar, servant of Sarai,” he said, “where have you come from, and where are you going?” “I am running away from my mistress Sarai,” she replied.
16009	So the angel of the LORD told her, “Return to your mistress and submit to her authority.”
16010	Then the angel added, “I will greatly multiply your offspring so that they will be too numerous to count.”
16011	The angel of the LORD proceeded: “Behold, you have conceived and will bear a son. And you shall name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your cry of affliction.
16012	He will be a wild donkey of a man, and his hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand against him; he will live in hostility toward all his brothers.”
16013	So Hagar gave this name to the LORD who had spoken to her: “You are the God who sees me,” for she said, “Here I have seen the One who sees me!”
16014	Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi. It is located between Kadesh and Bered.
16015	And Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.
16016	Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.
17001	When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, “I am God Almighty. Walk before Me and be blameless.
17002	I will establish My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.”
17003	Then Abram fell facedown, and God said to him,
17004	“As for Me, this is My covenant with you: You will be the father of many nations.
17005	No longer will you be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.
17006	I will make you exceedingly fruitful; I will make nations of you, and kings will descend from you.
17007	I will establish My covenant as an everlasting covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you, to be your God and the God of your descendants after you.
17008	And to you and your descendants I will give the land where you are residing—all the land of Canaan—as an eternal possession; and I will be their God.”
17009	God also said to Abraham, “You must keep My covenant—you and your descendants in the generations after you.
17010	This is My covenant with you and your descendants after you, which you are to keep: Every male among you must be circumcised.
17011	You are to circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and this will be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.
17012	Generation after generation, every male must be circumcised when he is eight days old, including those born in your household and those purchased from a foreigner—even those who are not your offspring.
17013	Whether they are born in your household or purchased, they must be circumcised. My covenant in your flesh will be an everlasting covenant.
17014	But if any male is not circumcised, he will be cut off from his people; he has broken My covenant.”
17015	Then God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, do not call her Sarai, for her name is to be Sarah.
17016	And I will bless her and will surely give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she will be the mother of nations; kings of peoples will descend from her.”
17017	Abraham fell facedown. Then he laughed and said to himself, “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Can Sarah give birth at the age of ninety?”
17018	And Abraham said to God, “O that Ishmael might live under Your blessing!”
17019	But God replied, “Your wife Sarah will indeed bear you a son, and you are to name him Isaac. I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.
17020	As for Ishmael, I have heard you, and I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly. He will become the father of twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation.
17021	But I will establish My covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year.”
17022	When He had finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him.
17023	On that very day Abraham took his son Ishmael and all those born in his household or purchased with his money—every male among the members of Abraham’s household—and he circumcised them, just as God had told him.
17024	So Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised,
17025	and his son Ishmael was thirteen;
17026	Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised on the same day.
17027	And all the men of Abraham’s household—both servants born in his household and those purchased from foreigners—were circumcised with him.
18001	Then the LORD appeared to Abraham by the Oaks of Mamre in the heat of the day, while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent.
18002	And Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground.
18003	“My lord,” said Abraham, “if I have found favor in your sight, please do not pass your servant by.
18004	Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.
18005	And I will bring a bit of bread so that you may refresh yourselves. This is why you have passed your servant’s way. After that, you may continue on your way.” “Yes,” they replied, “you may do as you have said.”
18006	So Abraham hurried into the tent and said to Sarah, “Quick! Prepare three seahs of fine flour, knead it, and bake some bread.”

18011	And Abraham and Sarah were already old and well along in years; Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
18012	So she laughed to herself, saying, “After I am worn out and my master is old, will I now have this pleasure?”

18014	Is anything too difficult for the LORD? At the appointed time I will return to you—in about a year—and Sarah will have a son.”
18015	But Sarah was afraid, so she denied it and said, “I did not laugh.” “No,” replied the LORD, “but you did laugh.”
18016	When the men got up to leave, they looked out over Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them off.
18017	And the LORD said, “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?
18018	Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and through him all the nations of the earth will be blessed.
18019	For I have chosen him, so that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just, in order that the LORD may bring upon Abraham what He has promised.”
18020	Then the LORD said, “The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great. Because their sin is so grievous,
18021	I will go down to see if their actions fully justify the outcry that has reached Me. If not, I will find out.”
18022	And the two men turned away and went toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before the LORD.
18023	Abraham stepped forward and said, “Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
18024	What if there are fifty righteous ones in the city? Will You really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous ones who are there?
18025	Far be it from You to do such a thing—to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike. Far be it from You! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?”
18026	So the LORD replied, “If I find fifty righteous ones within the city of Sodom, on their account I will spare the whole place.”
18027	Then Abraham answered, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord—though I am but dust and ashes—
18028	suppose the fifty righteous ones lack five. Will You destroy the whole city for the lack of five?” He replied, “If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it.”
18029	Once again Abraham spoke to the LORD, “Suppose forty are found there?” He answered, “On account of the forty, I will not do it.”
18030	Then Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak further. Suppose thirty are found there?” He replied, “If I find thirty there, I will not do it.”
18031	And Abraham said, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord, suppose twenty are found there?” He answered, “On account of the twenty, I will not destroy it.”
18032	Finally, Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak once more. Suppose ten are found there?” And He answered, “On account of the ten, I will not destroy it.”
18033	When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, He departed, and Abraham returned home.
19001	Now the two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city. When Lot saw them, he got up to meet them, bowed facedown,
19002	and said, “My lords, please turn aside into the house of your servant; wash your feet and spend the night. Then you can rise early and go on your way.” “No,” they answered, “we will spend the night in the square.”
19003	But Lot insisted so strongly that they followed him into his house. He prepared a feast for them and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
19004	Before they had gone to bed, all the men of the city of Sodom, both young and old, surrounded the house.
19005	They called out to Lot, saying, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Send them out to us so we can have relations with them!”
19006	Lot went outside to meet them, shutting the door behind him.
19007	“Please, my brothers,” he pleaded, “don’t do such a wicked thing!

19009	“Get out of the way!” they replied. And they declared, “This one came here as a foreigner, and he is already acting like a judge! Now we will treat you worse than them.” And they pressed in on Lot and moved in to break down the door.

19011	And they struck the men at the entrance, young and old, with blindness, so that they wearied themselves trying to find the door.

19013	because we are about to destroy this place. For the outcry to the LORD against its people is so great that He has sent us to destroy it.”
19014	So Lot went out and spoke to the sons-in-law who were pledged in marriage to his daughters. “Get up,” he said. “Get out of this place, for the LORD is about to destroy the city!” But his sons-in-law thought he was joking.
19015	At daybreak the angels hurried Lot along, saying, “Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away in the punishment of the city.”
19016	But when Lot hesitated, the men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters. And they led them safely out of the city, because of the LORD’s compassion for them.
19017	As soon as the men had brought them out, one of them said, “Run for your lives! Do not look back, and do not stop anywhere on the plain! Flee to the mountains, or you will be swept away!”
19018	But Lot replied, “No, my lords, please!
19019	Your servant has indeed found favor in your sight, and you have shown me great kindness by sparing my life. But I cannot run to the mountains; the disaster will overtake me, and I will die.
19020	Look, there is a town nearby where I can flee, and it is a small place. Please let me flee there—is it not a small place? Then my life will be saved.”
19021	“Very well,” he answered, “I will grant this request as well, and will not demolish the town you indicate.
19022	Hurry! Run there quickly, for I cannot do anything until you reach it.” That is why the town was called Zoar.
19023	And by the time the sun had risen over the land, Lot had reached Zoar.
19024	Then the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah—from the LORD out of the heavens.

19026	But Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
19027	Early the next morning, Abraham got up and returned to the place where he had stood before the LORD.
19028	He looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and all the land of the plain, and he saw the smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace.
19029	So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, He remembered Abraham, and He brought Lot out of the catastrophe that destroyed the cities where he had lived.
19030	Lot and his two daughters left Zoar and settled in the mountains—for he was afraid to stay in Zoar—where they lived in a cave.
19031	One day the older daughter said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is no man in the land to sleep with us, as is the custom over all the earth.
19032	Come, let us get our father drunk with wine so we can sleep with him and preserve his line.”
19033	So that night they got their father drunk with wine, and the firstborn went in and slept with her father; he was not aware when she lay down or when she got up.

20001	Now Abraham journeyed from there to the region of the Negev and settled between Kadesh and Shur. While he was staying in Gerar,
20002	Abraham said of his wife Sarah, “She is my sister.” So Abimelech king of Gerar had Sarah brought to him.
20003	One night, however, God came to Abimelech in a dream and told him, “You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken, for she is a married woman.”
20004	Now Abimelech had not gone near her, so he replied, “Lord, would You destroy a nation even though it is innocent?
20005	Didn’t Abraham tell me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself said, ‘He is my brother.’ I have done this in the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands.”
20006	Then God said to Abimelech in the dream, “Yes, I know that you did this with a clear conscience, and so I have kept you from sinning against Me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
20007	Now return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet; he will pray for you and you will live. But if you do not restore her, be aware that you will surely die—you and all who belong to you.”
20008	Early the next morning Abimelech got up and summoned all his servants; and when he described to them all that had happened, the men were terrified.
20009	Then Abimelech called Abraham and asked, “What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought such tremendous guilt upon me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should not be done.”
20010	Abimelech also asked Abraham, “What prompted you to do such a thing?”
20011	Abraham replied, “I thought to myself, ‘Surely there is no fear of God in this place. They will kill me on account of my wife.’
20012	Besides, she really is my sister, the daughter of my father—though not the daughter of my mother—and she became my wife.
20013	So when God had me journey from my father’s house, I said to Sarah, ‘This is how you can show your loyalty to me: Wherever we go, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
