26031	And they got up early the next morning and swore an oath to each other. Then Isaac sent them on their way, and they left him in peace.
26032	On that same day, Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well they had dug. “We have found water!” they told him.
26033	So he called it Shibah, and to this day the name of the city is Beersheba.
26034	When Esau was forty years old, he took as his wives Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite.
26035	And they brought grief to Isaac and Rebekah.
27001	When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see, he called his older son Esau and said to him, “My son.” “Here I am,” Esau replied.
27002	“Look,” said Isaac, “I am now old, and I do not know the day of my death.
27003	Take your weapons—your quiver and bow—and go out into the field to hunt some game for me.
27004	Then prepare a tasty dish that I love and bring it to me to eat, so that I may bless you before I die.”
27005	Now Rebekah was listening to what Isaac told his son Esau. So when Esau went into the field to hunt game and bring it back,
27006	Rebekah said to her son Jacob, “Behold, I overheard your father saying to your brother Esau,
27007	‘Bring me some game and prepare me a tasty dish to eat, so that I may bless you in the presence of the LORD before I die.’
27008	Now, my son, listen to my voice and do exactly as I tell you.
27009	Go out to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, so that I can make them into a tasty dish for your father—the kind he loves.
27010	Then take it to your father to eat, so that he may bless you before he dies.”
27011	Jacob answered his mother Rebekah, “Look, my brother Esau is a hairy man, but I am smooth-skinned.
27012	What if my father touches me? Then I would be revealed to him as a deceiver, and I would bring upon myself a curse rather than a blessing.”
27013	His mother replied, “Your curse be on me, my son. Just obey my voice and go get them for me.”
27014	So Jacob went and got two goats and brought them to his mother, who made the tasty food his father loved.
27015	And Rebekah took the finest clothes in the house that belonged to her older son Esau, and she put them on her younger son Jacob.
27016	She also put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.
27017	Then she handed her son Jacob the tasty food and bread she had made.
27018	So Jacob went to his father and said, “My father.” “Here I am!” he answered. “Which one are you, my son?”
27019	Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please sit up and eat some of my game, so that you may bless me.”
27020	But Isaac asked his son, “How did you ever find it so quickly, my son?” “Because the LORD your God brought it to me,” he replied.
27021	Then Isaac said to Jacob, “Please come closer so I can touch you, my son. Are you really my son Esau, or not?”
27022	So Jacob came close to his father Isaac, who touched him and said, “The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”
27023	Isaac did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like those of his brother Esau; so he blessed him.
27024	Again he asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” And he replied, “I am.”
27025	“Serve me,” said Isaac, “and let me eat some of my son’s game, so that I may bless you.” Jacob brought it to him, and he ate; then he brought him wine, and he drank.
27026	Then his father Isaac said to him, “Please come near and kiss me, my son.”
27027	So he came near and kissed him. When Isaac smelled his clothing, he blessed him and said: “Ah, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field that the LORD has blessed.
27028	May God give to you the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth— an abundance of grain and new wine.
27029	May peoples serve you and nations bow down to you. May you be the master of your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed, and those who bless you be blessed.”
27030	As soon as Isaac had finished blessing him and Jacob had left his father’s presence, his brother Esau returned from the hunt.
27031	He too made some tasty food, brought it to his father, and said to him, “My father, sit up and eat of your son’s game, so that you may bless me.”
27032	But his father Isaac replied, “Who are you?” “I am Esau, your firstborn son,” he answered.
27033	Isaac began to tremble violently and said, “Who was it, then, who hunted the game and brought it to me? Before you came in, I ate it all and blessed him—and indeed, he will be blessed!”
27034	When Esau heard his father’s words, he let out a loud and bitter cry and said to his father, “Bless me too, O my father!”
27035	But Isaac replied, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.”
27036	So Esau declared, “Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has cheated me twice. He took my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing.” Then he asked, “Haven’t you saved a blessing for me?”
27037	But Isaac answered Esau: “Look, I have made him your master and given him all his relatives as servants; I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What is left that I can do for you, my son?”
27038	Esau said to his father, “Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, O my father!” Then Esau wept aloud.
27039	His father Isaac answered him: “Behold, your dwelling place shall be away from the richness of the land, away from the dew of heaven above.
27040	You shall live by the sword and serve your brother. But when you rebel, you will tear his yoke from your neck.”
27041	Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him. And Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then I will kill my brother Jacob.”
27042	When the words of her older son Esau were relayed to Rebekah, she sent for her younger son Jacob and told him, “Look, your brother Esau is consoling himself by plotting to kill you.
27043	So now, my son, obey my voice and flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran.
27044	Stay with him for a while, until your brother’s fury subsides—
27045	until your brother’s rage against you wanes and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send for you and bring you back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?”
27046	Then Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of these Hittite women. If Jacob takes a Hittite wife from among them, what good is my life?”
28001	So Isaac called for Jacob and blessed him. “Do not take a wife from the Canaanite women,” he commanded.
28002	“Go at once to Paddan-aram, to the house of your mother’s father Bethuel, and take a wife from among the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
28003	May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you may become a company of peoples.
28004	And may He give the blessing of Abraham to you and your descendants, so that you may possess the land where you dwell as a foreigner, the land God gave to Abraham.”
28005	So Isaac sent Jacob to Paddan-aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, who was the mother of Jacob and Esau.
28006	Now Esau learned that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to take a wife there, commanding him, “Do not marry a Canaanite woman,”
28007	and that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and gone to Paddan-aram.
28008	And seeing that his father Isaac disapproved of the Canaanite women,
28009	Esau went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth and daughter of Abraham’s son Ishmael, in addition to the wives he already had.
28010	Meanwhile Jacob left Beersheba and set out for Haran.
28011	On reaching a certain place, he spent the night there because the sun had set. And taking one of the stones from that place, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep.
28012	And Jacob had a dream about a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven, and God’s angels were going up and down the ladder.
28013	And there at the top the LORD was standing and saying, “I am the LORD, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will give you and your descendants the land on which you now lie.
28014	Your descendants will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out to the west and east and north and south. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you and your offspring.
28015	Look, I am with you, and I will watch over you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. For I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.”
28016	When Jacob woke up, he said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was unaware of it.”
28017	And he was afraid and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven!”
28018	Early the next morning, Jacob took the stone that he had placed under his head, and he set it up as a pillar. He poured oil on top of it,
28019	and he called that place Bethel, though previously the city had been named Luz.
28020	Then Jacob made a vow, saying, “If God will be with me and watch over me on this journey, and if He will provide me with food to eat and clothes to wear,
28021	so that I may return safely to my father’s house, then the LORD will be my God.
28022	And this stone I have set up as a pillar will be God’s house, and of all that You give me I will surely give You a tenth.”
29001	Jacob resumed his journey and came to the land of the people of the east.
29002	He looked and saw a well in the field, and near it lay three flocks of sheep, because the sheep were watered from this well. And a large stone covered the mouth of the well.
29003	When all the flocks had been gathered there, the shepherds would roll away the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep. Then they would return the stone to its place over the mouth of the well.
29004	“My brothers,” Jacob asked the shepherds, “where are you from?” “We are from Haran,” they answered.
29005	“Do you know Laban the grandson of Nahor?” Jacob asked. “We know him,” they replied.
29006	“Is he well?” Jacob inquired. “Yes,” they answered, “and here comes his daughter Rachel with his sheep.”
29007	“Look,” said Jacob, “it is still broad daylight; it is not yet time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep and take them back to pasture.”
29008	But they replied, “We cannot, until all the flocks have been gathered and the stone has been rolled away from the mouth of the well. Then we will water the sheep.”
29009	While he was still speaking with them, Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.
29010	As soon as Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his mother’s brother Laban, with Laban’s sheep, he went up and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle’s sheep.
29011	Then Jacob kissed Rachel and wept aloud.
29012	He told Rachel that he was Rebekah’s son, a relative of her father, and she ran and told her father.
29013	When Laban heard the news about his sister’s son Jacob, he ran out to meet him. He embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him all that had happened.
29014	Then Laban declared, “You are indeed my own flesh and blood.” After Jacob had stayed with him a month,
29015	Laban said to him, “Just because you are my relative, should you work for nothing? Tell me what your wages should be.”
29016	Now Laban had two daughters; the older was named Leah, and the younger was named Rachel.
29017	Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel was shapely and beautiful.
29018	Since Jacob loved Rachel, he answered, “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.”
29019	Laban replied, “Better that I give her to you than to another. Stay here with me.”
29020	So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, yet it seemed but a few days because of his love for her.
29021	Finally Jacob said to Laban, “Grant me my wife, for my time is complete, and I want to sleep with her.”
29022	So Laban invited all the men of that place and prepared a feast.
29023	But when evening came, Laban took his daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob, and he slept with her.
29024	And Laban gave his servant girl Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maidservant.
29025	When morning came, there was Leah! “What have you done to me?” Jacob said to Laban. “Wasn’t it for Rachel that I served you? Why have you deceived me?”
29026	Laban replied, “It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older.
29027	Finish this week’s celebration, and we will give you the younger one in return for another seven years of work.”
29028	And Jacob did just that. He finished the week’s celebration, and Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
29029	Laban also gave his servant girl Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her maidservant.
29030	Jacob slept with Rachel as well, and indeed, he loved Rachel more than Leah. So he worked for Laban another seven years.
29031	When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
29032	And Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she named him Reuben, for she said, “The LORD has seen my affliction. Surely my husband will love me now.”
29033	Again she conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Because the LORD has heard that I am unloved, He has given me this son as well.” So she named him Simeon.
29034	Once again Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Now at last my husband will become attached to me, because I have borne him three sons.” So he was named Levi.
29035	And once more she conceived and gave birth to a son and said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” So she named him Judah. Then Leah stopped having children.
30001	When Rachel saw that she was not bearing any children for Jacob, she envied her sister. “Give me children, or I will die!” she said to Jacob.
30002	Jacob became angry with Rachel and said, “Am I in the place of God, who has withheld children from you?”
30003	Then she said, “Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Sleep with her, that she may bear children for me, so that through her I too can build a family.”
30004	So Rachel gave Jacob her servant Bilhah as a wife, and he slept with her,
30005	and Bilhah conceived and bore him a son.
30006	Then Rachel said, “God has vindicated me; He has heard my plea and given me a son.” So she named him Dan.
30007	And Rachel’s servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.
30008	Then Rachel said, “In my great struggles, I have wrestled with my sister and won.” So she named him Naphtali.
30009	When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife.
30010	And Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a son.
30011	Then Leah said, “How fortunate!” So she named him Gad.
30012	When Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a second son,
30013	Leah said, “How happy I am! For the women call me happy.” So she named him Asher.
30014	Now during the wheat harvest, Reuben went out and found some mandrakes in the field. When he brought them to his mother, Rachel begged Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”
30015	But Leah replied, “Is it not enough that you have taken away my husband? Now you want to take my son’s mandrakes as well?” “Very well,” said Rachel, “he may sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.”
30016	When Jacob came in from the field that evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, “You must come with me, for I have hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” So he slept with her that night.
30017	And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore a fifth son to Jacob.
30018	Then Leah said, “God has rewarded me for giving my maidservant to my husband.” So she named him Issachar.
30019	Again Leah conceived and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
30020	“God has given me a good gift,” she said. “This time my husband will honor me, because I have borne him six sons.” And she named him Zebulun.
30021	After that, Leah gave birth to a daughter and named her Dinah.
30022	Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and opened her womb,
30023	and she conceived and gave birth to a son. “God has taken away my shame,” she said.
30024	She named him Joseph, and said, “May the LORD add to me another son.”
30025	Now after Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me on my way so I can return to my homeland.
30026	Give me my wives and children for whom I have served you, that I may go on my way. You know how hard I have worked for you.”
30027	But Laban replied, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please stay. I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you.”
30028	And he added, “Name your wages, and I will pay them.”
30029	Then Jacob answered, “You know how I have served you and how your livestock have thrived under my care.
30030	Indeed, you had very little before my arrival, but now your wealth has increased many times over. The LORD has blessed you wherever I set foot. But now, when may I also provide for my own household?”
30031	“What can I give you?” Laban asked. “You do not need to give me anything,” Jacob replied. “If you do this one thing for me, I will keep on shepherding and keeping your flocks.
30032	Let me go through all your flocks today and remove from them every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-colored lamb, and every spotted or speckled goat. These will be my wages.
30033	So my honesty will testify for me when you come to check on my wages in the future. If I have any goats that are not speckled or spotted, or any lambs that are not dark-colored, they will be considered stolen.”
30034	“Agreed,” said Laban. “Let it be as you have said.”
30035	That very day Laban removed all the streaked or spotted male goats and every speckled or spotted female goat—every one that had any white on it—and every dark-colored lamb, and he placed them under the care of his sons.
30036	Then he put a three-day journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob was shepherding the rest of Laban’s flocks.
30037	Jacob, however, took fresh branches of poplar, almond, and plane trees, and peeled the bark, exposing the white inner wood of the branches.
30038	Then he set the peeled branches in the watering troughs in front of the flocks coming in to drink. So when the flocks were in heat and came to drink,
30039	they mated in front of the branches. And they bore young that were streaked or speckled or spotted.
30040	Jacob set apart the young, but made the rest face the streaked dark-colored sheep in Laban’s flocks. Then he set his own stock apart and did not put them with Laban’s animals.
30041	Whenever the stronger females of the flock were in heat, Jacob would place the branches in the troughs, in full view of the animals, so that they would breed in front of the branches.
30042	But if the animals were weak, he did not set out the branches. So the weaker animals went to Laban and the stronger ones to Jacob.
30043	Thus Jacob became exceedingly prosperous. He owned large flocks, maidservants and menservants, and camels and donkeys.
31001	Now Jacob heard that Laban’s sons were saying, “Jacob has taken away all that belonged to our father and built all this wealth at our father’s expense.”
31002	And Jacob saw from the countenance of Laban that his attitude toward him had changed.
31003	Then the LORD said to Jacob, “Go back to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.”
31004	So Jacob sent word and called Rachel and Leah to the field where his flocks were,
31005	and he told them, “I can see from your father’s countenance that his attitude toward me has changed; but the God of my father has been with me.
31006	You know that I have served your father with all my strength.
31007	And although he has cheated me and changed my wages ten times, God has not allowed him to harm me.
31008	If he said, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore speckled offspring. If he said, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore streaked offspring.
31009	Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock and given them to me.
31010	When the flocks were breeding, I saw in a dream that the streaked, spotted, and speckled males were mating with the females.
31011	In that dream the angel of God said to me, ‘Jacob!’ And I replied, ‘Here I am.’
31012	‘Look up,’ he said, ‘and see that all the males that are mating with the flock are streaked, spotted, or speckled; for I have seen all that Laban has done to you.
31013	I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the pillar and made a solemn vow to Me. Now get up, leave this land at once, and return to your native land.’”
31014	And Rachel and Leah replied, “Do we have any portion or inheritance left in our father’s house?
31015	Are we not regarded by him as outsiders? Not only has he sold us, but he has certainly squandered what was paid for us.
31016	Surely all the wealth that God has taken away from our father belongs to us and to our children. So do whatever God has told you.”
31017	Then Jacob got up and put his children and his wives on camels,
31018	and he drove all his livestock before him, along with all the possessions he had acquired in Paddan-aram, to go to his father Isaac in the land in Canaan.
31019	Now while Laban was out shearing his sheep, Rachel stole her father’s household idols.
31020	Moreover, Jacob deceived Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was running away.
31021	So he fled with all his possessions, crossed the Euphrates, and headed for the hill country of Gilead.
31022	On the third day Laban was informed that Jacob had fled.
31023	So he took his relatives with him, pursued Jacob for seven days, and overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.
31024	But that night God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream and warned him, “Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.”
31025	Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country of Gilead when Laban overtook him, and Laban and his relatives camped there as well.
31026	Then Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done? You have deceived me and carried off my daughters like captives of war!
31027	Why did you run away secretly and deceive me, without even telling me? I would have sent you away with joy and singing, with tambourines and harps.
31028	But you did not even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. Now you have done a foolish thing.
31029	I have power to do you great harm, but last night the God of your father said to me, ‘Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.’
31030	Now you have gone off because you long for your father’s house. But why have you stolen my gods?”
31031	“I was afraid,” Jacob answered, “for I thought you would take your daughters from me by force.
31032	If you find your gods with anyone here, he shall not live! In the presence of our relatives, see for yourself if anything is yours, and take it back.” For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols.
31033	So Laban went into Jacob’s tent, then Leah’s tent, and then the tents of the two maidservants, but he found nothing. Then he left Leah’s tent and entered Rachel’s tent.
31034	Now Rachel had taken Laban’s household idols, put them in the saddlebag of her camel, and was sitting on them. And Laban searched everything in the tent but found nothing.
31035	Rachel said to her father, “Sir, do not be angry that I cannot stand up before you; for I am having my period.” So Laban searched but could not find the household idols.
31036	Then Jacob became incensed and challenged Laban. “What is my crime?” he said. “For what sin of mine have you so hotly pursued me?
31037	You have searched all my goods! Have you found anything that belongs to you? Put it here before my brothers and yours, that they may judge between the two of us.
31038	I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not miscarried, nor have I eaten the rams of your flock.
31039	I did not bring you anything torn by wild beasts; I bore the loss myself. And you demanded payment from me for what was stolen by day or night.
31040	As it was, the heat consumed me by day and the frost by night, and sleep fled from my eyes.
31041	Thus for twenty years I have served in your household—fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks—and you have changed my wages ten times!
31042	If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, surely by now you would have sent me away empty-handed. But God has seen my affliction and the toil of my hands, and last night He rendered judgment.”
31043	But Laban answered Jacob, “These daughters are my daughters, these sons are my sons, and these flocks are my flocks! Everything you see is mine! Yet what can I do today about these daughters of mine or the children they have borne?
31044	Come now, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it serve as a witness between you and me.”
31045	So Jacob picked out a stone and set it up as a pillar,
31046	and he said to his relatives, “Gather some stones.” So they took stones and made a mound, and there by the mound they ate.
31047	Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.
31048	Then Laban declared, “This mound is a witness between you and me this day.” Therefore the place was called Galeed.
31049	It was also called Mizpah, because Laban said, “May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are absent from each other.
31050	If you mistreat my daughters or take other wives, although no one is with us, remember that God is a witness between you and me.”
31051	Laban also said to Jacob, “Here is the mound, and here is the pillar I have set up between you and me.
31052	This mound is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this mound to harm you, and you will not go past this mound and pillar to harm me.
31053	May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” So Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
31054	Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his relatives to eat a meal. And after they had eaten, they spent the night on the mountain.
31055	Early the next morning, Laban got up and kissed his grandchildren and daughters and blessed them. Then he left to return home.
32001	Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
32002	When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is the camp of God.” So he named that place Mahanaim.
32003	Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
32004	He instructed them, “You are to say to my master Esau, ‘Your servant Jacob says: I have been staying with Laban and have remained there until now.
32005	I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, menservants, and maidservants. I have sent this message to inform my master, so that I may find favor in your sight.’”
32006	When the messengers returned to Jacob, they said, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is coming to meet you—he and four hundred men with him.”
32007	In great fear and distress, Jacob divided his people into two camps, as well as the flocks and herds and camels.
32008	He thought, “If Esau comes and attacks one camp, then the other camp can escape.”
32009	Then Jacob declared, “O God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, the LORD who told me, ‘Go back to your country and to your kindred, and I will make you prosper,’
32010	I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness You have shown Your servant. Indeed, with only my staff I came across the Jordan, but now I have become two camps.
32011	Please deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid that he may come and attack me and the mothers and children with me.
32012	But You have said, ‘I will surely make you prosper, and I will make your offspring like the sand of the sea, too numerous to count.’”
32013	Jacob spent the night there, and from what he had brought with him, he selected a gift for his brother Esau:
32014	200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 ewes, 20 rams,
32015	30 milk camels with their young, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys.
32016	He entrusted them to his servants in separate herds and told them, “Go on ahead of me, and keep some distance between the herds.”
32017	He instructed the one in the lead, “When my brother Esau meets you and asks, ‘To whom do you belong, where are you going, and whose animals are these before you?’
32018	then you are to say, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift, sent to my lord Esau. And behold, Jacob is behind us.’”
32019	He also instructed the second, the third, and all those following behind the herds: “When you meet Esau, you are to say the same thing to him.
32020	You are also to say, ‘Look, your servant Jacob is right behind us.’” For he thought, “I will appease Esau with the gift that is going before me. After that I can face him, and perhaps he will accept me.”
32021	So Jacob’s gifts went on before him, while he spent the night in the camp.
32022	During the night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two maidservants, and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.
32023	He took them and sent them across the stream, along with all his possessions.
32024	So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
32025	When the man saw that he could not overpower Jacob, he struck the socket of Jacob’s hip and dislocated it as they wrestled.
32026	Then the man said, “Let me go, for it is daybreak.” But Jacob replied, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”
32027	“What is your name?” the man asked. “Jacob,” he replied.
32028	Then the man said, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed.”
32029	And Jacob requested, “Please tell me your name.” But he replied, “Why do you ask my name?” Then he blessed Jacob there.
32030	So Jacob named the place Peniel, saying, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.”
32031	The sun rose above him as he passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.
32032	Therefore to this day the Israelites do not eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.
33001	Now Jacob looked up and saw Esau coming toward him with four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two maidservants.
33002	He put the maidservants and their children in front, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph at the rear.
33003	But Jacob himself went on ahead and bowed to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.
33004	Esau, however, ran to him and embraced him, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him. And they both wept.
33005	When Esau looked up and saw the women and children, he asked, “Who are these with you?” Jacob answered, “These are the children God has graciously given your servant.”
33006	Then the maidservants and their children approached and bowed down.
33007	Leah and her children also approached and bowed down, and then Joseph and Rachel approached and bowed down.
33008	“What do you mean by sending this whole company to meet me?” asked Esau. “To find favor in your sight, my lord,” Jacob answered.
33009	“I already have plenty, my brother,” Esau replied. “Keep what belongs to you.”
33010	But Jacob insisted, “No, please! If I have found favor in your sight, then receive this gift from my hand. For indeed, I have seen your face, and it is like seeing the face of God, since you have received me favorably.
33011	Please accept my gift that was brought to you, because God has been gracious to me and I have all I need.” So Jacob pressed him until he accepted.
33012	Then Esau said, “Let us be on our way, and I will go ahead of you.”
33013	But Jacob replied, “My lord knows that the children are frail, and I must care for sheep and cattle that are nursing their young. If they are driven hard for even a day, all the animals will die.
33014	Please let my lord go ahead of his servant. I will continue on slowly, at a comfortable pace for the livestock and children, until I come to my lord at Seir.”
33015	“Let me leave some of my people with you,” Esau said. But Jacob replied, “Why do that? Let me find favor in the sight of my lord.”
33016	So that day Esau started on his way back to Seir,
33017	but Jacob went on to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and shelters for his livestock; that is why the place was called Succoth.
33018	After Jacob had come from Paddan-aram, he arrived safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan, and he camped just outside the city.
33019	And the plot of ground where he pitched his tent, he purchased from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for a hundred pieces of silver.
33020	There he set up an altar and called it El-Elohe-Israel.
34001	Now Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the daughters of the land.
34002	When Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the region, saw her, he took her and lay with her by force.
34003	And his soul was drawn to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob. He loved the young girl and spoke to her tenderly.
34004	So Shechem told his father Hamor, “Get me this girl as a wife.”
34005	Jacob heard that Shechem had defiled his daughter Dinah, but since his sons were with his livestock in the field, he remained silent about it until they returned.
34006	Meanwhile, Shechem’s father Hamor came to speak with Jacob.
34007	When Jacob’s sons heard what had happened, they returned from the field. They were filled with grief and fury, because Shechem had committed an outrage in Israel by lying with Jacob’s daughter—a thing that should not be done.
34008	But Hamor said to them, “My son Shechem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife.
34009	Intermarry with us; give us your daughters and take our daughters for yourselves.
34010	You may settle among us, and the land will be open to you. Live here, move about freely, and acquire your own property.”
34011	Then Shechem said to Dinah’s father and brothers, “Grant me this favor, and I will give you whatever you ask.
34012	Demand a high dowry and an expensive gift, and I will give you whatever you ask. Only give me the girl as my wife!”
34013	But because Shechem had defiled their sister Dinah, Jacob’s sons answered him and his father Hamor deceitfully.
34014	“We cannot do such a thing,” they said. “To give our sister to an uncircumcised man would be a disgrace to us.
34015	We will consent to this on one condition, that you become circumcised like us—every one of your males.
34016	Then we will give you our daughters and take your daughters for ourselves. We will dwell among you and become one people.
34017	But if you will not agree to be circumcised, then we will take our sister and go.”
34018	Their offer seemed good to Hamor and his son Shechem.
34019	The young man, who was the most respected of all his father’s household, did not hesitate to fulfill this request, because he was delighted with Jacob’s daughter.
34020	So Hamor and his son Shechem went to the gate of their city and addressed the men of their city:
34021	“These men are at peace with us. Let them live and trade in our land; indeed, it is large enough for them. Let us take their daughters in marriage and give our daughters to them.
34022	But only on this condition will the men agree to dwell with us and be one people: if all our men are circumcised as they are.
34023	Will not their livestock, their possessions, and all their animals become ours? Only let us consent to them, and they will dwell among us.”
34024	All the men who went out of the city gate listened to Hamor and his son Shechem, and every male of the city was circumcised.
34025	Three days later, while they were still in pain, two of Jacob’s sons (Dinah’s brothers Simeon and Levi) took their swords, went into the unsuspecting city, and slaughtered every male.
34026	They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with their swords, took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went away.
34027	Jacob’s other sons came upon the slaughter and looted the city, because their sister had been defiled.
34028	They took their flocks and herds and donkeys, and everything else in the city or in the field.
34029	They carried off all their possessions and women and children, and they plundered everything in their houses.
34030	Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought trouble upon me by making me a stench to the Canaanites and Perizzites, the people of this land. We are few in number; if they unite against me and attack me, I and my household will be destroyed.”
34031	But they replied, “Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?”
35001	Then God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and settle there. Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau.”
35002	So Jacob told his household and all who were with him, “Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you. Purify yourselves and change your garments.
35003	Then let us arise and go to Bethel. I will build an altar there to God, who answered me in my day of distress. He has been with me wherever I have gone.”
35004	So they gave Jacob all their foreign gods and all their earrings, and Jacob buried them under the oak near Shechem.
35005	As they set out, a terror from God fell over the surrounding cities, so that they did not pursue Jacob’s sons.
35006	So Jacob and everyone with him arrived in Luz (that is, Bethel) in the land of Canaan.
35007	There Jacob built an altar, and he called that place El-bethel, because it was there that God had revealed Himself to Jacob as he fled from his brother.
35008	Now Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died and was buried under the oak below Bethel. So Jacob named it Allon-bacuth.
35009	After Jacob had returned from Paddan-aram, God appeared to him again and blessed him.
35010	And God said to him, “Though your name is Jacob, you will no longer be called Jacob. Instead, your name will be Israel.” So God named him Israel.
35011	And God told him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation—even a company of nations—shall come from you, and kings shall descend from you.
35012	The land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you, and I will give this land to your descendants after you.”
35013	Then God went up from the place where He had spoken with him.
35014	So Jacob set up a pillar in the place where God had spoken with him—a stone marker—and he poured out a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil.
35015	Jacob called the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.
35016	Later, they set out from Bethel, and while they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth, and her labor was difficult.
35017	During her severe labor, the midwife said to her, “Do not be afraid, for you are having another son.”
35018	And with her last breath—for she was dying—she named him Ben-oni. But his father called him Benjamin.
35019	So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).
35020	Jacob set up a pillar on her grave; it marks Rachel’s tomb to this day.
35021	Israel again set out and pitched his tent beyond the Tower of Eder.
35022	While Israel was living in that region, Reuben went in and slept with his father’s concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard about it. Jacob had twelve sons:
35023	The sons of Leah were Reuben the firstborn of Jacob, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
35024	The sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.
35025	The sons of Rachel’s maidservant Bilhah were Dan and Naphtali.
35026	And the sons of Leah’s maidservant Zilpah were Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan-aram.
35027	Jacob returned to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had stayed.
35028	And Isaac lived 180 years.
35029	Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
36001	This is the account of Esau (that is, Edom).
36002	Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, Oholibamah daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite,
36003	and Basemath daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth.
36004	And Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, Basemath gave birth to Reuel,
36005	and Oholibamah gave birth to Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These were the sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.
36006	Later, Esau took his wives and sons and daughters and all the people of his household, along with his livestock, all his other animals, and all the property he had acquired in Canaan, and he moved to a land far away from his brother Jacob.
36007	For their possessions were too great for them to dwell together; the land where they stayed could not support them because of their livestock.
36008	So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the area of Mount Seir.
36009	This is the account of Esau, the father of the Edomites, in the area of Mount Seir.
36010	These are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz son of Esau’s wife Adah, and Reuel son of Esau’s wife Basemath.
36011	The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
36012	Additionally, Timna, a concubine of Esau’s son Eliphaz, gave birth to Amalek. These are the grandsons of Esau’s wife Adah.
36013	These are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. They are the grandsons of Esau’s wife Basemath.
36014	These are the sons of Esau’s wife Oholibamah (daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon) whom she bore to Esau: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
36015	These are the chiefs among the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: Chiefs Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
36016	Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. They are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom, and they are the grandsons of Adah.
36017	These are the sons of Esau’s son Reuel: Chiefs Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. They are the chiefs descended from Reuel in the land of Edom, and they are the grandsons of Esau’s wife Basemath.
36018	These are the sons of Esau’s wife Oholibamah: Chiefs Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. They are the chiefs descended from Esau’s wife Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.
36019	All these are the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and they were their chiefs.
36020	These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who were living in the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
36021	Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. They are the chiefs of the Horites, the descendants of Seir in the land of Edom.
36022	The sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam. Timna was Lotan’s sister.
36023	These are the sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
36024	These are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. (This is the Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness as he was pasturing the donkeys of his father Zibeon.)
36025	These are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah daughter of Anah.
36026	These are the sons of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
36027	These are the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
36028	These are the sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
36029	These are the chiefs of the Horites: Chiefs Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
36030	Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. They are the chiefs of the Horites, according to their divisions in the land of Seir.
36031	These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites:
36032	Bela son of Beor reigned in Edom; the name of his city was Dinhabah.
36033	When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.
36034	When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
36035	When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, reigned in his place. And the name of his city was Avith.
36036	When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.
36037	When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the Euphrates reigned in his place.
36038	When Shaul died, Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.
36039	When Baal-hanan son of Achbor died, Hadad reigned in his place. His city was named Pau, and his wife’s name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-zahab.
36040	These are the names of Esau’s chiefs, according to their families and regions, by their names: Chiefs Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
36041	Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
36042	Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
36043	Magdiel, and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom, according to their settlements in the land they possessed. Esau was the father of the Edomites.
37001	Now Jacob lived in the land where his father had resided, the land of Canaan.
37002	This is the account of Jacob. When Joseph was seventeen years old, he was tending the flock with his brothers, the sons of his father’s wives Bilhah and Zilpah, and he brought their father a bad report about them.
37003	Now Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons, because Joseph had been born to him in his old age; so he made him a robe of many colors.
37004	When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him.
37005	Then Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, they hated him even more.
37006	He said to them, “Listen to this dream I had:
37007	We were binding sheaves of grain in the field, and suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to mine.”
37008	“Do you intend to reign over us?” his brothers asked. “Will you actually rule us?” So they hated him even more because of his dream and his statements.
37009	Then Joseph had another dream and told it to his brothers. “Look,” he said, “I had another dream, and this time the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”
37010	He told his father and brothers, but his father rebuked him and said, “What is this dream that you have had? Will your mother and brothers and I actually come and bow down to the ground before you?”
37011	And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept in mind what he had said.
37012	Some time later, Joseph’s brothers had gone to pasture their father’s flocks near Shechem.
37013	Israel said to him, “Are not your brothers pasturing the flocks at Shechem? Get ready; I am sending you to them.” “I am ready,” Joseph replied.
37014	Then Israel told him, “Go now and see how your brothers and the flocks are faring, and bring word back to me.” So he sent him off from the Valley of Hebron. And when Joseph arrived in Shechem,
37015	a man found him wandering in the field and asked, “What are you looking for?”
37016	“I am looking for my brothers,” Joseph replied. “Can you please tell me where they are pasturing their flocks?”
37017	“They have moved on from here,” the man answered. “I heard them say, ‘Let us go to Dothan.’” So Joseph set out after his brothers and found them at Dothan.
37018	Now Joseph’s brothers saw him in the distance, and before he arrived, they plotted to kill him.
37019	“Here comes that dreamer!” they said to one another.
37020	“Come now, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits. We can say that a vicious animal has devoured him. Then we shall see what becomes of his dreams!”
37021	When Reuben heard this, he tried to rescue Joseph from their hands. “Let us not take his life,” he said.
37022	“Do not shed his blood. Throw him into this pit in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him.” Reuben said this so that he could rescue Joseph from their hands and return him to his father.
37023	So when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped him of his robe—the robe of many colors he was wearing—
37024	and they took him and threw him into the pit. Now the pit was empty, with no water in it.
37025	And as they sat down to eat a meal, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were carrying spices, balm, and myrrh on their way down to Egypt.
37026	Then Judah said to his brothers, “What profit will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?
37027	Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites and not lay a hand on him; for he is our brother, our own flesh.” And they agreed.
37028	So when the Midianite traders passed by, his brothers pulled Joseph out of the pit and sold him for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites, who took him to Egypt.
37029	When Reuben returned to the pit and saw that Joseph was not there, he tore his clothes,
37030	returned to his brothers, and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
37031	Then they took Joseph’s robe, slaughtered a young goat, and dipped the robe in its blood.
37032	They sent the robe of many colors to their father and said, “We found this. Examine it to see whether it is your son’s robe or not.”
37033	His father recognized it and said, “It is my son’s robe! A vicious animal has devoured him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces!”
37034	Then Jacob tore his clothes, put sackcloth around his waist, and mourned for his son many days.
37035	All his sons and daughters tried to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said. “I will go down to Sheol mourning for my son.” So his father wept for him.
37036	Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.
38001	About that time, Judah left his brothers and settled near a man named Hirah, an Adullamite.
38002	There Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite man named Shua, and he took her as a wife and slept with her.
38003	So she conceived and gave birth to a son, and Judah named him Er.
38004	Again she conceived and gave birth to a son, and she named him Onan.
38005	Then she gave birth to another son and named him Shelah; it was at Chezib that she gave birth to him.
38006	Now Judah acquired a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
38007	But Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD; so the LORD put him to death.
38008	Then Judah said to Onan, “Sleep with your brother’s wife. Perform your duty as her brother-in-law and raise up offspring for your brother.”
38009	But Onan knew that the offspring would not belong to him; so whenever he would sleep with his brother’s wife, he would spill his seed on the ground so that he would not produce offspring for his brother.
38010	What he did was wicked in the sight of the LORD, so He put Onan to death as well.
38011	Then Judah said to his daughter-in-law Tamar, “Live as a widow in your father’s house until my son Shelah grows up.” For he thought, “He may die too, like his brothers.” So Tamar went to live in her father’s house.
38012	After a long time Judah’s wife, the daughter of Shua, died. When Judah had finished mourning, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite went up to his sheepshearers at Timnah.
38013	When Tamar was told, “Your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep,”
38014	she removed her widow’s garments, covered her face with a veil to disguise herself, and sat at the entrance to Enaim, which is on the way to Timnah. For she saw that although Shelah had grown up, she had not been given to him as a wife.
38015	When Judah saw her, he thought she was a prostitute because she had covered her face.
38016	Not realizing that she was his daughter-in-law, he went over to her and said, “Come now, let me sleep with you.” “What will you give me for sleeping with you?” she inquired.
38017	“I will send you a young goat from my flock,” Judah answered. But she replied, “Only if you leave me something as a pledge until you send it.”
38018	“What pledge should I give you?” he asked. She answered, “Your seal and your cord, and the staff in your hand.” So he gave them to her and slept with her, and she became pregnant by him.
38019	Then Tamar got up and departed. And she removed her veil and put on her widow’s garments again.
38020	Now when Judah sent his friend Hirah the Adullamite with the young goat to collect the items he had left with the woman, he could not find her.
38021	He asked the men of that place, “Where is the shrine prostitute who was beside the road at Enaim?” “No shrine prostitute has been here,” they answered.
38022	So Hirah returned to Judah and said, “I could not find her, and furthermore, the men of that place said, ‘No shrine prostitute has been here.’”
38023	“Let her keep the items,” Judah replied. “Otherwise we will become a laughingstock. After all, I did send her this young goat, but you could not find her.”
38024	About three months later, Judah was told, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has prostituted herself, and now she is pregnant.” “Bring her out!” Judah replied. “Let her be burned to death!”
38025	As she was being brought out, Tamar sent a message to her father-in-law: “I am pregnant by the man to whom these items belong.” And she added, “Please examine them. Whose seal and cord and staff are these?”
38026	Judah recognized the items and said, “She is more righteous than I, since I did not give her to my son Shelah.” And he did not have relations with her again.
38027	When the time came for Tamar to give birth, there were twins in her womb.
38028	And as she was giving birth, one of them put out his hand; so the midwife took a scarlet thread and tied it around his wrist. “This one came out first,” she announced.
38029	But when he pulled his hand back and his brother came out, she said, “You have broken out first!” So he was named Perez.
38030	Then his brother came out with the scarlet thread around his wrist, and he was named Zerah.
39001	Meanwhile, Joseph had been taken down to Egypt, where an Egyptian named Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him there.
39002	And the LORD was with Joseph, and he became a successful man, serving in the household of his Egyptian master.
39003	When his master saw that the LORD was with him and made him prosper in all he did,
39004	Joseph found favor in his sight and became his personal attendant. Potiphar put him in charge of his household and entrusted him with everything he owned.
39005	From the time that he put Joseph in charge of his household and all he owned, the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s household on account of him. The LORD’s blessing was on everything he owned, both in his house and in his field.
39006	So Potiphar left all that he owned in Joseph’s care; he did not concern himself with anything except the food he ate. Now Joseph was well-built and handsome,
39007	and after some time his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, “Sleep with me.”
39008	But he refused. “Look,” he said to his master’s wife, “with me here, my master does not concern himself with anything in his house, and he has entrusted everything he owns to my care.
39009	No one in this house is greater than I am. He has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. So how could I do such a great evil and sin against God?”
39010	Although Potiphar’s wife spoke to Joseph day after day, he refused to go to bed with her or even be near her.
39011	One day, however, Joseph went into the house to attend to his work, and not a single household servant was inside.
39012	She grabbed Joseph by his cloak and said, “Sleep with me!” But leaving his cloak in her hand, he escaped and ran outside.
39013	When she saw that he had left his cloak in her hand and had run out of the house,
39014	she called her household servants. “Look,” she said, “this Hebrew has been brought to us to make sport of us. He came to me so he could sleep with me, but I screamed as loud as I could.
39015	When he heard me scream for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.”
39016	So Potiphar’s wife kept Joseph’s cloak beside her until his master came home.
39017	Then she told him the same story: “The Hebrew slave you brought us came to me to make sport of me,
39018	but when I screamed for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.”
39019	When his master heard the story his wife told him, saying, “This is what your slave did to me,” he burned with anger.
39020	So Joseph’s master took him and had him thrown into the prison where the king’s prisoners were confined. While Joseph was there in the prison,
39021	the LORD was with him and extended kindness to him, granting him favor in the eyes of the prison warden.
39022	And the warden put all the prisoners under Joseph’s care, so that he was responsible for all that was done in the prison.
39023	The warden did not concern himself with anything under Joseph’s care, because the LORD was with Joseph and gave him success in whatever he did.
40001	Some time later, the king’s cupbearer and baker offended their master, the king of Egypt.
40002	Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker,
40003	and imprisoned them in the house of the captain of the guard, the same prison where Joseph was confined.
40004	The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he became their personal attendant. After they had been in custody for some time,
40005	both of these men—the Egyptian king’s cupbearer and baker, who were being held in the prison—had a dream on the same night, and each dream had its own meaning.
40006	When Joseph came to them in the morning, he saw that they were distraught.
40007	So he asked the officials of Pharaoh who were in custody with him in his master’s house, “Why are your faces so downcast today?”
40008	“We both had dreams,” they replied, “but there is no one to interpret them.” Then Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.”
40009	So the chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream: “In my dream there was a vine before me,
40010	and on the vine were three branches. As it budded, its blossoms opened and its clusters ripened into grapes.
40011	Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes, squeezed them into his cup, and placed the cup in his hand.”
40012	Joseph replied, “This is the interpretation: The three branches are three days.
40013	Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore your position. You will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand, just as you did when you were his cupbearer.
40014	But when it goes well for you, please remember me and show me kindness by mentioning me to Pharaoh, that he might bring me out of this prison.
40015	For I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have done nothing for which they should have put me in this dungeon.”
40016	When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was favorable, he said to Joseph, “I too had a dream: There were three baskets of white bread on my head.
40017	In the top basket were all sorts of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.”
40018	Joseph replied, “This is the interpretation: The three baskets are three days.
40019	Within three days Pharaoh will lift off your head and hang you on a tree. Then the birds will eat the flesh of your body.”
40020	On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he held a feast for all his officials, and in their presence he lifted up the heads of the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
40021	Pharaoh restored the chief cupbearer to his position, so that he once again placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.
40022	But Pharaoh hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had described to them in his interpretation.
40023	The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot all about him.
41001	After two full years had passed, Pharaoh had a dream: He was standing beside the Nile,
41002	when seven cows, sleek and well-fed, came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.
41003	After them, seven other cows, sickly and thin, came up from the Nile and stood beside the well-fed cows on the bank of the river.
41004	And the cows that were sickly and thin devoured the seven sleek, well-fed cows. Then Pharaoh woke up,
41005	but he fell back asleep and dreamed a second time: Seven heads of grain, plump and ripe, came up on one stalk.
41006	After them, seven other heads of grain sprouted, thin and scorched by the east wind.
41007	And the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven plump, ripe ones. Then Pharaoh awoke and realized it was a dream.
41008	In the morning his spirit was troubled, so he summoned all the magicians and wise men of Egypt. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but no one could interpret them for him.
41009	Then the chief cupbearer said to Pharaoh, “Today I recall my failures.
41010	Pharaoh was once angry with his servants, and he put me and the chief baker in the custody of the captain of the guard.
41011	One night both the chief baker and I had dreams, and each dream had its own meaning.
41012	Now a young Hebrew was there with us, a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams and he interpreted them for us individually.
41013	And it happened to us just as he had interpreted: I was restored to my position, and the other man was hanged.”
41014	So Pharaoh sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of the dungeon. After he had shaved and changed his clothes, he went in before Pharaoh.
41015	Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I had a dream, and no one can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”
41016	“I myself cannot do it,” Joseph replied, “but God will give Pharaoh a sound answer.”
41017	Then Pharaoh said to Joseph: “In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile,
41018	when seven cows, well-fed and sleek, came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.
41019	After them, seven other cows—sickly, ugly, and thin—came up. I have never seen such ugly cows in all the land of Egypt!
41020	Then the thin, ugly cows devoured the seven well-fed cows that were there first.
41021	When they had devoured them, however, no one could tell that they had done so; their appearance was as ugly as it had been before. Then I awoke.
41022	In my dream I also saw seven heads of grain, plump and ripe, growing on a single stalk.
41023	After them, seven other heads of grain sprouted—withered, thin, and scorched by the east wind.
41024	And the thin heads of grain swallowed the seven plump ones. I told this dream to the magicians, but no one could explain it to me.”
41025	At this, Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dreams of Pharaoh are one and the same. God has revealed to Pharaoh what He is about to do.
41026	The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven ripe heads of grain are seven years. The dreams have the same meaning.
41027	Moreover, the seven thin, ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and so are the seven worthless heads of grain scorched by the east wind—they are seven years of famine.
41028	It is just as I said to Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do.
41029	Behold, seven years of great abundance are coming throughout the land of Egypt,
41030	but seven years of famine will follow them. Then all the abundance in the land of Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will devastate the land.
41031	The abundance in the land will not be remembered, since the famine that follows it will be so severe.
41032	Moreover, because the dream was given to Pharaoh in two versions, the matter has been decreed by God, and He will carry it out shortly.
41033	Now, therefore, Pharaoh should look for a discerning and wise man and set him over the land of Egypt.
41034	Let Pharaoh take action and appoint commissioners over the land to take a fifth of the harvest of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
41035	Under the authority of Pharaoh, let them collect all the excess food from these good years, that they may come and lay up the grain to be preserved as food in the cities.
41036	This food will be a reserve for the land during the seven years of famine to come upon the land of Egypt. Then the country will not perish in the famine.”
41037	This proposal pleased Pharaoh and all his officials.
41038	So Pharaoh asked them, “Can we find anyone like this man, in whom the Spirit of God abides?”
41039	Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you.
41040	You shall be in charge of my house, and all my people are to obey your commands. Only with regard to the throne will I be greater than you.”
41041	Pharaoh also told Joseph, “I hereby place you over all the land of Egypt.”
41042	Then Pharaoh removed the signet ring from his finger, put it on Joseph’s finger, clothed him in garments of fine linen, and placed a gold chain around his neck.
41043	He had Joseph ride in his second chariot, with men calling out before him, “Bow the knee!” So he placed him over all the land of Egypt.
41044	And Pharaoh declared to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, but without your permission, no one in all the land of Egypt shall lift his hand or foot.”
41045	Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah, and he gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be his wife. And Joseph took charge of all the land of Egypt.
41046	Now Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph left Pharaoh’s presence and traveled throughout the land of Egypt.
41047	During the seven years of abundance, the land brought forth bountifully.
41048	During those seven years, Joseph collected all the excess food in the land of Egypt and stored it in the cities. In every city he laid up the food from the fields around it.
41049	So Joseph stored up grain in such abundance, like the sand of the sea, that he stopped keeping track of it; for it was beyond measure.
41050	Before the years of famine arrived, two sons were born to Joseph by Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.
41051	Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh, saying, “God has made me forget all my hardship and all my father’s household.”
41052	And the second son he named Ephraim, saying, “God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
41053	When the seven years of abundance in the land of Egypt came to an end,
41054	the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. And although there was famine in every country, there was food throughout the land of Egypt.
41055	When extreme hunger came to all the land of Egypt and the people cried out to Pharaoh for food, he told all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph and do whatever he tells you.”
41056	When the famine had spread over all the land, Joseph opened up all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians; for the famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
41057	And every nation came to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was severe over all the earth.
42001	When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you staring at one another?”
42002	“Look,” he added, “I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy some for us, so that we may live and not die.”
42003	So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
42004	But Jacob did not send Joseph’s brother Benjamin with his brothers, for he said, “I am afraid that harm might befall him.”
42005	So the sons of Israel were among those who came to buy grain, since the famine had also spread to the land of Canaan.
42006	Now Joseph was the ruler of the land; he was the one who sold grain to all its people. So when his brothers arrived, they bowed down before him with their faces to the ground.
42007	And when Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, but he treated them as strangers and spoke harshly to them. “Where have you come from?” he asked. “From the land of Canaan,” they replied. “We are here to buy food.”
42008	Although Joseph recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him.
42009	Joseph remembered his dreams about them and said, “You are spies! You have come to see if our land is vulnerable.”
42010	“Not so, my lord,” they replied. “Your servants have come to buy food.
42011	We are all sons of one man. Your servants are honest men, not spies.”
42012	“No,” he told them. “You have come to see if our land is vulnerable.”
42013	But they answered, “Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and one is no more.”

42015	And this is how you will be tested: As surely as Pharaoh lives, you shall not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.
42016	Send one of your number to get your brother; the rest of you will be confined so that the truth of your words may be tested. If they are untrue, then as surely as Pharaoh lives, you are spies!”
42017	So Joseph imprisoned them for three days,
42018	and on the third day he said to them, “I fear God. So do this and you will live:
42019	If you are honest, leave one of your brothers in custody while the rest of you go and take back grain to relieve the hunger of your households.
42020	Then bring your youngest brother to me so that your words can be verified, that you may not die.” And to this they consented.
42021	Then they said to one another, “Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw his anguish when he pleaded with us, but we would not listen. That is why this distress has come upon us.”
42022	And Reuben responded, “Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy? But you would not listen. Now we must account for his blood!”

42024	And he turned away from them and wept. When he turned back and spoke to them, he took Simeon from them and had him bound before their eyes.
42025	Then Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain, to return each man’s silver to his sack, and to give them provisions for their journey. This order was carried out,

42027	At the place where they lodged for the night, one of them opened his sack to get feed for his donkey, and he saw his silver in the mouth of the sack.
42028	“My silver has been returned!” he said to his brothers. “It is here in my sack.” Their hearts sank, and trembling, they turned to one another and said, “What is this that God has done to us?”
42029	When they reached their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, they described to him all that had happened to them:
42030	“The man who is lord of the land spoke harshly to us and accused us of spying on the country.
42031	But we told him, ‘We are honest men, not spies.
42032	We are twelve brothers, sons of one father. One is no more, and the youngest is now with our father in the land of Canaan.’
42033	Then the man who is lord of the land said to us, ‘This is how I will know whether you are honest: Leave one brother with me, take food to relieve the hunger of your households, and go.
42034	But bring your youngest brother back to me so I will know that you are not spies but honest men. Then I will give your brother back to you, and you can trade in the land.’”
42035	As they began emptying their sacks, there in each man’s sack was his bag of silver! And when they and their father saw the bags of silver, they were dismayed.
42036	Their father Jacob said to them, “You have deprived me of my sons. Joseph is gone and Simeon is no more. Now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is going against me!”
42037	Then Reuben said to his father, “You may kill my two sons if I fail to bring him back to you. Put him in my care, and I will return him.”
42038	But Jacob replied, “My son will not go down there with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left. If any harm comes to him on your journey, you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.”
43001	Now the famine was still severe in the land.
43002	So when Jacob’s sons had eaten all the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go back and buy us a little more food.”
43003	But Judah replied, “The man solemnly warned us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’

43019	So they approached Joseph’s steward and spoke to him at the entrance to the house.
43020	“Please, sir,” they said, “we really did come down here the first time to buy food.

44001	Then Joseph instructed his steward: “Fill the men’s sacks with as much food as they can carry, and put each one’s silver in the mouth of his sack.

47011	So Joseph settled his father and brothers in the land of Egypt and gave them property in the best part of the land, the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
47012	Joseph also provided his father and brothers and all his father’s household with food for their families.
47013	There was no food, however, in all that region, because the famine was so severe; the lands of Egypt and Canaan had been exhausted by the famine.
47014	Joseph collected all the money to be found in the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan in exchange for the grain they were buying, and he brought it into Pharaoh’s palace.
47015	When the money from the lands of Egypt and Canaan was gone, all the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, “Give us food. Why should we die before your eyes? For our funds have run out!”
47016	“Then bring me your livestock,” said Joseph. “Since the money is gone, I will sell you food in exchange for your livestock.”
47017	So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and he gave them food in exchange for their horses, their flocks and herds, and their donkeys. Throughout that year he provided them with food in exchange for all their livestock.
47018	When that year was over, they came to him the second year and said, “We cannot hide from our lord that our money is gone and all our livestock belongs to you. There is nothing left for our lord except our bodies and our land.
47019	Why should we perish before your eyes—we and our land as well? Purchase us and our land in exchange for food. Then we, along with our land, will be slaves to Pharaoh. Give us seed that we may live and not die, and that the land may not become desolate.”
47020	So Joseph acquired for Pharaoh all the land in Egypt; the Egyptians, one and all, sold their fields because the famine was so severe upon them. The land became Pharaoh’s,
47021	and Joseph reduced the people to servitude from one end of Egypt to the other.
47022	However, he did not acquire the priests’ portion of the land, for it had been given to them by Pharaoh. They ate the rations that Pharaoh supplied; so they did not sell their land.
47023	Then Joseph said to the people, “Now that I have acquired you and your land for Pharaoh this day, here is seed for you to sow in the land.
47024	At harvest time, you are to give a fifth of it to Pharaoh, and four-fifths will be yours as seed for the field and food for yourselves and your households and children.”
47025	“You have saved our lives,” they said. “We have found favor in our lord’s eyes, and we will be Pharaoh’s servants.”
47026	So Joseph established a law that a fifth of the produce belongs to Pharaoh, and it is in effect in the land of Egypt to this day. Only the priests’ land does not belong to Pharaoh.
47027	Now the Israelites settled in the land of Egypt, in the region of Goshen. They acquired property there and became fruitful and increased greatly in number.
47028	And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the length of his life was 147 years.
47029	When the time drew near for Israel to die, he called his son Joseph and said to him, “If I have found favor in your eyes, put your hand under my thigh and promise to show me kindness and faithfulness. Do not bury me in Egypt,
47030	but when I lie down with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me with them.” Joseph answered, “I will do as you have requested.”
47031	“Swear to me,” Jacob said. So Joseph swore to him, and Israel bowed in worship at the head of his bed.
48001	Some time later Joseph was told, “Your father is ill.” So he set out with his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
48002	When Jacob was told, “Your son Joseph has come to you,” Israel rallied his strength and sat up in bed.
48003	Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and there He blessed me

48005	And now your two sons born to you in Egypt before I came to you here shall be reckoned as mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
48006	Any children born to you after them shall be yours, and they shall be called by the names of their brothers in the territory they inherit.
48007	Now as for me, when I was returning from Paddan, to my sorrow Rachel died along the way in the land of Canaan, some distance from Ephrath. So I buried her there beside the road to Ephrath” (that is, Bethlehem).
48008	When Israel saw the sons of Joseph, he asked, “Who are these?”
48009	Joseph said to his father, “They are the sons God has given me in this place.” So Jacob said, “Please bring them to me, that I may bless them.”

48011	“I never expected to see your face again,” Israel said to Joseph, “but now God has let me see your children as well.”
48012	Then Joseph removed his sons from his father’s knees and bowed facedown.
48013	And Joseph took both of them—with Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand—and brought them close to him.
48014	But Israel stretched out his right hand and put it on the head of Ephraim, the younger; and crossing his hands, he put his left on Manasseh’s head, although Manasseh was the firstborn.
48015	Then he blessed Joseph and said: “May the God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day,
48016	the angel who has redeemed me from all harm— may He bless these boys. And may they be called by my name and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they grow into a multitude upon the earth.”
48017	When Joseph saw that his father had placed his right hand on Ephraim’s head, he was displeased and took his father’s hand to move it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s.
48018	“Not so, my father!” Joseph said. “This one is the firstborn; put your right hand on his head.”
48019	But his father refused. “I know, my son, I know!” he said. “He too shall become a people, and he too shall be great; nevertheless, his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his offspring shall become a multitude of nations.”
48020	So that day Jacob blessed them and said: “By you shall Israel pronounce this blessing: ‘May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.’” So he put Ephraim before Manasseh.
48021	Then Israel said to Joseph, “Look, I am about to die, but God will be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers.

49001	Then Jacob called for his sons and said, “Gather around so that I can tell you what will happen to you in the days to come:
49002	Come together and listen, O sons of Jacob; listen to your father Israel.
49003	Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, excelling in honor, excelling in power.

49011	He ties his donkey to the vine, his colt to the choicest branch. He washes his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
49012	His eyes are darker than wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.

49015	He saw that his resting place was good and that his land was pleasant, so he bent his shoulder to the burden and submitted to labor as a servant.

49017	He will be a snake by the road, a viper in the path that bites the horse’s heels so that its rider tumbles backward.

49019	Gad will be attacked by raiders, but he will attack their heels.
49020	Asher’s food will be rich; he shall provide royal delicacies.

49022	Joseph is a fruitful vine— a fruitful vine by a spring, whose branches scale the wall.
49023	The archers attacked him with bitterness; they aimed at him in hostility.
49024	Yet he steadied his bow, and his strong arms were tempered by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, in the name of the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel,
