49026	The blessings of your father have surpassed the blessings of the ancient mountains and the bounty of the everlasting hills. May they rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince of his brothers.
49027	Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, in the evening he divides the plunder.”

49031	There Abraham and his wife Sarah are buried, there Isaac and his wife Rebekah are buried, and there I buried Leah.
49032	The field and the cave that is in it were purchased from the Hittites.”
49033	When Jacob had finished instructing his sons, he pulled his feet into the bed and breathed his last, and he was gathered to his people.
50001	Then Joseph fell upon his father’s face, wept over him, and kissed him.

1001015	Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah,
1001016	“When you help the Hebrew women give birth, observe them on the birthstools. If the child is a son, kill him; but if it is a daughter, let her live.”
1001017	The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed; they let the boys live.

1002001	Now a man of the house of Levi married a Levite woman,

1002004	And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.

1002006	When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the little boy was crying. So she had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”

1012001	Now the LORD said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt,
1012002	“This month is the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of your year.
1012003	Tell the whole congregation of Israel that on the tenth day of this month each man must select a lamb for his family, one per household.
1012004	If the household is too small for a whole lamb, they are to share with the nearest neighbor based on the number of people, and apportion the lamb accordingly.
1012005	Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male, and you may take it from the sheep or the goats.

1012007	They are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs.
1012008	They are to eat the meat that night, roasted over the fire, along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

1012015	For seven days you must eat unleavened bread. On the first day you are to remove the leaven from your houses. Whoever eats anything leavened from the first day through the seventh must be cut off from Israel.
1012016	On the first day you are to hold a sacred assembly, and another on the seventh day. You must not do any work on those days, except to prepare the meals—that is all you may do.
1012017	So you are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I brought your divisions out of the land of Egypt. You must keep this day as a permanent statute for the generations to come.
1012018	In the first month you are to eat unleavened bread, from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first day.
1012019	For seven days there must be no leaven found in your houses. If anyone eats something leavened, that person, whether a foreigner or native of the land, must be cut off from the congregation of Israel.
1012020	You are not to eat anything leavened; eat unleavened bread in all your homes.”

1013002	“Consecrate to Me every firstborn male. The firstborn from every womb among the Israelites belongs to Me, both of man and beast.”
1013003	So Moses told the people, “Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery; for the LORD brought you out of it by the strength of His hand. And nothing leavened shall be eaten.
1013004	Today, in the month of Abib, you are leaving.
1013005	And when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites—the land He swore to your fathers that He would give you, a land flowing with milk and honey—you shall keep this service in this month.
1013006	For seven days you are to eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to the LORD.
1013007	Unleavened bread shall be eaten during those seven days. Nothing leavened may be found among you, nor shall leaven be found anywhere within your borders.
1013008	And on that day you are to explain to your son, ‘This is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’
1013009	It shall be a sign for you on your hand and a reminder on your forehead that the Law of the LORD is to be on your lips. For with a mighty hand the LORD brought you out of Egypt.
1013010	Therefore you shall keep this statute at the appointed time year after year.
1013011	And after the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you, as He swore to you and your fathers,
1013012	you are to present to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb. All the firstborn males of your livestock belong to the LORD.
1013013	You must redeem every firstborn donkey with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. And every firstborn of your sons you must redeem.
1013014	In the future, when your son asks you, ‘What does this mean?’ you are to tell him, ‘With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
1013015	And when Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both of man and beast. This is why I sacrifice to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb, but I redeem all the firstborn of my sons.’
1013016	So it shall serve as a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead, for with a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.”
1013017	When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them along the road through the land of the Philistines, though it was shorter. For God said, “If the people face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.”
1013018	So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea. And the Israelites left the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.
1013019	Moses took the bones of Joseph with him because Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear a solemn oath when he said, “God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones with you from this place.”
1013020	They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham on the edge of the wilderness.
1013021	And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day, and in a pillar of fire to give them light by night, so that they could travel by day or night.
1013022	Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night left its place before the people.
1014001	Then the LORD said to Moses,
1014002	“Tell the Israelites to turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. You are to encamp by the sea, directly opposite Baal-zephon.

1014007	He took 600 of the best chariots, and all the other chariots of Egypt, with officers over all of them.

1014010	As Pharaoh approached, the Israelites looked up and saw the Egyptians marching after them, and they were terrified and cried out to the LORD.
1014011	They said to Moses, “Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us into the wilderness to die? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?

1014013	But Moses told the people, “Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the LORD’s salvation, which He will accomplish for you today; for the Egyptians you see today, you will never see again.
1014014	The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still.”
1014015	Then the LORD said to Moses, “Why are you crying out to Me? Tell the Israelites to go forward.
1014016	And as for you, lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, so that the Israelites can go through the sea on dry ground.
1014017	And I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them. Then I will gain honor by means of Pharaoh and all his army and chariots and horsemen.
1014018	The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I am honored through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen.”
1014019	And the angel of God, who had gone before the camp of Israel, withdrew and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them,
1014020	so that it came between the camps of Egypt and Israel. The cloud was there in the darkness, but it lit up the night. So all night long neither camp went near the other.

1014022	and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.

1014028	The waters flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen—the entire army of Pharaoh that had chased the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.
1014029	But the Israelites had walked through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.

1015001	Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD: “I will sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted. The horse and rider He has thrown into the sea.

1016001	On the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left the land of Egypt, the whole congregation of Israel set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.
1016002	And there in the desert the whole congregation of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron.
1016003	“If only we had died by the LORD’s hand in the land of Egypt!” they said. “There we sat by pots of meat and ate our fill of bread, but you have brought us into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death!”

1016005	Then on the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather on the other days.”

1016013	That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
1016014	When the layer of dew had evaporated, there were thin flakes on the desert floor, as fine as frost on the ground.
1016015	When the Israelites saw it, they asked one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. So Moses told them, “It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.
1016016	This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Each one is to gather as much as he needs. You may take an omer for each person in your tent.’”
1016017	So the Israelites did this. Some gathered more, and some less.
1016018	When they measured it by the omer, he who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall. Each one gathered as much as he needed to eat.
1016019	Then Moses said to them, “No one may keep any of it until morning.”
1016020	But they did not listen to Moses; some people left part of it until morning, and it became infested with maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.
1016021	Every morning each one gathered as much as was needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.
1016022	On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much food—two omers per person —and all the leaders of the congregation came and reported this to Moses.
1016023	He told them, “This is what the LORD has said: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil. Then set aside whatever remains and keep it until morning.’”
1016024	So they set it aside until morning as Moses had commanded, and it did not smell or contain any maggots.

1016026	For six days you may gather, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, it will not be there.”

1016028	Then the LORD said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and instructions?
1016029	Understand that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day He will give you bread for two days. On the seventh day, everyone must stay where he is; no one may leave his place.”
1016030	So the people rested on the seventh day.
1016031	Now the house of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.
1016032	Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Keep an omer of manna for the generations to come, so that they may see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”

1016035	The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where they could settle; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.

1018013	The next day Moses took his seat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening.
1018014	When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he asked, “What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone as judge, with all the people standing around you from morning till evening?”
1018015	“Because the people come to me to inquire of God,” Moses replied.
1018016	“Whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to me to judge between one man and another, and I make known to them the statutes and laws of God.”
1018017	But Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “What you are doing is not good.
1018018	Surely you and these people with you will wear yourselves out, because the task is too heavy for you. You cannot handle it alone.
1018019	Now listen to me; I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You must be the people’s representative before God and bring their causes to Him.
1018020	Teach them the statutes and laws, and show them the way to live and the work they must do.
1018021	Furthermore, select capable men from among the people—God-fearing, trustworthy men who are averse to dishonest gain. Appoint them over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
1018022	Have these men judge the people at all times. Then they can bring you any major issue, but all minor cases they can judge on their own, so that your load may be lightened as they share it with you.
1018023	If you follow this advice and God so directs you, then you will be able to endure, and all these people can go home in peace.”
1018024	Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
1018025	So Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
1018026	And they judged the people at all times; they would bring the difficult cases to Moses, but any minor issue they would judge themselves.
1018027	Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and Jethro returned to his own land.
1019001	In the third month, on the same day of the month that the Israelites had left the land of Egypt, they came to the Wilderness of Sinai.

1019013	No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot with arrows—whether man or beast, he must not live.’ Only when the ram’s horn sounds a long blast may they approach the mountain.”

1019017	Then Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet with God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
1019018	Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke, because the LORD had descended on it in fire. And the smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked violently.
1019019	And as the sound of the ram’s horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him in the thunder.
1019020	The LORD descended to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the summit. So Moses went up,
1019021	and the LORD said to him, “Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish.
1019022	Even the priests who approach the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them.”
1019023	But Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for You solemnly warned us, ‘Put a boundary around the mountain and set it apart as holy.’”
1019024	And the LORD replied, “Go down and bring Aaron with you. But the priests and the people must not break through to come up to the LORD, or He will break out against them.”
1019025	So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.
1020001	And God spoke all these words:
1020002	“I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
1020003	You shall have no other gods before Me.
1020004	You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.
1020005	You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
1020006	but showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments.
1020007	You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.
1020008	Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.
1020009	Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
1020010	but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God, on which you must not do any work—neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant or livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates.
1020011	For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth and the sea and all that is in them, but on the seventh day He rested. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy.
1020012	Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
1020013	You shall not murder.
1020014	You shall not commit adultery.
1020015	You shall not steal.
1020016	You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
1020017	You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his manservant or maidservant, or his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”
1020018	When all the people witnessed the thunder and lightning, the sounding of the ram’s horn, and the mountain enveloped in smoke, they trembled and stood at a distance.
1020019	“Speak to us yourself and we will listen,” they said to Moses. “But do not let God speak to us, or we will die.”
1020020	“Do not be afraid,” Moses replied. “For God has come to test you, so that the fear of Him may be before you, to keep you from sinning.”
1020021	And the people stood at a distance as Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.
1020022	Then the LORD said to Moses, “This is what you are to tell the Israelites: ‘You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken to you from heaven.
1020023	You are not to make any gods alongside Me; you are not to make for yourselves gods of silver or gold.
1020024	You are to make for Me an altar of earth, and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and peace offerings, your sheep and goats and cattle. In every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
1020025	Now if you make an altar of stones for Me, you must not build it with stones shaped by tools; for if you use a chisel on it, you will defile it.
1020026	And you must not go up to My altar on steps, lest your nakedness be exposed on it.’
1021001	“These are the ordinances that you are to set before them:
1021002	If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he shall go free without paying anything.
1021003	If he arrived alone, he is to leave alone; if he arrived with a wife, she is to leave with him.
1021004	If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and only the man shall go free.
1021005	But if the servant declares, ‘I love my master and my wife and children; I do not want to go free,’
1021006	then his master is to bring him before the judges. And he shall take him to the door or doorpost and pierce his ear with an awl. Then he shall serve his master for life.
1021007	And if a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free as the menservants do.
1021008	If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master who had designated her for himself, he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, since he has broken faith with her.
1021009	And if he chooses her for his son, he must deal with her as with a daughter.
1021010	If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the food, clothing, or marital rights of his first wife.
1021011	If, however, he does not provide her with these three things, she is free to go without monetary payment.
1021012	Whoever strikes and kills a man must surely be put to death.
1021013	If, however, he did not lie in wait, but God allowed it to happen, then I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.
1021014	But if a man schemes and acts willfully against his neighbor to kill him, you must take him away from My altar to be put to death.
1021015	Whoever strikes his father or mother must surely be put to death.
1021016	Whoever kidnaps another man must be put to death, whether he sells him or the man is found in his possession.
1021017	Anyone who curses his father or mother must surely be put to death.
1021018	If men are quarreling and one strikes the other with a stone or a fist, and he does not die but is confined to bed,
1021019	then the one who struck him shall go unpunished, as long as the other can get up and walk around outside with his staff. Nevertheless, he must compensate the man for his lost work and see that he is completely healed.
1021020	If a man strikes his manservant or maidservant with a rod, and the servant dies by his hand, he shall surely be punished.
1021021	However, if the servant gets up after a day or two, the owner shall not be punished, since the servant is his property.
1021022	If men who are fighting strike a pregnant woman and her child is born prematurely, but there is no further injury, he shall surely be fined as the woman’s husband demands and as the court allows.
1021023	But if a serious injury results, then you must require a life for a life—
1021024	eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
1021025	burn for burn, wound for wound, and stripe for stripe.
1021026	If a man strikes and blinds the eye of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the eye.
1021027	And if he knocks out the tooth of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the tooth.
1021028	If an ox gores a man or woman to death, the ox must surely be stoned, and its meat must not be eaten. But the owner of the ox shall not be held responsible.
1021029	But if the ox has a habit of goring, and its owner has been warned yet does not restrain it, and it kills a man or woman, then the ox must be stoned and its owner must also be put to death.
1021030	If payment is demanded of him instead, he may redeem his life by paying the full amount demanded of him.
1021031	If the ox gores a son or a daughter, it shall be done to him according to the same rule.
1021032	If the ox gores a manservant or maidservant, the owner must pay thirty shekels of silver to the master of that servant, and the ox must be stoned.
1021033	If a man opens or digs a pit and fails to cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
1021034	the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he must pay its owner, and the dead animal will be his.
1021035	If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they must sell the live one and divide the proceeds; they also must divide the dead animal.
1021036	But if it was known that the ox had a habit of goring, yet its owner failed to restrain it, he shall pay full compensation, ox for ox, and the dead animal will be his.
1022001	“If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters or sells it, he must repay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.
1022002	If a thief is caught breaking in and is beaten to death, no one shall be guilty of bloodshed.
1022003	But if it happens after sunrise, there is guilt for his bloodshed. A thief must make full restitution; if he has nothing, he himself shall be sold for his theft.
1022004	If what was stolen is actually found alive in his possession—whether ox or donkey or sheep—he must pay back double.
1022005	If a man grazes his livestock in a field or vineyard and allows them to stray so that they graze in someone else’s field, he must make restitution from the best of his own field or vineyard.
1022006	If a fire breaks out and spreads to thornbushes so that it consumes stacked or standing grain, or the whole field, the one who started the fire must make full restitution.
1022007	If a man gives his neighbor money or goods for safekeeping and they are stolen from the neighbor’s house, the thief, if caught, must pay back double.
1022008	If the thief is not found, the owner of the house must appear before the judges to determine whether he has taken his neighbor’s property.
1022009	In all cases of illegal possession of an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost item that someone claims, ‘This is mine,’ both parties shall bring their cases before the judges. The one whom the judges find guilty must pay back double to his neighbor.
1022010	If a man gives a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal to be cared for by his neighbor, but it dies or is injured or stolen while no one is watching,
1022011	an oath before the LORD shall be made between the parties to determine whether or not the man has taken his neighbor’s property. The owner must accept the oath and require no restitution.
1022012	But if the animal was actually stolen from the neighbor, he must make restitution to the owner.
1022013	If the animal was torn to pieces, he shall bring it as evidence; he need not make restitution for the torn carcass.
1022014	If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor and it is injured or dies while its owner is not present, he must make full restitution.
1022015	If the owner was present, no restitution is required. If the animal was rented, the fee covers the loss.
1022016	If a man seduces a virgin who is not pledged in marriage and sleeps with her, he must pay the full dowry for her to be his wife.
1022017	If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, the man still must pay an amount comparable to the bridal price of a virgin.
1022018	You must not allow a sorceress to live.
1022019	Whoever lies with an animal must surely be put to death.
1022020	If anyone sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone, he must be set apart for destruction.
1022021	You must not exploit or oppress a foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
1022022	You must not mistreat any widow or orphan.
1022023	If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to Me in distress, I will surely hear their cry.
1022024	My anger will be kindled, and I will kill you with the sword; then your wives will become widows and your children will be fatherless.
1022025	If you lend money to one of My people among you who is poor, you must not act as a creditor to him; you are not to charge him interest.
1022026	If you take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, return it to him by sunset,
1022027	because his cloak is the only covering he has for his body. What else will he sleep in? And if he cries out to Me, I will hear, for I am compassionate.
1022028	You must not blaspheme God or curse the ruler of your people.
1022029	You must not hold back offerings from your granaries or vats. You are to give Me the firstborn of your sons.
1022030	You shall do likewise with your cattle and your sheep. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day you are to give them to Me.
1022031	You are to be My holy people. You must not eat the meat of a mauled animal found in the field; you are to throw it to the dogs.
1023001	“You shall not spread a false report. Do not join the wicked by being a malicious witness.
1023002	You shall not follow the crowd in wrongdoing. When you testify in a lawsuit, do not pervert justice by siding with the crowd.
1023003	And do not show favoritism to a poor man in his lawsuit.
1023004	If you encounter your enemy’s stray ox or donkey, you must return it to him.
1023005	If you see the donkey of one who hates you fallen under its load, do not leave it there; you must help him with it.
1023006	You shall not deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits.
1023007	Stay far away from a false accusation. Do not kill the innocent or the just, for I will not acquit the guilty.
1023008	Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.
1023009	Do not oppress a foreign resident, since you yourselves know how it feels to be foreigners; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
1023010	For six years you are to sow your land and gather its produce,
1023011	but in the seventh year you must let it rest and lie fallow, so that the poor among your people may eat from the field and the wild animals may consume what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and olive grove.
1023012	For six days you are to do your work, but on the seventh day you must cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest and the son of your maidservant may be refreshed, as well as the foreign resident.
1023013	Pay close attention to everything I have said to you. You must not invoke the names of other gods; they must not be heard on your lips.
1023014	Three times a year you are to celebrate a feast to Me.
1023015	You are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread as I commanded you: At the appointed time in the month of Abib you are to eat unleavened bread for seven days, because that was the month you came out of Egypt. No one may appear before Me empty-handed.
1023016	You are also to keep the Feast of Harvest with the firstfruits of the produce from what you sow in the field. And keep the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather your produce from the field.
1023017	Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD.
1023018	You must not offer the blood of My sacrifices with anything leavened, nor may the fat of My feast remain until morning.
1023019	Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
1023020	Behold, I am sending an angel before you to protect you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
1023021	Pay attention to him and listen to his voice; do not defy him, for he will not forgive rebellion, since My Name is in him.
1023022	But if you will listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.
1023023	For My angel will go before you and bring you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will annihilate them.
1023024	You must not bow down to their gods or serve them or follow their practices. Instead, you are to demolish them and smash their sacred stones to pieces.
1023025	So you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water. And I will take away sickness from among you.
1023026	No woman in your land will miscarry or be barren; I will fulfill the number of your days.
1023027	I will send My terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every nation you encounter. I will make all your enemies turn and run.
1023028	I will send the hornet before you to drive the Hivites and Canaanites and Hittites out of your way.
1023029	I will not drive them out before you in a single year; otherwise the land would become desolate and wild animals would multiply against you.
1023030	Little by little I will drive them out ahead of you, until you become fruitful and possess the land.
1023031	And I will establish your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the Euphrates. For I will deliver the inhabitants into your hand, and you will drive them out before you.
1023032	You shall make no covenant with them or with their gods.
1023033	They must not remain in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me. For if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.”
1024001	Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD—you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders—and you are to worship at a distance.
1024002	Moses alone shall approach the LORD, but the others must not come near. And the people may not go up with him.”
1024003	When Moses came and told the people all the words and ordinances of the LORD, they all responded with one voice: “All the words that the LORD has spoken, we will do.”
1024004	And Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. Early the next morning he got up and built an altar at the base of the mountain, along with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
1024005	Then he sent out some young men of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.
1024006	Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and the other half he splattered on the altar.
1024007	Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it to the people, who replied, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will be obedient.”
1024008	So Moses took the blood, splattered it on the people, and said, “This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words.”
1024009	Then Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel,
1024010	and they saw the God of Israel. Under His feet was a work like a pavement made of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself.
1024011	But God did not lay His hand on the nobles of Israel; they saw Him, and they ate and drank.
1024012	Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to Me on the mountain and stay here, so that I may give you the tablets of stone, with the law and commandments I have written for their instruction.”
1024013	So Moses set out with Joshua his attendant and went up on the mountain of God.
1024014	And he said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are here with you. Whoever has a dispute can go to them.”
1024015	When Moses went up on the mountain, the cloud covered it,
1024016	and the glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai. For six days the cloud covered it, and on the seventh day the LORD called to Moses from within the cloud.
1024017	And the sight of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the mountaintop in the eyes of the Israelites.
1024018	Moses entered the cloud as he went up on the mountain, and he remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

1026001	“You are to construct the tabernacle itself with ten curtains of finely spun linen, each with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and cherubim skillfully worked into them.
1026002	Each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide —all curtains the same size.

1028043	Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they will not incur guilt and die. This is to be a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants.
1029001	“Now this is what you are to do to consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests: Take a young bull and two rams without blemish,
1029002	along with unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil. Make them out of fine wheat flour,
1029003	put them in a basket, and present them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
1029004	Then present Aaron and his sons at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
1029005	Take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself, and the breastplate. Fasten the ephod on him with its woven waistband.
1029006	Put the turban on his head and attach the holy diadem to the turban.
1029007	Then take the anointing oil and anoint him by pouring it on his head.
1029008	Present his sons as well and clothe them with tunics.
1029009	Wrap the sashes around Aaron and his sons and tie headbands on them. The priesthood shall be theirs by a permanent statute. In this way you are to ordain Aaron and his sons.
1029010	You are to present the bull at the front of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.
1029011	And you shall slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
1029012	Take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger; then pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
1029013	Take all the fat that covers the entrails and the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
1029014	But burn the flesh of the bull and its hide and dung outside the camp; it is a sin offering.
1029015	Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.
1029016	You are to slaughter the ram, take its blood, and splatter it on all sides of the altar.
1029017	Cut the ram into pieces, wash the entrails and legs, and place them with its head and other pieces.
1029018	Then burn the entire ram on the altar; it is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
1029019	Take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.
1029020	Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Splatter the remaining blood on all sides of the altar.
1029021	And take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments, as well as on his sons and their garments. Then he and his garments will be consecrated, as well as his sons and their garments.
1029022	Take the fat from the ram, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, both kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh (since this is a ram for ordination),
1029023	along with one loaf of bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
1029024	Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and wave them before the LORD as a wave offering.
1029025	Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar atop the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma before the LORD; it is a food offering to the LORD.
1029026	Take the breast of the ram of Aaron’s ordination and wave it before the LORD as a wave offering, and it will be your portion.
1029027	Consecrate for Aaron and his sons the breast of the wave offering that is waved and the thigh of the heave offering that is lifted up from the ram of ordination.
1029028	This will belong to Aaron and his sons as a regular portion from the Israelites, for it is the heave offering the Israelites will make to the LORD from their peace offerings.
1029029	The holy garments that belong to Aaron will belong to his sons after him, so they can be anointed and ordained in them.
1029030	The son who succeeds him as priest and enters the Tent of Meeting to minister in the Holy Place must wear them for seven days.
1029031	You are to take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.
1029032	At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket.
1029033	They must eat those things by which atonement was made for their ordination and consecration. But no outsider may eat them, because these things are sacred.
1029034	And if any of the meat of ordination or any bread is left until the morning, you are to burn up the remainder. It must not be eaten, because it is sacred.
1029035	This is what you are to do for Aaron and his sons based on all that I have commanded you, taking seven days to ordain them.
1029036	Sacrifice a bull as a sin offering each day for atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
1029037	For seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will become most holy; whatever touches the altar will be holy.
1029038	This is what you are to offer regularly on the altar, each day: two lambs that are a year old.
1029039	Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight.
1029040	With the first lamb offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, mixed with a quarter hin of oil from pressed olives, and a drink offering of a quarter hin of wine.
1029041	And offer the second lamb at twilight with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
1029042	For the generations to come, this burnt offering shall be made regularly at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, where I will meet you to speak with you.
1029043	I will also meet with the Israelites there, and that place will be consecrated by My glory.
1029044	So I will consecrate the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.
1029045	Then I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.
1029046	And they will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might dwell among them. I am the LORD their God.
1030001	“You are also to make an altar of acacia wood for the burning of incense.
1030002	It is to be square, a cubit long, a cubit wide, and two cubits high. Its horns must be of one piece.
1030003	Overlay with pure gold the top and all the sides and horns, and make a molding of gold around it.

1030033	Anyone who mixes perfume like it or puts it on an outsider shall be cut off from his people.’”

1030037	You are never to use this formula to make incense for yourselves; you shall regard it as holy to the LORD.

2001001	Then the LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,
2001002	“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, you may bring as your offering an animal from the herd or the flock.
2001003	If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he is to present an unblemished male. He must bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for its acceptance before the LORD.
2001004	He is to lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, so it can be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him.
2001005	And he shall slaughter the young bull before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons the priests are to present the blood and splatter it on all sides of the altar at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
2001006	Next, he is to skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
2001007	The sons of Aaron the priest shall put a fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
2001008	Then Aaron’s sons the priests are to arrange the pieces, including the head and the fat, atop the burning wood on the altar.
2001009	The entrails and legs must be washed with water, and the priest shall burn all of it on the altar as a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
2001010	If, however, one’s offering is a burnt offering from the flock—from the sheep or goats—he is to present an unblemished male.
2001011	He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons the priests are to splatter its blood against the altar on all sides.
2001012	He is to cut the animal into pieces, and the priest shall arrange them, including the head and fat, atop the burning wood that is on the altar.
2001013	The entrails and legs must be washed with water, and the priest shall present all of it and burn it on the altar; it is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
2001014	If, instead, one’s offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he is to present a turtledove or a young pigeon.
2001015	Then the priest shall bring it to the altar, twist off its head, and burn it on the altar; its blood should be drained out on the side of the altar.
2001016	And he is to remove the crop with its contents and throw it to the east side of the altar, in the place for ashes.
2001017	He shall tear it open by its wings, without dividing the bird completely. And the priest is to burn it on the altar atop the burning wood. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
2002001	“When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, his offering must consist of fine flour. He is to pour olive oil on it, put frankincense on it,
2002002	and bring it to Aaron’s sons the priests. The priest shall take a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the frankincense, and burn this as a memorial portion on the altar, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
2002003	The remainder of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD.
2002004	Now if you bring an offering of grain baked in an oven, it must consist of fine flour, either unleavened cakes mixed with oil or unleavened wafers coated with oil.
2002005	If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it must be unleavened bread made of fine flour mixed with oil.
2002006	Crumble it and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
2002007	If your offering is a grain offering cooked in a pan, it must consist of fine flour with oil.
2002008	When you bring to the LORD the grain offering made in any of these ways, it is to be presented to the priest, and he shall take it to the altar.
2002009	The priest is to remove the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
2002010	But the remainder of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD.
2002011	No grain offering that you present to the LORD may be made with leaven, for you are not to burn any leaven or honey as a food offering to the LORD.
2002012	You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of firstfruits, but they must not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
2002013	And you shall season each of your grain offerings with salt. You must not leave the salt of the covenant of your God out of your grain offering; you are to add salt to each of your offerings.
2002014	If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, you shall offer crushed heads of new grain roasted on the fire.
2002015	And you are to put oil and frankincense on it; it is a grain offering.
2002016	The priest shall then burn the memorial portion of the crushed grain and the oil, together with all its frankincense, as a food offering to the LORD.

2004001	Then the LORD said to Moses,
2004002	“Tell the Israelites to do as follows with one who sins unintentionally against any of the LORD’s commandments and does what is forbidden by them:
2004003	If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt on the people, he must bring to the LORD a young bull without blemish as a sin offering for the sin he has committed.
2004004	He must bring the bull to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, lay his hand on the bull’s head, and slaughter it before the LORD.
2004005	Then the anointed priest shall take some of the bull’s blood and bring it into the Tent of Meeting.
2004006	The priest is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times before the LORD, in front of the veil of the sanctuary.
2004007	The priest must then put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that is before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting. And he is to pour out the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
2004008	Then he shall remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering—the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,
2004009	both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys—
2004010	just as the fat is removed from the ox of the peace offering. Then the priest shall burn them on the altar of burnt offering.
2004011	But the hide of the bull and all its flesh, with its head and legs and its entrails and dung—
2004012	all the rest of the bull—he must take outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place where the ashes are poured out, and there he must burn it on a wood fire on the ash heap.
2004013	Now if the whole congregation of Israel strays unintentionally and the matter escapes the notice of the assembly so that they violate any of the LORD’s commandments and incur guilt by doing what is forbidden,
2004014	when they become aware of the sin they have committed, then the assembly must bring a young bull as a sin offering and present it before the Tent of Meeting.
2004015	The elders of the congregation are to lay their hands on the bull’s head before the LORD, and it shall be slaughtered before the LORD.
2004016	Then the anointed priest is to bring some of the bull’s blood into the Tent of Meeting,
2004017	and he is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD in front of the veil.
2004018	He is also to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting, and he must pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
2004019	And he is to remove all the fat from it and burn it on the altar.
2004020	He shall offer this bull just as he did the bull for the sin offering; in this way the priest will make atonement on their behalf, and they will be forgiven.
2004021	Then he is to take the bull outside the camp and burn it, just as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly.
2004022	When a leader sins unintentionally and does what is prohibited by any of the commandments of the LORD his God, he incurs guilt.
2004023	When he becomes aware of the sin he has committed, he must bring an unblemished male goat as his offering.
2004024	He is to lay his hand on the head of the goat and slaughter it at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering.
2004025	Then the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
2004026	He must burn all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the peace offerings; thus the priest will make atonement for that man’s sin, and he will be forgiven.
2004027	And if one of the common people sins unintentionally and does what is prohibited by any of the LORD’s commandments, he incurs guilt.
2004028	When he becomes aware of the sin he has committed, he must bring an unblemished female goat as his offering for that sin.
2004029	He is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place of the burnt offering.
2004030	Then the priest is to take some of its blood with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
2004031	Then he is to remove all the fat, just as it is removed from the peace offering, and the priest is to burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
2004032	If, however, he brings a lamb as a sin offering, he must bring an unblemished female.
2004033	And he is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it as a sin offering at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
2004034	Then the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.
2004035	And he shall remove all the fat, just as the fat of the lamb is removed from the peace offerings, and he shall burn it on the altar along with the food offerings to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.
2005001	“If someone sins by failing to testify when he hears a public charge about something he has witnessed, whether he has seen it or learned of it, he shall bear the iniquity.
2005002	Or if a person touches anything unclean—whether the carcass of any unclean wild animal or livestock or crawling creature—even if he is unaware of it, he is unclean and guilty.
2005003	Or if he touches human uncleanness—anything by which one becomes unclean—even if he is unaware of it, when he realizes it, he is guilty.
2005004	Or if someone swears thoughtlessly with his lips to do anything good or evil—in whatever matter a man may rashly pronounce an oath—even if he is unaware of it, when he realizes it, he is guilty in the matter.
2005005	If someone incurs guilt in one of these ways, he must confess the sin he has committed,
2005006	and he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD for the sin he has committed: a female lamb or goat from the flock as a sin offering. And the priest will make atonement for him concerning his sin.
2005007	If, however, he cannot afford a lamb, he may bring to the LORD as restitution for his sin two turtledoves or two young pigeons—one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering.
2005008	He is to bring them to the priest, who shall first present the one for the sin offering. He is to twist its head at the front of its neck without severing it;
2005009	then he is to sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, while the rest of the blood is drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
2005010	And the priest must prepare the second bird as a burnt offering according to the ordinance. In this way the priest will make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.
2005011	But if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he may bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He must not put olive oil or frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
2005012	He is to bring it to the priest, who shall take a handful from it as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar atop the food offerings to the LORD; it is a sin offering.
2005013	In this way the priest will make atonement for him for any of these sins he has committed, and he will be forgiven. The remainder will belong to the priest, like the grain offering.”
2005014	Then the LORD said to Moses,
2005015	“If someone acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally against any of the LORD’s holy things, he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD: an unblemished ram from the flock, of proper value in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel; it is a guilt offering.
2005016	Regarding any holy thing he has harmed, he must make restitution by adding a fifth of its value to it and giving it to the priest, who will make atonement on his behalf with the ram as a guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
2005017	If someone sins and violates any of the LORD’s commandments even though he was unaware, he is guilty and shall bear his punishment.
2005018	He is to bring to the priest an unblemished ram of proper value from the flock as a guilt offering. Then the priest will make atonement on his behalf for the wrong he has committed in ignorance, and he will be forgiven.
2005019	It is a guilt offering; he was certainly guilty before the LORD.”
2006001	And the LORD said to Moses,
2006002	“If someone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor in regard to a deposit or security entrusted to him or stolen, or if he extorts his neighbor
2006003	or finds lost property and lies about it and swears falsely, or if he commits any such sin that a man might commit—
2006004	once he has sinned and becomes guilty, he must return what he has stolen or taken by extortion, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost property he found,
2006005	or anything else about which he has sworn falsely. He must make restitution in full, add a fifth of the value, and pay it to the owner on the day he acknowledges his guilt.
2006006	Then he must bring to the priest his guilt offering to the LORD: an unblemished ram of proper value from the flock.
2006007	In this way the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for anything he may have done to incur guilt.”
2006008	Then the LORD said to Moses,
2006009	“Command Aaron and his sons that this is the law of the burnt offering: The burnt offering is to remain on the hearth of the altar all night, until morning, and the fire must be kept burning on the altar.
2006010	And the priest shall put on his linen robe and linen undergarments, and he shall remove from the altar the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has consumed and place them beside it.
2006011	Then he must take off his garments, put on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place.
2006012	The fire on the altar shall be kept burning; it must not be extinguished. Every morning the priest is to add wood to the fire, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat portions of the peace offerings on it.
2006013	The fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it must not be extinguished.
2006014	Now this is the law of the grain offering: Aaron’s sons shall present it before the LORD in front of the altar.
2006015	The priest is to remove a handful of fine flour and olive oil, together with all the frankincense from the grain offering, and burn the memorial portion on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
2006016	Aaron and his sons are to eat the remainder. It must be eaten without leaven in a holy place; they are to eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
2006017	It must not be baked with leaven; I have assigned it as their portion of My food offerings. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
2006018	Any male among the sons of Aaron may eat it. This is a permanent portion from the food offerings to the LORD for the generations to come. Anything that touches them will become holy.”
2006019	Then the LORD said to Moses,
2006020	“This is the offering that Aaron and his sons must present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half in the evening.
2006021	It shall be prepared with oil on a griddle; you are to bring it well-kneaded and present it as a grain offering broken in pieces, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
2006022	The priest, who is one of Aaron’s sons and will be anointed to take his place, is to prepare it. As a permanent portion for the LORD, it must be burned completely.
2006023	Every grain offering for a priest shall be burned completely; it is not to be eaten.”
2006024	And the LORD said to Moses,
2006025	“Tell Aaron and his sons that this is the law of the sin offering: In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered before the LORD; it is most holy.
2006026	The priest who offers it shall eat it; it must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
2006027	Anything that touches its flesh will become holy, and if any of the blood is spattered on a garment, you must wash it in a holy place.
2006028	The clay pot in which the sin offering is boiled must be broken; if it is boiled in a bronze pot, the pot must be scoured and rinsed with water.
2006029	Any male among the priests may eat it; it is most holy.
2006030	But no sin offering may be eaten if its blood has been brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place; it must be burned.
2007001	“Now this is the law of the guilt offering, which is most holy:
2007002	The guilt offering must be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and the priest shall splatter its blood on all sides of the altar.
2007003	And all the fat from it shall be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails,
2007004	both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which is to be removed with the kidneys.
2007005	The priest shall burn them on the altar as a food offering to the LORD; it is a guilt offering.
2007006	Every male among the priests may eat of it. It must be eaten in a holy place; it is most holy.
2007007	The guilt offering is like the sin offering; the same law applies to both. It belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.
2007008	As for the priest who presents a burnt offering for anyone, the hide of that offering belongs to him.
2007009	Likewise, every grain offering that is baked in an oven or cooked in a pan or on a griddle belongs to the priest who presents it,
2007010	and every grain offering, whether dry or mixed with oil, belongs equally to all the sons of Aaron.
2007011	Now this is the law of the peace offering that one may present to the LORD:
2007012	If he offers it in thanksgiving, then along with the sacrifice of thanksgiving he shall offer unleavened cakes mixed with olive oil, unleavened wafers coated with oil, and well-kneaded cakes of fine flour mixed with oil.
2007013	Along with his peace offering of thanksgiving he is to present an offering with cakes of leavened bread.
2007014	From the cakes he must present one portion of each offering as a contribution to the LORD. It belongs to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering.
2007015	The meat of the sacrifice of his peace offering of thanksgiving must be eaten on the day he offers it; none of it may be left until morning.
2007016	If, however, the sacrifice he offers is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, but the remainder may be eaten on the next day.
2007017	But any meat of the sacrifice remaining until the third day must be burned up.
2007018	If any of the meat from his peace offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not be credited to the one who presented it; it shall be an abomination, and the one who eats of it shall bear his iniquity.
2007019	Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten; it is to be burned up. As for any other meat, anyone who is ceremonially clean may eat it.
2007020	But if anyone who is unclean eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.
2007021	If one touches anything unclean, whether human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean, detestable thing, and then eats any of the meat of the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.”
2007022	Then the LORD said to Moses,
2007023	“Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘You are not to eat any of the fat of an ox, a sheep, or a goat.
2007024	The fat of an animal found dead or mauled by wild beasts may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it.
2007025	If anyone eats the fat of an animal from which a food offering may be presented to the LORD, the one who eats it must be cut off from his people.
2007026	You must not eat the blood of any bird or animal in any of your dwellings.
2007027	If anyone eats blood, that person must be cut off from his people.’”
2007028	Then the LORD said to Moses,
2007029	“Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘Anyone who presents a peace offering to the LORD must bring it as his sacrifice to the LORD.
2007030	With his own hands he is to bring the food offerings to the LORD; he shall bring the fat, together with the breast, and wave the breast as a wave offering before the LORD.
2007031	The priest is to burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
2007032	And you are to give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your peace offering.
2007033	The son of Aaron who presents the blood and fat of the peace offering shall have the right thigh as a portion.
2007034	I have taken from the sons of Israel the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution of their peace offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a permanent portion from the sons of Israel.’”
2007035	This is the portion of the food offerings to the LORD for Aaron and his sons since the day they were presented to serve the LORD as priests.
2007036	On the day they were anointed, the LORD commanded that this be given them by the sons of Israel. It is a permanent portion for the generations to come.
2007037	This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the peace offering,
2007038	which the LORD gave Moses on Mount Sinai on the day He commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai.

2011001	The LORD spoke again to Moses and Aaron, telling them,
2011002	“Say to the Israelites, ‘Of all the beasts of the earth, these ones you may eat:
2011003	You may eat any animal that has a split hoof completely divided and that chews the cud.
2011004	But of those that only chew the cud or only have a divided hoof, you are not to eat the following: The camel, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
2011005	The rock badger, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
2011006	The rabbit, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
2011007	And the pig, though it has a split hoof completely divided, does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you.
2011008	You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
2011009	Of all the creatures that live in the water, whether in the seas or in the streams, you may eat anything with fins and scales.
2011010	But the following among all the teeming life and creatures in the water are detestable to you: everything in the seas or streams that does not have fins and scales.
2011011	They shall be an abomination to you; you must not eat their meat, and you must detest their carcasses.
2011012	Everything in the water that does not have fins and scales shall be detestable to you.
2011013	Additionally, you are to detest the following birds, and they must not be eaten because they are detestable: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
2011014	the kite, any kind of falcon,
2011015	any kind of raven,
2011016	the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk,
2011017	the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
2011018	the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
2011019	the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
2011020	All flying insects that walk on all fours are detestable to you.
2011021	However, you may eat the following kinds of flying insects that walk on all fours: those having jointed legs above their feet for hopping on the ground.
2011022	Of these you may eat any kind of locust, katydid, cricket, or grasshopper.
2011023	All other flying insects that have four legs are detestable to you.
2011024	These creatures will make you unclean. Whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening,
2011025	and whoever picks up one of their carcasses must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening.
2011026	Every animal with hooves not completely divided or that does not chew the cud is unclean for you. Whoever touches any of them will be unclean.
2011027	All the four-footed animals that walk on their paws are unclean for you; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening,
2011028	and anyone who picks up a carcass must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
2011029	The following creatures that move along the ground are unclean for you: the mole, the mouse, any kind of great lizard,
2011030	the gecko, the monitor lizard, the common lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
2011031	These animals are unclean for you among all the crawling creatures. Whoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.
2011032	When one of them dies and falls on something, that article becomes unclean; any article of wood, clothing, leather, sackcloth, or any implement used for work must be rinsed with water and will remain unclean until evening; then it will be clean.
2011033	If any of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it will be unclean; you must break the pot.
2011034	Any food coming into contact with water from that pot will be unclean, and any drink in such a container will be unclean.
2011035	Anything upon which one of their carcasses falls will be unclean. If it is an oven or cooking pot, it must be smashed; it is unclean and will remain unclean for you.
2011036	Nevertheless, a spring or cistern containing water will remain clean, but one who touches a carcass in it will be unclean.
2011037	If a carcass falls on any seed for sowing, the seed is clean;
2011038	but if water has been put on the seed and a carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
2011039	If an animal that you may eat dies, anyone who touches the carcass will be unclean until evening.
2011040	Whoever eats from the carcass must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening, and anyone who picks up the carcass must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening.
2011041	Every creature that moves along the ground is detestable; it must not be eaten.
2011042	Do not eat any creature that moves along the ground, whether it crawls on its belly or walks on four or more feet; for such creatures are detestable.
2011043	Do not defile yourselves by any crawling creature; do not become unclean or defiled by them.
2011044	For I am the LORD your God; consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, because I am holy. You must not defile yourselves by any creature that crawls along the ground.
2011045	For I am the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt so that I would be your God; therefore be holy, because I am holy.
2011046	This is the law regarding animals, birds, all living creatures that move in the water, and all creatures that crawl along the ground.
2011047	You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between animals that may be eaten and those that may not.’”
2012001	Then the LORD said to Moses,
2012002	“Say to the Israelites, ‘A woman who becomes pregnant and gives birth to a son will be unclean for seven days, as she is during the days of her menstruation.
2012003	And on the eighth day the flesh of the boy’s foreskin is to be circumcised.
2012004	The woman shall continue in purification from her bleeding for thirty-three days. She must not touch anything sacred or go into the sanctuary until the days of her purification are complete.
2012005	If, however, she gives birth to a daughter, the woman will be unclean for two weeks as she is during her menstruation. Then she must continue in purification from her bleeding for sixty-six days.
2012006	When the days of her purification are complete, whether for a son or for a daughter, she is to bring to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering.
2012007	And the priest will present them before the LORD and make atonement for her; and she shall be ceremonially cleansed from her flow of blood. This is the law for a woman giving birth, whether to a male or to a female.
2012008	But if she cannot afford a lamb, she shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. Then the priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean.’”
2013001	Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
2013002	“When someone has a swelling or rash or bright spot on his skin that may be an infectious skin disease, he must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who is a priest.
2013003	The priest is to examine the infection on his skin, and if the hair in the infection has turned white and the sore appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a skin disease. After the priest examines him, he must pronounce him unclean.
2013004	If, however, the spot on his skin is white and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.
2013005	On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine him, and if he sees that the infection is unchanged and has not spread on the skin, the priest must isolate him for another seven days.
2013006	The priest will examine him again on the seventh day, and if the sore has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean; it is a rash. The person must wash his clothes and be clean.
2013007	But if the rash spreads further on his skin after he has shown himself to the priest for his cleansing, he must present himself again to the priest.
2013008	The priest will reexamine him, and if the rash has spread on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a skin disease.
2013009	When anyone develops a skin disease, he must be brought to the priest.
2013010	The priest will examine him, and if there is a white swelling on the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling,
2013011	it is a chronic skin disease and the priest must pronounce him unclean. He need not isolate him, for he is unclean.
2013012	But if the skin disease breaks out all over his skin so that it covers all the skin of the infected person from head to foot, as far as the priest can see,
2013013	the priest shall examine him, and if the disease has covered his entire body, he is to pronounce the infected person clean. Since it has all turned white, he is clean.
2013014	But whenever raw flesh appears on someone, he will be unclean.
2013015	When the priest sees the raw flesh, he must pronounce him unclean. The raw flesh is unclean; it is a skin disease.
2013016	But if the raw flesh changes and turns white, he must go to the priest.
2013017	The priest will reexamine him, and if the infection has turned white, the priest is to pronounce the infected person clean; then he is clean.
2013018	When a boil appears on someone’s skin and it heals,
2013019	and a white swelling or a reddish-white spot develops where the boil was, he must present himself to the priest.
2013020	The priest shall examine it, and if it appears to be beneath the skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection that has broken out in the boil.
2013021	But when the priest examines it, if there is no white hair in it, and it is not beneath the skin and has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
2013022	If it spreads any further on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is an infection.
2013023	But if the spot remains unchanged and does not spread, it is only the scar from the boil, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
2013024	When there is a burn on someone’s skin and the raw area of the burn becomes reddish-white or white,
2013025	the priest must examine it. If the hair in the spot has turned white and the spot appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection.
2013026	But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the spot, and it is not beneath the skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
2013027	On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine him, and if it has spread further on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection.
2013028	But if the spot is unchanged and has not spread on the skin but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn, and the priest is to pronounce him clean; for it is only the scar from the burn.
2013029	If a man or woman has an infection on the head or chin,
2013030	the priest shall examine the infection, and if it appears to be deeper than the skin and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a scaly outbreak, an infectious disease of the head or chin.
2013031	But if the priest examines the scaly infection and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.
2013032	On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine the infection, and if the scaly outbreak has not spread and there is no yellow hair in it, and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin,
2013033	then the person must shave himself except for the scaly area. Then the priest shall isolate him for another seven days.
2013034	On the seventh day the priest shall examine the scaly outbreak, and if it has not spread on the skin and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, the priest is to pronounce him clean. He must wash his clothes, and he will be clean.
2013035	If, however, the scaly outbreak spreads further on the skin after his cleansing,
2013036	the priest is to examine him, and if the scaly outbreak has spread on the skin, the priest need not look for yellow hair; the person is unclean.
2013037	If, however, in his sight the scaly outbreak is unchanged and black hair has grown in it, then it has healed. He is clean, and the priest is to pronounce him clean.
2013038	When a man or a woman has white spots on the skin,
2013039	the priest shall examine them, and if the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; the person is clean.
2013040	Now if a man loses his hair and is bald, he is still clean.
2013041	Or if his hairline recedes and he is bald on his forehead, he is still clean.
2013042	But if there is a reddish-white sore on the bald head or forehead, it is an infectious disease breaking out on it.
2013043	The priest is to examine him, and if the swelling of the infection on his bald head or forehead is reddish-white like a skin disease,
2013044	the man is diseased; he is unclean. The priest must pronounce him unclean because of the infection on his head.
2013045	A diseased person must wear torn clothes and let his hair hang loose, and he must cover his mouth and cry out, ‘Unclean, unclean!’
2013046	As long as he has the infection, he remains unclean. He must live alone in a place outside the camp.
2013047	If any fabric is contaminated with mildew —any wool or linen garment,
2013048	any weave or knit of linen or wool, or any article of leather—
2013049	and if the mark in the fabric, leather, weave, knit, or leather article is green or red, then it is contaminated with mildew and must be shown to the priest.
2013050	And the priest is to examine the mildew and isolate the contaminated fabric for seven days.
2013051	On the seventh day the priest shall reexamine it, and if the mildew has spread in the fabric, weave, knit, or leather, then regardless of how it is used, it is a harmful mildew; the article is unclean.
2013052	He is to burn the fabric, weave, or knit, whether the contaminated item is wool or linen or leather. Since the mildew is harmful, the article must be burned up.
2013053	But when the priest reexamines it, if the mildew has not spread in the fabric, weave, knit, or leather article,
2013054	the priest is to order the contaminated article to be washed and isolated for another seven days.
2013055	After it has been washed, the priest is to reexamine it, and if the mildewed article has not changed in appearance, it is unclean. Even though the mildew has not spread, you must burn it, whether the rot is on the front or back.
2013056	If the priest examines it and the mildew has faded after it has been washed, he must cut the contaminated section out of the fabric, leather, weave, or knit.
2013057	But if it reappears in the fabric, weave, or knit, or on any leather article, it is spreading. You must burn the contaminated article.
2013058	If the mildew disappears from the fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article after washing, then it is to be washed again, and it will be clean.
2013059	This is the law concerning a mildew contamination in wool or linen fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article, for pronouncing it clean or unclean.”

2014020	and offer it on the altar, with the grain offering, to make atonement for him, and he will be clean.
