2015001	And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
2015002	“Say to the Israelites, ‘When any man has a bodily discharge, the discharge is unclean.
2015003	This uncleanness is from his discharge, whether his body allows the discharge to flow or blocks it. So his discharge will bring about uncleanness.
2015004	Any bed on which the man with the discharge lies will be unclean, and any furniture on which he sits will be unclean.
2015005	Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
2015006	Whoever sits on furniture on which the man with the discharge was sitting must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
2015007	Whoever touches the body of the man with a discharge must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
2015008	If the man with the discharge spits on one who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
2015009	Any saddle on which the man with the discharge rides will be unclean.
2015010	Whoever touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
2015011	If the man with the discharge touches anyone without first rinsing his hands with water, the one who was touched must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.

2015031	You must keep the children of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die by defiling My tabernacle, which is among them.
2015032	This is the law of him who has a discharge, of the man who has an emission of semen whereby he is unclean,

2016018	Then he shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He is to take some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood and put it on all the horns of the altar.

2016020	When Aaron has finished purifying the Most Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he is to bring forward the live goat.
2016021	Then he is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities and rebellious acts of the Israelites in regard to all their sins. He is to put them on the goat’s head and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man appointed for the task.
2016022	The goat will carry on itself all their iniquities into a solitary place, and the man will release it into the wilderness.
2016023	Then Aaron is to enter the Tent of Meeting, take off the linen garments he put on before entering the Most Holy Place, and leave them there.
2016024	He is to bathe himself with water in a holy place and put on his own clothes. Then he must go out and sacrifice his burnt offering and the people’s burnt offering to make atonement for himself and for the people.
2016025	He is also to burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
2016026	The man who released the goat as the scapegoat must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water; afterward he may reenter the camp.
2016027	The bull for the sin offering and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place to make atonement, must be taken outside the camp; and their hides, flesh, and dung must be burned up.
2016028	The one who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water, and afterward he may reenter the camp.
2016029	This is to be a permanent statute for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month, you shall humble yourselves and not do any work—whether the native or the foreigner who resides among you—
2016030	because on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you, and you will be clean from all your sins before the LORD.
2016031	It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, that you may humble yourselves; it is a permanent statute.

2016033	and make atonement for the Most Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, and for the priests and all the people of the assembly.

2025004	But in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land—a Sabbath to the LORD. You are not to sow your field or prune your vineyard.
2025005	You are not to reap the aftergrowth of your harvest or gather the grapes of your untended vines. The land must have a year of complete rest.
2025006	Whatever the land yields during the Sabbath year shall be food for you—for yourself, your manservant and maidservant, the hired hand or foreigner who stays with you,
2025007	and for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its growth may serve as food.
2025008	And you shall count off seven Sabbaths of years—seven times seven years—so that the seven Sabbaths of years amount to forty-nine years.
2025009	Then you are to sound the horn far and wide on the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement. You shall sound it throughout your land.
2025010	So you are to consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty in the land for all its inhabitants. It shall be your Jubilee, when each of you is to return to his property and to his clan.
2025011	The fiftieth year will be a Jubilee for you; you are not to sow the land or reap its aftergrowth or harvest the untended vines.
2025012	For it is a Jubilee; it shall be holy to you. You may eat only the crops taken directly from the field.
2025013	In this Year of Jubilee, each of you shall return to his own property.
2025014	If you make a sale to your neighbor or a purchase from him, you must not take advantage of each other.
2025015	You are to buy from your neighbor according to the number of years since the last Jubilee; he is to sell to you according to the number of harvest years remaining.
2025016	You shall increase the price in proportion to a greater number of years, or decrease it in proportion to a lesser number of years; for he is selling you a given number of harvests.
2025017	Do not take advantage of each other, but fear your God; for I am the LORD your God.
2025018	You are to keep My statutes and carefully observe My judgments, so that you may dwell securely in the land.
2025019	Then the land will yield its fruit, so that you can eat your fill and dwell in safety in the land.
2025020	Now you may wonder, ‘What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather our produce?’
2025021	But I will send My blessing upon you in the sixth year, so that the land will yield a crop sufficient for three years.
2025022	While you are sowing in the eighth year, you will be eating from the previous harvest, until the ninth year’s harvest comes in.
2025023	The land must not be sold permanently, because it is Mine, and you are but foreigners and residents with Me.
2025024	Thus for every piece of property you possess, you must provide for the redemption of the land.
2025025	If your brother becomes impoverished and sells some of his property, his nearest of kin may come and redeem what his brother has sold.
2025026	Or if a man has no one to redeem it for him, but he prospers and acquires enough to redeem his land,
2025027	he shall calculate the years since its sale, repay the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his property.
2025028	But if he cannot obtain enough to repay him, what he sold will remain in possession of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee, however, it is to be released, so that he may return to his property.
2025029	If a man sells a house in a walled city, he retains his right of redemption until a full year after its sale; during that year it may be redeemed.
2025030	If it is not redeemed by the end of a full year, then the house in the walled city is permanently transferred to its buyer and his descendants. It is not to be released in the Jubilee.
2025031	But houses in villages with no walls around them are to be considered as open fields. They may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.
2025032	As for the cities of the Levites, the Levites always have the right to redeem their houses in the cities they possess.
2025033	So whatever belongs to the Levites may be redeemed—a house sold in a city they possess—and must be released in the Jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the Israelites.
2025034	But the open pastureland around their cities may not be sold, for this is their permanent possession.
2025035	Now if your countryman becomes destitute and cannot support himself among you, then you are to help him as you would a foreigner or stranger, so that he can continue to live among you.
2025036	Do not take any interest or profit from him, but fear your God, that your countryman may live among you.
2025037	You must not lend him your silver at interest or sell him your food for profit.
2025038	I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
2025039	If a countryman among you becomes destitute and sells himself to you, then you must not force him into slave labor.
2025040	Let him stay with you as a hired worker or temporary resident; he is to work for you until the Year of Jubilee.
2025041	Then he and his children are to be released, and he may return to his clan and to the property of his fathers.
2025042	Because the Israelites are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt, they are not to be sold as slaves.
2025043	You are not to rule over them harshly, but you shall fear your God.
2025044	Your menservants and maidservants shall come from the nations around you, from whom you may purchase them.
2025045	You may also purchase them from the foreigners residing among you or their clans living among you who are born in your land. These may become your property.
2025046	You may leave them to your sons after you to inherit as property; you can make them slaves for life. But as for your brothers, the Israelites, no man may rule harshly over his brother.
2025047	If a foreigner residing among you prospers, but your countryman dwelling near him becomes destitute and sells himself to the foreigner or to a member of his clan,
2025048	he retains the right of redemption after he has sold himself. One of his brothers may redeem him:
2025049	either his uncle or cousin or any close relative from his clan may redeem him. Or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.
2025050	He and his purchaser will then count the time from the year he sold himself up to the Year of Jubilee. The price of his sale will be determined by the number of years, based on the daily wages of a hired hand.
2025051	If many years remain, he must pay for his redemption in proportion to his purchase price.
2025052	If only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, he is to calculate and pay his redemption according to his remaining years.
2025053	He shall be treated like a man hired from year to year, but a foreign owner must not rule over him harshly in your sight.
2025054	Even if he is not redeemed in any of these ways, he and his children shall be released in the Year of Jubilee.
2025055	For the Israelites are My servants. They are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
2026001	“You must not make idols for yourselves or set up a carved image or sacred pillar; you must not place a sculpted stone in your land to bow down to it. For I am the LORD your God.
2026002	You must keep My Sabbaths and have reverence for My sanctuary. I am the LORD.
2026003	If you follow My statutes and carefully keep My commandments,
2026004	I will give you rains in their season, and the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will bear their fruit.
2026005	Your threshing will continue until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will continue until sowing time; you will have your fill of food to eat and will dwell securely in your land.
2026006	And I will give peace to the land, and you will lie down with nothing to fear. I will rid the land of dangerous animals, and no sword will pass through your land.
2026007	You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall by the sword before you.
2026008	Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand, and your enemies will fall by the sword before you.
2026009	I will turn toward you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will establish My covenant with you.
2026010	You will still be eating the old supply of grain when you need to clear it out to make room for the new.
2026011	And I will make My dwelling place among you, and My soul will not despise you.
2026012	I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people.
2026013	I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be slaves to the Egyptians. I broke the bars of your yoke and enabled you to walk in uprightness.
2026014	If, however, you fail to obey Me and to carry out all these commandments,
2026015	and if you reject My statutes, despise My ordinances, and neglect to carry out all My commandments, and so break My covenant,
2026016	then this is what I will do to you: I will bring upon you sudden terror, wasting disease, and fever that will destroy your sight and drain your life. You will sow your seed in vain, because your enemies will eat it.
2026017	And I will set My face against you, so that you will be defeated by your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one pursues you.
2026018	And if after all this you will not obey Me, I will proceed to punish you sevenfold for your sins.
2026019	I will break down your stubborn pride and make your sky like iron and your land like bronze,
2026020	and your strength will be spent in vain. For your land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not bear their fruit.
2026021	If you walk in hostility toward Me and refuse to obey Me, I will multiply your plagues seven times, according to your sins.
2026022	I will send wild animals against you to rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and reduce your numbers, until your roads lie desolate.
2026023	And if in spite of these things you do not accept My discipline, but continue to walk in hostility toward Me,
2026024	then I will act with hostility toward you, and I will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
2026025	And I will bring a sword against you to execute the vengeance of the covenant. Though you withdraw into your cities, I will send a plague among you, and you will be delivered into the hand of the enemy.
2026026	When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven and dole out your bread by weight, so that you will eat but not be satisfied.
2026027	But if in spite of all this you do not obey Me, but continue to walk in hostility toward Me,
2026028	then I will walk in fury against you, and I, even I, will punish you sevenfold for your sins.
2026029	You will eat the flesh of your own sons and daughters.
2026030	I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and heap your lifeless bodies on the lifeless remains of your idols; and My soul will despise you.
2026031	I will reduce your cities to rubble and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will refuse to smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices.
2026032	And I will lay waste the land, so that your enemies who dwell in it will be appalled.
2026033	But I will scatter you among the nations and will draw out a sword after you as your land becomes desolate and your cities are laid waste.
2026034	Then the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths all the days it lies desolate, while you are in the land of your enemies. At that time the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
2026035	As long as it lies desolate, the land will have the rest it did not receive during the Sabbaths when you lived in it.
2026036	As for those of you who survive, I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, so that even the sound of a windblown leaf will put them to flight. And they will flee as one flees the sword, and fall when no one pursues them.
2026037	They will stumble over one another as before the sword, though no one is behind them. So you will not be able to stand against your enemies.
2026038	You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you.
2026039	Those of you who survive in the lands of your enemies will waste away in their iniquity and will decay in the sins of their fathers.
2026040	But if they will confess their iniquity and that of their fathers in the unfaithfulness that they practiced against Me, by which they have also walked in hostility toward Me—
2026041	and I acted with hostility toward them and brought them into the land of their enemies—and if their uncircumcised hearts will be humbled and they will make amends for their iniquity,
2026042	then I will remember My covenant with Jacob and My covenant with Isaac and My covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.
2026043	For the land will be abandoned by them, and it will enjoy its Sabbaths by lying desolate without them. And they will pay the penalty for their iniquity, because they rejected My ordinances and abhorred My statutes.
2026044	Yet in spite of this, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject or despise them so as to destroy them and break My covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God.
2026045	But for their sake I will remember the covenant with their fathers, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God. I am the LORD.”
2026046	These are the statutes, ordinances, and laws that the LORD established between Himself and the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.
2027001	Then the LORD said to Moses,
2027002	“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘When someone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the value of persons,
2027003	if the valuation concerns a male from twenty to sixty years of age, then your valuation shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel.
2027004	Or if it is a female, then your valuation shall be thirty shekels.
2027005	And if the person is from five to twenty years of age, then your valuation for the male shall be twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
2027006	Now if the person is from one month to five years of age, then your valuation for the male shall be five shekels of silver, and for the female three shekels of silver.
2027007	And if the person is sixty years of age or older, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels for the male and ten shekels for the female.
2027008	But if the one making the vow is too poor to pay the valuation, he is to present the person before the priest, who shall set the value according to what the one making the vow can afford.
2027009	If he vows an animal that may be brought as an offering to the LORD, any such animal given to the LORD shall be holy.
2027010	He must not replace it or exchange it, either good for bad or bad for good. But if he does substitute one animal for another, both that animal and its substitute will be holy.
2027011	But if the vow involves any of the unclean animals that may not be brought as an offering to the LORD, the animal must be presented before the priest.
2027012	The priest shall set its value, whether high or low; as the priest values it, the price will be set.
2027013	If, however, the owner decides to redeem the animal, he must add a fifth to its value.
2027014	Now if a man consecrates his house as holy to the LORD, then the priest shall value it either as good or bad. The price will stand just as the priest values it.
2027015	But if he who consecrated his house redeems it, he must add a fifth to the assessed value, and it will belong to him.
2027016	If a man consecrates to the LORD a parcel of his land, then your valuation shall be proportional to the seed required for it—fifty shekels of silver for every homer of barley seed.
2027017	If he consecrates his field during the Year of Jubilee, the price will stand according to your valuation.
2027018	But if he consecrates his field after the Jubilee, the priest is to calculate the price in proportion to the years left until the next Year of Jubilee, so that your valuation will be reduced.
2027019	And if the one who consecrated the field decides to redeem it, he must add a fifth to the assessed value, and it shall belong to him.
2027020	If, however, he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold it to another man, it may no longer be redeemed.
2027021	When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will become holy, like a field devoted to the LORD; it becomes the property of the priests.
2027022	Now if a man consecrates to the LORD a field he has purchased, which is not a part of his own property,
2027023	then the priest shall calculate for him the value up to the Year of Jubilee, and the man shall pay the assessed value on that day as a sacred offering to the LORD.
2027024	In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought—the original owner of the land.
2027025	Every valuation will be according to the sanctuary shekel, twenty gerahs to the shekel.
2027026	But no one may consecrate a firstborn of the livestock, because a firstborn belongs to the LORD. Whether it is an ox or a sheep, it is the LORD’s.
2027027	But if it is among the unclean animals, then he may redeem it according to your valuation and add a fifth of its value. If it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your valuation.
2027028	Nothing that a man sets apart to the LORD from all he owns—whether a man, an animal, or his inherited land—can be sold or redeemed; everything so devoted is most holy to the LORD.
2027029	No person set apart for destruction may be ransomed; he must surely be put to death.
2027030	Thus any tithe from the land, whether from the seed of the land or the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.
2027031	If a man wishes to redeem part of his tithe, he must add a fifth to its value.
2027032	Every tenth animal from the herd or flock that passes under the shepherd’s rod will be holy to the LORD.
2027033	He must not inspect whether it is good or bad, and he shall not make any substitution. But if he does make a substitution, both the animal and its substitute shall become holy; they cannot be redeemed.’”
2027034	These are the commandments that the LORD gave to Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.

3005001	Then the LORD said to Moses,
3005002	“Command the Israelites to send away from the camp anyone with a skin disease, anyone who has a bodily discharge, and anyone who is defiled by a dead body.
3005003	You must send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them.”
3005004	So the Israelites did this, sending such people outside the camp. They did just as the LORD had instructed Moses.
3005005	And the LORD said to Moses,
3005006	“Tell the Israelites that when a man or woman acts unfaithfully against the LORD by committing any sin against another, that person is guilty
3005007	and must confess the sin he has committed. He must make full restitution, add a fifth to its value, and give all this to the one he has wronged.
3005008	But if the man has no relative to whom restitution can be made for the wrong, the restitution belongs to the LORD and must be given to the priest along with the ram of atonement, by which the atonement is made for him.
3005009	Every sacred contribution the Israelites bring to the priest shall belong to him.
3005010	Each man’s sacred gifts are his own, but whatever he gives to the priest will belong to the priest.”
3005011	Then the LORD said to Moses,
3005012	“Speak to the Israelites and tell them that if any man’s wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him
3005013	by sleeping with another man, and it is concealed from her husband and her impurity is undetected (since there is no witness against her and she was not caught in the act),
3005014	and if a feeling of jealousy comes over her husband and he suspects his wife who has defiled herself—or if a feeling of jealousy comes over him and he suspects her even though she has not defiled herself—
3005015	then he is to bring his wife to the priest. He must also bring for her an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He is not to pour oil over it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, an offering of memorial as a reminder of iniquity.
3005016	The priest is to bring the wife forward and have her stand before the LORD.
3005017	Then he is to take some holy water in a clay jar and put some of the dust from the tabernacle floor into the water.
3005018	After the priest has the woman stand before the LORD, he is to let down her hair and place in her hands the grain offering of memorial, which is the grain offering for jealousy. The priest is to hold the bitter water that brings a curse.
3005019	And he is to put the woman under oath and say to her, ‘If no other man has slept with you and you have not gone astray and become defiled while under your husband’s authority, may you be immune to this bitter water that brings a curse.
3005020	But if you have gone astray while under your husband’s authority and have defiled yourself and lain carnally with a man other than your husband’—
3005021	and the priest shall have the woman swear under the oath of the curse—‘then may the LORD make you an attested curse among your people by making your thigh shrivel and your belly swell.
3005022	May this water that brings a curse enter your stomach and cause your belly to swell and your thigh to shrivel.’ Then the woman is to say, ‘Amen, Amen.’
3005023	And the priest shall write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.
3005024	He is to have the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and it will enter her and may cause her bitter suffering.
3005025	The priest shall take from her hand the grain offering for jealousy, wave it before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
3005026	Then the priest is to take a handful of the grain offering as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar; after that he is to have the woman drink the water.
3005027	When he has made her drink the water, if she has defiled herself and been unfaithful to her husband, then the water that brings a curse will enter her and cause bitter suffering; her belly will swell, her thigh will shrivel, and she will become accursed among her people.
3005028	But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be unaffected and able to conceive children.
3005029	This is the law of jealousy when a wife goes astray and defiles herself while under her husband’s authority,
3005030	or when a feeling of jealousy comes over a husband and he suspects his wife. He is to have the woman stand before the LORD, and the priest is to apply to her this entire law.
3005031	The husband will be free from guilt, but the woman shall bear her iniquity.”
3006001	And the LORD said to Moses,
3006002	“Speak to the Israelites and tell them that if a man or woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD,
3006003	he is to abstain from wine and strong drink. He must not drink vinegar made from wine or strong drink, and he must not drink any grape juice or eat fresh grapes or raisins.
3006004	All the days of his separation, he is not to eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or skins.
3006005	For the entire period of his vow of separation, no razor shall touch his head. He must be holy until the time of his separation to the LORD is complete; he must let the hair of his head grow long.
3006006	Throughout the days of his separation to the LORD, he must not go near a dead body.
3006007	Even if his father or mother or brother or sister should die, he is not to defile himself, because the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head.
3006008	Throughout the time of his separation, he is holy to the LORD.
3006009	If someone suddenly dies in his presence and defiles his consecrated head of hair, he must shave his head on the day of his cleansing—the seventh day.
3006010	On the eighth day he must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
3006011	And the priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to make atonement for him, because he has sinned by being in the presence of the dead body. On that day he must consecrate his head again.
3006012	He must rededicate his time of separation to the LORD and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. But the preceding days shall not be counted, because his separation was defiled.
3006013	Now this is the law of the Nazirite when his time of separation is complete: He must be brought to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting,
3006014	and he is to present an offering to the LORD of an unblemished year-old male lamb as a burnt offering, an unblemished year-old female lamb as a sin offering, and an unblemished ram as a peace offering—
3006015	together with their grain offerings and drink offerings—and a basket of unleavened cakes made from fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened wafers coated with oil.
3006016	The priest is to present all these before the LORD and make the sin offering and the burnt offering.
3006017	He shall also offer the ram as a peace offering to the LORD, along with the basket of unleavened bread. And the priest is to offer the accompanying grain offering and drink offering.
3006018	Then at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the Nazirite is to shave his consecrated head, take the hair, and put it on the fire under the peace offering.
3006019	And the priest is to take the boiled shoulder from the ram, one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them into the hands of the Nazirite who has just shaved the hair of his consecration.
3006020	The priest shall then wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. This is a holy portion for the priest, in addition to the breast of the wave offering and the thigh that was presented. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.
3006021	This is the law of the Nazirite who vows his offering to the LORD for his separation, in addition to whatever else he can afford; he must fulfill whatever vow he makes, according to the law of his separation.”
3006022	Then the LORD said to Moses,
3006023	“Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
3006024	‘May the LORD bless you and keep you;
3006025	may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious to you;
3006026	may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you and give you peace.’
3006027	So they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.”

3008015	After you have cleansed them and presented them as a wave offering, they may come to serve at the Tent of Meeting.
3008016	For the Levites have been wholly given to Me from among the sons of Israel. I have taken them for Myself in place of all who come first from the womb, the firstborn of all the sons of Israel.
3008017	For every firstborn male in Israel is Mine, both man and beast. I set them apart for Myself on the day I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt.
3008018	But I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the sons of Israel.
3008019	And I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to perform the service for the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting and to make atonement on their behalf, so that no plague will come against the Israelites when they approach the sanctuary.”
3008020	So Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of Israel did with the Levites everything that the LORD had commanded Moses they should do.
3008021	The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes, and Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the LORD. Aaron also made atonement for them to cleanse them.
3008022	After that, the Levites came to perform their service at the Tent of Meeting in the presence of Aaron and his sons. Thus they did with the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
3008023	And the LORD said to Moses,
3008024	“This applies to the Levites: Men twenty-five years of age or older shall enter to perform the service in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
3008025	But at the age of fifty, they must retire from performing the work and no longer serve.
3008026	After that, they may assist their brothers in fulfilling their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they themselves are not to do the work. This is how you are to assign responsibilities to the Levites.”
3009001	In the first month of the second year after Israel had come out of the land of Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai:
3009002	“The Israelites are to observe the Passover at its appointed time.
3009003	You are to observe it at the appointed time, at twilight on the fourteenth day of this month, in accordance with its statutes and ordinances.”
3009004	So Moses told the Israelites to observe the Passover,
3009005	and they did so in the Wilderness of Sinai, at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
3009006	But there were some men who were unclean due to a dead body, so they could not observe the Passover on that day. And they came before Moses and Aaron that same day
3009007	and said to Moses, “We are unclean because of a dead body, but why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?”
3009008	“Wait here until I find out what the LORD commands concerning you,” Moses replied.
3009009	Then the LORD said to Moses,
3009010	“Tell the Israelites: ‘When any one of you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead body, or is away on a journey, he may still observe the Passover to the LORD.
3009011	Such people are to observe it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month. They are to eat the lamb, together with unleavened bread and bitter herbs;
3009012	they may not leave any of it until morning or break any of its bones. They must observe the Passover according to all its statutes.
3009013	But if a man who is ceremonially clean and is not on a journey still fails to observe the Passover, he must be cut off from his people, because he did not present the LORD’s offering at its appointed time. That man will bear the consequences of his sin.
3009014	If a foreigner dwelling among you wants to observe the Passover to the LORD, he is to do so according to the Passover statute and its ordinances. You are to apply the same statute to both the foreigner and the native of the land.’”
3009015	On the day that the tabernacle, the Tent of the Testimony, was set up, the cloud covered it and appeared like fire above the tabernacle from evening until morning.
3009016	It remained that way continually; the cloud would cover the tabernacle by day, and at night it would appear like fire.
3009017	Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the Tent, the Israelites would set out, and wherever the cloud settled, there the Israelites would camp.
3009018	At the LORD’s command the Israelites set out, and at the LORD’s command they camped. As long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle, they remained encamped.
3009019	Even when the cloud lingered over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the LORD’s charge and did not set out.
3009020	Sometimes the cloud remained over the tabernacle for only a few days, and they would camp at the LORD’s command and set out at the LORD’s command.
3009021	Sometimes the cloud remained only from evening until morning, and when it lifted in the morning, they would set out. Whether it was by day or by night, when the cloud was taken up, they would set out.
3009022	Whether the cloud lingered for two days, a month, or longer, the Israelites camped and did not set out as long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle; but when it was lifted, they would set out.
3009023	They camped at the LORD’s command, and they set out at the LORD’s command; they carried out the LORD’s charge according to His command through Moses.
3010001	Then the LORD said to Moses,
3010002	“Make two trumpets of hammered silver to be used for calling the congregation and for having the camps set out.
3010003	When both are sounded, the whole congregation is to assemble before you at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
3010004	But if only one is sounded, then the leaders, the heads of the clans of Israel, are to gather before you.
3010005	When you sound short blasts, the camps that lie on the east side are to set out.
3010006	When you sound the short blasts a second time, the camps that lie on the south side are to set out. The blasts are to signal them to set out.
3010007	To convene the assembly, you are to sound long blasts, not short ones.
3010008	The sons of Aaron, the priests, are to sound the trumpets. This shall be a permanent statute for you and the generations to come.
3010009	When you enter into battle in your land against an adversary who attacks you, sound short blasts on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies.
3010010	And on your joyous occasions, your appointed feasts, and the beginning of each month, you are to blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings to serve as a reminder for you before your God. I am the LORD your God.”
3010011	On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle of the Testimony,
3010012	and the Israelites set out from the Wilderness of Sinai, traveling from place to place until the cloud settled in the Wilderness of Paran.
3010013	They set out this first time according to the LORD’s command through Moses.
3010014	First, the divisions of the camp of Judah set out under their standard, with Nahshon son of Amminadab in command.
3010015	Nethanel son of Zuar was over the division of the tribe of Issachar,
3010016	and Eliab son of Helon was over the division of the tribe of Zebulun.
3010017	Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites set out, transporting it.
3010018	Then the divisions of the camp of Reuben set out under their standard, with Elizur son of Shedeur in command.
3010019	Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the division of the tribe of Simeon,
3010020	and Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the division of the tribe of Gad.
3010021	Then the Kohathites set out, transporting the holy objects; the tabernacle was to be set up before their arrival.
3010022	Next, the divisions of the camp of Ephraim set out under their standard, with Elishama son of Ammihud in command.
3010023	Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the division of the tribe of Manasseh,
3010024	and Abidan son of Gideoni was over the division of the tribe of Benjamin.
3010025	Finally, the divisions of the camp of Dan set out under their standard, serving as the rear guard for all units, with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai in command.
3010026	Pagiel son of Ocran was over the division of the tribe of Asher,
3010027	and Ahira son of Enan was over the division of the tribe of Naphtali.
3010028	This was the order of march for the Israelite divisions as they set out.
3010029	Then Moses said to Hobab, the son of Moses’ father-in-law Reuel the Midianite, “We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said: ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things to Israel.”
3010030	“I will not go,” Hobab replied. “Instead, I am going back to my own land and my own people.”
3010031	“Please do not leave us,” Moses said, “since you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can serve as our eyes.
3010032	If you come with us, we will share with you whatever good things the LORD gives us.”
3010033	So they set out on a three-day journey from the mountain of the LORD, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD traveling ahead of them for those three days to seek a resting place for them.
3010034	And the cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
3010035	Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, “Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered; may those who hate You flee before You.”
3010036	And when it came to rest, he would say: “Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel.”
3011001	Soon the people began to complain about their hardship in the hearing of the LORD, and when He heard them, His anger was kindled, and fire from the LORD blazed among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp.
3011002	And the people cried out to Moses, and he prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
3011003	So that place was called Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.
3011004	Meanwhile, the rabble among them had a strong craving for other food, and again the Israelites wept and said, “Who will feed us meat?
3011005	We remember the fish we ate freely in Egypt, along with the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
3011006	But now our appetite is gone; there is nothing to see but this manna!”
3011007	Now the manna resembled coriander seed, and its appearance was like that of gum resin.
3011008	The people walked around and gathered it, ground it on a handmill or crushed it in a mortar, then boiled it in a cooking pot or shaped it into cakes. It tasted like pastry baked with fine oil.
3011009	When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna would fall with it.
3011010	Then Moses heard the people of family after family weeping at the entrances to their tents, and the anger of the LORD was kindled greatly, and Moses was also displeased.
3011011	So Moses asked the LORD, “Why have You brought this trouble on Your servant? Why have I not found favor in Your sight, that You have laid upon me the burden of all these people?
3011012	Did I conceive all these people? Did I give them birth, so that You should tell me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries an infant,’ to the land that You swore to give their fathers?
3011013	Where can I get meat for all these people? For they keep crying out to me, ‘Give us meat to eat!’
3011014	I cannot carry all these people by myself; it is too burdensome for me.
3011015	If this is how You are going to treat me, please kill me right now—if I have found favor in Your eyes—and let me not see my own wretchedness.”
3011016	Then the LORD said to Moses, “Bring Me seventy of the elders of Israel known to you as leaders and officers of the people. Bring them to the Tent of Meeting and have them stand there with you.
3011017	And I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put that Spirit on them. They will help you bear the burden of the people, so that you do not have to bear it by yourself.
3011018	And say to the people: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat, because you have cried out in the hearing of the LORD, saying: ‘Who will feed us meat? For we were better off in Egypt!’ Therefore the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.
3011019	You will eat it not for one or two days, nor for five or ten or twenty days,
3011020	but for a whole month—until it comes out of your nostrils and makes you nauseous—because you have rejected the LORD, who is among you, and have cried out before Him, saying, ‘Why did we ever leave Egypt?’”
3011021	But Moses replied, “Here I am among 600,000 men on foot, yet You say, ‘I will give them meat, and they will eat for a month.’
3011022	If all our flocks and herds were slaughtered for them, would they have enough? Or if all the fish in the sea were caught for them, would they have enough?”
3011023	The LORD answered Moses, “Is the LORD’s arm too short? Now you will see whether or not My word will come to pass.”
3011024	So Moses went out and relayed to the people the words of the LORD, and he gathered seventy of the elders of the people and had them stand around the tent.
3011025	Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and placed that Spirit on the seventy elders. As the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied—but they never did so again.
3011026	Two men, however, had remained in the camp—one named Eldad and the other Medad—and the Spirit rested on them. They were among those listed, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
3011027	A young man ran and reported to Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
3011028	Joshua son of Nun, the attendant to Moses since youth, spoke up and said, “Moses, my lord, stop them!”
3011029	But Moses replied, “Are you jealous on my account? I wish that all the LORD’s people were prophets and that the LORD would place His Spirit on them!”
3011030	Then Moses returned to the camp, along with the elders of Israel.
3011031	Now a wind sent by the LORD came up, drove in quail from the sea, and brought them near the camp, about two cubits above the surface of the ground, for a day’s journey in every direction around the camp.
3011032	All that day and night, and all the next day, the people stayed up gathering the quail. No one gathered less than ten homers, and they spread them out all around the camp.
3011033	But while the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck them with a severe plague.
3011034	So they called that place Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.
3011035	From Kibroth-hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, where they remained for some time.
3012001	Then Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had taken a Cushite wife.
3012002	“Does the LORD speak only through Moses?” they said. “Does He not also speak through us?” And the LORD heard this.
3012003	Now Moses was a very humble man, more so than any man on the face of the earth.
3012004	And suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “You three, come out to the Tent of Meeting.” So the three went out,
3012005	and the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud, stood at the entrance to the Tent, and summoned Aaron and Miriam. When both of them had stepped forward,
3012006	He said, “Hear now My words: If there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, will reveal Myself to him in a vision; I will speak to him in a dream.
3012007	But this is not so with My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house.
3012008	I speak with him face to face, clearly and not in riddles; he sees the form of the LORD. Why then were you unafraid to speak against My servant Moses?”
3012009	So the anger of the LORD burned against them, and He departed.
3012010	As the cloud lifted from above the Tent, suddenly Miriam became leprous, white as snow. Aaron turned toward her, saw that she was leprous,
3012011	and said to Moses, “My lord, please do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.
3012012	Please do not let her be like a stillborn infant whose flesh is half consumed when he comes out of his mother’s womb.”
3012013	So Moses cried out to the LORD, “O God, please heal her!”
3012014	But the LORD answered Moses, “If her father had but spit in her face, would she not have been in disgrace for seven days? Let her be confined outside the camp for seven days; after that she may be brought back in.”
3012015	So Miriam was confined outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on until she was brought in again.
3012016	After that, the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the Wilderness of Paran.

3013021	So they went up and spied out the land from the Wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, toward Lebo-hamath.

3013028	Nevertheless, the people living in the land are strong, and the cities are large and fortified. We even saw the descendants of Anak there.
3013029	The Amalekites live in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.”
3013030	Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “We must go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly conquer it!”
3013031	But the men who had gone up with him replied, “We cannot go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are!”
3013032	So they gave the Israelites a bad report about the land that they had spied out: “The land we explored devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw there are great in stature.
3013033	We even saw the Nephilim there—the descendants of Anak that come from the Nephilim! We seemed like grasshoppers in our own sight, and we must have seemed the same to them!”
3014001	Then the whole congregation lifted up their voices and cried out, and that night the people wept.
3014002	All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt, or if only we had died in this wilderness!
3014003	Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and children will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to go back to Egypt?”
3014004	So they said to one another, “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.”
3014005	Then Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel.
3014006	Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes
3014007	and said to the whole congregation of Israel, “The land we passed through and explored is an exceedingly good land.

3014009	Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for they will be like bread for us. Their protection has been removed, and the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them!”
3014010	But the whole congregation threatened to stone Joshua and Caleb. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to all the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting.
3014011	And the LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people treat Me with contempt? How long will they refuse to believe in Me, despite all the signs I have performed among them?

They have already heard that You, O LORD, are in the midst of this people, that You, O LORD, have been seen face to face, that Your cloud stands over them, and that You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
3014015	If You kill this people as one man, the nations who have heard of Your fame will say,

3014020	“I have pardoned them as you requested,” the LORD replied.
3014021	“Yet as surely as I live and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD,
3014022	not one of the men who have seen My glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness—yet have tested Me and disobeyed Me these ten times—
3014023	not one will ever see the land that I swore to give their fathers. None of those who have treated Me with contempt will see it.
3014024	But because My servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed Me wholeheartedly, I will bring him into the land he has entered, and his descendants will inherit it.

3014027	“How long will this wicked congregation grumble against Me? I have heard the complaints that the Israelites are making against Me.
3014028	So tell them: As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly as I heard you say.

3014031	But I will bring your children, whom you said would become plunder, into the land you have rejected—and they will enjoy it.
3014032	As for you, however, your bodies will fall in this wilderness.

3014035	I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will surely do these things to this entire wicked congregation, which has conspired against Me. They will meet their end in the wilderness, and there they will die.”

3014037	those men who had brought out the bad report about the land—were struck down by a plague before the LORD.

3014041	But Moses said, “Why are you transgressing the commandment of the LORD? This will not succeed!

3015001	Then the LORD said to Moses,
3015002	“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: After you enter the land that I am giving you as a home
3015003	and you present a food offering to the LORD from the herd or flock to produce a pleasing aroma to the LORD—either a burnt offering or a sacrifice, for a special vow or freewill offering or appointed feast—
3015004	then the one presenting his offering to the LORD shall also present a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of olive oil.
3015005	With the burnt offering or sacrifice of each lamb, you are to prepare a quarter hin of wine as a drink offering.
3015006	With a ram you are to prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of olive oil,
3015007	and a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
3015008	When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or sacrifice to fulfill a vow or as a peace offering to the LORD,
3015009	present with the bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of olive oil.
3015010	Also present half a hin of wine as a drink offering. It is a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
3015011	This is to be done for each bull, ram, lamb, or goat.
3015012	This is how you must prepare each one, no matter how many.
3015013	Everyone who is native-born shall prepare these things in this way when he presents a food offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
3015014	And for the generations to come, if a foreigner residing with you or someone else among you wants to prepare a food offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD, he is to do exactly as you do.
3015015	The assembly is to have the same statute both for you and for the foreign resident; it is a permanent statute for the generations to come. You and the foreigner shall be the same before the LORD.
3015016	The same law and the same ordinance will apply both to you and to the foreigner residing with you.”
3015017	Then the LORD said to Moses,
3015018	“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land to which I am bringing you
3015019	and you eat the food of the land, you shall lift up an offering to the LORD.
3015020	From the first of your dough, you are to lift up a cake as a contribution; offer it just like an offering from the threshing floor.
3015021	Throughout your generations, you are to give the LORD an offering from the first of your dough.
3015022	Now if you stray unintentionally and do not obey all these commandments that the LORD has spoken to Moses—
3015023	all that the LORD has commanded you through Moses from the day the LORD gave them and continuing through the generations to come—
3015024	and if it was done unintentionally without the knowledge of the congregation, then the whole congregation is to prepare one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and drink offering according to the regulation, and one male goat as a sin offering.
3015025	The priest is to make atonement for the whole congregation of Israel, so that they may be forgiven; for the sin was unintentional and they have brought to the LORD a food offering and a sin offering, presented before the LORD for their unintentional sin.
3015026	Then the whole congregation of Israel and the foreigners residing among them will be forgiven, since it happened to all the people unintentionally.
3015027	Also, if one person sins unintentionally, he is to present a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
3015028	And the priest shall make atonement before the LORD on behalf of the person who erred by sinning unintentionally; and when atonement has been made for him, he will be forgiven.
3015029	You shall have the same law for the one who acts in error, whether he is a native-born Israelite or a foreigner residing among you.
3015030	But the person who sins defiantly, whether a native or foreigner, blasphemes the LORD. That person shall be cut off from among his people.
3015031	He shall certainly be cut off, because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken His commandment; his guilt remains on him.”
3015032	While the Israelites were in the wilderness, a man was found gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
3015033	Those who found the man gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation,
3015034	and because it had not been declared what should be done to him, they placed him in custody.

3015037	And the LORD said to Moses,

3015039	These will serve as tassels for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD, that you may obey them and not prostitute yourselves by following your own heart and your own eyes.
3015040	Then you will remember and obey all My commandments, and you will be holy to your God.
3015041	I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.”
3016001	Now Korah son of Izhar, the son of Kohath son of Levi, along with some Reubenites—Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth—conducted
3016002	a rebellion against Moses, along with 250 men of Israel renowned as leaders of the congregation and representatives in the assembly.

3016010	He has brought you near, you and all your fellow Levites, but you are seeking the priesthood as well.

3016015	Then Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, “Do not regard their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them or mistreated a single one of them.”

3016019	When Korah had gathered his whole assembly against them at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole congregation.
3016020	And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
3016021	“Separate yourselves from this congregation so that I may consume them in an instant.”

3016029	If these men die a natural death, or if they suffer the fate of all men, then the LORD has not sent me.

3016040	just as the LORD commanded him through Moses. This was to be a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should approach to offer incense before the LORD, lest he become like Korah and his followers.
3016041	The next day the whole congregation of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You have killed the LORD’s people!”

3016044	and the LORD said to Moses,

3016047	So Aaron took the censer as Moses had ordered and ran into the midst of the assembly. And seeing that the plague had begun among the people, he offered the incense and made atonement for the people.

3017001	And the LORD said to Moses,

3018002	But bring with you also your brothers from the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, that they may join you and assist you and your sons before the Tent of the Testimony.

3018009	A portion of the most holy offerings reserved from the fire will be yours. From all the offerings they render to Me as most holy offerings, whether grain offerings or sin offerings or guilt offerings, that part belongs to you and your sons.

3018019	All the holy offerings that the Israelites present to the LORD I give to you and to your sons and daughters as a permanent statute. It is a permanent covenant of salt before the LORD for you and your offspring.”
3018020	Then the LORD said to Aaron, “You will have no inheritance in their land, nor will you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.

3018028	So you are to present an offering to the LORD from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites, and from these you are to give the LORD’s offering to Aaron the priest.
3018029	You must present the offering due the LORD from all the best of every gift, the holiest part of it.’
3018030	Therefore say to the Levites, ‘When you have presented the best part, it will be reckoned to you as the produce of the threshing floor or winepress.
3018031	And you and your households may eat the rest of it anywhere; it is the compensation for your work at the Tent of Meeting.

3019001	Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
3019002	“This is the statute of the law that the LORD has commanded: Instruct the Israelites to bring you an unblemished red heifer that has no defect and has never been placed under a yoke.
3019003	Give it to Eleazar the priest, and he will have it brought outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
3019004	Eleazar the priest is to take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tent of Meeting.
3019005	Then the heifer must be burned in his sight. Its hide, its flesh, and its blood are to be burned, along with its dung.
3019006	The priest is to take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet wool and throw them onto the burning heifer.
3019007	Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; after that he may enter the camp, but he will be ceremonially unclean until evening.
3019008	The one who burned the heifer must also wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he too will be ceremonially unclean until evening.
3019009	Then a man who is ceremonially clean is to gather up the ashes of the heifer and store them in a ceremonially clean place outside the camp. They must be kept by the congregation of Israel for preparing the water of purification; this is for purification from sin.
3019010	The man who has gathered up the ashes of the heifer must also wash his clothes, and he will be ceremonially unclean until evening. This is a permanent statute for the Israelites and for the foreigner residing among them.
3019011	Whoever touches any dead body will be unclean for seven days.
3019012	He must purify himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day; then he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third and seventh days, he will not be clean.
3019013	Anyone who touches a human corpse and fails to purify himself defiles the tabernacle of the LORD. That person must be cut off from Israel. He remains unclean, because the water of purification has not been sprinkled on him, and his uncleanness is still on him.
3019014	This is the law when a person dies in a tent: Everyone who enters the tent and everyone already in the tent will be unclean for seven days,
3019015	and any open container without a lid fastened on it is unclean.
3019016	Anyone in the open field who touches someone who has been killed by the sword or has died of natural causes, or anyone who touches a human bone or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
3019017	For the purification of the unclean person, take some of the ashes of the burnt sin offering, put them in a jar, and pour fresh water over them.
3019018	Then a man who is ceremonially clean is to take some hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent, all the furnishings, and the people who were there. He is also to sprinkle the one who touched a bone, a grave, or a person who has died or been slain.
3019019	The man who is ceremonially clean is to sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. After he purifies the unclean person on the seventh day, the one being cleansed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and that evening he will be clean.
3019020	But if a person who is unclean does not purify himself, he will be cut off from the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water of purification has not been sprinkled on him; he is unclean.
3019021	This is a permanent statute for the people: The one who sprinkles the water of purification must wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification will be unclean until evening.
3019022	Anything the unclean person touches will become unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening.”

3029019	Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
3029020	On the third day you are to present eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
3029021	along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
3029022	Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
3029023	On the fourth day you are to present ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
3029024	along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
3029025	Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
3029026	On the fifth day you are to present nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
3029027	along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
3029028	Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
3029029	On the sixth day you are to present eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
3029030	along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
3029031	Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
3029032	On the seventh day you are to present seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
3029033	along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
3029034	Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
3029035	On the eighth day you are to hold a solemn assembly; you must not do any regular work.
3029036	As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present a food offering, a burnt offering of one bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
3029037	along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
3029038	Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
3029039	You are to present these offerings to the LORD at your appointed times, in addition to your vow and freewill offerings, whether burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, or peace offerings.”
3029040	So Moses spoke all this to the Israelites just as the LORD had commanded him.
3030001	Then Moses said to the heads of the tribes of Israel, “This is what the LORD has commanded:
3030002	If a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath to obligate himself by a pledge, he must not break his word; he must do everything he has promised.
3030003	And if a woman in her father’s house during her youth makes a vow to the LORD or obligates herself by a pledge,
3030004	and her father hears about her vow or pledge but says nothing to her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.
3030005	But if her father prohibits her on the day he hears about it, then none of the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand. The LORD will absolve her because her father has prohibited her.
3030006	If a woman marries while under a vow or rash promise by which she has bound herself,
3030007	and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her on that day, then the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.
3030008	But if her husband prohibits her when he hears of it, he nullifies the vow that binds her or the rash promise she has made, and the LORD will absolve her.
3030009	Every vow a widow or divorced woman pledges to fulfill is binding on her.
3030010	If a woman in her husband’s house has made a vow or put herself under an obligation with an oath,
3030011	and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her and does not prohibit her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.
3030012	But if her husband nullifies them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether her vows or pledges, shall stand. Her husband has nullified them, and the LORD will absolve her.
3030013	Her husband may confirm or nullify any vow or any sworn pledge to deny herself.
3030014	But if her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he confirms all the vows and pledges that bind her. He has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard about them.
3030015	But if he nullifies them after he hears of them, then he will bear her iniquity.”
3030016	These are the statutes that the LORD commanded Moses concerning the relationship between a man and his wife, and between a father and a young daughter still in his home.

3031044	36,000 cattle,

3035001	Again the LORD spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho:
3035002	“Command the Israelites to give, from the inheritance they will possess, cities for the Levites to live in and pasturelands around the cities.
3035003	The cities will be for them to live in, and the pasturelands will be for their herds, their flocks, and all their other livestock.
3035004	The pasturelands around the cities you are to give the Levites will extend a thousand cubits from the wall on every side.
3035005	You are also to measure two thousand cubits outside the city on the east, two thousand on the south, two thousand on the west, and two thousand on the north, with the city in the center. These areas will serve as larger pasturelands for the cities.
3035006	Six of the cities you give the Levites are to be appointed as cities of refuge, to which a manslayer may flee. In addition to these, give the Levites forty-two other cities.
3035007	The total number of cities you give the Levites will be forty-eight, with their corresponding pasturelands.
3035008	The cities that you apportion from the territory of the Israelites should be given to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance of each tribe: more from a larger tribe and less from a smaller one.”
3035009	Then the LORD said to Moses,
3035010	“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
3035011	designate cities to serve as your cities of refuge, so that a person who kills someone unintentionally may flee there.
3035012	You are to have these cities as a refuge from the avenger, so that the manslayer will not die until he stands trial before the assembly.
3035013	The cities you select will be your six cities of refuge.
3035014	Select three cities across the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan as cities of refuge.
3035015	These six cities will serve as a refuge for the Israelites and for the foreigner or stranger among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
3035016	If, however, anyone strikes a person with an iron object and kills him, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death.
3035017	Or if anyone has in his hand a stone of deadly size, and he strikes and kills another, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death.
3035018	If anyone has in his hand a deadly object of wood, and he strikes and kills another, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death.
3035019	The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death; when he finds him, he is to kill him.
3035020	Likewise, if anyone maliciously pushes another or intentionally throws an object at him and kills him,
3035021	or if in hostility he strikes him with his hand and he dies, the one who struck him must surely be put to death; he is a murderer. When the avenger of blood finds the murderer, he is to kill him.
3035022	But if anyone pushes a person suddenly, without hostility, or throws an object at him unintentionally,
3035023	or without looking drops a heavy stone that kills him, but he was not an enemy and did not intend to harm him,
3035024	then the congregation must judge between the slayer and the avenger of blood according to these ordinances.
3035025	The assembly is to protect the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood. Then the assembly will return him to the city of refuge to which he fled, and he must live there until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.
3035026	But if the manslayer ever goes outside the limits of the city of refuge to which he fled
3035027	and the avenger of blood finds him outside of his city of refuge and kills him, then the avenger will not be guilty of bloodshed,
3035028	because the manslayer must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. Only after the death of the high priest may he return to the land he owns.
3035029	This will be a statutory ordinance for you for the generations to come, wherever you live.
3035030	If anyone kills a person, the murderer is to be put to death on the testimony of the witnesses. But no one is to be put to death based on the testimony of a lone witness.
3035031	You are not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die; he must surely be put to death.
3035032	Nor should you accept a ransom for the person who flees to a city of refuge and allow him to return and live on his own land before the death of the high priest.
3035033	Do not pollute the land where you live, for bloodshed pollutes the land, and no atonement can be made for the land on which the blood is shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
3035034	Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell. For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.”
3036001	Now the family heads of the clan of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, one of the clans of Joseph, approached Moses and the leaders who were the heads of the Israelite families and addressed them,
3036002	saying, “When the LORD commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance to the Israelites by lot, He also commanded him to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.
