4014021	You are not to eat any carcass; you may give it to the foreigner residing within your gates, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner. For you are a holy people belonging to the LORD your God. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
4014022	You must be sure to set aside a tenth of all the produce brought forth each year from your fields.
4014023	And you are to eat a tenth of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the LORD your God at the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always.
4014024	But if the distance is too great for you to carry that with which the LORD your God has blessed you, because the place where the LORD your God will choose to put His Name is too far away,
4014025	then exchange it for money, take the money in your hand, and go to the place the LORD your God will choose.
4014026	Then you may spend the money on anything you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or anything you wish. You are to feast there in the presence of the LORD your God and rejoice with your household.
4014027	And do not neglect the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.
4014028	At the end of every three years, bring a tenth of all your produce for that year and lay it up within your gates.
4014029	Then the Levite (because he has no portion or inheritance among you), the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow within your gates may come and eat and be satisfied. And the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands.
4015001	At the end of every seven years you must cancel debts.
4015002	This is the manner of remission: Every creditor shall cancel what he has loaned to his neighbor. He is not to collect anything from his neighbor or brother, because the LORD’s time of release has been proclaimed.
4015003	You may collect something from a foreigner, but you must forgive whatever your brother owes you.
4015004	There will be no poor among you, however, because the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess as an inheritance,
4015005	if only you obey the LORD your God and are careful to follow all these commandments I am giving you today.
4015006	When the LORD your God blesses you as He has promised, you will lend to many nations but borrow from none; you will rule over many nations but be ruled by none.
4015007	If there is a poor man among your brothers within any of the gates in the land that the LORD your God is giving you, then you are not to harden your heart or shut your hand from your poor brother.
4015008	Instead, you are to open your hand to him and freely loan him whatever he needs.
4015009	Be careful not to harbor this wicked thought in your heart: “The seventh year, the year of release, is near,” so that you look upon your poor brother begrudgingly and give him nothing. He will cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
4015010	Give generously to him, and do not let your heart be grieved when you do so. And because of this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything to which you put your hand.
4015011	For there will never cease to be poor in the land; that is why I am commanding you to open wide your hand to your brother and to the poor and needy in your land.
4015012	If a fellow Hebrew, a man or a woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, then in the seventh year you must set him free.
4015013	And when you release him, do not send him away empty-handed.
4015014	You are to furnish him liberally from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. You shall give to him as the LORD your God has blessed you.
4015015	Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you; that is why I am giving you this command today.
4015016	But if your servant says to you, ‘I do not want to leave you,’ because he loves you and your household and is well off with you,
4015017	then take an awl and pierce it through his ear into the door, and he will become your servant for life. And treat your maidservant the same way.
4015018	Do not regard it as a hardship to set your servant free, because his six years of service were worth twice the wages of a hired hand. And the LORD your God will bless you in all you do.
4015019	You must set apart to the LORD your God every firstborn male produced by your herds and flocks. You are not to put the firstborn of your oxen to work, nor are you to shear the firstborn of your flock.
4015020	Each year you and your household are to eat it before the LORD your God in the place the LORD will choose.
4015021	But if an animal has a defect, is lame or blind, or has any serious flaw, you must not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
4015022	Eat it within your gates; both the ceremonially unclean and clean may eat it as they would a gazelle or a deer.
4015023	But you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.
4016001	Observe the month of Abib and celebrate the Passover to the LORD your God, because in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
4016002	You are to offer to the LORD your God the Passover sacrifice from the herd or flock in the place the LORD will choose as a dwelling for His Name.
4016003	You must not eat leavened bread with it; for seven days you are to eat with it unleavened bread, the bread of affliction, because you left the land of Egypt in haste—so that you may remember for the rest of your life the day you left the land of Egypt.
4016004	No leaven is to be found in all your land for seven days, and none of the meat you sacrifice in the evening of the first day shall remain until morning.
4016005	You are not to sacrifice the Passover animal in any of the towns that the LORD your God is giving you.
4016006	You must only offer the Passover sacrifice at the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for His Name. Do this in the evening as the sun sets, at the same time you departed from Egypt.
4016007	And you shall roast it and eat it in the place the LORD your God will choose, and in the morning you shall return to your tents.
4016008	For six days you must eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day you shall hold a solemn assembly to the LORD your God, and you must not do any work.
4016009	You are to count off seven weeks from the time you first put the sickle to the standing grain.
4016010	And you shall celebrate the Feast of Weeks to the LORD your God with a freewill offering that you give in proportion to how the LORD your God has blessed you,
4016011	and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God in the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name—you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levite within your gates, as well as the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widows among you.
4016012	Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and carefully follow these statutes.
4016013	You are to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days after you have gathered the produce of your threshing floor and your winepress.
4016014	And you shall rejoice in your feast—you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levite, as well as the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widows among you.
4016015	For seven days you shall celebrate a feast to the LORD your God in the place He will choose, because the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, so that your joy will be complete.
4016016	Three times a year all your men are to appear before the LORD your God in the place He will choose: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles. No one should appear before the LORD empty-handed.
4016017	Everyone must appear with a gift as he is able, according to the blessing the LORD your God has given you.
4016018	You are to appoint judges and officials for your tribes in every town that the LORD your God is giving you. They are to judge the people with righteous judgment.
4016019	Do not deny justice or show partiality. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
4016020	Pursue justice, and justice alone, so that you may live, and you may possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
4016021	Do not set up any wooden Asherah pole next to the altar you will build for the LORD your God,
4016022	and do not set up for yourselves a sacred pillar, which the LORD your God hates.
4017001	You shall not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep with any defect or serious flaw, for that is detestable to the LORD your God.
4017002	If a man or woman among you in one of the towns that the LORD your God gives you is found doing evil in the sight of the LORD your God by transgressing His covenant
4017003	and going to worship other gods, bowing down to them or to the sun or moon or any of the host of heaven—which I have forbidden—
4017004	and if it is reported and you hear about it, you must investigate it thoroughly. If the report is true and such an abomination has happened in Israel,
4017005	you must bring out to your gates the man or woman who has done this evil thing, and you must stone that person to death.
4017006	On the testimony of two or three witnesses a man shall be put to death, but he shall not be executed on the testimony of a lone witness.
4017007	The hands of the witnesses shall be the first in putting him to death, and after that, the hands of all the people. So you must purge the evil from among you.
4017008	If a case is too difficult for you to judge, whether the controversy within your gates is regarding bloodshed, lawsuits, or assaults, you must go up to the place the LORD your God will choose.
4017009	You are to go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who presides at that time. Inquire of them, and they will give you a verdict in the case.
4017010	You must abide by the verdict they give you at the place the LORD will choose. Be careful to do everything they instruct you,
4017011	according to the terms of law they give and the verdict they proclaim. Do not turn aside to the right or to the left from the decision they declare to you.
4017012	But the man who acts presumptuously, refusing to listen either to the priest who stands there to serve the LORD your God, or to the judge, must be put to death. You must purge the evil from Israel.
4017013	Then all the people will hear and be afraid, and will no longer behave arrogantly.
4017014	When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you and have taken possession of it and settled in it, and you say, “Let us set a king over us like all the nations around us,”
4017015	you are to appoint over yourselves the king whom the LORD your God shall choose. Appoint a king from among your brothers; you are not to set over yourselves a foreigner who is not one of your brothers.
4017016	But the king must not acquire many horses for himself or send the people back to Egypt to acquire more horses, for the LORD has said, ‘You are never to go back that way again.’
4017017	He must not take many wives for himself, lest his heart go astray. He must not accumulate for himself large amounts of silver and gold.
4017018	When he is seated on his royal throne, he must write for himself a copy of this instruction on a scroll in the presence of the Levitical priests.
4017019	It is to remain with him, and he is to read from it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God by carefully observing all the words of this instruction and these statutes.
4017020	Then his heart will not be exalted above his countrymen, and he will not turn aside from the commandment, to the right or to the left, in order that he and his sons may reign many years over his kingdom in Israel.
4018001	The Levitical priests—indeed the whole tribe of Levi—shall have no portion or inheritance with Israel. They are to eat the food offerings to the LORD; that is their inheritance.
4018002	Although they have no inheritance among their brothers, the LORD is their inheritance, as He promised them.
4018003	This shall be the priests’ share from the people who offer a sacrifice, whether a bull or a sheep: the priests are to be given the shoulder, the jowls, and the stomach.
4018004	You are to give them the firstfruits of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the first wool sheared from your flock.
4018005	For the LORD your God has chosen Levi and his sons out of all your tribes to stand and minister in His name for all time.
4018006	Now if a Levite moves from any town of residence throughout Israel and comes in all earnestness to the place the LORD will choose,
4018007	then he shall serve in the name of the LORD his God like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
4018008	They shall eat equal portions, even though he has received money from the sale of his father’s estate.
4018009	When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, do not imitate the detestable ways of the nations there.
4018010	Let no one be found among you who sacrifices his son or daughter in the fire, practices divination or conjury, interprets omens, practices sorcery,
4018011	casts spells, consults a medium or spiritist, or inquires of the dead.
4018012	For whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD. And because of these detestable things, the LORD your God is driving out the nations before you.
4018013	You must be blameless before the LORD your God.
4018014	Though these nations, which you will dispossess, listen to conjurers and diviners, the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.
4018015	The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to him.
4018016	This is what you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, “Let us not hear the voice of the LORD our God or see this great fire anymore, so that we will not die!”
4018017	Then the LORD said to me, “They have spoken well.
4018018	I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put My words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
4018019	And I will hold accountable anyone who does not listen to My words that the prophet speaks in My name.
4018020	But if any prophet dares to speak a message in My name that I have not commanded him to speak, or to speak in the name of other gods, that prophet must be put to death.”
4018021	You may ask in your heart, “How can we recognize a message that the LORD has not spoken?”
4018022	When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the message does not come to pass or come true, that is a message the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.
4019001	When the LORD your God has cut off the nations whose land He is giving you, and when you have driven them out and settled in their cities and houses,
4019002	then you are to set apart for yourselves three cities within the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
4019003	You are to build roads for yourselves and divide into three regions the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that any manslayer can flee to these cities.
4019004	Now this is the situation regarding the manslayer who flees to one of these cities to save his life, having killed his neighbor accidentally, without intending to harm him:
4019005	If he goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut timber and swings his axe to chop down a tree, but the blade flies off the handle and strikes and kills his neighbor, he may flee to one of these cities to save his life.
4019006	Otherwise, the avenger of blood might pursue the manslayer in a rage, overtake him if the distance is great, and strike him dead though he did not deserve to die, since he did not intend any harm.
4019007	This is why I am commanding you to set apart for yourselves three cities.
4019008	And if the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as He swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land He promised them,
4019009	and if you carefully keep all these commandments I am giving you today, loving the LORD your God and walking in His ways at all times, then you are to add three more cities to these three.
4019010	Thus innocent blood will not be shed in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that you will not be guilty of bloodshed.
4019011	If, however, a man hates his neighbor and lies in wait, attacks him and kills him, and then flees to one of these cities,
4019012	the elders of his city must send for him, bring him back, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to die.
4019013	You must show him no pity. You are to purge from Israel the guilt of shedding innocent blood, that it may go well with you.
4019014	You must not move your neighbor’s boundary marker, which was set up by your ancestors to mark the inheritance you shall receive in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
4019015	A lone witness is not sufficient to establish any wrongdoing or sin against a man, regardless of what offense he may have committed. A matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
4019016	If a false witness testifies against someone, accusing him of a crime,
4019017	both parties to the dispute must stand in the presence of the LORD, before the priests and judges who are in office at that time.
4019018	The judges shall investigate thoroughly, and if the witness is proven to be a liar who has falsely accused his brother,
4019019	you must do to him as he intended to do to his brother. So you must purge the evil from among you.
4019020	Then the rest of the people will hear and be afraid, and they will never again do anything so evil among you.
4019021	You must show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, and foot for foot.
4020001	When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses, chariots, and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them; for the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, is with you.
4020002	When you are about to go into battle, the priest is to come forward and address the army,
4020003	saying to them, “Hear, O Israel, today you are going into battle with your enemies. Do not be fainthearted or afraid; do not be alarmed or terrified because of them.
4020004	For the LORD your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies, to give you the victory.”
4020005	Furthermore, the officers are to address the army, saying, “Has any man built a new house and not dedicated it? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man dedicate it.
4020006	Has any man planted a vineyard and not begun to enjoy its fruit? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man enjoy its fruit.
4020007	Has any man become pledged to a woman and not married her? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man marry her.”
4020008	Then the officers shall speak further to the army, saying, “Is any man afraid or fainthearted? Let him return home, so that the hearts of his brothers will not melt like his own.”
4020009	When the officers have finished addressing the army, they are to appoint commanders to lead it.
4020010	When you approach a city to fight against it, you are to make an offer of peace.
4020011	If they accept your offer of peace and open their gates, all the people there will become forced laborers to serve you.
4020012	But if they refuse to make peace with you and wage war against you, lay siege to that city.
4020013	When the LORD your God has delivered it into your hand, you must put every male to the sword.
4020014	But the women, children, livestock, and whatever else is in the city—all its spoil—you may take as plunder, and you shall use the spoil of your enemies that the LORD your God gives you.
4020015	This is how you are to treat all the cities that are far away from you and do not belong to the nations nearby.
4020016	However, in the cities of the nations that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you must not leave alive anything that breathes.
4020017	For you must devote them to complete destruction —the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—as the LORD your God has commanded you,
4020018	so that they cannot teach you to do all the detestable things they do for their gods, and so cause you to sin against the LORD your God.
4020019	When you lay siege to a city for an extended time while fighting against it to capture it, you must not destroy its trees by putting an axe to them, because you can eat their fruit. You must not cut them down. Are the trees of the field human, that you should besiege them?
4020020	But you may destroy the trees that you know do not produce fruit. Use them to build siege works against the city that is waging war against you, until it falls.
4021001	If one is found slain, lying in a field in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess, and it is not known who killed him,
4021002	your elders and judges must come out and measure the distance from the victim to the neighboring cities.
4021003	Then the elders of the city nearest the victim shall take a heifer that has never been yoked or used for work,
4021004	bring the heifer to a valley with running water that has not been plowed or sown, and break its neck there by the stream.
4021005	And the priests, the sons of Levi, shall come forward, for the LORD your God has chosen them to serve Him and pronounce blessings in His name and to give a ruling in every dispute and case of assault.
4021006	Then all the elders of the city nearest the victim shall wash their hands by the stream over the heifer whose neck has been broken,
4021007	and they shall declare, “Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see it.
4021008	Accept this atonement, O LORD, for Your people Israel whom You have redeemed, and do not hold the shedding of innocent blood against them.” And the bloodshed will be atoned for.
4021009	So you shall purge from among you the guilt of shedding innocent blood, since you have done what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
4021010	When you go to war against your enemies and the LORD your God delivers them into your hand and you take them captive,
4021011	if you see a beautiful woman among them, and you desire her and want to take her as your wife,
4021012	then you shall bring her into your house. She must shave her head, trim her nails,
4021013	and put aside the clothing of her captivity. After she has lived in your house a full month and mourned her father and mother, you may have relations with her and be her husband, and she shall be your wife.
4021014	And if you are not pleased with her, you are to let her go wherever she wishes. But you must not sell her for money or treat her as a slave, since you have dishonored her.
4021015	If a man has two wives, one beloved and the other unloved, and both bear him sons, but the unloved wife has the firstborn son,
4021016	when that man assigns his inheritance to his sons he must not appoint the son of the beloved wife as the firstborn over the son of the unloved wife.
4021017	Instead, he must acknowledge the firstborn, the son of his unloved wife, by giving him a double portion of all that he has. For that son is the firstfruits of his father’s strength; the right of the firstborn belongs to him.
4021018	If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who does not obey his father and mother and does not listen to them when disciplined,
4021019	his father and mother are to lay hold of him and bring him to the elders of his city, to the gate of his hometown,
4021020	and say to the elders, “This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he does not obey us. He is a glutton and a drunkard.”
4021021	Then all the men of his city will stone him to death. So you must purge the evil from among you, and all Israel will hear and be afraid.
4021022	If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is executed, and you hang his body on a tree,
4021023	you must not leave the body on the tree overnight, but you must be sure to bury him that day, because anyone who is hung on a tree is under God’s curse. You must not defile the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
4022001	If you see your brother’s ox or sheep straying, you must not ignore it; be sure to return it to your brother.
4022002	If your brother does not live near you, or if you do not know who he is, you are to take the animal home to remain with you until your brother comes seeking it; then you can return it to him.
4022003	And you shall do the same for his donkey, his cloak, or anything your brother has lost and you have found. You must not ignore it.
4022004	If you see your brother’s donkey or ox fallen on the road, you must not ignore it; you must help him lift it up.
4022005	A woman must not wear men’s clothing, and a man must not wear women’s clothing, for whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD your God.
4022006	If you come across a bird’s nest with chicks or eggs, either in a tree or on the ground along the road, and the mother is sitting on the chicks or eggs, you must not take the mother along with the young.
4022007	You may take the young, but be sure to let the mother go, so that it may be well with you and that you may prolong your days.
4022008	If you build a new house, you are to construct a railing around your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if someone falls from it.
4022009	Do not plant your vineyard with two types of seed; if you do, the entire harvest will be defiled —both the crop you plant and the fruit of your vineyard.
4022010	Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.
4022011	Do not wear clothes of wool and linen woven together.
4022012	You are to make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear.
4022013	Suppose a man marries a woman, has relations with her, and comes to hate her,
4022014	and he then accuses her of shameful conduct and gives her a bad name, saying, “I married this woman and had relations with her, but I discovered she was not a virgin.”
4022015	Then the young woman’s father and mother shall bring the proof of her virginity to the city elders at the gate
4022016	and say to the elders, “I gave my daughter in marriage to this man, but he has come to hate her.
4022017	And now he has accused her of shameful conduct, saying, ‘I discovered that your daughter was not a virgin.’ But here is the proof of her virginity.” And they shall spread out the cloth before the city elders.
4022018	Then the elders of that city shall take the man and punish him.
4022019	They are also to fine him a hundred shekels of silver and give them to the young woman’s father, because this man has given a virgin of Israel a bad name. And she shall remain his wife; he must not divorce her as long as he lives.
4022020	If, however, this accusation is true, and no proof of the young woman’s virginity can be found,
4022021	she shall be brought to the door of her father’s house, and there the men of her city will stone her to death. For she has committed an outrage in Israel by being promiscuous in her father’s house. So you must purge the evil from among you.
4022022	If a man is found lying with another man’s wife, both the man who slept with her and the woman must die. You must purge the evil from Israel.
4022023	If there is a virgin pledged in marriage to a man, and another man encounters her in the city and sleeps with her,
4022024	you must take both of them out to the gate of that city and stone them to death—the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he has violated his neighbor’s wife. So you must purge the evil from among you.
4022025	But if the man encounters a betrothed woman in the open country, and he overpowers her and lies with her, only the man who has done this must die.
4022026	Do nothing to the young woman, because she has committed no sin worthy of death. This case is just like one in which a man attacks his neighbor and murders him.
4022027	When he found her in the field, the betrothed woman cried out, but there was no one to save her.
4022028	If a man encounters a virgin who is not pledged in marriage, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are discovered,
4022029	then the man who lay with her must pay the young woman’s father fifty shekels of silver, and she must become his wife because he has violated her. He must not divorce her as long as he lives.
4022030	A man is not to marry his father’s wife, so that he will not dishonor his father’s marriage bed.
4023001	No man with crushed or severed genitals may enter the assembly of the LORD.
4023002	No one of illegitimate birth may enter the assembly of the LORD, nor may any of his descendants, even to the tenth generation.
4023003	No Ammonite or Moabite or any of their descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD, even to the tenth generation.
4023004	For they did not meet you with food and water on your way out of Egypt, and they hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram-naharaim to curse you.
4023005	Yet the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam, and the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loves you.
4023006	You are not to seek peace or prosperity from them as long as you live.
4023007	Do not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother. Do not despise an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.
4023008	The third generation of children born to them may enter the assembly of the LORD.
4023009	When you are encamped against your enemies, then you shall keep yourself from every wicked thing.
4023010	If any man among you becomes unclean because of a nocturnal emission, he must leave the camp and stay outside.
4023011	When evening approaches, he must wash with water, and when the sun sets he may return to the camp.
4023012	You must have a place outside the camp to go and relieve yourself.
4023013	And you must have a digging tool in your equipment so that when you relieve yourself you can dig a hole and cover up your excrement.
4023014	For the LORD your God walks throughout your camp to protect you and deliver your enemies to you. Your camp must be holy, lest He see anything unclean among you and turn away from you.
4023015	Do not return a slave to his master if he has taken refuge with you.
4023016	Let him live among you wherever he chooses, in the town of his pleasing. Do not oppress him.
4023017	No daughter or son of Israel is to be a shrine prostitute.
4023018	You must not bring the wages of a prostitute, whether female or male, into the house of the LORD your God to fulfill any vow, because both are detestable to the LORD your God.
4023019	Do not charge your brother interest on money, food, or any other type of loan.
4023020	You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your brother, so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything to which you put your hand in the land that you are entering to possess.
4023021	If you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not be slow to keep it, because He will surely require it of you, and you will be guilty of sin.
4023022	But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.
4023023	Be careful to follow through on what comes from your lips, because you have freely vowed to the LORD your God with your own mouth.
4023024	When you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat your fill of grapes, but you must not put any in your basket.
4023025	When you enter your neighbor’s grainfield, you may pluck the heads of grain with your hand, but you must not put a sickle to your neighbor’s grain.
4024001	If a man marries a woman, but she becomes displeasing to him because he finds some indecency in her, he may write her a certificate of divorce, hand it to her, and send her away from his house.
4024002	If, after leaving his house, she goes and becomes another man’s wife,
4024003	and the second man hates her, writes her a certificate of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house, or if he dies,
4024004	then the husband who divorced her first may not remarry her after she has been defiled, for that is an abomination to the LORD. You must not bring sin upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
4024005	If a man is newly married, he must not be sent to war or be pressed into any duty. For one year he is free to stay at home and bring joy to the wife he has married.
4024006	Do not take a pair of millstones or even an upper millstone as security for a debt, because that would be taking one’s livelihood as security.
4024007	If a man is caught kidnapping one of his Israelite brothers, whether he treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must die. So you must purge the evil from among you.
4024008	In cases of infectious skin diseases, be careful to diligently follow everything the Levitical priests instruct you. Be careful to do as I have commanded them.
4024009	Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the journey after you came out of Egypt.
4024010	When you lend anything to your neighbor, do not enter his house to collect security.
4024011	You are to stand outside while the man to whom you are lending brings the security out to you.
4024012	If he is a poor man, you must not go to sleep with the security in your possession;
4024013	be sure to return it to him by sunset, so that he may sleep in his own cloak and bless you, and this will be credited to you as righteousness before the LORD your God.
4024014	Do not oppress a hired hand who is poor and needy, whether he is a brother or a foreigner residing in one of your towns.
4024015	You are to pay his wages each day before sunset, because he is poor and depends on them. Otherwise he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
4024016	Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.
4024017	Do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless, and do not take a widow’s cloak as security.
4024018	Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from that place. Therefore I am commanding you to do this.
4024019	If you are harvesting in your field and forget a sheaf there, do not go back to get it. It is to be left for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
4024020	When you beat the olives from your trees, you must not go over the branches again. What remains will be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
4024021	When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you must not go over the vines again. What remains will be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
4024022	Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. Therefore I am commanding you to do this.
4025001	If there is a dispute between men, they are to go to court to be judged, so that the innocent may be acquitted and the guilty condemned.
4025002	If the guilty man deserves to be beaten, the judge shall have him lie down and be flogged in his presence with the number of lashes his crime warrants.
4025003	He may receive no more than forty lashes, lest your brother be beaten any more than that and be degraded in your sight.
4025004	Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.
4025005	When brothers dwell together and one of them dies without a son, the widow must not marry outside the family. Her husband’s brother is to take her as his wife and fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law for her.
4025006	The first son she bears will carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name will not be blotted out from Israel.
4025007	But if the man does not want to marry his brother’s widow, she is to go to the elders at the city gate and say, “My husband’s brother refuses to preserve his brother’s name in Israel. He is not willing to perform the duty of a brother-in-law for me.”
4025008	Then the elders of his city shall summon him and speak with him. If he persists and says, “I do not want to marry her,”

4025015	You must maintain accurate and honest weights and measures, so that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.

5005014	“Neither,” He replied. “I have now come as Commander of the LORD’s army.” Then Joshua fell facedown in reverence and asked Him, “What does my Lord have to say to His servant?”
5005015	The Commander of the LORD’s army replied, “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy.” And Joshua did so.
5006001	Now Jericho was tightly shut up because of the Israelites. No one went out and no one came in.
5006002	And the LORD said to Joshua, “Behold, I have delivered Jericho into your hand, along with its king and its mighty men of valor.
5006003	March around the city with all the men of war, circling the city one time. Do this for six days.
5006004	Have seven priests carry seven rams’ horns in front of the ark. Then on the seventh day, march around the city seven times, while the priests blow the horns.
5006005	And when there is a long blast of the ram’s horn and you hear its sound, have all the people give a mighty shout. Then the wall of the city will collapse and all your people will charge straight into the city.”
5006006	So Joshua son of Nun summoned the priests and said, “Take up the ark of the covenant and have seven priests carry seven rams’ horns in front of the ark of the LORD.”
5006007	And he told the people, “Advance and march around the city, with the armed troops going ahead of the ark of the LORD.”
5006008	After Joshua had spoken to the people, seven priests carrying seven rams’ horns before the LORD advanced and blew the horns, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD followed them.
5006009	While the horns continued to sound, the armed troops marched ahead of the priests who blew the horns, and the rear guard followed the ark.
5006010	But Joshua had commanded the people: “Do not give a battle cry or let your voice be heard; do not let one word come out of your mouth until the day I tell you to shout. Then you are to shout!”
5006011	So he had the ark of the LORD carried around the city, circling it once. And the people returned to the camp and spent the night there.
5006012	Joshua got up early the next morning, and the priests took the ark of the LORD.
5006013	And the seven priests carrying seven rams’ horns kept marching ahead of the ark of the LORD and blowing the horns. The armed troops went in front of them and the rear guard followed the ark of the LORD, while the horns kept sounding.
5006014	So on the second day they marched around the city once and returned to the camp. They did this for six days.
5006015	Then on the seventh day, they got up at dawn and marched around the city seven times in the same manner. That was the only day they circled the city seven times.
5006016	After the seventh time around, the priests blew the horns, and Joshua commanded the people, “Shout! For the LORD has given you the city!
5006017	Now the city and everything in it must be devoted to the LORD for destruction. Only Rahab the prostitute and all those with her in her house will live, because she hid the spies we sent.
5006018	But keep away from the things devoted to destruction, lest you yourself be set apart for destruction. If you take any of these, you will set apart the camp of Israel for destruction and bring disaster upon it.
5006019	For all the silver and gold and all the articles of bronze and iron are holy to the LORD; they must go into His treasury.”
5006020	So when the rams’ horns sounded, the people shouted. When they heard the blast of the horn, the people gave a great shout, and the wall collapsed. Then all the people charged straight into the city and captured it.
5006021	With the edge of the sword they devoted to destruction everything in the city—man and woman, young and old, oxen, sheep, and donkeys.
5006022	Meanwhile, Joshua told the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the house of the prostitute and bring out the woman and all who are with her, just as you promised her.”
5006023	So the young spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father and mother and brothers, and all who belonged to her. They brought out her whole family and settled them outside the camp of Israel.
5006024	Then the Israelites burned up the city and everything in it. However, they put the silver and gold and articles of bronze and iron into the treasury of the LORD’s house.
5006025	And Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, with her father’s household and all who belonged to her, because she hid the men Joshua had sent to spy out Jericho. So she has lived among the Israelites to this day.
5006026	At that time Joshua invoked this solemn oath: “Cursed before the LORD is the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Jericho; at the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundations; at the cost of his youngest he will set up its gates.”
5006027	So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout the land.
5007001	The Israelites, however, acted unfaithfully regarding the things devoted to destruction. Achan son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was set apart. So the anger of the LORD burned against the Israelites.
5007002	Meanwhile, Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Beth-aven to the east of Bethel, and told them, “Go up and spy out the land.” So the men went up and spied out Ai.
5007003	On returning to Joshua, they reported, “There is no need to send all the people; two or three thousand men are enough to go up and attack Ai. Since the people of Ai are so few, you need not wear out all our people there.”
5007004	So about three thousand men went up, but they fled before the men of Ai.
5007005	And the men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them, chasing them from the gate as far as the quarries and striking them down on the slopes. So the hearts of the people melted and became like water.
5007006	Then Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown before the ark of the LORD until evening, as did the elders of Israel; and they all sprinkled dust on their heads.
5007007	“O, Lord GOD,” Joshua said, “why did You ever bring this people across the Jordan to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites to be destroyed? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!
5007008	O Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned its back and run from its enemies?
5007009	When the Canaanites and all who live in the land hear about this, they will surround us and wipe out our name from the earth. Then what will You do for Your great name?”
5007010	But the LORD said to Joshua, “Stand up! Why have you fallen on your face?
5007011	Israel has sinned; they have transgressed My covenant that I commanded them, and they have taken some of what was devoted to destruction. Indeed, they have stolen and lied, and they have put these things with their own possessions.
5007012	This is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They will turn their backs and run from their enemies, because they themselves have been set apart for destruction. I will no longer be with you unless you remove from among you whatever is devoted to destruction.
5007013	Get up and consecrate the people, saying, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Among you, O Israel, there are things devoted to destruction. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove them.
5007014	In the morning you must present yourselves tribe by tribe. The tribe that the LORD selects shall come forward clan by clan, and the clan that the LORD selects shall come forward family by family, and the family that the LORD selects shall come forward man by man.
5007015	The one who is caught with the things devoted to destruction must be burned, along with all that belongs to him, because he has transgressed the covenant of the LORD and committed an outrage in Israel.’”
5007016	So Joshua arose early the next morning and had Israel come forward tribe by tribe, and the tribe of Judah was selected.
5007017	He had the clans of Judah come forward, and the clan of the Zerahites was selected. He had the clan of the Zerahites come forward, and the family of Zabdi was selected.
5007018	And he had the family of Zabdi come forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was selected.
5007019	So Joshua said to Achan, “My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and make a confession to Him. I urge you to tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me.”
5007020	“It is true,” Achan replied, “I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did:
5007021	When I saw among the spoils a beautiful cloak from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels, I coveted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath.”
5007022	So Joshua sent messengers who ran to the tent, and there it all was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.
5007023	They took the things from inside the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and spread them out before the LORD.
5007024	Then Joshua, together with all Israel, took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the cloak, the bar of gold, his sons and daughters, his oxen and donkeys and sheep, his tent, and everything else he owned, and brought them to the Valley of Achor.
5007025	“Why have you brought this trouble upon us?” said Joshua. “Today the LORD will bring trouble upon you!” And all Israel stoned him to death. Then they stoned the others and burned their bodies.
5007026	And they heaped over Achan a large pile of rocks that remains to this day. So the LORD turned from His burning anger. Therefore that place is called the Valley of Achor to this day.
5008001	Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid or discouraged. Take the whole army with you, and go up and attack Ai. See, I have delivered into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.
5008002	And you shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that you may carry off their plunder and livestock for yourselves. Set up an ambush behind the city.”
5008003	So Joshua and the whole army set out to attack Ai. Joshua chose 30,000 mighty men of valor and sent them out at night
5008004	with these orders: “Pay attention. You are to lie in ambush behind the city, not too far from it. All of you must be ready.
5008005	Then I and all the troops with me will advance on the city. When they come out against us as they did the first time, we will flee from them.
5008006	They will pursue us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, ‘The Israelites are running away from us as they did before.’ So as we flee from them,
5008007	you are to rise from the ambush and seize the city, for the LORD your God will deliver it into your hand.
5008008	And when you have taken the city, set it on fire. Do as the LORD has commanded! See, I have given you orders.”
5008009	So Joshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush and lay in wait between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night among the people.
5008010	Joshua got up early the next morning and mobilized his men, and he and the elders of Israel marched before them up to Ai.
5008011	Then all the troops who were with him marched up and approached the city. They arrived in front of Ai and camped to the north of it, with the valley between them and the city.
5008012	Now Joshua had taken about five thousand men and set up an ambush between Bethel and Ai, to the west of the city.
5008013	So the forces were stationed with the main camp to the north of the city and the rear guard to the west of the city. And that night Joshua went into the valley.
5008014	When the king of Ai saw the Israelites, he hurried out early in the morning with the men of the city to engage them in battle at an appointed place overlooking the Arabah. But he did not know that an ambush had been set up against him behind the city.
5008015	Joshua and all Israel let themselves be beaten back before them, and they fled toward the wilderness.
5008016	Then all the men of Ai were summoned to pursue them, and they followed Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
5008017	Not a man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel, leaving the city wide open while they pursued Israel.
5008018	Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Hold out your battle lance toward Ai, for into your hand I will deliver the city.” So Joshua held out his battle lance toward Ai,
5008019	and as soon as he did so, the men in ambush rose quickly from their position. They rushed forward, entered the city, captured it, and immediately set it on fire.
5008020	When the men of Ai turned and looked back, the smoke of the city was rising into the sky. They could not escape in any direction, and the troops who had fled to the wilderness now turned against their pursuers.
5008021	When Joshua and all Israel saw that the men in ambush had captured the city and that smoke was rising from it, they turned around and struck down the men of Ai.
5008022	Meanwhile, those in the ambush came out of the city against them, and the men of Ai were trapped between the Israelite forces on both sides. So Israel struck them down until no survivor or fugitive remained.
5008023	But they took the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.
5008024	When Israel had finished killing all the men of Ai who had pursued them into the field and wilderness, and when every last one of them had fallen by the sword, all the Israelites returned to Ai and put it to the sword as well.
5008025	A total of twelve thousand men and women fell that day—all the people of Ai.
5008026	Joshua did not draw back the hand that held his battle lance until he had devoted to destruction all who lived in Ai.
5008027	Israel took for themselves only the cattle and plunder of that city, as the LORD had commanded Joshua.
5008028	So Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent heap of ruins, a desolation to this day.
5008029	He hung the king of Ai on a tree until evening, and at sunset Joshua commanded that they take down the body from the tree and throw it down at the entrance of the city gate. And over it they raised a large pile of rocks, which remains to this day.
5008030	At that time Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal to the LORD, the God of Israel,
5008031	just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites. He built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses: “an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used.” And on it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD, and they sacrificed peace offerings.
5008032	And there in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua inscribed on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written.
5008033	All Israel, foreigners and citizens alike, with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD facing the Levitical priests who carried it. Half of the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded earlier, to bless the people of Israel.
5008034	Afterward, Joshua read aloud all the words of the law—the blessings and the curses—according to all that is written in the Book of the Law.
5008035	There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua failed to read before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who lived among them.
5009001	Now when news of this reached all the kings west of the Jordan—those in the hill country, the foothills, and all along the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon (the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites)—
5009002	they came together to wage war against Joshua and Israel.
5009003	But the people of Gibeon, having heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,
5009004	acted deceptively and set out as envoys, carrying on their donkeys worn-out sacks and old wineskins, cracked and mended.
5009005	They put worn, patched sandals on their feet and threadbare clothing on their bodies, and their whole supply of bread was dry and moldy.
5009006	They went to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal and said to him and the men of Israel, “We have come from a distant land; please make a treaty with us.”
5009007	But the men of Israel said to the Hivites, “Perhaps you dwell near us. How can we make a treaty with you?”
5009008	“We are your servants,” they said to Joshua. Then Joshua asked them, “Who are you and where have you come from?”
5009009	“Your servants have come from a very distant land,” they replied, “because of the fame of the LORD your God. For we have heard the reports about Him: all that He did in Egypt,
5009010	and all that He did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan—Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth.
5009011	So the elders and inhabitants of our land told us, ‘Take provisions for your journey; go to meet them and say to them: We are your servants. Please make a treaty with us.’
5009012	This bread of ours was warm when we packed it at home on the day we left to come to you. But look, it is now dry and moldy.
5009013	These wineskins were new when we filled them, but look, they are cracked. And these clothes and sandals are worn out from our very long journey.”
5009014	Then the men of Israel sampled their provisions but did not seek the counsel of the LORD.
5009015	And Joshua made a treaty of peace with them to let them live, and the leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.
5009016	Three days after they had made the treaty with the Gibeonites, the Israelites learned that they were neighbors, living among them.
5009017	So the Israelites set out and on the third day arrived at their cities—Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.
5009018	But the Israelites did not attack them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. And the whole congregation grumbled against the leaders.
5009019	All the leaders answered, “We have sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.
5009020	This is how we will treat them: We will let them live, so that no wrath will fall on us because of the oath we swore to them.”
5009021	They continued, “Let them live, but let them be woodcutters and water carriers for the whole congregation.” So the leaders kept their promise.
5009022	Then Joshua summoned the Gibeonites and said, “Why did you deceive us by telling us you live far away from us, when in fact you live among us?
5009023	Now therefore you are under a curse and will perpetually serve as woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God.”
5009024	The Gibeonites answered, “Your servants were told clearly that the LORD your God had commanded His servant Moses to give you all the land and wipe out all its inhabitants before you. So we greatly feared for our lives because of you, and that is why we have done this.
5009025	Now we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you.”
5009026	So Joshua did this and delivered them from the hands of the Israelites, and they did not kill the Gibeonites.
5009027	On that day he made them woodcutters and water carriers, as they are to this day for the congregation of the LORD and for the altar at the place He would choose.
5010001	Now Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction —doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king—and that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living near them.
5010002	So Adoni-zedek and his people were greatly alarmed, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities; it was larger than Ai, and all its men were mighty.
5010003	Therefore Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, saying,
5010004	“Come up and help me. We will attack Gibeon, because they have made peace with Joshua and the Israelites.”
5010005	So the five kings of the Amorites—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon—joined forces and advanced with all their armies. They camped before Gibeon and made war against it.
5010006	Then the men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal: “Do not abandon your servants. Come quickly and save us! Help us, because all the kings of the Amorites from the hill country have joined forces against us.”
5010007	So Joshua and his whole army, including all the mighty men of valor, came from Gilgal.
5010008	The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for I have delivered them into your hand. Not one of them shall stand against you.”
5010009	After marching all night from Gilgal, Joshua caught them by surprise.
5010010	And the LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, who defeated them in a great slaughter at Gibeon, pursued them along the ascent to Beth-horon, and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.
5010011	As they fled before Israel along the descent from Beth-horon to Azekah, the LORD cast down on them large hailstones from the sky, and more of them were killed by the hailstones than by the swords of the Israelites.
5010012	On the day that the LORD gave the Amorites over to the Israelites, Joshua spoke to the LORD in the presence of Israel: “O sun, stand still over Gibeon, O moon, over the Valley of Aijalon.”
5010013	So the sun stood still and the moon stopped until the nation took vengeance upon its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? “So the sun stopped in the middle of the sky and delayed going down about a full day.”
5010014	There has been no day like it before or since, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, because the LORD fought for Israel.
5010015	Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.
5010016	Now the five kings had fled and hidden in the cave at Makkedah.
5010017	And Joshua was informed: “The five kings have been found; they are hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”
5010018	So Joshua said, “Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave, and post men there to guard them.
5010019	But you, do not stop there. Pursue your enemies and attack them from behind. Do not let them reach their cities, for the LORD your God has delivered them into your hand.”
5010020	So Joshua and the Israelites continued to inflict a terrible slaughter until they had finished them off, and the remaining survivors retreated to the fortified cities.
5010021	The whole army returned safely to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah, and no one dared to utter a word against the Israelites.
5010022	Then Joshua said, “Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me.”
5010023	So they brought the five kings out of the cave—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
5010024	When they had brought the kings to Joshua, he summoned all the men of Israel and said to the army commanders who had accompanied him, “Come here and put your feet on the necks of these kings.” So the commanders came forward and put their feet on their necks.
5010025	“Do not be afraid or discouraged,” Joshua said. “Be strong and courageous, for the LORD will do this to all the enemies you fight.”
5010026	After this, Joshua struck down and killed the kings, and he hung their bodies on five trees and left them there until evening.
5010027	At sunset Joshua ordered that they be taken down from the trees and thrown into the cave in which they had hidden. Then large stones were placed against the mouth of the cave, and the stones are there to this day.
5010028	On that day Joshua captured Makkedah and put it to the sword, along with its king. He devoted to destruction everyone in the city, leaving no survivors. So he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
5010029	Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against Libnah.
5010030	And the LORD also delivered that city and its king into the hand of Israel, and Joshua put all the people to the sword, leaving no survivors. And he did to the king of Libnah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
5010031	And Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Libnah to Lachish. They laid siege to it and fought against it.
5010032	And the LORD delivered Lachish into the hand of Israel, and Joshua captured it on the second day. He put all the people to the sword, just as he had done to Libnah.
5010033	At that time Horam king of Gezer went to help Lachish, but Joshua struck him down along with his people, leaving no survivors.
5010034	So Joshua moved on from Lachish to Eglon, and all Israel with him. They laid siege to it and fought against it.
5010035	That day they captured Eglon and put it to the sword, and Joshua devoted to destruction everyone in the city, just as he had done to Lachish.
5010036	Then Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.
5010037	They captured it and put to the sword its king, all its villages, and all the people. Joshua left no survivors, just as he had done at Eglon; he devoted to destruction Hebron and everyone in it.
5010038	Finally Joshua and all Israel with him turned toward Debir and fought against it.
5010039	And they captured Debir, its king, and all its villages. They put them to the sword and devoted to destruction everyone in the city, leaving no survivors. Joshua did to Debir and its king as he had done to Hebron and as he had done to Libnah and its king.
5010040	So Joshua conquered the whole region—the hill country, the Negev, the foothills, and the slopes, together with all their kings—leaving no survivors. He devoted to destruction everything that breathed, just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
5010041	Joshua conquered the area from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and the whole region of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
5010042	And because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel, Joshua captured all these kings and their land in one campaign.
5010043	Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.
5011001	Now when Jabin king of Hazor heard about these things, he sent word to Jobab king of Madon; to the kings of Shimron and Achshaph;

5011020	For it was of the LORD to harden their hearts to engage Israel in battle, so that they would be set apart for destruction and would receive no mercy, being annihilated as the LORD had commanded Moses.
5011021	At that time Joshua proceeded to eliminate the Anakim from the hill country of Hebron, Debir, and Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and of Israel. Joshua devoted them to destruction, along with their cities.
5011022	No Anakim were left in the land of the Israelites; only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod did any survive.

5013001	Now Joshua was old and well along in years, and the LORD said to him, “You are old and well along in years, but very much of the land remains to be possessed.
5013002	This is the land that remains: All the territory of the Philistines and the Geshurites,
5013003	from the Shihor east of Egypt to the territory of Ekron on the north (considered to be Canaanite territory)—that of the five Philistine rulers of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron, as well as that of the Avvites;
5013004	to the south, all the land of the Canaanites, from Mearah of the Sidonians to Aphek, as far as the border of the Amorites;
5013005	the land of the Gebalites; and all Lebanon to the east, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath.
5013006	All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim—all the Sidonians—I Myself will drive out before the Israelites. Be sure to divide it by lot as an inheritance to Israel, as I have commanded you.
5013007	Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.”
5013008	The other half of Manasseh, along with the Reubenites and Gadites, had received the inheritance Moses had given them beyond the Jordan to the east, just as Moses the servant of the LORD had assigned to them:
5013009	The area from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, along with the city in the middle of the valley, the whole plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon,
5013010	and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites;
5013011	also Gilead and the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites, all of Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah—

5013013	but the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. So Geshur and Maacath dwell among the Israelites to this day.
5013014	To the tribe of Levi, however, Moses had given no inheritance. The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them.
5013015	This is what Moses had given to the clans of the tribe of Reuben:
5013016	The territory from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, along with the city in the middle of the valley, to the whole plateau beyond Medeba,

5013021	all the cities of the plateau and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon until Moses killed him and the chiefs of Midian (Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba), the princes of Sihon who lived in the land.
5013022	The Israelites also killed the diviner Balaam son of Beor along with the others they put to the sword.

5013025	The territory of Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer, near Rabbah;

5013027	and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, with the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon (the territory on the east side of the Jordan up to the edge of the Sea of Chinnereth).
5013028	This was the inheritance of the clans of the Gadites, including the cities and villages.
5013029	This is what Moses had given to the clans of the half-tribe of Manasseh, that is, to half the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh:
5013030	The territory from Mahanaim through all Bashan—all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, including all the towns of Jair that are in Bashan, sixty cities;
5013031	half of Gilead; and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the royal cities of Og in Bashan. All this was for the clans of the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, that is, half of the descendants of Machir.
5013032	These were the portions Moses had given them on the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho.
5013033	To the tribe of Levi, however, Moses had given no inheritance. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, just as He had promised them.
5014001	Now these are the portions that the Israelites inherited in the land of Canaan, as distributed by Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the families of the tribes of Israel.
5014002	Their inheritance was assigned by lot for the nine and a half tribes, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
5014003	For Moses had given the inheritance east of the Jordan to the other two and a half tribes. But he granted no inheritance among them to the Levites.
5014004	The descendants of Joseph became two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. And no portion of the land was given to the Levites, except for cities in which to live, along with pasturelands for their flocks and herds.
5014005	So the Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they divided the land.
5014006	Then the sons of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You know what the LORD said to Moses the man of God at Kadesh-barnea about you and me.
5014007	I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I brought back to him an honest report.
5014008	Although my brothers who went with me made the hearts of the people melt with fear, I remained loyal to the LORD my God.
5014009	On that day Moses swore to me, saying, ‘Surely the land on which you have set foot will be an inheritance to you and your children forever, because you have wholly followed the LORD my God.’
5014010	Now behold, as the LORD promised, He has kept me alive these forty-five years since He spoke this word to Moses, while Israel wandered in the wilderness. So here I am today, eighty-five years old,
5014011	still as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me out. As my strength was then, so it is now for war, for going out, and for coming in.
5014012	Now therefore give me this hill country that the LORD promised me on that day, for you yourself heard then that the Anakim were there, with great and fortified cities. Perhaps with the LORD’s help I will drive them out, as the LORD has spoken.”
5014013	Then Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his inheritance.
5014014	Therefore Hebron belongs to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite as an inheritance to this day, because he wholly followed the LORD, the God of Israel.

5017014	Then the sons of Joseph said to Joshua, “Why have you given us only one portion as an inheritance? We have many people, because the LORD has blessed us abundantly.”
5017015	Joshua answered them, “If you have so many people that the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you, go to the forest and clear for yourself an area in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim.”
5017016	“The hill country is not enough for us,” they replied, “and all the Canaanites who live in the valley have iron chariots, both in Beth-shean with its towns and in the Valley of Jezreel.”
5017017	So Joshua said to the house of Joseph—to Ephraim and Manasseh—“You have many people and great strength. You shall not have just one allotment,
5017018	because the hill country will be yours as well. It is a forest; clear it, and its farthest limits will be yours. Although the Canaanites have iron chariots and although they are strong, you can drive them out.”
5018001	Then the whole congregation of Israel assembled at Shiloh and set up the Tent of Meeting there. And though the land was subdued before them,
5018002	there were still seven tribes of Israel who had not yet received their inheritance.

5018005	and divide the land into seven portions. Judah shall remain in their territory in the south, and the house of Joseph shall remain in their territory in the north.
5018006	When you have mapped out the seven portions of land and brought it to me, I will cast lots for you here in the presence of the LORD our God.
5018007	The Levites, however, have no portion among you, because their inheritance is the priesthood of the LORD. And Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh have already received the inheritance that Moses the servant of the LORD gave them beyond the Jordan to the east.”

5020001	Then the LORD said to Joshua,
5020002	“Tell the Israelites to designate the cities of refuge, as I instructed you through Moses,
5020003	so that anyone who kills another unintentionally or accidentally may flee there. These will be your refuge from the avenger of blood.
5020004	When someone flees to one of these cities, stands at the entrance of the city gate, and states his case before its elders, they are to bring him into the city and give him a place to live among them.
5020005	Now if the avenger of blood pursues him, they must not surrender the manslayer into his hand, because that man killed his neighbor accidentally without prior malice.
5020006	He is to stay in that city until he stands trial before the assembly and until the death of the high priest serving at that time. Then the manslayer may return to his own home in the city from which he fled.”
5020007	So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the hill country of Judah.
5020008	And beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho, they designated Bezer on the wilderness plateau from the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.
5020009	These are the cities appointed for all the Israelites and foreigners among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood prior to standing trial before the assembly.
5021001	Now the family heads of the Levites approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the other tribes of Israel
5021002	at Shiloh in the land of Canaan and said to them, “The LORD commanded through Moses that we be given cities in which to live, together with pasturelands for our livestock.”
5021003	So by the command of the LORD, the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and their pasturelands out of their own inheritance:
5021004	The first lot came out for the Kohathite clans. The Levites who were descendants of Aaron the priest received thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
5021005	The remaining descendants of Kohath received ten cities by lot from the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
5021006	The descendants of Gershon received thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
5021007	And the descendants of Merari received twelve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
5021008	So the Israelites allotted to the Levites these cities, together with their pasturelands, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
5021009	From the tribes of Judah and Simeon, they designated these cities by name
5021010	to the descendants of Aaron from the Kohathite clans of the Levites, because the first lot fell to them:
5021011	They gave them Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), with its surrounding pasturelands, in the hill country of Judah. (Arba was the father of Anak.)
5021012	But they had given the fields and villages around the city to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his possession.
5021013	So to the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave these cities, together with their pasturelands: Hebron, a city of refuge for the manslayer, Libnah,
5021014	Jattir, Eshtemoa,
5021015	Holon, Debir,
5021016	Ain, Juttah, and Beth-shemesh—nine cities from these two tribes, together with their pasturelands.
5021017	And from the tribe of Benjamin they gave them Gibeon, Geba,
5021018	Anathoth, and Almon—four cities, together with their pasturelands.
5021019	In all, thirteen cities, together with their pasturelands, were given to the priests, the descendants of Aaron.
