9005003	So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, where King David made with them a covenant before the LORD. And they anointed him king over Israel.
9005004	David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years.
9005005	In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
9005006	Now the king and his men marched to Jerusalem against the Jebusites who inhabited the land. The Jebusites said to David: “You will never get in here. Even the blind and lame can repel you.” For they thought, “David cannot get in here.”
9005007	Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion (that is, the City of David).
9005008	On that day he said, “Whoever attacks the Jebusites must use the water shaft to reach the lame and blind who are despised by David.” That is why it is said, “The blind and the lame will never enter the palace.”
9005009	So David took up residence in the fortress and called it the City of David. He built it up all the way around, from the supporting terraces inward.
9005010	And David became greater and greater, for the LORD God of Hosts was with him.
9005011	Now Hiram king of Tyre sent envoys to David, along with cedar logs, carpenters, and stonemasons, and they built a palace for David.
9005012	And David realized that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for the sake of His people Israel.
9005013	After he had arrived from Hebron, David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him.
9005014	These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
9005015	Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
9005016	Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
9005017	When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, they all went in search of him; but David learned of this and went down to the stronghold.
9005018	Now the Philistines had come and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
9005019	So David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will You deliver them into my hand?” “Go up,” replied the LORD, “for I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hand.”
9005020	So David went to Baal-perazim, where he defeated the Philistines and said, “Like a bursting flood, the LORD has burst out against my enemies before me.” So he called that place Baal-perazim.
9005021	There the Philistines abandoned their idols, and David and his men carried them away.
9005022	Once again the Philistines came up and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
9005023	So David inquired of the LORD, who answered, “Do not march straight up, but circle around behind them and attack them in front of the balsam trees.
9005024	As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move quickly, because this will mean that the LORD has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines.”
9005025	So David did as the LORD had commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.
9006001	David again assembled the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand in all.
9006002	And he and all his troops set out for Baale of Judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name— the name of the LORD of Hosts, who is enthroned between the cherubim that are on it.
9006003	They set the ark of God on a new cart and brought it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were guiding the new cart,
9006004	bringing with it the ark of God. And Ahio was walking in front of the ark.
9006005	David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of wood instruments, harps, stringed instruments, tambourines, sistrums, and cymbals.
9006006	When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark of God, because the oxen had stumbled.
9006007	And the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down on the spot for his irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.
9006008	Then David became angry because the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah. So he named that place Perez-uzzah, as it is called to this day.
9006009	That day David feared the LORD and asked, “How can the ark of the LORD ever come to me?”
9006010	So he was unwilling to move the ark of the LORD to the City of David; instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
9006011	Thus the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed him and all his household.
9006012	Now it was reported to King David, “The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God.” So David went and had the ark of God brought up from the house of Obed-edom into the City of David with rejoicing.
9006013	When those carrying the ark of the LORD had advanced six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
9006014	And David, wearing a linen ephod, danced with all his might before the LORD,
9006015	while he and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and the sounding of the ram’s horn.
9006016	As the ark of the LORD was entering the City of David, Saul’s daughter Michal looked down from a window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.
9006017	So they brought the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it. Then David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
9006018	When David had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts.
9006019	Then he distributed to every man and woman among the multitude of Israel a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake. And all the people departed, each to his own home.
9006020	When David returned home to bless his own household, Saul’s daughter Michal came out to meet him. “How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today!” she said. “He has uncovered himself today in the sight of the maidservants of his subjects, like a vulgar person would do.”
9006021	But David said to Michal, “I was dancing before the LORD, who chose me over your father and all his house when He appointed me ruler over the LORD’s people Israel. I will celebrate before the LORD,
9006022	and I will humiliate and humble myself even more than this. Yet I will be honored by the maidservants of whom you have spoken.”
9006023	And Michal the daughter of Saul had no children to the day of her death.
9007001	After the king had settled into his palace and the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies around him,
9007002	he said to Nathan the prophet, “Here I am, living in a house of cedar, while the ark of God remains in a tent.”
9007003	And Nathan replied to the king, “Go and do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you.”
9007004	But that night the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,
9007005	“Go and tell My servant David that this is what the LORD says: Are you the one to build for Me a house to dwell in?
9007006	For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the Israelites up out of Egypt until this day, but I have moved about with a tent as My dwelling.
9007007	In all My journeys with all the Israelites, have I ever asked any of the leaders I appointed to shepherd My people Israel, ‘Why haven’t you built Me a house of cedar?’
9007008	Now then, you are to tell My servant David that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be the ruler over My people Israel.
9007009	I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. Now I will make for you a name like that of the greatest in the land.
9007010	And I will provide a place for My people Israel and will plant them so that they may dwell in a place of their own and be disturbed no more. No longer will the sons of wickedness oppress them as they did at the beginning
9007011	and have done since the day I appointed judges over My people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies. The LORD declares to you that He Himself will establish a house for you.
9007012	And when your days are fulfilled and you rest with your fathers, I will raise up your descendant after you, who will come from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.
9007013	He will build a house for My Name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
9007014	I will be his Father, and he will be My son. When he does wrong, I will discipline him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men.
9007015	But My loving devotion will never be removed from him as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
9007016	Your house and kingdom will endure forever before Me, and your throne will be established forever.”
9007017	So Nathan relayed to David all the words of this entire revelation.
9007018	Then King David went in, sat before the LORD, and said, “Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?
9007019	And as if this was a small thing in Your eyes, O Lord GOD, You have also spoken about the future of the house of Your servant. Is this Your custom with man, O Lord GOD?
9007020	What more can David say to You? For You know Your servant, O Lord GOD.
9007021	For the sake of Your word and according to Your own heart, You have accomplished this great thing and revealed it to Your servant.
9007022	How great You are, O Lord GOD! For there is none like You, and there is no God but You, according to everything we have heard with our own ears.
9007023	And who is like Your people Israel—the one nation on earth whom God went out to redeem as a people for Himself and to make a name for Himself? You performed great and awesome wonders by driving out nations and their gods from before Your people, whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt.
9007024	For You have established Your people Israel as Your very own forever, and You, O LORD, have become their God.
9007025	And now, O LORD God, confirm forever the word You have spoken concerning Your servant and his house. Do as You have promised,
9007026	so that Your name will be magnified forever when it is said, ‘The LORD of Hosts is God over Israel.’ And the house of Your servant David will be established before You.
9007027	For You, O LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, have revealed this to Your servant when You said, ‘I will build a house for you.’ Therefore Your servant has found the courage to offer this prayer to You.
9007028	And now, O Lord GOD, You are God! Your words are true, and You have promised this goodness to Your servant.
9007029	Now therefore, may it please You to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You. For You, O Lord GOD, have spoken, and with Your blessing the house of Your servant will be blessed forever.”
9008001	Some time later, David defeated the Philistines, subdued them, and took Metheg-ammah from the hand of the Philistines.
9008002	David also defeated the Moabites, made them lie down on the ground, and measured them off with a cord. He measured off with two lengths those to be put to death, and with one length those to be spared. So the Moabites became subject to David and brought him tribute.
9008003	David also defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, who had marched out to restore his dominion along the Euphrates River.
9008004	David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand charioteers, and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and he hamstrung all the horses except a hundred he kept for the chariots.
9008005	When the Arameans of Damascus came to help King Hadadezer of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of their men.
9008006	Then he placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became subject to David and brought him tribute. So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went.
9008007	And David took the gold shields that belonged to the officers of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.
9008008	And from Betah and Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a large amount of bronze.
9008009	When King Toi of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer,
9008010	he sent his son Joram to greet King David and bless him for fighting and defeating Hadadezer, who had been at war with Toi. Joram brought with him articles of silver and gold and bronze,
9008011	and King David dedicated these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had dedicated from all the nations he had subdued—
9008012	from Edom and Moab, from the Ammonites and Philistines and Amalekites, and from the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
9008013	And David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
9008014	He placed garrisons throughout Edom, and all the Edomites were subject to David. So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went.
9008015	Thus David reigned over all Israel and administered justice and righteousness for all his people:
9008016	Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
9008017	Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was the scribe;
9008018	Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites; and David’s sons were priestly leaders.
9009001	Then David asked, “Is there anyone left from the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan?”
9009002	And there was a servant of the house of Saul named Ziba. They summoned him to David, and the king inquired, “Are you Ziba?” “I am your servant,” he replied.
9009003	So the king asked, “Is there anyone left of the house of Saul to whom I can show the kindness of God?” Ziba answered, “There is still Jonathan’s son, who is lame in both feet.”
9009004	“Where is he?” replied the king. And Ziba said, “Indeed, he is in Lo-debar at the house of Machir son of Ammiel.”
9009005	So King David had him brought from the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar.
9009006	And when Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown in reverence. Then David said, “Mephibosheth!” “I am your servant,” he replied.
9009007	“Do not be afraid,” said David, “for surely I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land of your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table.”
9009008	Mephibosheth bowed down and said, “What is your servant, that you should show regard for a dead dog like me?”
9009009	Then the king summoned Saul’s servant Ziba and said to him, “I have given to your master’s grandson all that belonged to Saul and to all his house.
9009010	You and your sons and servants are to work the ground for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master’s grandson may have food to eat. But Mephibosheth, your master’s grandson, is always to eat at my table.” Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
9009011	And Ziba said to the king, “Your servant will do all that my lord the king has commanded.” So Mephibosheth ate at David’s table like one of the king’s own sons.
9009012	And Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants of Mephibosheth.
9009013	So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king’s table, and he was lame in both feet.
9010001	Some time later, the king of the Ammonites died and was succeeded by his son Hanun.
9010002	And David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent some of his servants to console Hanun concerning his father. But when they arrived in the land of the Ammonites,
9010003	the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun their lord, “Just because David has sent you comforters, do you really believe he is showing respect for your father? Has not David instead sent his servants to explore the city, spy it out, and overthrow it?”
9010004	So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved off half of each man’s beard, cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away.
9010005	When this was reported to David, he sent messengers to meet the men, since they had been thoroughly humiliated. The king told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return.”
9010006	When the Ammonites realized that they had become a stench to David, they hired twenty thousand Aramean foot soldiers from Beth-rehob and Zoba, as well as a thousand men from the king of Maacah and twelve thousand men from Tob.
9010007	On hearing this, David sent Joab and the entire army of mighty men.
9010008	The Ammonites marched out and arrayed themselves for battle at the entrance of the city gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open country.
9010009	When Joab saw the battle lines before him and behind him, he selected some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans.
9010010	And he placed the rest of the troops under the command of his brother Abishai, who arrayed them against the Ammonites.
9010011	“If the Arameans are too strong for me,” said Joab, “then you will come to my rescue. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to your rescue.
9010012	Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do what is good in His sight.”
9010013	So Joab and his troops advanced to fight the Arameans, who fled before him.
9010014	When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled before Abishai, and they entered the city. So Joab returned from fighting against the Ammonites and came to Jerusalem.
9010015	When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they regrouped.
9010016	Hadadezer sent messengers to bring more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates, and they came to Helam with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer’s army leading them.
9010017	When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and went to Helam. Then the Arameans arrayed themselves against David and fought against him.
9010018	But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also struck down Shobach the commander of their army, who died there.
9010019	When all the kings who were subject to Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with Israel and became subject to them. So the Arameans were afraid to help the Ammonites anymore.
9011001	In the spring, at the time when kings march out to war, David sent out Joab and his servants with the whole army of Israel. They destroyed the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah, but David remained in Jerusalem.
9011002	One evening David got up from his bed and strolled around on the roof of the palace. And from the roof he saw a woman bathing—a very beautiful woman.
9011003	So David sent and inquired about the woman, and he was told, “This is Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam and the wife of Uriah the Hittite.”
9011004	Then David sent messengers to get her, and when she came to him, he slept with her. (Now she had just purified herself from her uncleanness.) Then she returned home.
9011005	And the woman conceived and sent word to David, saying, “I am pregnant.”
9011006	At this, David sent orders to Joab: “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” So Joab sent him to David.
9011007	When Uriah came to him, David asked how Joab and the troops were doing and how the war was going.
9011008	Then he said to Uriah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.” So Uriah left the palace, and a gift from the king followed him.
9011009	But Uriah slept at the door of the palace with all his master’s servants; he did not go down to his house.
9011010	And David was told, “Uriah did not go home.” “Haven’t you just arrived from a journey?” David asked Uriah. “Why didn’t you go home?”
9011011	Uriah answered, “The ark and Israel and Judah are dwelling in tents, and my master Joab and his soldiers are camped in the open field. How can I go to my house to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? As surely as you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do such a thing!”
9011012	“Stay here one more day,” David said to Uriah, “and tomorrow I will send you back.” So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next.
9011013	Then David invited Uriah to eat and drink with him, and he got Uriah drunk. And in the evening Uriah went out to lie down on his cot with his master’s servants, but he did not go home.
9011014	The next morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it with Uriah.
9011015	In the letter he wrote: “Put Uriah at the front of the fiercest battle; then withdraw from him, so that he may be struck down and killed.”
9011016	So as Joab besieged the city, he assigned Uriah to a place where he knew the strongest enemy soldiers were.
9011017	And when the men of the city came out and fought against Joab, some of David’s servants fell, and Uriah the Hittite also died.
9011018	Joab sent to David a full account of the battle
9011019	and instructed the messenger, “When you have finished giving the king a full account of the battle,
9011020	if the king’s anger flares, he may ask you, ‘Why did you get so close to the city to fight? Did you not realize they would shoot from atop the wall?
9011021	Who struck Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? Was it not a woman who dropped an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died in Thebez? Why did you get so close to the wall?’ If he asks you this, then you are to say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.’”
9011022	So the messenger set out and reported to David all that Joab had sent him to say.
9011023	The messenger said to David, “The men overpowered us and came out against us in the field, but we drove them back to the entrance of the gate.
9011024	Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall, and some of the king’s servants were killed. And your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.”
9011025	Then David told the messenger, “Say this to Joab: ‘Do not let this matter upset you, for the sword devours one as well as another. Strengthen your attack against the city and demolish it.’ Encourage him with these words.”
9011026	When Uriah’s wife heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
9011027	And when the time of mourning was over, David had her brought to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done was evil in the sight of the LORD.
9012001	Then the LORD sent Nathan to David, and when he arrived, he said, “There were two men in a certain city, one rich and the other poor.
9012002	The rich man had a great number of sheep and cattle,
9012003	but the poor man had nothing except one small ewe lamb that he had bought. He raised it, and it grew up with him and his children. It shared his food and drank from his cup; it slept in his arms and was like a daughter to him.
9012004	Now a traveler came to the rich man, who refrained from taking one of his own sheep or cattle to prepare for the traveler who had come to him. Instead, he took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for his guest.”
9012005	David burned with anger against the man and said to Nathan: “As surely as the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die!
9012006	Because he has done this thing and has shown no pity, he must pay for the lamb four times over.”
9012007	Then Nathan said to David, “You are that man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.
9012008	I gave your master’s house to you and your master’s wives into your arms. I gave you the house of Israel and Judah, and if that was not enough, I would have given you even more.
9012009	Why then have you despised the command of the LORD by doing evil in His sight? You put Uriah the Hittite to the sword and took his wife as your own. You have slain him with the sword of the Ammonites.
9012010	Now, therefore, the sword will never depart from your house, because you have despised Me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your own.’
9012011	This is what the LORD says: ‘I will raise up adversity against you from your own house. Before your very eyes I will take your wives and give them to another, and he will lie with them in broad daylight.
9012012	You have acted in secret, but I will do this thing in broad daylight before all Israel.’”
9012013	Then David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against the LORD.” “The LORD has taken away your sin,” Nathan replied. “You will not die.
9012014	Nevertheless, because by this deed you have shown utter contempt for the word of the LORD, the son born to you will surely die.”
9012015	After Nathan had gone home, the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife had borne to David, and he became ill.
9012016	David pleaded with God for the boy. He fasted and went into his house and spent the night lying in sackcloth on the ground.
9012017	The elders of his household stood beside him to help him up from the ground, but he was unwilling and would not eat anything with them.
9012018	On the seventh day the child died. But David’s servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, “Look, while the child was alive, we spoke to him, and he would not listen to us. So how can we tell him the child is dead? He may even harm himself.”
9012019	When David saw that his servants were whispering to one another, he perceived that the child was dead. So he asked his servants, “Is the child dead?” “He is dead,” they replied.
9012020	Then David got up from the ground, washed and anointed himself, changed his clothes, and went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. Then he went to his own house, and at his request they set food before him, and he ate.
9012021	“What is this you have done?” his servants asked. “While the child was alive, you fasted and wept, but when he died, you got up and ate.”
9012022	David answered, “While the child was alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, ‘Who knows? The LORD may be gracious to me and let him live.’
9012023	But now that he is dead, why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.”
9012024	Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba, and he went to her and lay with her. So she gave birth to a son, and they named him Solomon. Now the LORD loved the child
9012025	and sent word through Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah because the LORD loved him.
9012026	Meanwhile, Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal fortress.
9012027	Then Joab sent messengers to David to say, “I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the water supply of the city.
9012028	Now, therefore, assemble the rest of the troops, lay siege to the city, and capture it. Otherwise I will capture the city, and it will be named after me.”
9012029	So David assembled all the troops and went to Rabbah; and he fought against it and captured it.
9012030	Then he took the crown from the head of their king. It weighed a talent of gold and was set with precious stones, and it was placed on David’s head. And David took a great amount of plunder from the city.
9012031	David brought out the people who were there and put them to work with saws, iron picks, and axes, and he made them work at the brick kilns. He did the same to all the Ammonite cities. Then David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem.
9013001	After some time, David’s son Amnon fell in love with Tamar, the beautiful sister of David’s son Absalom.
9013002	Amnon was sick with frustration over his sister Tamar, for she was a virgin, and it seemed implausible for him to do anything to her.
9013003	Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah. Jonadab was a very shrewd man,
9013004	and he asked Amnon, “Why are you, the son of the king, so depressed morning after morning? Won’t you tell me?” Amnon replied, “I am in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.”
9013005	Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend you are ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare it in my sight so I may watch her and eat it from her hand.’”
9013006	So Amnon lay down and feigned illness. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes in my sight, so that I may eat from her hand.”
9013007	Then David sent word to Tamar at the palace: “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare a meal for him.”
9013008	So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, who was lying down. She took some dough, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked them.
9013009	Then she brought the pan and set it down before him, but he refused to eat. “Send everyone away!” said Amnon. And everyone went out.
9013010	Then Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the bedroom, so that I may eat it from your hand.” Tamar took the cakes she had made and went to her brother Amnon’s bedroom.
9013011	And when she had brought them to him to eat, he took hold of her and said, “Come lie with me, my sister!”
9013012	“No, my brother!” she cried. “Do not violate me, for such a thing should never be done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful thing!
9013013	Where could I ever take my shame? And you would be like one of the fools in Israel! Please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you.”
9013014	But Amnon refused to listen to her, and being stronger, he violated her and lay with her.
9013015	Then Amnon hated Tamar with such intensity that his hatred was greater than the love he previously had. “Get up!” he said to her. “Be gone!”
9013016	“No,” she replied, “sending me away is worse than this great wrong you have already done to me!” But he refused to listen to her.
9013017	Instead, he called to his attendant and said, “Throw this woman out and bolt the door behind her!”
9013018	So Amnon’s attendant threw her out and bolted the door behind her. Now Tamar was wearing a robe of many colors, because this is what the king’s virgin daughters wore.
9013019	And Tamar put ashes on her head and tore her robe. And putting her hand on her head, she went away crying aloud.
9013020	Her brother Absalom said to her, “Has your brother Amnon been with you? Be quiet for now, my sister. He is your brother. Do not take this thing to heart.” So Tamar lived as a desolate woman in the house of her brother Absalom.
9013021	When King David heard all this, he was furious.
9013022	And Absalom never said a word to Amnon, either good or bad, because he hated Amnon for violating his sister Tamar.
9013023	Two years later, when Absalom’s sheepshearers were at Baal-hazor near Ephraim, he invited all the sons of the king.
9013024	And he went to the king and said, “Your servant has just hired shearers. Will the king and his servants please come with me?”
9013025	“No, my son,” the king replied, “we should not all go, or we would be a burden to you.” Although Absalom urged him, he was not willing to go, but gave him his blessing.
9013026	“If not,” said Absalom, “please let my brother Amnon go with us.” “Why should he go with you?” the king asked.
9013027	But Absalom urged him, so the king sent Amnon and the rest of his sons.
9013028	Now Absalom had ordered his young men, “Watch Amnon until his heart is merry with wine, and when I order you to strike Amnon down, you are to kill him. Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be courageous and valiant!”
9013029	So Absalom’s young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had ordered. Then all the other sons of the king got up, and each one fled on his mule.
9013030	While they were on the way, a report reached David: “Absalom has struck down all the sons of the king; not one of them is left!”
9013031	Then the king stood up, tore his clothes, and lay down on the ground. And all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.
9013032	But Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah, spoke up: “My lord must not think they have killed all the sons of the king, for only Amnon is dead. In fact, Absalom has planned this since the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.
9013033	So now, my lord the king, do not take to heart the report that all the sons of the king are dead. Only Amnon is dead.”
9013034	Meanwhile, Absalom had fled. When the young man standing watch looked up, he saw many people coming down the road west of him, along the side of the hill. And the watchman went and reported to the king, “I see men coming from the direction of Horonaim, along the side of the hill.”
9013035	So Jonadab said to the king, “Look, the sons of the king have arrived! It is just as your servant said.”
9013036	And as he finished speaking, the sons of the king came in, wailing loudly. Then the king and all his servants also wept very bitterly.
9013037	Now Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. But David mourned for his son every day.
9013038	After Absalom had fled and gone to Geshur, he stayed there three years.
9013039	And King David longed to go to Absalom, for he had been consoled over Amnon’s death.
9014001	Now Joab son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart longed for Absalom.
9014002	So Joab sent to Tekoa to bring a wise woman from there. He told her, “Please pretend to be a mourner; put on clothes for mourning and do not anoint yourself with oil. Act like a woman who has mourned for the dead a long time.
9014003	Then go to the king and speak these words to him.” And Joab put the words in her mouth.
9014004	When the woman from Tekoa went to the king, she fell facedown in homage and said, “Help me, O king!”
9014005	“What troubles you?” the king asked her. “Indeed,” she said, “I am a widow, for my husband is dead.
9014006	And your maidservant had two sons who were fighting in the field with no one to separate them, and one struck the other and killed him.
9014007	Now the whole clan has risen up against your maidservant and said, ‘Hand over the one who struck down his brother, that we may put him to death for the life of the brother whom he killed. Then we will cut off the heir as well!’ So they would extinguish my one remaining ember by not preserving my husband’s name or posterity on the earth.”
9014008	“Go home,” the king said to the woman, “and I will give orders on your behalf.”
9014009	But the woman of Tekoa said to the king, “My lord the king, may any blame be on me and on my father’s house, and may the king and his throne be guiltless.”
9014010	“If anyone speaks to you,” said the king, “bring him to me, and he will not trouble you again!”
9014011	“Please,” she replied, “may the king invoke the LORD your God to prevent the avenger of blood from increasing the devastation, so that my son may not be destroyed!” “As surely as the LORD lives,” he vowed, “not a hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground.”
9014012	Then the woman said, “Please, may your servant speak a word to my lord the king?” “Speak,” he replied.
9014013	The woman asked, “Why have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, since he has not brought back his own banished son?
9014014	For we will surely die and be like water poured out on the ground, which cannot be recovered. Yet God does not take away a life, but He devises ways that the banished one may not be cast out from Him.
9014015	Now therefore, I have come to present this matter to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king. Perhaps he will grant the request of his maidservant.
9014016	For the king will hear and deliver his maidservant from the hand of the man who would cut off both me and my son from God’s inheritance.’
9014017	And now your servant says, ‘May the word of my lord the king bring me rest, for my lord the king is able to discern good and evil, just like the angel of God. May the LORD your God be with you.’”
9014018	Then the king said to the woman, “I am going to ask you something; do not conceal it from me!” “Let my lord the king speak,” she replied.
9014019	So the king asked, “Is the hand of Joab behind all this?” The woman answered, “As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything that my lord the king says. Yes, your servant Joab is the one who gave me orders; he told your maidservant exactly what to say.
9014020	Joab your servant has done this to bring about this change of affairs, but my lord has wisdom like the wisdom of the angel of God, to know everything that happens in the land.”
9014021	Then the king said to Joab, “I hereby grant this request. Go, bring back the young man Absalom.”
9014022	Joab fell facedown in homage and blessed the king. “Today,” said Joab, “your servant knows that he has found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has granted his request.”
9014023	So Joab got up, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
9014024	But the king added, “He may return to his house, but he must not see my face.” So Absalom returned to his own house, but he did not see the face of the king.
9014025	Now there was not a man in all Israel as handsome and highly praised as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the top of his head, he did not have a single flaw.
9014026	And when he cut the hair of his head—he shaved it every year because his hair got so heavy—he would weigh it out to be two hundred shekels, according to the royal standard.
9014027	Three sons were born to Absalom, and a daughter named Tamar, who was a beautiful woman.
9014028	Now Absalom lived in Jerusalem two years without seeing the face of the king.
9014029	Then he sent for Joab to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him. So Absalom sent a second time, but Joab still would not come.
9014030	Then Absalom said to his servants, “Look, Joab’s field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire!” And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
9014031	Then Joab came to Absalom’s house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
9014032	“Look,” said Absalom, “I sent for you and said, ‘Come here. I want to send you to the king to ask: Why have I come back from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there.’ So now, let me see the king’s face, and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me.”
9014033	So Joab went and told the king, and David summoned Absalom, who came to him and bowed facedown before him. Then the king kissed Absalom.
9015001	Some time later, Absalom provided for himself a chariot with horses and fifty men to run ahead of him.
9015002	He would get up early and stand beside the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone had a grievance to bring before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out and ask, “What city are you from?” And if he replied, “Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel,”
9015003	Absalom would say, “Look, your claims are good and right, but the king has no deputy to hear you.”
9015004	And he would add, “If only someone would appoint me judge in the land, then everyone with a grievance or dispute could come to me, and I would give him justice.”
9015005	Also, when anyone approached to bow down to him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him.
9015006	Absalom did this to all the Israelites who came to the king for justice. In this way he stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
9015007	After four years had passed, Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go to Hebron to fulfill a vow I have made to the LORD.
9015008	For your servant made a vow while dwelling in Geshur of Aram, saying: ‘If indeed the LORD brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD in Hebron.’”
9015009	“Go in peace,” said the king. So Absalom got up and went to Hebron.
9015010	Then Absalom sent spies throughout the tribes of Israel with this message: “When you hear the sound of the horn, you are to say, ‘Absalom reigns in Hebron!’”
9015011	Two hundred men from Jerusalem accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and they went along innocently, for they knew nothing about the matter.
9015012	While Absalom was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, to come from his hometown of Giloh. So the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom’s following kept increasing.
9015013	Then a messenger came to David and reported, “The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom.”
9015014	And David said to all the servants with him in Jerusalem, “Arise and let us flee, or we will not escape from Absalom! We must leave quickly, or he will soon overtake us, heap disaster on us, and put the city to the sword.”
9015015	The king’s servants replied, “Whatever our lord the king decides, we are your servants.”
9015016	Then the king set out, and his entire household followed him. But he left behind ten concubines to take care of the palace.
9015017	So the king set out with all the people following him. He stopped at the last house,
9015018	and all his servants marched past him—all the Cherethites and Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath.
9015019	Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you also go with us? Go back and stay with the new king, since you are both a foreigner and an exile from your homeland.
9015020	In fact, you arrived only yesterday; should I make you wander around with us today while I do not know where I am going? Go back and take your brothers with you. May the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness.”
9015021	But Ittai answered the king, “As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be!”
9015022	“March on then,” said David to Ittai. So Ittai the Gittite marched past with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.
9015023	Everyone in the countryside was weeping loudly as all the people passed by. And as the king crossed the Kidron Valley, all the people also passed toward the way of the wilderness.
9015024	Zadok was also there, and all the Levites with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had passed out of the city.
9015025	Then the king said to Zadok, “Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place again.
9015026	But if He should say, ‘I do not delight in you,’ then here I am; let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him.”
9015027	The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace—you with your son Ahimaaz, and Abiathar with his son Jonathan.
9015028	See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”
9015029	So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and stayed there.
9015030	But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went up. His head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.
9015031	Now someone told David: “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” So David pleaded, “O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!”
9015032	When David came to the summit, where he used to worship God, Hushai the Archite was there to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head.
9015033	David said to him, “If you go on with me, you will be a burden to me.
9015034	But you can thwart the counsel of Ahithophel for me if you return to the city and say to Absalom: ‘I will be your servant, my king; in the past I was your father’s servant, but now I will be your servant.’
9015035	Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you? Report to them everything you hear from the king’s palace.
9015036	Indeed, their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with everything you hear.”
9015037	So David’s friend Hushai arrived in Jerusalem just as Absalom was entering the city.
9016001	When David had gone a little beyond the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth was there to meet him. He had a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
9016002	“Why do you have these?” asked the king. Ziba replied, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.”
9016003	“Where is your master’s grandson?” asked the king. And Ziba answered, “Indeed, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he has said, ‘Today, the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my grandfather.’”
9016004	So the king said to Ziba, “All that belongs to Mephibosheth is now yours!” “I humbly bow before you,” said Ziba. “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king!”
9016005	As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the family of the house of Saul was just coming out. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and as he approached, he kept yelling out curses.
9016006	He threw stones at David and at all the servants of the king, though the troops and all the mighty men were on David’s right and left.
9016007	And as he yelled curses, Shimei said, “Get out, get out, you worthless man of bloodshed!
9016008	The LORD has paid you back for all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom. See, you have come to ruin because you are a man of bloodshed!”
9016009	Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head!”
9016010	But the king replied, “What have I to do with you, O sons of Zeruiah? If he curses me because the LORD told him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why did you do this?’”
9016011	Then David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Behold, my own son, my own flesh and blood, seeks my life. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone and let him curse me, for the LORD has told him so.
9016012	Perhaps the LORD will see my affliction and repay me with good for the cursing I receive today.”
9016013	So David and his men proceeded along the road as Shimei went along the ridge of the hill opposite him. As Shimei went, he yelled curses, threw stones, and flung dust at David.
9016014	Finally, the king and all the people with him arrived, exhausted. And there he refreshed himself.
9016015	Then Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
9016016	And David’s friend Hushai the Archite went to Absalom and said to him, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
9016017	“Is this the loyalty you show your friend?” Absalom replied. “Why did you not go with your friend?”
9016018	“Not at all,” Hushai answered. “For the one chosen by the LORD, by this people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and with him I will remain.
9016019	Furthermore, whom should I serve if not his son? As I served in your father’s presence, so also I will serve in yours.”
9016020	Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give me counsel. What should we do?”
9016021	Ahithophel replied, “Sleep with your father’s concubines, whom he has left to take care of the palace. When all Israel hears that you have become a stench to your father, then the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened.”
9016022	So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
9016023	Now in those days the advice of Ahithophel was like the consultation of the word of God. Such was the regard that both David and Absalom had for Ahithophel’s advice.
9017001	Furthermore, Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.
9017002	I will attack him while he is weak and weary; I will throw him into a panic, and all the people with him will flee; I will strike down only the king
9017003	and bring all the people back to you as a bride returning to her husband. You seek the life of only one man; then all the people will be at peace.”
9017004	This proposal seemed good to Absalom and all the elders of Israel.
9017005	Then Absalom said, “Summon Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he too has to say.”
9017006	So Hushai came to Absalom, who told him, “Ahithophel has spoken this proposal. Should we carry it out? If not, what do you say?”
9017007	Hushai replied, “This time the advice of Ahithophel is not sound.”
9017008	He continued, “You know your father and his men. They are mighty men, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Moreover, your father is a man of war who will not spend the night with the troops.
9017009	Surely by now he is hiding in a cave or some other location. If some of your troops fall first, whoever hears of it will say, ‘There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.’
9017010	Then even the most valiant soldier with the heart of a lion will melt with fear, because all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man who has valiant men with him.
9017011	Instead, I advise that all Israel from Dan to Beersheba—a multitude like the sand on the seashore—be gathered to you, and that you yourself lead them into battle.
9017012	Then we will attack David wherever we find him, and we will descend on him like dew on the ground. And of all the men with him, not even one will remain.
9017013	If he retreats to a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a pebble can be found there.”
9017014	Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than that of Ahithophel.” For the LORD had purposed to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom.
9017015	So Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, “This is what Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this is what I have advised.
9017016	Now send quickly and tell David, ‘Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness, but be sure to cross over. Otherwise the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.’”
9017017	Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, where a servant girl would come and pass along information to them. They in turn would go and inform King David, for they dared not be seen entering the city.
9017018	But a young man did see them and told Absalom. So the two left quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.
9017019	Then the man’s wife took a covering, spread it over the mouth of the well, and scattered grain over it so nobody would know a thing.
9017020	When Absalom’s servants came to the woman at the house, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” “They have crossed over the brook,” she replied. The men searched but did not find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.
9017021	After the men had gone, Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed up out of the well and went to inform King David, saying, “Get up and cross over the river at once, for Ahithophel has given this advice against you.”
9017022	So David and all the people with him got up and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, there was no one left who had not crossed the Jordan.
9017023	When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his affairs in order and hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb.
9017024	Then David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.
9017025	Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra, the Ishmaelite who had married Abigail, the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.
9017026	So the Israelites and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.
9017027	When David came to Mahanaim, he was met by Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim.
9017028	They brought beds, basins, and earthen vessels, as well as wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils,
9017029	honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd for David and his people to eat. For they said, “The people have become hungry, exhausted, and thirsty in the wilderness.”
9018001	Then David reviewed his troops and appointed over them commanders of thousands and of hundreds.
9018002	He sent out the troops, a third under Joab, a third under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the troops, “I will surely march out with you as well.”
9018003	But the people pleaded, “You must not go out! For if we have to flee, they will not care about us. Even if half of us die, they will not care. But you are worth ten thousand of us. It is better now if you support us from the city.”
9018004	“I will do whatever seems best to you,” the king replied. So he stood beside the gate, while all the troops marched out by hundreds and by thousands.
9018005	Now the king had commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, “Treat the young man Absalom gently for my sake.” And all the people heard the king’s orders to each of the commanders regarding Absalom.
9018006	So David’s army marched into the field to engage Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
9018007	There the people of Israel were defeated by David’s servants, and the slaughter was great that day—twenty thousand men.
9018008	The battle spread over the whole countryside, and that day the forest devoured more people than the sword.
9018009	Now Absalom was riding on his mule when he met the servants of David, and as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak, Absalom’s head was caught fast in the tree. The mule under him kept going, so that he was suspended in midair.
9018010	When one of the men saw this, he told Joab, “I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree!”
9018011	“You just saw him!” Joab exclaimed. “Why did you not strike him to the ground right there? I would have given you ten shekels of silver and a warrior’s belt!”
9018012	The man replied, “Even if a thousand shekels of silver were weighed out into my hands, I would not raise my hand against the son of the king. For we heard the king command you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.’
9018013	If I had jeopardized my own life —and nothing is hidden from the king—you would have abandoned me.”
9018014	But Joab declared, “I am not going to wait like this with you!” And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the oak tree.
9018015	And ten young men who carried Joab’s armor surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.
9018016	Then Joab blew the ram’s horn, and the troops broke off their pursuit of Israel because Joab had restrained them.
9018017	They took Absalom, cast him into a large pit in the forest, and piled a huge mound of stones over him. Meanwhile, all the Israelites fled, each to his home.
9018018	During his lifetime, Absalom had set up for himself a pillar in the King’s Valley, for he had said, “I have no son to preserve the memory of my name.” So he gave the pillar his name, and to this day it is called Absalom’s Monument.
9018019	Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, “Please let me run and tell the king the good news that the LORD has avenged him of his enemies.”
9018020	But Joab replied, “You are not the man to take good news today. You may do it another day, but you must not do so today, because the king’s son is dead.”
9018021	So Joab said to a Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen.” The Cushite bowed to Joab and took off running.
9018022	Ahimaaz son of Zadok, however, persisted and said to Joab, “No matter what, please let me also run behind the Cushite!” “My son,” Joab replied, “why do you want to run, since you will not receive a reward?”
9018023	“No matter what, I want to run!” he replied. “Then run!” Joab told him. So Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
9018024	Now David was sitting between the two gates when the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall, looked out, and saw a man running alone.
9018025	So he called out and told the king. “If he is alone,” the king replied, “he bears good news.” As the first runner drew near,
9018026	the watchman saw another man running, and he called out to the gatekeeper, “Look! Another man is running alone!” “This one also brings good news,” said the king.
9018027	The watchman said, “The first man appears to me to be running like Ahimaaz son of Zadok.” “This is a good man,” said the king. “He comes with good news.”
9018028	Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, “All is well!” And he bowed facedown before the king. He continued, “Blessed be the LORD your God! He has delivered up the men who raised their hands against my lord the king.”
9018029	The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And Ahimaaz replied, “When Joab sent the king’s servant and your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I do not know what it was.”
9018030	“Move aside,” said the king, “and stand here.” So he stepped aside.
9018031	Just then the Cushite came and said, “May my lord the king hear the good news: Today the LORD has avenged you of all who rose up against you!”
9018032	The king asked the Cushite, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And the Cushite replied, “May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you to harm you be like that young man.”
9018033	The king was shaken and went up to the chamber over the gate and wept. And as he walked, he cried out, “O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you, O Absalom, my son, my son!”
9019001	Then it was reported to Joab, “The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom.”
9019002	And that day’s victory was turned into mourning for all the people, because on that day they were told, “The king is grieving over his son.”
9019003	So they returned to the city quietly that day, as people steal away in humiliation after fleeing a battle.
9019004	But the king covered his face and cried out at the top of his voice, “O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!”
9019005	Then Joab went into the house and said to the king, “Today you have disgraced all your servants who have saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters, of your wives, and of your concubines.
9019006	You love those who hate you and hate those who love you! For you have made it clear today that the commanders and soldiers mean nothing to you. I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, it would have pleased you!
9019007	Now therefore get up! Go out and speak comfort to your servants, for I swear by the LORD that if you do not go out, not a man will remain with you tonight. This will be worse for you than all the adversity that has befallen you from your youth until now!”

10006001	In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, the second month, he began to build the house of the LORD.
10006002	The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
10006003	The portico at the front of the main hall of the temple was twenty cubits long, extending across the width of the temple and projecting out ten cubits in front of the temple.
10006004	He also had narrow windows framed high in the temple.

10006006	The bottom floor was five cubits wide, the middle floor six cubits, and the third floor seven cubits. He also placed offset ledges around the outside of the temple, so that nothing would be inserted into its walls.
10006007	The temple was constructed using finished stones cut at the quarry, so that no hammer or chisel or any other iron tool was heard in the temple while it was being built.
10006008	The entrance to the bottom floor was on the south side of the temple. A stairway led up to the middle level, and from there to the third floor.
10006009	So Solomon built the temple and finished it, roofing it with beams and planks of cedar.
10006010	He built chambers all along the temple, each five cubits high and attached to the temple with beams of cedar.
10006011	Then the word of the LORD came to Solomon, saying:
10006012	“As for this temple you are building, if you walk in My statutes, carry out My ordinances, and keep all My commandments by walking in them, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David.
10006013	And I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel.”
10006014	So Solomon built the temple and finished it.
10006015	He lined the interior walls with cedar paneling from the floor of the temple to the ceiling, and he covered the floor with cypress boards.
10006016	He partitioned off the twenty cubits at the rear of the temple with cedar boards from floor to ceiling to form within the temple an inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
10006017	And the main hall in front of this room was forty cubits long.
10006018	The cedar paneling inside the temple was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar; not a stone could be seen.
10006019	Solomon also prepared the inner sanctuary within the temple to set the ark of the covenant of the LORD there.
10006020	The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold, and he also overlaid the altar of cedar.
10006021	So Solomon overlaid the inside of the temple with pure gold, and he extended gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which was overlaid with gold.
10006022	So he overlaid with gold the whole interior of the temple, until everything was completely finished. He also overlaid with gold the entire altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary.
10006023	In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim, each ten cubits high, out of olive wood.
10006024	One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, and the other wing was five cubits long as well. So the full wingspan was ten cubits.
10006025	The second cherub also measured ten cubits; both cherubim had the same size and shape,
10006026	and the height of each cherub was ten cubits.
10006027	And he placed the cherubim inside the innermost room of the temple. Since their wings were spread out, the wing of the first cherub touched one wall, while the wing of the second cherub touched the other wall, and in the middle of the room their wingtips touched.
10006028	He also overlaid the cherubim with gold.
10006029	Then he carved the walls all around the temple, in both the inner and outer sanctuaries, with carved engravings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
