10006033	In the same way he made four-sided doorposts of olive wood for the sanctuary entrance.
10006034	The two doors were made of cypress wood, and each had two folding panels.
10006035	He carved into them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and he overlaid them with gold hammered evenly over the carvings.
10006036	Solomon built the inner courtyard with three rows of dressed stone and one row of trimmed cedar beams.
10006037	The foundation of the house of the LORD was laid in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign, in the month of Ziv.
10006038	In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, the eighth month, the temple was finished in every detail and according to every specification. So he built the temple in seven years.
10007001	Solomon, however, took thirteen years to complete the construction of his entire palace.
10007002	He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, with four rows of cedar pillars supporting the cedar beams.
10007003	The house was roofed with cedar above the beams that rested on the pillars—forty-five beams, fifteen per row.
10007004	There were three rows of high windows facing one another in three tiers.
10007005	All the doorways had rectangular frames, with the openings facing one another in three tiers.
10007006	Solomon made his colonnade fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide, with a portico in front of it and a canopy with pillars in front of the portico.
10007007	In addition, he built a hall for the throne, the Hall of Justice, where he was to judge. It was paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling.
10007008	And the palace where Solomon would live, set further back, was of similar construction. He also made a palace like this hall for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had married.
10007009	All these buildings were constructed with costly stones, cut to size and trimmed with saws inside and out from the foundation to the eaves, and from the outside to the great courtyard.
10007010	The foundations were laid with large, costly stones, some ten cubits long and some eight cubits long.
10007011	Above these were costly stones, cut to size, and cedar beams.
10007012	The great courtyard was surrounded by three rows of dressed stone and a row of trimmed cedar beams, as were the inner courtyard and portico of the house of the LORD.
10007013	Now King Solomon sent to bring Huram from Tyre.
10007014	He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze. Huram had great skill, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of bronze work. So he came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.
10007015	He cast two pillars of bronze, each eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference.
10007016	He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on top of the pillars, each capital five cubits high.
10007017	For the capitals on top of the pillars he made a network of lattice, with wreaths of chainwork, seven for each capital.
10007018	Likewise, he made the pillars with two rows of pomegranates around each grating to cover each capital atop the pillars.
10007019	And the capitals atop the pillars in the portico were shaped like lilies, four cubits high.
10007020	On the capitals of both pillars, just above the rounded projection next to the network, were the two hundred pomegranates in rows encircling each capital.
10007021	Thus he set up the pillars at the portico of the temple. The pillar to the south he named Jachin, and the pillar to the north he named Boaz.
10007022	And the tops of the pillars were shaped like lilies. So the work of the pillars was completed.
10007023	He also made the Sea of cast metal. It was circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.
10007024	Below the rim, ornamental buds encircled it, ten per cubit all the way around the Sea, cast in two rows as a part of the Sea.
10007025	The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea rested on them, with all their hindquarters toward the center.
10007026	It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold two thousand baths.
10007027	In addition, he made ten movable stands of bronze, each four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.
10007028	This was the design of the stands: They had side panels attached to uprights,
10007029	and on the panels between the uprights were lions, oxen, and cherubim. On the uprights was a pedestal above, and below the lions and oxen were wreaths of beveled work.
10007030	Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles and a basin resting on four supports, with wreaths at each side.
10007031	The opening to each stand inside the crown at the top was one cubit deep, with a round opening like the design of a pedestal, a cubit and a half wide. And around its opening were engravings, but the panels of the stands were square, not round.
10007032	There were four wheels under the panels, and the axles of the wheels were attached to the stand; each wheel was a cubit and a half in diameter.
10007033	The wheels were made like chariot wheels; their axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were all of cast metal.
10007034	Each stand had four handles, one for each corner, projecting from the stand.
10007035	At the top of each stand was a circular band half a cubit high. The supports and panels were cast as a unit with the top of the stand.
10007036	He engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees on the surfaces of the supports and panels, wherever each had space, with wreaths all around.
10007037	In this way he made the ten stands, each with the same casting, dimensions, and shape.
10007038	He also made ten bronze basins, each holding forty baths and measuring four cubits across, one basin for each of the ten stands.
10007039	He set five stands on the south side of the temple and five on the north, and he put the Sea on the south side, at the southeast corner of the temple.
10007040	Additionally, Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished all the work that he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of the LORD:
10007041	the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals atop the pillars; the two sets of network covering both bowls of the capitals atop the pillars;
10007042	the four hundred pomegranates for the two sets of network (two rows of pomegranates for each network covering both the bowl-shaped capitals atop the pillars);
10007043	the ten stands; the ten basins on the stands;
10007044	the Sea; the twelve oxen underneath the Sea;
10007045	and the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. All the articles that Huram made for King Solomon in the house of the LORD were made of burnished bronze.
10007046	The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zarethan.
10007047	Solomon left all these articles unweighed, because there were so many. The weight of the bronze could not be determined.
10007048	Solomon also made all the furnishings for the house of the LORD: the golden altar; the golden table on which was placed the Bread of the Presence;
10007049	the lampstands of pure gold in front of the inner sanctuary, five on the right side and five on the left; the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs;
10007050	the pure gold basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, and censers; and the gold hinges for the doors of the inner temple (that is, the Most Holy Place) as well as for the doors of the main hall of the temple.
10007051	So all the work that King Solomon had performed for the house of the LORD was completed. Then Solomon brought in the items his father David had dedicated—the silver, the gold, and the furnishings—and he placed them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
10008001	At that time Solomon assembled before him in Jerusalem the elders of Israel—all the tribal heads and family leaders of the Israelites—to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Zion, the City of David.
10008002	And all the men of Israel came together to King Solomon at the feast in the seventh month, the month of Ethanim.
10008003	When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the priests took up the ark,
10008004	and they brought up the ark of the LORD and the Tent of Meeting with all its sacred furnishings. So the priests and Levites carried them up.
10008005	There, before the ark, King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel who had assembled with him sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
10008006	Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
10008007	For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and overshadowed the ark and its poles.
10008008	The poles extended far enough that their ends were visible from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside the Holy Place; and they are there to this day.
10008009	There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the LORD had made a covenant with the Israelites after they had come out of the land of Egypt.
10008010	And when the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD
10008011	so that the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud. For the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
10008012	Then Solomon declared: “The LORD has said that He would dwell in the thick cloud.
10008013	I have indeed built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever.”
10008014	And as the whole assembly of Israel stood there, the king turned around and blessed them all
10008015	and said: “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has fulfilled with His own hand what He spoke with His mouth to my father David, saying,
10008016	‘Since the day I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel in which to build a house so that My Name would be there. But I have chosen David to be over My people Israel.’
10008017	Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
10008018	But the LORD said to my father David, ‘Since it was in your heart to build a house for My Name, you have done well to have this in your heart.
10008019	Nevertheless, you are not the one to build it; but your son, your own offspring, will build the house for My Name.’
10008020	Now the LORD has fulfilled the word that He spoke. I have succeeded my father David, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised. I have built the house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
10008021	And there I have provided a place for the ark, which contains the covenant of the LORD that He made with our fathers when He brought them out of the land of Egypt.”
10008022	Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel, spread out his hands toward heaven,
10008023	and said: “O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven above or on earth below, keeping Your covenant of loving devotion with Your servants who walk before You with all their hearts.
10008024	You have kept Your promise to Your servant, my father David. What You spoke with Your mouth You have fulfilled with Your hand this day.
10008025	Therefore now, O LORD, God of Israel, keep for Your servant, my father David, what You promised when You said: ‘You will never fail to have a man to sit before Me on the throne of Israel, if only your descendants guard their way to walk before Me as you have done.’
10008026	And now, O God of Israel, please confirm what You promised to Your servant, my father David.
10008027	But will God indeed dwell upon the earth? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.
10008028	Yet regard the prayer and plea of Your servant, O LORD my God, so that You may hear the cry and the prayer that Your servant is praying before You today.
10008029	May Your eyes be open toward this temple night and day, toward the place of which You said, ‘My Name shall be there,’ so that You may hear the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
10008030	Hear the plea of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. May You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place. May You hear and forgive.
10008031	When a man sins against his neighbor and is required to take an oath, and he comes to take an oath before Your altar in this temple,
10008032	then may You hear from heaven and act. May You judge Your servants, condemning the wicked man by bringing down on his own head what he has done, and justifying the righteous man by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
10008033	When Your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they return to You and confess Your name, praying and pleading with You in this temple,
10008034	then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel. May You restore them to the land You gave to their fathers.
10008035	When the skies are shut and there is no rain because Your people have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your name, and they turn from their sins because You have afflicted them,
10008036	then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Israel, so that You may teach them the good way in which they should walk. May You send rain on the land that You gave Your people as an inheritance.
10008037	When famine or plague comes upon the land, or blight or mildew or locusts or grasshoppers, or when their enemy besieges them in their cities, whatever plague or sickness may come,
10008038	then may whatever prayer or petition Your people Israel make—each knowing his own afflictions and spreading out his hands toward this temple—
10008039	be heard by You from heaven, Your dwelling place. And may You forgive and act, and repay each man according to all his ways, since You know his heart—for You alone know the hearts of all men—
10008040	so that they may fear You all the days they live in the land that You gave to our fathers.
10008041	And as for the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of Your name—
10008042	for they will hear of Your great name and mighty hand and outstretched arm—when he comes and prays toward this temple,
10008043	then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to You. Then all the peoples of the earth will know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel, and they will know that this house I have built is called by Your Name.
10008044	When Your people go to war against their enemies, wherever You send them, and when they pray to the LORD in the direction of the city You have chosen and the house I have built for Your Name,
10008045	then may You hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and may You uphold their cause.
10008046	When they sin against You—for there is no one who does not sin—and You become angry with them and deliver them to an enemy who takes them as captives to his own land, whether far or near,
10008047	and when they come to their senses in the land to which they were taken, and they repent and plead with You in the land of their captors, saying, ‘We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly,’
10008048	and when they return to You with all their heart and soul in the land of the enemies who took them captive, and when they pray to You in the direction of the land that You gave to their fathers, the city You have chosen, and the house I have built for Your Name,
10008049	then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, their prayer and petition, and may You uphold their cause.
10008050	May You forgive Your people who have sinned against You and all the transgressions they have committed against You, and may You grant them compassion in the eyes of their captors to show them mercy.
10008051	For they are Your people and Your inheritance; You brought them out of Egypt, out of the furnace for iron.
10008052	May Your eyes be open to the pleas of Your servant and of Your people Israel, and may You listen to them whenever they call to You.
10008053	For You, O Lord GOD, have set them apart from all the peoples of the earth as Your inheritance, as You spoke through Your servant Moses when You brought our fathers out of Egypt.”
10008054	Now when Solomon had finished praying this entire prayer and petition to the LORD, he got up before the altar of the LORD, where he had been kneeling with his hands spread out toward heaven.
10008055	And he stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice, saying:
10008056	“Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to His people Israel according to all that He promised. Not one word has failed of all the good promises He made through His servant Moses.
10008057	May the LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers. May He never leave us or forsake us.
10008058	May He incline our hearts to Himself, to walk in all His ways and to keep the commandments and statutes and ordinances He commanded our fathers.
10008059	And may these words with which I have made my petition before the LORD be near to the LORD our God day and night, so that He may uphold the cause of His servant and of His people Israel as each day requires,
10008060	so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God. There is no other!
10008061	So let your heart be fully devoted to the LORD our God, as it is this day, to walk in His statutes and to keep His commandments.”
10008062	Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the LORD.
10008063	And Solomon offered as peace offerings to the LORD 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. So the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD.
10008064	On that same day the king consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, and there he offered the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings, since the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to contain all these offerings.
10008065	So at that time Solomon and all Israel with him—a great assembly of people from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt—kept the feast before the LORD our God for seven days and seven more days—fourteen days in all.
10008066	On the fifteenth day Solomon sent the people away. So they blessed the king and went home, joyful and glad in heart for all the good things that the LORD had done for His servant David and for His people Israel.
10009001	Now when Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and had achieved all that he had desired to do,
10009002	the LORD appeared to him a second time, as He had appeared to him at Gibeon.
10009003	And the LORD said to him: “I have heard your prayer and petition before Me. I have consecrated this temple, which you have built, by putting My Name there forever; My eyes and My heart will be there for all time.
10009004	And as for you, if you walk before Me as your father David walked, with a heart of integrity and uprightness, doing all I have commanded you, and if you keep My statutes and ordinances,
10009005	then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever, as I promised your father David when I said, ‘You will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.’
10009006	But if indeed you or your sons turn away from following Me and do not keep the commandments and statutes I have set before you, and if you go off to serve and worship other gods,
10009007	then I will cut off Israel from the land that I have given them, and I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name. Then Israel will become an object of scorn and ridicule among all peoples.
10009008	And when this temple has become a heap of rubble, all who pass by it will be appalled and will hiss and say, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?’
10009009	And others will answer, ‘Because they have forsaken the LORD their God who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them—because of this, the LORD has brought all this disaster upon them.’”
10009010	Now at the end of the twenty years during which Solomon built these two houses, the house of the LORD and the royal palace,
10009011	King Solomon gave twenty towns in the land of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold for his every desire.
10009012	So Hiram went out from Tyre to inspect the towns that Solomon had given him, but he was not pleased with them.
10009013	“What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” asked Hiram, and he called them the Land of Cabul, as they are called to this day.
10009014	And Hiram had sent the king 120 talents of gold.
10009015	This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon imposed to build the house of the LORD, his own palace, the supporting terraces, and the wall of Jerusalem, as well as Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
10009016	Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer. He had set it on fire, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.

10009020	As for all the people who remained of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites (the people who were not Israelites)—
10009021	their descendants who remained in the land, those whom the Israelites were unable to devote to destruction —Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day.
10009022	But Solomon did not consign any of the Israelites to slavery, because they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
10009023	They were also the chief officers over Solomon’s projects: 550 supervisors over the people who did the work.
10009024	As soon as Pharaoh’s daughter had come up from the City of David to the palace that Solomon had built for her, he built the supporting terraces.

10010001	Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to test him with difficult questions.
10010002	She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large caravan—with camels bearing spices, gold in great abundance, and precious stones. And she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was on her mind.
10010003	And Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for the king to explain.

10010015	not including the revenue from the merchants, traders, and all the Arabian kings and governors of the land.

10010019	The throne had six steps, and its back had a rounded top. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, with a lion standing beside each armrest.

10010021	All King Solomon’s drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. There was no silver, because it was accounted as nothing in the days of Solomon.

10010023	So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.

10010025	Year after year, each visitor would bring his tribute: articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
10010026	Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.
10010027	The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.
10010028	Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.
10010029	A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Likewise, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.
10011001	King Solomon, however, loved many foreign women along with the daughter of Pharaoh—women of Moab, Ammon, Edom, and Sidon, as well as Hittite women.
10011002	These women were from the nations about which the LORD had told the Israelites, “You must not intermarry with them, for surely they will turn your hearts after their gods.” Yet Solomon clung to these women in love.

10011014	Then the LORD raised up against Solomon an adversary, Hadad the Edomite, from the royal line of Edom.

10011019	There Hadad found such great favor in the sight of Pharaoh that he gave to him in marriage the sister of Queen Tahpenes, his own wife.
10011020	And the sister of Tahpenes bore Hadad a son named Genubath. Tahpenes herself weaned him in Pharaoh’s palace, and Genubath lived there among the sons of Pharaoh.

10011022	But Pharaoh asked him, “What have you lacked here with me that you suddenly want to go back to your own country?” “Nothing,” Hadad replied, “but please let me go.”
10011023	And God raised up against Solomon another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah,

10011026	Now Jeroboam son of Nebat was an Ephraimite from Zeredah whose mother was a widow named Zeruah. Jeroboam was a servant of Solomon, but he rebelled against the king,
10011027	and this is the account of his rebellion against the king. Solomon had built the supporting terraces and repaired the gap in the wall of the city of his father David.
10011028	Now Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor. So when Solomon noticed that the young man was industrious, he put him in charge of the whole labor force of the house of Joseph.
10011029	During that time, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam on the road as he was going out of Jerusalem. Now Ahijah had wrapped himself in a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open field.

10011031	and said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Behold, I will tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten tribes.
10011032	But one tribe will remain for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.
10011033	For they have forsaken Me to worship Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in My ways, nor done what is right in My eyes, nor kept My statutes and judgments, as Solomon’s father David did.
10011034	Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom out of Solomon’s hand, because I have made him ruler all the days of his life for the sake of David My servant, whom I chose because he kept My commandments and statutes.
10011035	But I will take ten tribes of the kingdom from the hand of his son and give them to you.
10011036	I will give one tribe to his son, so that My servant David will always have a lamp before Me in Jerusalem, the city where I chose to put My Name.
10011037	But as for you, I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your heart desires, and you will be king over Israel.
10011038	If you listen to all that I command you, walk in My ways, and do what is right in My sight in order to keep My statutes and commandments as My servant David did, then I will be with you. I will build you a lasting dynasty just as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
10011039	Because of this, I will humble David’s descendants—but not forever.’”
10011040	Solomon therefore sought to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, where he remained until the death of Solomon.
10011041	As for the rest of the acts of Solomon—all that he did, as well as his wisdom—are they not written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon?
10011042	Thus the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
10011043	And Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David. And his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
10012001	Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had gone there to make him king.
10012002	When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about this, he was still in Egypt where he had fled from King Solomon and had been living ever since.
10012003	So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam and said,
10012004	“Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you must lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”
10012005	Rehoboam answered, “Go away for three days and then return to me.” So the people departed.
10012006	Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.
10012007	They replied, “If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
10012008	But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
10012009	He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
10012010	The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you must make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
10012011	Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.’”
10012012	After three days, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
10012013	And the king answered the people harshly. He rejected the advice of the elders
10012014	and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”
10012015	So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from the LORD, to fulfill the word He had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite.
10012016	When all Israel saw that the king had refused to listen to them, they answered the king: “What portion do we have in David, and what inheritance in the son of Jesse? To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!” So the Israelites went home,
10012017	but Rehoboam still reigned over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.
10012018	Then King Rehoboam sent out Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem.
10012019	So to this day Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David.
10012020	When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they summoned him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah followed the house of David.
10012021	And when Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mobilized the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin—180,000 chosen warriors—to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
10012022	But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God:
10012023	“Tell Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah, all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and the rest of the people
10012024	that this is what the LORD says: ‘You are not to go up and fight against your brothers, the Israelites. Each of you must return home, for this is My doing.’” So they listened to the word of the LORD and turned back according to the word of the LORD.
10012025	Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. And from there he went out and built Penuel.
10012026	Jeroboam said in his heart, “Now the kingdom might revert to the house of David.
10012027	If these people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the LORD at Jerusalem, their hearts will return to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah; then they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.”
10012028	After seeking advice, the king made two golden calves and said to the people, “Going up to Jerusalem is too much for you. Here, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.”
10012029	One calf he set up in Bethel, and the other in Dan.
10012030	And this thing became a sin; the people walked as far as Dan to worship before one of the calves.
10012031	Jeroboam also built shrines on the high places and appointed from every class of people priests who were not Levites.
10012032	And Jeroboam ordained a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the feast that was in Judah, and he offered sacrifices on the altar; he made this offering in Bethel to sacrifice to the calves he had set up, and he installed priests in Bethel for the high places he had set up.
10012033	On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a month of his own choosing, Jeroboam offered sacrifices on the altar he had set up in Bethel. So he ordained a feast for the Israelites, offered sacrifices on the altar, and burned incense.
10013001	Suddenly, as Jeroboam was standing beside the altar to burn incense, there came a man of God from Judah to Bethel by the word of the LORD.
10013002	And he cried out against the altar by the word of the LORD, “O altar, O altar, this is what the LORD says: ‘A son named Josiah will be born to the house of David, and upon you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense upon you, and human bones will be burned upon you.’”
10013003	That day the man of God gave a sign, saying, “The LORD has spoken this sign: ‘Surely the altar will be split apart, and the ashes upon it will be poured out.’”
10013004	Now when King Jeroboam, who was at the altar in Bethel, heard the word that the man of God had cried out against it, he stretched out his hand and said, “Seize him!” But the hand he stretched out toward him withered, so that he could not pull it back.
10013005	And the altar was split apart, and the ashes poured out, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.
10013006	Then the king responded to the man of God, “Intercede with the LORD your God and pray for me that my hand may be restored.” So the man of God interceded with the LORD, and the king’s hand was restored to him as it was before.
10013007	Then the king said to the man of God, “Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward.”
10013008	But the man of God replied, “If you were to give me half your possessions, I still would not go with you, nor would I eat bread or drink water in this place.
10013009	For this is what I was commanded by the word of the LORD: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water or return by the way you came.’”
10013010	So the man of God went another way and did not return by the way he had come to Bethel.
10013011	Now a certain old prophet was living in Bethel, and his sons came and told him all the deeds that the man of God had done that day in Bethel. They also told their father the words that the man had spoken to the king.
10013012	“Which way did he go?” their father asked. And his sons showed him the way taken by the man of God, who had come from Judah.
10013013	So the prophet said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” Then they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it
10013014	and went after the man of God. He found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?” “I am,” he replied.
10013015	So the prophet said to the man of God, “Come home with me and eat some bread.”
10013016	But the man replied, “I cannot go home with you, and I will not eat bread or drink water with you in this place.
10013017	For I have been told by the word of the LORD: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water there or return by the way you came.’”
10013018	Then the prophet replied, “I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the LORD, saying, ‘Bring him back with you to your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water.’” The old prophet was lying to him,
10013019	but the man of God went back with him, ate bread in his house, and drank water.
10013020	While they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back,
10013021	and the prophet cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Because you have defied the word of the LORD and have not kept the commandment that the LORD your God gave you,
10013022	but you went back and ate bread and drank water in the place where He told you not to do so, your body shall never reach the tomb of your fathers.’”
10013023	And after the man of God had finished eating and drinking, the old prophet who had brought him back saddled the donkey for him.
10013024	As he went on his way, a lion met him on the road and killed him, and his body was left lying in the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it.
10013025	And there were men passing by who saw the body lying in the road with the lion standing beside it, and they went and reported this in the city where the old prophet lived.
10013026	When the prophet who had brought him back from his journey heard this, he said, “It is the man of God who disobeyed the command of the LORD. Therefore the LORD has delivered him to the lion, and it has mauled him and killed him, according to the word that the LORD had spoken to him.”
10013027	Then the old prophet instructed his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” So they saddled it,
10013028	and he went and found the body lying in the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it. The lion had not eaten the body or mauled the donkey.
10013029	So the old prophet lifted up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back to his own city to mourn for him and bury him.
10013030	Then he laid the body in his own tomb, and they lamented over him, “Oh, my brother!”
10013031	After he had buried him, the prophet said to his sons, “When I die, you must bury me in the tomb where the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones,
10013032	for the message that he cried out by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel and against all the shrines on the high places in the cities of Samaria will surely come to pass.”
10013033	Even after these events, Jeroboam did not repent of his evil ways, but again he appointed priests for the high places from every class of people. He ordained anyone who desired to be a priest of the high places.
10013034	And this was the sin of the house of Jeroboam that led to its extermination and destruction from the face of the earth.
10014001	At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam became ill,

10014016	So He will give Israel over on account of the sins Jeroboam has committed and has caused Israel to commit.”

10014021	Meanwhile, Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel in which to put His Name. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite.
10014022	And Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD, and by the sins they committed they provoked Him to jealous anger more than all their fathers had done.
10014023	They also built for themselves high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.

10014028	And whenever the king entered the house of the LORD, the guards would bear the shields, and later they would return them to the guardroom.
10014029	As for the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, along with all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

10015001	In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king of Judah,

10017001	Now Elijah the Tishbite, who was among the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except at my word!”

10017006	The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening, and he would drink from the brook.
10017007	Some time later, however, the brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land.
10017008	Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah:
10017009	“Get up and go to Zarephath of Sidon, and stay there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.”
10017010	So Elijah got up and went to Zarephath. When he arrived at the city gate, there was a widow gathering sticks. Elijah called to her and said, “Please bring me a little water in a cup, so that I may drink.”
10017011	And as she was going to get it, he called to her and said, “Please bring me a piece of bread.”
10017012	But she replied, “As surely as the LORD your God lives, I have no bread—only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. Look, I am gathering a couple of sticks to take home and prepare a meal for myself and my son, so that we may eat it and die.”
10017013	“Do not be afraid,” Elijah said to her. “Go and do as you have said. But first make me a small cake of bread from what you have, and bring it out to me. Afterward, make some for yourself and your son,

10017015	So she went and did according to the word of Elijah, and there was food every day for Elijah and the woman and her household.
10017016	The jar of flour was not exhausted and the jug of oil did not run dry, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through Elijah.
10017017	Later, the son of the woman who owned the house became ill, and his sickness grew worse and worse, until no breath remained in him.

10017021	Then he stretched himself out over the child three times and cried out to the LORD, “O LORD my God, please let this boy’s life return to him!”

10018001	After a long time, in the third year of the drought, the word of the LORD came to Elijah: “Go and present yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain upon the face of the earth.”

10018024	Then you may call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the LORD. The God who answers by fire, He is God.” And all the people answered, “What you say is good.”
