17002008	And Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself as he sat among the ashes.
17002009	Then Job’s wife said to him, “Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die!”
17002010	“You speak as a foolish woman speaks,” he told her. “Should we accept from God only good and not adversity?” In all this, Job did not sin in what he said.
17002011	Now when Job’s three friends—Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite—heard about all this adversity that had come upon him, each of them came from his home, and they met together to go and sympathize with Job and comfort him.
17002012	When they lifted up their eyes from afar, they could barely recognize Job. They began to weep aloud, and each man tore his robe and threw dust in the air over his head.
17002013	Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights, but no one spoke a word to him because they saw how intense his suffering was.
17003001	After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
17003002	And this is what he said:
17003003	“May the day of my birth perish, and the night it was said, ‘A boy is conceived.’
17003004	If only that day had turned to darkness! May God above disregard it; may no light shine upon it.
17003005	May darkness and gloom reclaim it, and a cloud settle over it; may the blackness of the day overwhelm it.
17003006	If only darkness had taken that night away! May it not appear among the days of the year; may it never be entered in any of the months.
17003007	Behold, may that night be barren; may no joyful voice come into it.
17003008	May it be cursed by those who curse the day — those prepared to rouse Leviathan.
17003009	May its morning stars grow dark; may it wait in vain for daylight; may it not see the breaking of dawn.
17003010	For that night did not shut the doors of the womb to hide the sorrow from my eyes.
17003011	Why did I not perish at birth; why did I not die as I came from the womb?
17003012	Why were there knees to receive me, and breasts that I should be nursed?
17003013	For now I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest
17003014	with kings and counselors of the earth, who built for themselves cities now in ruins,
17003015	or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
17003016	Or why was I not hidden like a stillborn child, like an infant who never sees daylight?
17003017	There the wicked cease from raging, and there the weary find rest.
17003018	The captives enjoy their ease; they do not hear the voice of the oppressor.
17003019	Both small and great are there, and the slave is freed from his master.
17003020	Why is light given to the miserable, and life to the bitter of soul,
17003021	who long for death that does not come, and search for it like hidden treasure,
17003022	who rejoice and greatly exult when they reach the grave?
17003023	Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
17003024	I sigh when food is put before me, and my groans pour out like water.
17003025	For the thing I feared has overtaken me, and what I dreaded has befallen me.
17003026	I am not at ease or quiet; I have no rest, for trouble has come.”
17004001	Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
17004002	“If one ventures a word with you, will you be wearied? Yet who can keep from speaking?
17004003	Surely you have instructed many, and have strengthened their feeble hands.
17004004	Your words have steadied those who stumbled; you have braced the knees that were buckling.
17004005	But now trouble has come upon you, and you are weary. It strikes you, and you are dismayed.
17004006	Is your reverence not your confidence, and the uprightness of your ways your hope?
17004007	Consider now, I plead: Who, being innocent, has ever perished? Or where have the upright been destroyed?
17004008	As I have observed, those who plow iniquity and those who sow trouble reap the same.
17004009	By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of His anger they are consumed.
17004010	The lion may roar, and the fierce lion may growl, yet the teeth of the young lions are broken.
17004011	The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
17004012	Now a word came to me secretly; my ears caught a whisper of it.
17004013	In disquieting visions in the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
17004014	fear and trembling came over me and made all my bones shudder.
17004015	Then a spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body bristled.
17004016	It stood still, but I could not discern its appearance; a form loomed before my eyes, and I heard a whispering voice:
17004017	‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God, or a man more pure than his Maker?
17004018	If God puts no trust in His servants, and He charges His angels with error,
17004019	how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundations are in the dust, who can be crushed like a moth!
17004020	They are smashed to pieces from dawn to dusk; unnoticed, they perish forever.
17004021	Are not their tent cords pulled up, so that they die without wisdom?’
17005001	“Call out if you please, but who will answer? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
17005002	For resentment kills a fool, and envy slays the simple.
17005003	I have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly his house was cursed.
17005004	His sons are far from safety, crushed in court without a defender.
17005005	The hungry consume his harvest, taking it even from the thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.
17005006	For distress does not spring from the dust, and trouble does not sprout from the ground.
17005007	Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
17005008	However, if I were you, I would appeal to God and lay my cause before Him—
17005009	the One who does great and unsearchable things, wonders without number.
17005010	He gives rain to the earth and sends water upon the fields.
17005011	He sets the lowly on high, so that mourners are lifted to safety.
17005012	He thwarts the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands find no success.
17005013	He catches the wise in their craftiness, and sweeps away the plans of the cunning.
17005014	They encounter darkness by day and grope at noon as in the night.
17005015	He saves the needy from the sword in their mouth and from the clutches of the powerful.
17005016	So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.
17005017	Blessed indeed is the man whom God corrects; so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
17005018	For He wounds, but He also binds; He strikes, but His hands also heal.
17005019	He will rescue you from six calamities; no harm will touch you in seven.
17005020	In famine He will redeem you from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.
17005021	You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, and will not fear havoc when it comes.
17005022	You will laugh at destruction and famine, and need not fear the beasts of the earth.
17005023	For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.
17005024	You will know that your tent is secure, and find nothing amiss when inspecting your home.
17005025	You will know that your offspring will be many, your descendants like the grass of the earth.
17005026	You will come to the grave in full vigor, like a sheaf of grain gathered in season.
17005027	Indeed, we have investigated, and it is true! So hear it and know for yourself.”
17006001	Then Job replied:
17006002	“If only my grief could be weighed and placed with my calamity on the scales.
17006003	For then it would outweigh the sand of the seas— no wonder my words have been rash.
17006004	For the arrows of the Almighty have pierced me; my spirit drinks in their poison; the terrors of God are arrayed against me.
17006005	Does a wild donkey bray over fresh grass, or an ox low over its fodder?
17006006	Is tasteless food eaten without salt, or is there flavor in the white of an egg?
17006007	My soul refuses to touch them; they are loathsome food to me.
17006008	If only my request were granted and God would fulfill my hope:
17006009	that God would be willing to crush me, to unleash His hand and cut me off!
17006010	It still brings me comfort, and joy through unrelenting pain, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
17006011	What strength do I have, that I should still hope? What is my future, that I should be patient?
17006012	Is my strength like that of stone, or my flesh made of bronze?
17006013	Is there any help within me now that success is driven from me?
17006014	A despairing man should have the kindness of his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
17006015	But my brothers are as faithless as wadis, as seasonal streams that overflow,
17006016	darkened because of the ice and the inflow of melting snow,
17006017	but ceasing in the dry season and vanishing from their channels in the heat.
17006018	Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go into the wasteland and perish.
17006019	The caravans of Tema look for water; the travelers of Sheba hope to find it.
17006020	They are confounded because they had hoped; their arrival brings disappointment.
17006021	For now you are of no help; you see terror, and you are afraid.
17006022	Have I ever said, ‘Give me something; offer me a bribe from your wealth;
17006023	deliver me from the hand of the enemy; redeem me from the grasp of the ruthless’?
17006024	Teach me, and I will be silent. Help me understand how I have erred.
17006025	How painful are honest words! But what does your argument prove?
17006026	Do you intend to correct my words, and treat as wind my cry of despair?
17006027	You would even cast lots for an orphan and barter away your friend.
17006028	But now, please look at me. Would I lie to your face?
17006029	Reconsider; do not be unjust. Reconsider, for my righteousness is at stake.
17006030	Is there iniquity on my tongue? Can my mouth not discern malice?
17007001	“Is not man consigned to labor on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired hand?
17007002	Like a slave he longs for shade; like a hireling he waits for his wages.
17007003	So I am allotted months of futility, and nights of misery are appointed to me.
17007004	When I lie down I think: ‘When will I get up?’ But the night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn.
17007005	My flesh is clothed with worms and encrusted with dirt; my skin is cracked and festering.
17007006	My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle; they come to an end without hope.
17007007	Remember that my life is but a breath. My eyes will never again see happiness.
17007008	The eye that beholds me will no longer see me. You will look for me, but I will be no more.
17007009	As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so he who goes down to Sheol does not come back up.
17007010	He never returns to his house; his place remembers him no more.
17007011	Therefore I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
17007012	Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that You must keep me under guard?
17007013	When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,
17007014	then You frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions,
17007015	so that I would prefer strangling and death over my life in this body.
17007016	I loathe my life! I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
17007017	What is man that You should exalt him, that You should set Your heart upon him,
17007018	that You attend to him every morning, and test him every moment?
17007019	Will You never look away from me, or leave me alone to swallow my spittle?
17007020	If I have sinned, what have I done to You, O watcher of mankind? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to You?
17007021	Why do You not pardon my transgression and take away my iniquity? For soon I will lie down in the dust; You will seek me, but I will be no more.”
17008001	Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
17008002	“How long will you go on saying such things? The words of your mouth are a blustering wind.
17008003	Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?
17008004	When your children sinned against Him, He gave them over to their rebellion.
17008005	But if you would earnestly seek God and ask the Almighty for mercy,
17008006	if you are pure and upright, even now He will rouse Himself on your behalf and restore your righteous estate.
17008007	Though your beginnings were modest, your latter days will flourish.
17008008	Please inquire of past generations and consider the discoveries of their fathers.
17008009	For we were born yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are but a shadow.
17008010	Will they not teach you and tell you, and speak from their understanding?
17008011	Does papyrus grow where there is no marsh? Do reeds flourish without water?
17008012	While the shoots are still uncut, they dry up more quickly than grass.
17008013	Such is the destiny of all who forget God; so the hope of the godless will perish.
17008014	His confidence is fragile; his security is in a spider’s web.
17008015	He leans on his web, but it gives way; he holds fast, but it does not endure.
17008016	He is a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden.
17008017	His roots wrap around the rock heap; he looks for a home among the stones.
17008018	If he is uprooted from his place, it will disown him, saying, ‘I never saw you.’
17008019	Surely this is the joy of his way; yet others will spring from the dust.
17008020	Behold, God does not reject the blameless, nor will He strengthen the hand of evildoers.
17008021	He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy.
17008022	Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.”
17009001	Then Job answered:
17009002	“Yes, I know that it is so, but how can a mortal be righteous before God?
17009003	If one wished to contend with God, he could not answer Him one time out of a thousand.
17009004	God is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has resisted Him and prospered?
17009005	He moves mountains without their knowledge and overturns them in His anger.
17009006	He shakes the earth from its place, so that its foundations tremble.
17009007	He commands the sun not to shine; He seals off the stars.
17009008	He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.
17009009	He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion, of the Pleiades and the constellations of the south.
17009010	He does great things beyond searching out, and wonders without number.
17009011	Were He to pass by me, I would not see Him; were He to move, I would not recognize Him.
17009012	If He takes away, who can stop Him? Who dares to ask Him, ‘What are You doing?’
17009013	God does not restrain His anger; the helpers of Rahab cower beneath Him.
17009014	How then can I answer Him or choose my arguments against Him?
17009015	For even if I were right, I could not answer. I could only beg my Judge for mercy.
17009016	If I summoned Him and He answered me, I do not believe He would listen to my voice.
17009017	For He would crush me with a tempest and multiply my wounds without cause.
17009018	He does not let me catch my breath, but overwhelms me with bitterness.
17009019	If it is a matter of strength, He is indeed mighty! If it is a matter of justice, who can summon Him?
17009020	Even if I were righteous, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would declare me guilty.
17009021	Though I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life.
17009022	It is all the same, and so I say, ‘He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.’
17009023	When the scourge brings sudden death, He mocks the despair of the innocent.
17009024	The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He blindfolds its judges. If it is not He, then who is it?
17009025	My days are swifter than a runner; they flee without seeing good.
17009026	They sweep by like boats of papyrus, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
17009027	If I were to say, ‘I will forget my complaint and change my expression and smile,’
17009028	I would still dread all my sufferings; I know that You will not acquit me.
17009029	Since I am already found guilty, why should I labor in vain?
17009030	If I should wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with lye,
17009031	then You would plunge me into the pit, and even my own clothes would despise me.
17009032	For He is not a man like me, that I can answer Him, that we can take each other to court.
17009033	Nor is there a mediator between us, to lay his hand upon us both.
17009034	Let Him remove His rod from me, so that His terror will no longer frighten me.
17009035	Then I would speak without fear of Him. But as it is, I am on my own.
17010001	“I loathe my own life; I will express my complaint and speak in the bitterness of my soul.
17010002	I will say to God: Do not condemn me! Let me know why You prosecute me.
17010003	Does it please You to oppress me, to reject the work of Your hands and favor the schemes of the wicked?
17010004	Do You have eyes of flesh? Do You see as man sees?
17010005	Are Your days like those of a mortal, or Your years like those of a man,
17010006	that You should seek my iniquity and search out my sin—
17010007	though You know that I am not guilty, and there is no deliverance from Your hand?
17010008	Your hands shaped me and altogether formed me. Would You now turn and destroy me?
17010009	Please remember that You molded me like clay. Would You now return me to dust?
17010010	Did You not pour me out like milk, and curdle me like cheese?
17010011	You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
17010012	You have granted me life and loving devotion, and Your care has preserved my spirit.
17010013	Yet You concealed these things in Your heart, and I know that this was in Your mind:
17010014	If I sinned, You would take note, and would not acquit me of my iniquity.
17010015	If I am guilty, woe to me! And even if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head. I am full of shame and aware of my affliction.
17010016	Should I hold my head high, You would hunt me like a lion, and again display Your power against me.
17010017	You produce new witnesses against me and multiply Your anger toward me. Hardships assault me in wave after wave.
17010018	Why then did You bring me from the womb? Oh, that I had died, and no eye had seen me!
17010019	If only I had never come to be, but had been carried from the womb to the grave.
17010020	Are my days not few? Withdraw from me, that I may have a little comfort,
17010021	before I go—never to return— to a land of darkness and gloom,
17010022	to a land of utter darkness, of deep shadow and disorder, where even the light is like darkness.”
17011001	Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:
17011002	“Should this stream of words go unanswered and such a speaker be vindicated?
17011003	Should your babbling put others to silence? Will you scoff without rebuke?
17011004	You have said, ‘My doctrine is sound, and I am pure in Your sight.’
17011005	But if only God would speak and open His lips against you,
17011006	and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Know then that God exacts from you less than your iniquity deserves.
17011007	Can you fathom the deep things of God or discover the limits of the Almighty?
17011008	They are higher than the heavens—what can you do? They are deeper than Sheol—what can you know?
17011009	Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
17011010	If He comes along to imprison you, or convenes a court, who can stop Him?
17011011	Surely He knows the deceit of men. If He sees iniquity, does He not take note?
17011012	But a witless man can no more become wise than the colt of a wild donkey can be born a man!
17011013	As for you, if you direct your heart and lift up your hands to Him,
17011014	if you put away the iniquity in your hand, and allow no injustice to dwell in your tents,
17011015	then indeed you will lift up your face without blemish; you will stand firm and unafraid.
17011016	For you will forget your misery, recalling it only as waters gone by.
17011017	Your life will be brighter than noonday; its darkness will be like the morning.
17011018	You will be secure, because there is hope, and you will look around and lie down in safety.
17011019	You will lie down without fear, and many will court your favor.
17011020	But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; they will hope for their last breath.”
17012001	Then Job answered:
17012002	“Truly then you are the people with whom wisdom itself will die!
17012003	But I also have a mind; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know such things as these?
17012004	I am a laughingstock to my friends, though I called on God, and He answered. The righteous and upright man is a laughingstock.
17012005	The one at ease scorns misfortune as the fate of those whose feet are slipping.
17012006	The tents of robbers are safe, and those who provoke God are secure— those who carry their god in their hands.
17012007	But ask the animals, and they will instruct you; ask the birds of the air, and they will tell you.
17012008	Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; let the fish of the sea inform you.
17012009	Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
17012010	The life of every living thing is in His hand, as well as the breath of all mankind.
17012011	Does not the ear test words as the tongue tastes its food?
17012012	Wisdom is found with the elderly, and understanding comes with long life.
17012013	Wisdom and strength belong to God; counsel and understanding are His.
17012014	What He tears down cannot be rebuilt; the man He imprisons cannot be released.
17012015	If He holds back the waters, they dry up, and if He releases them, they overwhelm the land.
17012016	True wisdom and power belong to Him. The deceived and the deceiver are His.
17012017	He leads counselors away barefoot and makes fools of judges.
17012018	He loosens the bonds placed by kings and fastens a belt around their waists.
17012019	He leads priests away barefoot and overthrows the established.
17012020	He deprives the trusted of speech and takes away the discernment of elders.
17012021	He pours out contempt on nobles and disarms the mighty.
17012022	He reveals the deep things of darkness and brings deep shadows into light.
17012023	He makes nations great and destroys them; He enlarges nations, then disperses them.
17012024	He deprives the earth’s leaders of reason and makes them wander in a trackless wasteland.
17012025	They grope in the darkness without light; He makes them stagger like drunkards.
17013001	“Indeed, my eyes have seen all this; my ears have heard and understood.
17013002	What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.
17013003	Yet I desire to speak to the Almighty and argue my case before God.
17013004	You, however, smear with lies; you are all worthless physicians.
17013005	If only you would remain silent; for that would be your wisdom!
17013006	Hear now my argument, and listen to the plea of my lips.
17013007	Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf or speak deceitfully for Him?
17013008	Would you show Him partiality or argue in His defense?
17013009	Would it be well when He examined you? Could you deceive Him as you would deceive a man?
17013010	Surely He would rebuke you if you secretly showed partiality.
17013011	Would His majesty not terrify you? Would the dread of Him not fall upon you?
17013012	Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.
17013013	Be silent, and I will speak. Then let come to me what may.
17013014	Why do I put myself at risk and take my life in my own hands?
17013015	Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.
17013016	Moreover, this will be my salvation, for no godless man can appear before Him.
17013017	Listen carefully to my words; let my declaration ring in your ears.
17013018	See now, I have prepared my case; I know that I will be vindicated.
17013019	Can anyone indict me? If so, I will be silent and die.
17013020	Only grant these two things to me, so that I need not hide from You:
17013021	Withdraw Your hand from me, and do not let Your terror frighten me.
17013022	Then call me, and I will answer, or let me speak, and You can reply.
17013023	How many are my iniquities and sins? Reveal to me my transgression and sin.
17013024	Why do You hide Your face and consider me as Your enemy?
17013025	Would You frighten a windblown leaf? Would You chase after dry chaff?
17013026	For You record bitter accusations against me and bequeath to me the iniquities of my youth.
17013027	You put my feet in the stocks and stand watch over all my paths; You set a limit for the soles of my feet.
17013028	So man wastes away like something rotten, like a moth-eaten garment.
17014001	“Man, who is born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.
17014002	Like a flower, he comes forth, then withers away; like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure.
17014003	Do You open Your eyes to one like this? Will You bring him into judgment before You?
17014004	Who can bring out clean from unclean? No one!
17014005	Since his days are determined and the number of his months is with You, and since You have set limits that he cannot exceed,
17014006	look away from him and let him rest, so he can enjoy his day as a hired hand.
17014007	For there is hope for a tree: If it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its tender shoots will not fail.
17014008	If its roots grow old in the ground and its stump dies in the soil,
17014009	at the scent of water it will bud and put forth twigs like a sapling.
17014010	But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last, and where is he?
17014011	As water disappears from the sea and a river becomes parched and dry,
17014012	so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, he will not be awakened or roused from sleep.
17014013	If only You would hide me in Sheol and conceal me until Your anger has passed! If only You would appoint a time for me and then remember me!
17014014	When a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, until my renewal comes.
17014015	You will call, and I will answer; You will desire the work of Your hands.
17014016	For then You would count my steps, but would not keep track of my sin.
17014017	My transgression would be sealed in a bag, and You would cover over my iniquity.
17014018	But as a mountain erodes and crumbles and a rock is dislodged from its place,
17014019	as water wears away the stones and torrents wash away the soil, so You destroy a man’s hope.
17014020	You forever overpower him, and he passes on; You change his countenance and send him away.
17014021	If his sons receive honor, he does not know it; if they are brought low, he is unaware.
17014022	He feels only the pain of his own body and mourns only for himself.”
17015001	Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
17015002	“Does a wise man answer with empty counsel or fill his belly with the hot east wind?
17015003	Should he argue with useless words or speeches that serve no purpose?
17015004	But you even undermine the fear of God and hinder meditation before Him.
17015005	For your iniquity instructs your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.
17015006	Your own mouth, not mine, condemns you; your own lips testify against you.
17015007	Were you the first man ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
17015008	Do you listen in on the council of God or limit wisdom to yourself?
17015009	What do you know that we do not? What do you understand that is not clear to us?
17015010	Both the gray-haired and the aged are on our side— men much older than your father.
17015011	Are the consolations of God not enough for you, even words spoken gently to you?
17015012	Why has your heart carried you away, and why do your eyes flash,
17015013	so that you turn your spirit against God and pour such words from your mouth?
17015014	What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?
17015015	If God puts no trust in His holy ones, if even the heavens are not pure in His eyes,
17015016	how much less man, who is vile and corrupt, who drinks injustice like water?
17015017	Listen to me and I will inform you. I will describe what I have seen,
17015018	what was declared by wise men and was not concealed from their fathers,
17015019	to whom alone the land was given when no foreigner passed among them.
17015020	A wicked man writhes in pain all his days; only a few years are reserved for the ruthless.
17015021	Sounds of terror fill his ears; in his prosperity the destroyer attacks him.
17015022	He despairs of his return from darkness; he is marked for the sword.
17015023	He wanders about as food for vultures; he knows the day of darkness is at hand.
17015024	Distress and anguish terrify him, overwhelming him like a king poised to attack.
17015025	For he has stretched out his hand against God and has vaunted himself against the Almighty,
17015026	rushing headlong at Him with a thick, studded shield.
17015027	Though his face is covered with fat and his waistline bulges with flesh,
17015028	he will dwell in ruined cities, in abandoned houses destined to become rubble.
17015029	He will no longer be rich; his wealth will not endure. His possessions will not overspread the land.
17015030	He will not escape from the darkness; the flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God’s mouth will carry him away.
17015031	Let him not deceive himself with trust in emptiness, for emptiness will be his reward.
17015032	It will be paid in full before his time, and his branch will not flourish.
17015033	He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes, like an olive tree that sheds its blossoms.
17015034	For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of bribery.
17015035	They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb is pregnant with deceit.”
17016001	Then Job answered:
17016002	“I have heard many things like these; miserable comforters are you all.
17016003	Is there no end to your long-winded speeches? What provokes you to continue testifying?
17016004	I could also speak like you if you were in my place; I could heap up words against you and shake my head at you.
17016005	But I would encourage you with my mouth, and the consolation of my lips would bring relief.
17016006	Even if I speak, my pain is not relieved, and if I hold back, how will it go away?
17016007	Surely He has now exhausted me; You have devastated all my family.
17016008	You have bound me, and it has become a witness; my frailty rises up and testifies against me.
17016009	His anger has torn me and opposed me; He gnashes His teeth at me. My adversary pierces me with His eyes.
17016010	They open their mouths against me and strike my cheeks with contempt; they join together against me.
17016011	God has delivered me to unjust men; He has thrown me to the clutches of the wicked.

17016013	His archers surround me. He pierces my kidneys without mercy and spills my gall on the ground.

17016016	My face is red with weeping, and deep shadows ring my eyes;

17016020	My friends are my scoffers as my eyes pour out tears to God.
17016021	Oh, that a man might plead with God as he pleads with his neighbor!
17016022	For when only a few years are past I will go the way of no return.
17017001	“My spirit is broken; my days are extinguished; the grave awaits me.
17017002	Surely mockers surround me, and my eyes must gaze at their rebellion.
17017003	Give me, I pray, the pledge You demand. Who else will be my guarantor?
17017004	You have closed their minds to understanding; therefore You will not exalt them.
17017005	If a man denounces his friends for a price, the eyes of his children will fail.
17017006	He has made me a byword among the people, a man in whose face they spit.
17017007	My eyes have grown dim with grief, and my whole body is but a shadow.
17017008	The upright are appalled at this, and the innocent are stirred against the godless.
17017009	Yet a righteous one holds to his way, and the one with clean hands grows stronger.
17017010	But come back and try again, all of you. For I will not find a wise man among you.
17017011	My days have passed; my plans are broken off— even the desires of my heart.
17017012	They have turned night into day, making light seem near in the face of darkness.
17017013	If I look for Sheol as my home, if I spread out my bed in darkness,
17017014	and say to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ and to the worm, ‘My mother,’ or ‘My sister,’
17017015	where then is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?
17017016	Will it go down to the gates of Sheol? Will we go down together into the dust?”
17018001	Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
17018002	“How long until you end these speeches? Show some sense, and then we can talk.
17018003	Why are we regarded as cattle, as stupid in your sight?
17018004	You who tear yourself in anger— should the earth be forsaken on your account, or the rocks be moved from their place?
17018005	Indeed, the lamp of the wicked is extinguished; the flame of his fire does not glow.
17018006	The light in his tent grows dark, and the lamp beside him goes out.
17018007	His vigorous stride is shortened, and his own schemes trip him up.
17018008	For his own feet lead him into a net, and he wanders into its mesh.
17018009	A trap seizes his heel; a snare grips him.
17018010	A noose is hidden in the ground, and a trap lies in his path.
17018011	Terrors frighten him on every side and harass his every step.
17018012	His strength is depleted, and calamity is ready at his side.
17018013	It devours patches of his skin; the firstborn of death devours his limbs.

17018017	The memory of him perishes from the earth, and he has no name in the land.
17018018	He is driven from light into darkness and is chased from the inhabited world.
17018019	He has no offspring or posterity among his people, no survivor where he once lived.
17018020	Those in the west are appalled at his fate, while those in the east tremble in horror.
17018021	Surely such is the dwelling of the wicked and the place of one who does not know God.”
17019001	Then Job answered:
17019002	“How long will you torment me and crush me with your words?
17019003	Ten times now you have reproached me; you shamelessly mistreat me.
17019004	Even if I have truly gone astray, my error concerns me alone.
17019005	If indeed you would exalt yourselves above me and use my disgrace against me,
17019006	then understand that it is God who has wronged me and drawn His net around me.
17019007	Though I cry out, ‘Violence!’ I get no response; though I call for help, there is no justice.
17019008	He has blocked my way so I cannot pass; He has veiled my paths with darkness.
17019009	He has stripped me of my honor and removed the crown from my head.
17019010	He tears me down on every side until I am gone; He uproots my hope like a tree.
17019011	His anger burns against me, and He counts me among His enemies.
17019012	His troops advance together; they construct a ramp against me and encamp around my tent.
17019013	He has removed my brothers from me; my acquaintances have abandoned me.
17019014	My kinsmen have failed me, and my friends have forgotten me.
17019015	My guests and maidservants count me as a stranger; I am a foreigner in their sight.
17019016	I call for my servant, but he does not answer, though I implore him with my own mouth.
17019017	My breath is repulsive to my wife, and I am loathsome to my own family.
17019018	Even little boys scorn me; when I appear, they deride me.
17019019	All my best friends despise me, and those I love have turned against me.
17019020	My skin and flesh cling to my bones; I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
17019021	Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me.
17019022	Why do you persecute me as God does? Will you never get enough of my flesh?
17019023	I wish that my words were recorded and inscribed in a book,
17019024	by an iron stylus on lead, or chiseled in stone forever.
17019025	But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end He will stand upon the earth.
17019026	Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.
17019027	I will see Him for myself; my eyes will behold Him, and not as a stranger. How my heart yearns within me!
17019028	If you say, ‘Let us persecute him, since the root of the matter lies with him,’
17019029	then you should fear the sword yourselves, because wrath brings punishment by the sword, so that you may know there is a judgment.”
17020001	Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:
17020002	“So my anxious thoughts compel me to answer, because of the turmoil within me.
17020003	I have heard a rebuke that insults me, and my understanding prompts a reply.
17020004	Do you not know that from antiquity, since man was placed on the earth,
17020005	the triumph of the wicked has been brief and the joy of the godless momentary?
17020006	Though his arrogance reaches the heavens, and his head touches the clouds,
17020007	he will perish forever, like his own dung; those who had seen him will ask, ‘Where is he?’
17020008	He will fly away like a dream, never to be found; he will be chased away like a vision in the night.
17020009	The eye that saw him will see him no more, and his place will no longer behold him.
17020010	His sons will seek the favor of the poor, for his own hands must return his wealth.
17020011	The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie down with him in the dust.
17020012	Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he conceals it under his tongue,
17020013	though he cannot bear to let it go and keeps it in his mouth,
17020014	yet in his stomach his food sours into the venom of cobras within him.
17020015	He swallows wealth but vomits it out; God will force it from his stomach.
17020016	He will suck the poison of cobras; the fangs of a viper will kill him.
17020017	He will not enjoy the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and cream.
17020018	He must return the fruit of his labor without consuming it; he cannot enjoy the profits of his trading.
17020019	For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor; he has seized houses he did not build.
17020020	Because his appetite is never satisfied, he cannot escape with his treasure.
17020021	Nothing is left for him to consume; thus his prosperity will not endure.
17020022	In the midst of his plenty, he will be distressed; the full force of misery will come upon him.
17020023	When he has filled his stomach, God will vent His fury upon him, raining it down on him as he eats.
17020024	Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow will pierce him.
17020025	It is drawn out of his back, the gleaming point from his liver. Terrors come over him.
17020026	Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.
17020027	The heavens will expose his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.
17020028	The possessions of his house will be removed, flowing away on the day of God’s wrath.
17020029	This is the wicked man’s portion from God, the inheritance God has appointed him.”
17021001	Then Job answered:
17021002	“Listen carefully to my words; let this be your consolation to me.
17021003	Bear with me while I speak; then, after I have spoken, you may go on mocking.
17021004	Is my complaint against a man? Then why should I not be impatient?
17021005	Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth.
17021006	When I remember, terror takes hold, and my body trembles in horror.
17021007	Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?
17021008	Their descendants are established around them, and their offspring before their eyes.
17021009	Their homes are safe from fear; no rod of punishment from God is upon them.
17021010	Their bulls breed without fail; their cows bear calves and do not miscarry.
17021011	They send forth their little ones like a flock; their children skip about,
17021012	singing to the tambourine and lyre and making merry at the sound of the flute.
17021013	They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in peace.
17021014	Yet they say to God: ‘Leave us alone! For we have no desire to know Your ways.
17021015	Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him, and what would we gain if we pray to Him?’

17021018	Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?

17021020	Let his eyes see his own destruction; let him drink for himself the wrath of the Almighty.

17021022	Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since He judges those on high?
17021023	One man dies full of vigor, completely secure and at ease.

17021025	Yet another man dies in the bitterness of his soul, having never tasted prosperity.
17021026	But together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.
17021027	Behold, I know your thoughts full well, the schemes by which you would wrong me.

17021029	Have you never asked those who travel the roads? Do you not accept their reports?
17021030	Indeed, the evil man is spared from the day of calamity, delivered from the day of wrath.
17021031	Who denounces his behavior to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?
17021032	He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.
17021033	The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows behind him, and those before him are without number.
17021034	So how can you comfort me with empty words? For your answers remain full of falsehood.”
17022001	Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
17022002	“Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?
17022003	Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous? Does He profit if your ways are blameless?
17022004	Is it for your reverence that He rebukes you and enters into judgment against you?
17022005	Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless?
17022006	For you needlessly demanded security from your brothers and deprived the naked of their clothing.
17022007	You gave no water to the weary and withheld food from the famished,
17022008	while the land belonged to a mighty man, and a man of honor lived on it.
17022009	You sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless was crushed.
17022010	Therefore snares surround you, and sudden peril terrifies you;
17022011	it is so dark you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.
17022012	Is not God as high as the heavens? Look at the highest stars, how lofty they are!
17022013	Yet you say: ‘What does God know? Does He judge through thick darkness?

17022016	They were snatched away before their time, and their foundations were swept away by a flood.

17022019	The righteous see it and are glad; the innocent mock them:
17022020	‘Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire has consumed their excess.’
17022021	Reconcile now and be at peace with Him; thereby good will come to you.
17022022	Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.
17022023	If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you remove injustice from your tents
17022024	and consign your gold to the dust and the gold of Ophir to the stones of the ravines,

17022026	Surely then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
17022027	You will pray to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
17022028	Your decisions will be carried out, and light will shine on your ways.
17022029	When men are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’ then He will save the lowly.
17022030	He will deliver even one who is not innocent, rescuing him through the cleanness of your hands.”
17023001	Then Job answered:
17023002	“Even today my complaint is bitter. His hand is heavy despite my groaning.
17023003	If only I knew where to find Him, so that I could go to His seat.
17023004	I would plead my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.
17023005	I would learn how He would answer, and consider what He would say.
17023006	Would He contend with me in His great power? No, He would certainly take note of me.
17023007	Then an upright man could reason with Him, and I would be delivered forever from my Judge.
17023008	If I go east, He is not there, and if I go west, I cannot find Him.
17023009	When He is at work in the north, I cannot behold Him; when He turns to the south, I cannot see Him.
17023010	Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come forth as gold.
17023011	My feet have followed in His tracks; I have kept His way without turning aside.
17023012	I have not departed from the command of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my daily bread.
17023013	But He is unchangeable, and who can oppose Him? He does what He desires.
17023014	For He carries out His decree against me, and He has many such plans.
17023015	Therefore I am terrified in His presence; when I consider this, I fear Him.
17023016	God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.
17023017	Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.
17024001	“Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those who know Him never see His days?
17024002	Men move boundary stones; they pasture stolen flocks.
17024003	They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge.
17024004	They push the needy off the road and force all the poor of the land into hiding.
17024005	Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work foraging for food; the wasteland is food for their children.
17024006	They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.
17024007	Without clothing, they spend the night naked; they have no covering against the cold.
17024008	Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks for want of shelter.
17024009	The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast; the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt.
17024010	Without clothing, they wander about naked. They carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.
17024011	They crush olives within their walls; they tread the winepresses, but go thirsty.
17024012	From the city, men groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out, yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.
17024013	Then there are those who rebel against the light, not knowing its ways or staying on its paths.
17024014	When daylight is gone, the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief.
17024015	The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight. Thinking, ‘No eye will see me,’ he covers his face.
17024016	In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in, never to experience the light.
17024017	For to them, deep darkness is their morning; surely they are friends with the terrors of darkness!
17024018	They are but foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one turns toward their vineyards.
17024019	As drought and heat consume the melting snow, so Sheol steals those who have sinned.
17024020	The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is broken like a tree.
17024021	They prey on the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow.
17024022	Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty; though rising up, they have no assurance of life.
17024023	He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways.
17024024	They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.
17024025	If this is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?”
17025001	Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
17025002	“Dominion and awe belong to God; He establishes harmony in the heights of heaven.
17025003	Can His troops be numbered? On whom does His light not rise?
17025004	How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
17025005	If even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not pure in His sight,

17026001	Then Job answered:
17026002	“How you have helped the powerless and saved the arm that is feeble!
17026003	How you have counseled the unwise and provided fully sound insight!
17026004	To whom have you uttered these words? And whose spirit spoke through you?
17026005	The dead tremble— those beneath the waters and those who dwell in them.
17026006	Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.

17027001	Job continued his discourse:
17027002	“As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice— the Almighty, who has embittered my soul—

17028001	“Surely there is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.
17028002	Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore.
17028003	Man puts an end to the darkness; he probes the farthest recesses for ore in deepest darkness.

17028008	Proud beasts have never trodden it; no lion has ever prowled over it.

17029002	“How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,

17030001	“But now they mock me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would have refused to put with my sheep dogs.

17030011	Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence.

17041013	Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can approach him with a bridle?
17041014	Who can open his jaws, ringed by his fearsome teeth?
17041015	His rows of scales are his pride, tightly sealed together.
17041016	One scale is so near to another that no air can pass between them.
17041017	They are joined to one another; they clasp and cannot be separated.
17041018	His snorting flashes with light, and his eyes are like the rays of dawn.
17041019	Firebrands stream from his mouth; fiery sparks shoot forth!
17041020	Smoke billows from his nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.
17041021	His breath sets coals ablaze, and flames pour from his mouth.
17041022	Strength resides in his neck, and dismay leaps before him.
17041023	The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.
17041024	His chest is as hard as a rock, as hard as a lower millstone!
17041025	When Leviathan rises up, the mighty are terrified; they withdraw before his thrashing.
17041026	The sword that reaches him has no effect, nor does the spear or dart or arrow.
17041027	He regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.
17041028	No arrow can make him flee; slingstones become like chaff to him.
17041029	A club is regarded as straw, and he laughs at the sound of the lance.
17041030	His undersides are jagged potsherds, spreading out the mud like a threshing sledge.
17041031	He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron; he makes the sea like a jar of ointment.
17041032	He leaves a glistening wake behind him; one would think the deep had white hair!
17041033	Nothing on earth is his equal— a creature devoid of fear!
17041034	He looks down on all the haughty; he is king over all the proud.”
17042001	Then Job replied to the LORD:
17042002	“I know that You can do all things and that no plan of Yours can be thwarted.
17042003	You asked, ‘Who is this who conceals My counsel without knowledge?’ Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.
17042004	You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak. I will question you, and you shall inform Me.’
17042005	My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.
17042006	Therefore I despise myself, and I repent in dust and ashes.”
17042007	After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends. For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.
17042008	So now, take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken accurately about Me, as My servant Job has.”
17042009	So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job’s prayer.
17042010	After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.
17042011	All his brothers and sisters and prior acquaintances came and dined with him in his house. They consoled him and comforted him over all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him. And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
17042012	So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first. He owned 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
17042013	And he also had seven sons and three daughters.
17042014	He named his first daughter Jemimah, his second Keziah, and his third Keren-happuch.
17042015	No women as beautiful as Job’s daughters could be found in all the land, and their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers.
17042016	After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
17042017	And so Job died, old and full of years.
