20001001	These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
20001002	“Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “futility of futilities! Everything is futile!”
20001003	What does a man gain from all his labor, at which he toils under the sun?
20001004	Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.
20001005	The sun rises and the sun sets; it hurries back to where it rises.
20001006	The wind blows southward, then turns northward; round and round it swirls, ever returning on its course.
20001007	All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full; to the place from which the streams come, there again they flow.
20001008	All things are wearisome, more than one can describe; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear content with hearing.
20001009	What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.
20001010	Is there a case where one can say, “Look, this is new”? It has already existed in the ages before us.
20001011	There is no remembrance of those who came before, and those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow after.
20001012	I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
20001013	And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a miserable task God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them!
20001014	I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and have found them all to be futile, a pursuit of the wind.
20001015	What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
20001016	I said to myself, “Behold, I have grown and increased in wisdom beyond all those before me who were over Jerusalem, and my mind has observed a wealth of wisdom and knowledge.”
20001017	So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.
20001018	For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and as knowledge grows, grief increases.
20002001	I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good!” But it proved to be futile.
20002002	I said of laughter, “It is folly,” and of pleasure, “What does it accomplish?”
20002003	I sought to cheer my body with wine and to embrace folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom—until I could see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.
20002004	I expanded my pursuits. I built houses and planted vineyards for myself.
20002005	I made gardens and parks for myself, where I planted all kinds of fruit trees.
20002006	I built reservoirs to water my groves of flourishing trees.
20002007	I acquired menservants and maidservants, and servants were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me,
20002008	and I accumulated for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I gathered to myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men—many concubines.
20002009	So I became great and surpassed all in Jerusalem who had preceded me; and my wisdom remained with me.
20002010	Anything my eyes desired, I did not deny myself. I refused my heart no pleasure. For my heart took delight in all my work, and this was the reward for all my labor.
20002011	Yet when I considered all the works that my hands had accomplished and what I had toiled to achieve, I found everything to be futile, a pursuit of the wind; there was nothing to be gained under the sun.
20002012	Then I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what more can the king’s successor do than what has already been accomplished?
20002013	And I saw that wisdom exceeds folly, just as light exceeds darkness:
20002014	The wise man has eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also came to realize that one fate overcomes them both.
20002015	So I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will also befall me. What then have I gained by being wise?” And I said to myself that this too is futile.
20002016	For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise, just as with the fool, seeing that both will be forgotten in the days to come. Alas, the wise man will die just like the fool!
20002017	So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. For everything is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
20002018	I hated all for which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
20002019	And who knows whether that man will be wise or foolish? Yet he will take over all the labor at which I have worked skillfully under the sun. This too is futile.
20002020	So my heart began to despair over all the labor that I had done under the sun.
20002021	When there is a man who has labored with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and he must give his portion to a man who has not worked for it, this too is futile and a great evil.
20002022	For what does a man get for all the toil and striving with which he labors under the sun?
20002023	Indeed, all his days are filled with grief, and his task is sorrowful; even at night, his mind does not rest. This too is futile.
20002024	Nothing is better for a man than to eat and drink and enjoy his work. I have also seen that this is from the hand of God.
20002025	For apart from Him, who can eat and who can find enjoyment?
20002026	To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
20003001	To everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
20003002	a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot,
20003003	a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build,
20003004	a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance,
20003005	a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,
20003006	a time to search and a time to count as lost, a time to keep and a time to discard,
20003007	a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak,
20003008	a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
20003009	What does the worker gain from his toil?
20003010	I have seen the burden that God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them.
20003011	He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the hearts of men, yet they cannot fathom the work that God has done from beginning to end.
20003012	I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good while they live,
20003013	and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor—this is the gift of God.
20003014	I know that everything God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God does it so that they should fear Him.
20003015	What exists has already been, and what will be has already been, for God will call to account what has passed.
20003016	Furthermore, I saw under the sun that in the place of judgment there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.
20003017	I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, since there is a time for every activity and every deed.”
20003018	I said to myself, “As for the sons of men, God tests them so that they may see for themselves that they are but beasts.”
20003019	For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other—they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.
20003020	All go to one place; all come from dust, and all return to dust.
20003021	Who knows if the spirit of man rises upward and the spirit of the animal descends into the earth?
20003022	I have seen that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will come after him?
20004001	Again I looked, and I considered all the oppression taking place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; the power lay in the hands of their oppressors, and there was no comforter.
20004002	So I admired the dead, who had already died, above the living, who are still alive.
20004003	But better than both is he who has not yet existed, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.
20004004	I saw that all labor and success spring from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
20004005	The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.
20004006	Better one handful with tranquility than two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.
20004007	Again, I saw futility under the sun.
20004008	There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.
20004009	Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.
20004010	For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!
20004011	Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?
20004012	And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
20004013	Better is a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning.
20004014	For the youth has come from the prison to the kingship, though he was born poor in his own kingdom.
20004015	I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed this second one, the youth who succeeded the king.
20004016	There is no limit to all the people who were before them. Yet the successor will not be celebrated by those who come even later. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
20005001	Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.
20005002	Do not be quick to speak, and do not be hasty in your heart to utter a word before God. For God is in heaven and you are on earth. So let your words be few.
20005003	As a dream comes through many cares, so the speech of a fool comes with many words.
20005004	When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it, because He takes no pleasure in fools. Fulfill your vow.
20005005	It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.
20005006	Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not tell the messenger that your vow was a mistake. Why should God be angry with your words and destroy the work of your hands?
20005007	For as many dreams bring futility, so do many words. Therefore, fear God.
20005008	If you see the oppression of the poor and the denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one official is watched by a superior, and others higher still are over them.
20005009	The produce of the earth is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.
20005010	He who loves money is never satisfied by money, and he who loves wealth is never satisfied by income. This too is futile.
20005011	When good things increase, so do those who consume them; what then is the profit to the owner, except to behold them with his eyes?
20005012	The sleep of the worker is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich man permits him no sleep.
20005013	There is a grievous evil I have seen under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owner,
20005014	or wealth lost in a failed venture, so when that man has a son there is nothing to pass on.
20005015	As a man came from his mother’s womb, so he will depart again, naked as he arrived. He takes nothing for his labor to carry in his hands.
20005016	This too is a grievous affliction: Exactly as a man is born, so he will depart. What does he gain as he toils for the wind?
20005017	Moreover, all his days he eats in darkness, with much sorrow, sickness, and anger.
20005018	Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of life that God has given him—for this is his lot.
20005019	Furthermore, God has given riches and wealth to every man, and He has enabled him to enjoy them, to accept his lot, and to rejoice in his labor. This is a gift from God.
20005020	For a man seldom considers the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.
20006001	There is another evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon mankind:
20006002	God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; but God does not allow him to enjoy them. Instead, a stranger will enjoy them. This is futile and a grievous affliction.
20006003	A man may father a hundred children and live for many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he is unsatisfied with his prosperity and does not even receive a proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.
20006004	For a stillborn child enters in futility and departs in darkness, and his name is shrouded in obscurity.
20006005	The child, though neither seeing the sun nor knowing anything, has more rest than that man,
20006006	even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?
20006007	All a man’s labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.
20006008	What advantage, then, has the wise man over the fool? What gain comes to the poor man who knows how to conduct himself before others?
20006009	Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
20006010	Whatever exists was named long ago, and it is known what man is; but he cannot contend with one stronger than he.
20006011	For the more words, the more futility—and how does that profit anyone?
20006012	For who knows what is good for a man during the few days in which he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun?
20007001	A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.
20007002	It is better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, since death is the end of every man, and the living should take this to heart.
20007003	Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad countenance is good for the heart.
20007004	The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
20007005	It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.
20007006	For like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This too is futile.
20007007	Surely extortion turns a wise man into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
20007008	The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.
20007009	Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger settles in the lap of a fool.
20007010	Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is unwise of you to ask about this.
20007011	Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good, and it benefits those who see the sun.
20007012	For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
20007013	Consider the work of God: Who can straighten what He has bent?
20007014	In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.
20007015	In my futile life I have seen both of these: A righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.
20007016	Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
20007017	Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
20007018	It is good to grasp the one and not let the other slip from your hand. For he who fears God will follow both warnings.
20007019	Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers in a city.
20007020	Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.
20007021	Do not pay attention to every word that is spoken, or you may hear your servant cursing you.
20007022	For you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.
20007023	All this I tested by wisdom, saying, “I resolve to be wise.” But it was beyond me.
20007024	What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?
20007025	I directed my mind to understand, to explore, to search out wisdom and explanations, and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the folly of madness.
20007026	And I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net, and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is ensnared.
20007027	“Behold,” says the Teacher, “I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation.
20007028	While my soul was still searching but not finding, among a thousand I have found one upright man, but among all these I have not found one such woman.
20007029	Only this have I found: I have discovered that God made mankind upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”
20008001	Who is like the wise man? Who knows the interpretation of a matter? A man’s wisdom brightens his face, and the sternness of his face is changed.
20008002	Keep the king’s command, I say, because of your oath before God.
20008003	Do not hasten to leave his presence, and do not persist in a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.
20008004	For the king’s word is supreme, and who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
20008005	Whoever keeps his command will come to no harm, and a wise heart knows the right time and procedure.
20008006	For there is a right time and procedure to every purpose, though a man’s misery weighs heavily upon him.
20008007	Since no one knows what will happen, who can tell him what is to come?
20008008	As no man has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has authority over his day of death. As no one can be discharged in wartime, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.
20008009	All this I have seen, applying my mind to every deed that is done under the sun; there is a time when one man lords it over another to his own detriment.
20008010	Then too, I saw the burial of the wicked who used to go in and out of the holy place, and they were praised in the city where they had done so. This too is futile.
20008011	When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed, the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil.
20008012	Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives long, yet I also know that it will go well with those who fear God, who are reverent in His presence.
20008013	Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.
20008014	There is a futility that is done on the earth: There are righteous men who get what the actions of the wicked deserve, and there are wicked men who get what the actions of the righteous deserve. I say that this too is futile.
20008015	So I commended the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for a man under the sun than to eat and drink and be merry. For this joy will accompany him in his labor during the days of his life that God gives him under the sun.
20008016	When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the task that one performs on the earth—though his eyes do not see sleep in the day or even in the night—
20008017	I saw every work of God, and that a man is unable to comprehend the work that is done under the sun. Despite his efforts to search it out, he cannot find its meaning; even if the wise man claims to know, he is unable to comprehend.
20009001	So I took all this to heart and concluded that the righteous and the wise, as well as their deeds, are in God’s hands. Man does not know what lies ahead, whether love or hate.
20009002	It is the same for all: There is a common fate for the righteous and the wicked, for the good and the bad, for the clean and the unclean, for the one who sacrifices and the one who does not. As it is for the good, so it is for the sinner; as it is for the one who makes a vow, so it is for the one who refuses to take a vow.
20009003	This is an evil in everything that is done under the sun: There is one fate for everyone. Furthermore, the hearts of men are full of evil and madness while they are alive, and afterward they join the dead.
20009004	There is hope, however, for anyone who is among the living; for even a live dog is better than a dead lion.
20009005	For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
20009006	Their love, their hate, and their envy have already vanished, and they will never again have a share in all that is done under the sun.
20009007	Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:
20009008	Let your garments always be white, and never spare the oil for your head.
20009009	Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun—all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.
20009010	Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
20009011	I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.
20009012	For surely no man knows his time: Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare, so men are ensnared in an evil time that suddenly falls upon them.
20009013	I have also seen this wisdom under the sun, and it was great to me:
20009014	There was a small city with few men. A mighty king came against it, surrounded it, and built large siege ramps against it.
20009015	Now a poor wise man was found in the city, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
20009016	And I said, “Wisdom is better than strength, but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded.”
20009017	The calm words of the wise are heeded over the shouts of a ruler among fools.
20009018	Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
20010001	As dead flies bring a stench to the perfumer’s oil, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
20010002	A wise man’s heart inclines to the right, but the heart of a fool to the left.
20010003	Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.
20010004	If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.
20010005	There is an evil I have seen under the sun— an error that proceeds from the ruler:
20010006	Folly is appointed to great heights, but the rich sit in lowly positions.
20010007	I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.
20010008	He who digs a pit may fall into it, and he who breaches a wall may be bitten by a snake.
20010009	The one who quarries stones may be injured by them, and he who splits logs endangers himself.
20010010	If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened, more strength must be exerted, but skill produces success.
20010011	If the snake bites before it is charmed, there is no profit for the charmer.
20010012	The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, but the lips of a fool consume him.
20010013	The beginning of his talk is folly, and the end of his speech is evil madness.
20010014	Yet the fool multiplies words. No one knows what is coming, and who can tell him what will come after him?
20010015	The toil of a fool wearies him, for he does not know the way to the city.
20010016	Woe to you, O land whose king is a youth, and whose princes feast in the morning.
20010017	Blessed are you, O land whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes feast at the proper time— for strength and not for drunkenness.
20010018	Through laziness the roof caves in, and in the hands of the idle, the house leaks.
20010019	A feast is prepared for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.
20010020	Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich even in your bedroom, for a bird of the air may carry your words, and a winged creature may report your speech.
20011001	Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.
20011002	Divide your portion among seven, or even eight, for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.
20011003	If the clouds are full, they will pour out rain upon the earth; whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.
20011004	He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.
20011005	As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
20011006	Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.
20011007	Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.
20011008	So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all. But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything to come is futile.
20011009	Rejoice, O young man, while you are young, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.
20011010	So banish sorrow from your heart, and cast off pain from your body, for youth and vigor are fleeting.
20012001	Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of adversity come and the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”
20012002	before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened, and the clouds return after the rain,
20012003	on the day the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men stoop, when those grinding cease because they are few and those watching through windows see dimly,
20012004	when the doors to the street are shut and the sound of the mill fades away, when one rises at the sound of a bird and all the daughters of song grow faint,
20012005	when men fear the heights and dangers of the road, when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper loses its spring, and the caper berry shrivels— for then man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets.
20012006	Remember Him before the silver cord is snapped and the golden bowl is crushed, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel is broken at the well,
20012007	before the dust returns to the ground from which it came and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
20012008	“Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher. “Everything is futile!”
20012009	Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people knowledge; he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.
20012010	The Teacher searched to find delightful sayings and to record accurate words of truth.
20012011	The words of the wise are like goads, and the anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd.
20012012	And by these, my son, be further warned: There is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the body.

20012014	For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
21001001	This is Solomon’s Song of Songs.
21001002	Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is more delightful than wine.

21003001	On my bed at night I sought the one I love; I sought him, but did not find him.

23020017	because he did not kill me in the womb so that my mother might have been my grave, and her womb forever enlarged.
23020018	Why did I come out of the womb to see only trouble and sorrow, and to end my days in shame?
23021001	This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchijah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. They said,

23022001	This is what the LORD says: “Go down to the palace of the king of Judah and proclaim this message there,

23022006	For this is what the LORD says concerning the house of the king of Judah: “You are like Gilead to Me, like the summit of Lebanon; but I will surely turn you into a desert, like cities that are uninhabited.
23022007	I will appoint destroyers against you, each man with his weapons, and they will cut down the choicest of your cedars and throw them into the fire.

23022010	Do not weep for him who is dead; do not mourn his loss. Weep bitterly for him who is exiled, for he will never return to see his native land.

23023001	“Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of My pasture!” declares the LORD.
23023002	Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the shepherds who tend My people: “You have scattered My flock and driven them away, and have not attended to them. Behold, I will attend to you for the evil of your deeds, declares the LORD.

23023006	In His days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely. And this is His name by which He will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness.

23023009	As for the prophets: My heart is broken within me, and all my bones tremble. I have become like a drunkard, like a man overcome by wine, because of the LORD, because of His holy words.
23023010	For the land is full of adulterers— because of the curse, the land mourns and the pastures of the wilderness have dried up— their course is evil and their power is misused.
23023011	“For both prophet and priest are ungodly; even in My house I have found their wickedness,” declares the LORD.
23023012	“Therefore their path will become slick; they will be driven away into the darkness and fall into it. For I will bring disaster upon them in the year of their punishment,” declares the LORD.
23023013	“Among the prophets of Samaria I saw an offensive thing: They prophesied by Baal and led My people Israel astray.
23023014	And among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing: They commit adultery and walk in lies. They strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns his back on wickedness. They are all like Sodom to Me; the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah.”
23023015	Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts says concerning the prophets: “I will feed them wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink, for from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has spread throughout the land.”
23023016	This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. They are filling you with false hopes. They speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD.
23023017	They keep saying to those who despise Me, ‘The LORD says that you will have peace,’ and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart, ‘No harm will come to you.’
23023018	But which of them has stood in the council of the LORD to see and hear His word? Who has given heed to His word and obeyed it?
23023019	Behold, the storm of the LORD has gone out with fury, a whirlwind swirling down upon the heads of the wicked.
23023020	The anger of the LORD will not turn back until He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart. In the days to come you will understand this clearly.
23023021	I did not send these prophets, yet they have run with their message; I did not speak to them, yet they have prophesied.
23023022	But if they had stood in My council, they would have proclaimed My words to My people and turned them back from their evil ways and deeds.”
23023023	“Am I only a God nearby,” declares the LORD, “and not a God far away?”
23023024	“Can a man hide in secret places where I cannot see him?” declares the LORD. “Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?” declares the LORD.
23023025	“I have heard the sayings of the prophets who prophesy lies in My name: ‘I had a dream! I had a dream!’
23023026	How long will this continue in the hearts of these prophets who prophesy falsehood, these prophets of the delusion of their own minds?
23023027	They suppose the dreams that they tell one another will make My people forget My name, just as their fathers forgot My name through the worship of Baal.
23023028	Let the prophet who has a dream retell it, but let him who has My word speak it truthfully. For what is straw compared to grain?” declares the LORD.
23023029	“Is not My word like fire,” declares the LORD, “and like a hammer that smashes a rock?”
23023030	“Therefore behold,” declares the LORD, “I am against the prophets who steal from one another words they attribute to Me.”
23023031	“Yes,” declares the LORD, “I am against the prophets who wag their own tongues and proclaim, ‘The LORD declares it.’”
23023032	“Indeed,” declares the LORD, “I am against those who prophesy false dreams and retell them to lead My people astray with their reckless lies. It was not I who sent them or commanded them, and they are of no benefit at all to these people,” declares the LORD.
23023033	“Now when this people or a prophet or priest asks you, ‘What is the burden of the LORD?’ you are to say to them, ‘What burden? I will forsake you, declares the LORD.’
23023034	As for the prophet or priest or anyone who claims, ‘This is the burden of the LORD,’ I will punish that man and his household.
23023035	This is what each man is to say to his friend and to his brother: ‘What has the LORD answered?’ or ‘What has the LORD spoken?’
23023036	But refer no more to the burden of the LORD, for each man’s word becomes the burden, so that you pervert the words of the living God, the LORD of Hosts, our God.
23023037	Thus you are to say to the prophet: ‘What has the LORD answered you?’ and ‘What has the LORD spoken?’
23023038	But if you claim, ‘This is the burden of the LORD,’ then this is what the LORD says: Because you have said, ‘This is the burden of the LORD,’ and I specifically told you not to make this claim,
23023039	therefore I will surely forget you and will cast you out of My presence, both you and the city that I gave to you and your fathers.
23023040	And I will bring upon you everlasting shame and perpetual humiliation that will never be forgotten.”
23024001	After Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, as well as the officials of Judah and the craftsmen and metalsmiths from Jerusalem, and had brought them to Babylon, the LORD showed me two baskets of figs placed in front of the temple of the LORD.
23024002	One basket had very good figs, like those that ripen early, but the other basket contained very poor figs, so bad they could not be eaten.
23024003	“Jeremiah,” the LORD asked, “what do you see?” “Figs!” I replied. “The good figs are very good, but the bad figs are very bad, so bad they cannot be eaten.”

23027001	At the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah son of Josiah king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD.

23027015	For I have not sent them, declares the LORD, and yet they are prophesying falsely in My name; therefore I will banish you, and you will perish—you and the prophets who prophesy to you.”
23027016	Then I said to the priests and to all this people, “This is what the LORD says: Do not listen to the words of your prophets who prophesy to you, saying, ‘Look, very soon now the articles from the house of the LORD will be brought back from Babylon.’ They are prophesying to you a lie.
23027017	Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon and live! Why should this city become a ruin?

23028001	In the fifth month of that same year, the fourth year, near the beginning of the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur, who was from Gibeon, said to me in the house of the LORD in the presence of the priests and all the people:

23028005	Then the prophet Jeremiah replied to the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests and all the people who were standing in the house of the LORD.
