39005001	When Jesus saw the crowds, He went up on the mountain and sat down. His disciples came to Him,
39005002	and He began to teach them, saying:
39005003	“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
39005004	Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
39005005	Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
39005006	Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.
39005007	Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
39005008	Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
39005009	Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.
39005010	Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
39005011	Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of Me.
39005012	Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven, for in the same way they persecuted the prophets before you.
39005013	You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its savor, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by men.
39005014	You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden.
39005015	Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a basket. Instead, they set it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.
39005016	In the same way, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.
39005017	Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them.
39005018	For I tell you truly, until heaven and earth pass away, not a single jot, not a stroke of a pen, will disappear from the Law until everything is accomplished.
39005019	So then, whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do likewise will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever practices and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
39005020	For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
39005021	You have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not murder’ and ‘Anyone who murders will be subject to judgment.’
39005022	But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment. Again, anyone who says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be subject to the Sanhedrin. But anyone who says, ‘You fool!’ will be subject to the fire of hell.
39005023	So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
39005024	leave your gift there before the altar. First go and be reconciled to your brother; then come and offer your gift.
39005025	Reconcile quickly with your adversary, while you are still on the way to court. Otherwise, he may hand you over to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and you may be thrown into prison.
39005026	Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny.
39005027	You have heard that it was said, ‘Do not commit adultery.’
39005028	But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
39005029	If your right eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
39005030	And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to depart into hell.
39005031	It has also been said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’
39005032	But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, brings adultery upon her. And he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
39005033	Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill your vows to the Lord.’
39005034	But I tell you not to swear at all: either by heaven, for it is God’s throne;
39005035	or by the earth, for it is His footstool; or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
39005036	Nor should you swear by your head, for you cannot make a single hair white or black.
39005037	Simply let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’ Anything more comes from the evil one.
39005038	You have heard that it was said, ‘Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.’
39005039	But I tell you not to resist an evil person. If someone slaps you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also;
39005040	if someone wants to sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well;
39005041	and if someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles.
39005042	Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.
39005043	You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor’ and ‘Hate your enemy.’
39005044	But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
39005045	that you may be sons of your Father in heaven. He causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
39005046	If you love those who love you, what reward will you get? Do not even tax collectors do the same?
39005047	And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing more than others? Do not even Gentiles do the same?
39005048	Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
39006001	“Be careful not to perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.
39006002	So when you give to the needy, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honored by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.
39006003	But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
39006004	so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
39006005	And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.
39006006	But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
39006007	And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.
39006008	Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.
39006009	So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name.
39006010	Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
39006011	Give us this day our daily bread.
39006012	And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
39006013	And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’
39006014	For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
39006015	But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours.
39006016	When you fast, do not be somber like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces to show men they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.
39006017	But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
39006018	so that your fasting will not be obvious to men, but only to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
39006019	Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
39006020	But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moth and rust do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.
39006021	For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
39006022	The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.
39006023	But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
39006024	No one can serve two masters: Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.
39006025	Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?
39006026	Look at the birds of the air: They do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?
39006027	Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
39006028	And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.
39006029	Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
39006030	If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?
39006031	Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’
39006032	For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.
39006033	But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you.
39006034	Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.
39007001	“Do not judge, or you will be judged.
39007002	For with the same judgment you pronounce, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.
39007003	Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?
39007004	How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while there is still a beam in your own eye?
39007005	You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
39007006	Do not give dogs what is holy; do not throw your pearls before swine. If you do, they may trample them under their feet, and then turn and tear you to pieces.
39007007	Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
39007008	For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.
39007009	Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?
39007010	Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?
39007011	So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!
39007012	In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets.
39007013	Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.
39007014	But small is the gate and narrow the way that leads to life, and only a few find it.
39007015	Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.
39007016	By their fruit you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
39007017	Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.
39007018	A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.
39007019	Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
39007020	So then, by their fruit you will recognize them.
39007021	Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven.
39007022	Many will say to Me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name drive out demons and perform many miracles?’
39007023	Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness!’
39007024	Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
39007025	The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.
39007026	But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
39007027	The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell—and great was its collapse!”
39007028	When Jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were astonished at His teaching,
39007029	because He taught as one who had authority, and not as their scribes.
39008001	When Jesus came down from the mountain, large crowds followed Him.

39008033	Those tending the pigs ran off into the town and reported all this, including the account of the demon-possessed men.
39008034	Then the whole town went out to meet Jesus. And when they saw Him, they begged Him to leave their region.
39009001	Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to His own town.
39009002	Just then some men brought to Him a paralytic lying on a mat. When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven.”
39009003	On seeing this, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is blaspheming!”
39009004	But Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, “Why do you harbor evil in your hearts?
39009005	Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
39009006	But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” Then He said to the paralytic, “Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
39009007	And the man got up and went home.
39009008	When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
39009009	As Jesus went on from there, He saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Matthew got up and followed Him.
39009010	Later, as Jesus was dining at Matthew’s house, many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Him and His disciples.

39009012	On hearing this, Jesus said, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.

39009014	Then John’s disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Why is it that we and the Pharisees fast so often, but Your disciples do not fast?”
39009015	Jesus replied, “How can the guests of the bridegroom mourn while He is with them? But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.
39009016	No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. For the patch will pull away from the garment, and a worse tear will result.
39009017	Neither do men pour new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins will burst, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.”
39009018	While Jesus was saying these things, a synagogue leader came and knelt before Him. “My daughter has just died,” he said. “But come and place Your hand on her, and she will live.”
39009019	So Jesus got up and went with him, along with His disciples.
39009020	Suddenly a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years came up behind Him and touched the fringe of His cloak.
39009021	She said to herself, “If only I touch His cloak, I will be healed.”
39009022	Jesus turned and saw her. “Take courage, daughter,” He said, “your faith has healed you.” And the woman was healed from that very hour.
39009023	When Jesus entered the house of the synagogue leader, He saw the flute players and the noisy crowd.
39009024	“Go away,” He told them. “The girl is not dead, but asleep.” And they laughed at Him.

39010001	And calling His twelve disciples to Him, Jesus gave them authority over unclean spirits, so that they could drive them out and heal every disease and sickness.
39010002	These are the names of the twelve apostles: first Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee, and his brother John;

39010024	A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master.

39010032	Therefore everyone who confesses Me before men, I will also confess him before My Father in heaven.
39010033	But whoever denies Me before men, I will also deny him before My Father in heaven.

39010035	For I have come to turn ‘a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
39010036	A man’s enemies will be the members of his own household.’
39010037	Anyone who loves his father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; anyone who loves his son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me;
39010038	and anyone who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me.
39010039	Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for My sake will find it.
39010040	He who receives you receives Me, and he who receives Me receives the One who sent Me.
39010041	Whoever receives a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever receives a righteous man because he is a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.
39010042	And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is My disciple, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.”

39013007	Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings.
39013008	Still other seed fell on good soil and produced a crop—a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold.

39013019	When anyone hears the message of the kingdom but does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the seed sown along the path.
39013020	The seed sown on rocky ground is the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.

39018001	At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”
39018002	Jesus invited a little child to stand among them.
39018003	“Truly I tell you,” He said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
39018004	Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
39018005	And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me.
39018006	But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.
39018007	Woe to the world for the causes of sin. These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!
39018008	If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
39018009	And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
39018010	See that you do not look down on any of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven.
39018012	What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?
39018013	And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.
39018014	In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish.
39018015	If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.
39018016	But if he will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’
39018017	If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.
39018018	Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
39018019	Again, I tell you truly that if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven.
39018020	For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them.”
39018021	Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”
39018022	Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!
39018023	Because of this, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
39018024	As he began the settlements, a debtor owing ten thousand talents was brought to him.
39018025	Since the man was unable to pay, the master ordered that he be sold to pay his debt, along with his wife and children and everything he owned.
39018026	Then the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Have patience with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’
39018027	His master had compassion on him, forgave his debt, and released him.
39018028	But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him and began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe me!’
39018029	So his fellow servant fell down and begged him, ‘Have patience with me, and I will pay you back.’
39018030	But he refused. Instead, he went and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay his debt.
39018031	When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and they went and recounted all of this to their master.
39018032	Then the master summoned him and said, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave all your debt because you begged me.
39018033	Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had on you?’
39018034	In anger his master turned him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he should repay all that he owed.
39018035	That is how My heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother from your heart.”
39019001	When Jesus had finished saying these things, He left Galilee and went into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.

39019007	“Why then,” they asked, “did Moses order a man to give his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away?”

39020001	“For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
39020002	He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.
39020003	About the third hour he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace doing nothing.

39020006	About the eleventh hour he went out and found still others standing around. ‘Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing?’ he asked.
39020007	‘Because no one has hired us,’ they answered. So he told them, ‘You also go into my vineyard.’
39020008	When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, starting with the last ones hired and moving on to the first.’
39020009	The workers who were hired about the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius.
39020010	So when the original workers came, they assumed they would receive more. But each of them also received a denarius.

40002001	A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum. And when the people heard that He was home,

40002021	No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. If he does, the new piece will pull away from the old, and a worse tear will result.
40002022	And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.”

40004001	Once again Jesus began to teach beside the sea, and such a large crowd gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat in it, while all the people crowded along the shore.
40004002	And He taught them many things in parables, and in His teaching He said,
40004003	“Listen! A farmer went out to sow his seed.
40004004	And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.
40004005	Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.
40004006	But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.
40004007	Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings, and they yielded no crop.
40004008	Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprouted, grew up, and produced a crop—one bearing thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, and another a hundredfold.”

40004010	As soon as Jesus was alone with the Twelve and those around Him, they asked Him about the parable.
40004011	He replied, “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables,
40004012	so that, ‘they may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.’”
40004013	Then Jesus said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand any of the parables?
40004014	The farmer sows the word.
40004015	Some are like the seeds along the path, where the word is sown. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.
40004016	Some are like the seeds sown on rocky ground. They hear the word and at once receive it with joy.
40004017	But they themselves have no root, and they remain for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.
40004018	Others are like the seeds sown among the thorns. They hear the word,
40004019	but the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desire for other things come in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
40004020	Still others are like the seeds sown on good soil. They hear the word, receive it, and produce a crop—thirtyfold, sixtyfold, or a hundredfold.”
40004021	Jesus also said to them, “Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed? Doesn’t he set it on a stand?

40007001	Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus,

40014003	While Jesus was in Bethany reclining at the table in the home of Simon the Leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, made of pure nard. She broke open the jar and poured it on Jesus’ head.
40014004	Some of those present, however, expressed their indignation to one another: “Why this waste of perfume?
40014005	It could have been sold for over three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they scolded her.
40014006	But Jesus said, “Leave her alone; why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.
40014007	The poor you will always have with you, and you can help them whenever you want. But you will not always have Me.
40014008	She has done what she could to anoint My body in advance of My burial.
40014009	And truly I tell you, wherever the gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
40014010	Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus to them.
40014011	They were delighted to hear this, and they promised to give him money. So Judas began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus.
40014012	On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed, Jesus’ disciples asked Him, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”
40014013	So He sent two of His disciples and told them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him,
40014014	and whichever house he enters, say to the owner, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is My guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’
40014015	And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. Make preparations for us there.”
40014016	So the disciples left and went into the city, where they found everything as Jesus had described. And they prepared the Passover.
40014017	When evening came, Jesus arrived with the Twelve.
40014018	And while they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with Me will betray Me.”
40014019	They began to be grieved and to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I?”
40014020	He answered, “It is one of the Twelve—the one who is dipping his hand into the bowl with Me.
40014021	The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed! It would be better for him if he had not been born.”
40014022	While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take it; this is My body.”
40014023	Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
40014024	He said to them, “This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.
40014025	Truly I tell you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God.”
40014026	And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
40014027	Then Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away, for it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
40014028	But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
40014029	Peter declared, “Even if all fall away, I never will.”
40014030	“Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”
40014031	But Peter kept insisting, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” And all the others said the same thing.
40014032	Then they came to a place called Gethsemane, and Jesus told His disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
40014033	He took with Him Peter, James, and John, and began to be deeply troubled and distressed.
40014034	Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”
40014035	Going a little farther, He fell to the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour would pass from Him.
40014036	“Abba, Father,” He said, “all things are possible for You. Take this cup from Me. Yet not what I will, but what You will.”
40014037	Then Jesus returned and found them sleeping. “Simon, are you asleep?” He asked. “Were you not able to keep watch for one hour?
40014038	Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
40014039	Again He went away and prayed, saying the same thing.
40014040	And again Jesus returned and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy. And they did not know what to answer Him.
40014041	When Jesus returned the third time, He said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? That is enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
40014042	Rise, let us go. See, My betrayer is approaching!”
40014043	While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, accompanied by a crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests, scribes, and elders.
40014044	Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him and lead Him away securely.”
40014045	Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Rabbi!” and kissed Him.
40014046	Then the men seized Jesus and arrested Him.
40014047	And one of the bystanders drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.
40014048	Jesus asked the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw?
40014049	Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me. But this has happened that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.”
40014050	Then everyone deserted Him and fled.
40014051	One young man who had been following Jesus was wearing a linen cloth around his body. They caught hold of him,
40014052	but he pulled free of the linen cloth and ran away naked.
40014053	They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders, and scribes assembled.
40014054	Peter followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. And he sat with the officers and warmed himself by the fire.
40014055	Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but they did not find any.
40014056	For many bore false witness against Jesus, but their testimony was inconsistent.
40014057	Then some men stood up and testified falsely against Him:
40014058	“We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this man-made temple, and in three days I will build another that is made without hands.’”
40014059	But even their testimony was inconsistent.
40014060	So the high priest stood up before them and questioned Jesus, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”
40014061	But Jesus remained silent and made no reply. Again the high priest questioned Him, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
40014062	“I am,” said Jesus, “and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
40014063	At this, the high priest tore his clothes and declared, “Why do we need any more witnesses?
40014064	You have heard the blasphemy. What is your verdict?” And they all condemned Him as deserving of death.
40014065	Then some of them began to spit on Him. They blindfolded Him, struck Him with their fists, and said to Him, “Prophesy!” And the officers received Him with slaps in His face.
40014066	While Peter was in the courtyard below, one of the servant girls of the high priest came down
40014067	and saw him warming himself there. She looked at Peter and said, “You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
40014068	But he denied it. “I do not know or even understand what you are talking about,” he said. Then he went out to the gateway, and the rooster crowed.
40014069	There the servant girl saw him and again said to those standing nearby, “This man is one of them.”
40014070	But he denied it again. After a little while, those standing nearby said once more to Peter, “Surely you are one of them, for you too are a Galilean.”
40014071	But he began to curse and swear, “I do not know this man of whom you speak!”
40014072	And immediately the rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” And he broke down and wept.
40015001	Early in the morning, the chief priests, elders, scribes, and the whole Sanhedrin devised a plan. They bound Jesus, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.
40015002	So Pilate questioned Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.
40015003	And the chief priests began to accuse Him of many things.
40015004	Then Pilate questioned Him again, “Have You no answer? Look how many charges they are bringing against You!”
40015005	But to Pilate’s amazement, Jesus made no further reply.
40015006	Now it was Pilate’s custom at the feast to release to the people a prisoner of their choosing.
40015007	And a man named Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection.
40015008	So the crowd went up and began asking Pilate to keep his custom.
40015009	“Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?” Pilate asked.
40015010	For he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over.
40015011	But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead.
40015012	So Pilate asked them again, “What then do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?”
40015013	And they shouted back, “Crucify Him!”
40015014	“Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!”
40015015	And wishing to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified.
40015016	Then the soldiers led Jesus away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium) and called the whole company together.
40015017	They dressed Him in a purple robe, twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on His head.
40015018	And they began to salute Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
40015019	They kept striking His head with a staff and spitting on Him. And they knelt down and bowed before Him.
40015020	After they had mocked Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.
40015021	Now Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and the soldiers forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.
40015022	They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull.
40015023	There they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
40015024	And they crucified Him. They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take.
40015025	It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
40015026	And the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
40015027	Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.
40015029	And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
40015030	come down from the cross and save Yourself!”
40015031	In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!
40015032	Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!” And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him.
40015033	From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
40015034	At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
40015035	When some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, “Behold, He is calling Elijah.”
40015036	And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”
40015037	But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.
40015038	And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
40015039	When the centurion standing there in front of Jesus saw how He had breathed His last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
40015040	And there were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
40015041	These women had followed Jesus and ministered to Him while He was in Galilee, and there were many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Him.
40015042	Now it was already evening. Since it was Preparation Day (that is, the day before the Sabbath),
40015043	Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent Council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, boldly went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
40015044	Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead, so he summoned the centurion to ask if this was so.
40015045	When Pilate had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
40015046	So Joseph bought a linen cloth, took down the body of Jesus, wrapped it in the cloth, and placed it in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.
40015047	Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph saw where His body was placed.
40016001	When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so they could go and anoint the body of Jesus.
40016002	Very early on the first day of the week, just after sunrise, they went to the tomb.
40016003	They were asking one another, “Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb?”
40016004	But when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, even though it was extremely large.
40016005	When they entered the tomb, they saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side, and they were alarmed.
40016006	But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here! See the place where they put Him.
40016007	But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.’”
40016008	So the women left the tomb and ran away, trembling and bewildered. And in their fear they did not say a word to anyone.
40016009	Early on the first day of the week, after Jesus had risen, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had driven out seven demons.
40016010	She went and told those who had been with Him, who were mourning and weeping.
40016011	And when they heard that Jesus was alive and she had seen Him, they did not believe it.
40016012	After this, Jesus appeared in a different form to two of them as they walked along in the country.
40016013	And they went back and reported it to the rest, but they did not believe them either.
40016014	Later, as they were eating, Jesus appeared to the Eleven and rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen Him after He had risen.
40016015	And He said to them, “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.
40016016	Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
40016017	And these signs will accompany those who believe: In My name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues;
40016018	they will pick up snakes with their hands, and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not harm them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will be made well.”
40016019	After the Lord Jesus had spoken to them, He was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
40016020	And they went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked through them, confirming His word by the signs that accompanied it.
41001001	Many have undertaken to compose an account of the things that have been fulfilled among us,
41001002	just as they were handed down to us by the initial eyewitnesses and servants of the word.
41001003	Therefore, having carefully investigated everything from the beginning, it seemed good also to me to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus,
41001004	so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught.
41001005	In the time of Herod king of Judea there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah, and whose wife Elizabeth was a descendant of Aaron.
41001006	Both of them were righteous in the sight of God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and decrees of the Lord.
41001007	But they had no children, because Elizabeth was barren, and they were both well along in years.
41001008	One day while Zechariah’s division was on duty and he was serving as priest before God,
41001009	he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to enter the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
41001010	And at the hour of the incense offering, the whole congregation was praying outside.
41001011	Just then an angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.
41001012	When Zechariah saw him, he was startled and gripped with fear.
41001013	But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to give him the name John.
41001014	He will be a joy and delight to you, and many will rejoice at his birth,
41001015	for he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He shall never take wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.
41001016	Many of the sons of Israel he will turn back to the Lord their God.
41001017	And he will go on before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to their children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous—to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.”
41001018	“How can I be sure of this?” Zechariah asked the angel. “I am an old man, and my wife is well along in years.”
41001019	“I am Gabriel,” replied the angel. “I stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
41001020	And now you will be silent and unable to speak until the day this comes to pass, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their proper time.”
41001021	Meanwhile, the people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering why he took so long in the temple.
41001022	When he came out and was unable to speak to them, they realized he had seen a vision in the temple. He kept making signs to them but remained unable to speak.
41001023	And when the days of his service were complete, he returned home.
41001024	After these days, his wife Elizabeth became pregnant and for five months remained in seclusion. She declared,
41001025	“The Lord has done this for me. In these days He has shown me favor and taken away my disgrace among the people.”
41001026	In the sixth month, God sent the angel Gabriel to a town in Galilee called Nazareth,
41001027	to a virgin pledged in marriage to a man named Joseph, who was of the house of David. And the virgin’s name was Mary.
41001028	The angel appeared to her and said, “Greetings, you who are highly favored! The Lord is with you.”
41001029	Mary was greatly troubled at his words and wondered what kind of greeting this might be.
41001030	So the angel told her, “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
41001031	Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus.
41001032	He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David,
41001033	and He will reign over the house of Jacob forever. His kingdom will never end!”
41001034	“How can this be,” Mary asked the angel, “since I am a virgin?”
41001035	The angel replied, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the Holy One to be born will be called the Son of God.
41001036	Look, even Elizabeth your relative has conceived a son in her old age, and she who was called barren is in her sixth month.
41001037	For no word from God will ever fail.”
41001038	“I am the Lord’s servant,” Mary answered. “May it happen to me according to your word.” Then the angel left her.
41001039	In those days Mary got ready and hurried to a town in the hill country of Judah,
41001040	where she entered the home of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
41001041	When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
41001042	In a loud voice she exclaimed, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
41001043	And why am I so honored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
41001044	For as soon as the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy.
41001045	Blessed is she who has believed that the Lord’s word to her will be fulfilled.”
41001046	Then Mary said: “My soul magnifies the Lord,
41001047	and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior!
41001048	For He has looked with favor on the humble state of His servant. From now on all generations will call me blessed.
41001049	For the Mighty One has done great things for me. Holy is His name.
41001050	His mercy extends to those who fear Him, from generation to generation.
41001051	He has performed mighty deeds with His arm; He has scattered those who are proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
41001052	He has brought down rulers from their thrones, but has exalted the humble.
41001053	He has filled the hungry with good things, but has sent the rich away empty.
41001054	He has helped His servant Israel, remembering to be merciful,
41001055	as He promised to our fathers, to Abraham and his descendants forever.”
41001056	Mary stayed with Elizabeth for about three months and then returned home.
41001057	When the time came for Elizabeth to have her child, she gave birth to a son.
41001058	Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown her great mercy, and they rejoiced with her.
41001059	On the eighth day, when they came to circumcise the child, they were going to name him after his father Zechariah.
41001060	But his mother replied, “No! He shall be called John.”
41001061	They said to her, “There is no one among your relatives who bears this name.”

41001069	He has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of His servant David,
41001070	as He spoke through His holy prophets, those of ages past,
41001071	salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,
41001072	to show mercy to our fathers and to remember His holy covenant,
41001073	the oath He swore to our father Abraham, to grant us
41001074	deliverance from hostile hands, that we may serve Him without fear,
41001075	in holiness and righteousness before Him all the days of our lives.
41001076	And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High; for you will go on before the Lord to prepare the way for Him,
41001077	to give to His people the knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins,
41001078	because of the tender mercy of our God, by which the Dawn will visit us from on high,
41001079	to shine on those who live in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the path of peace.”
41001080	And the child grew and became strong in spirit; and he lived in the wilderness until the time of his public appearance to Israel.
41002001	Now in those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that a census should be taken of the whole empire.
41002002	This was the first census to take place while Quirinius was governor of Syria.
41002003	And everyone went to his own town to register.
41002004	So Joseph also went up from Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem, since he was from the house and line of David.

41002047	And all who heard Him were astounded at His understanding and His answers.

42018001	After Jesus had spoken these words, He went out with His disciples across the Kidron Valley, where they entered a garden.

42018030	“If He were not a criminal,” they replied, “we would not have handed Him over to you.”

42019001	Then Pilate took Jesus and had Him flogged.

42019020	Many of the Jews read this sign, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
42019021	So the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’”

42019031	It was the day of Preparation, and the next day was a High Sabbath. In order that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath, the Jews asked Pilate to have the legs broken and the bodies removed.

42019033	But when they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.

42019035	The one who saw it has testified to this, and his testimony is true. He knows that he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe.
42019036	Now these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not one of His bones will be broken.”
42019037	And, as another Scripture says: “They will look on the One they have pierced.”

42019041	Now there was a garden in the place where Jesus was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.

43003022	For Moses said, ‘The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to Him in everything He tells you.
43003023	Everyone who does not listen to Him will be completely cut off from among his people.’
43003024	Indeed, all the prophets from Samuel on, as many as have spoken, have proclaimed these days.
43003025	And you are sons of the prophets and of the covenant God made with your fathers when He said to Abraham, ‘Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed.’
43003026	When God raised up His Servant, He sent Him first to you to bless you by turning each of you from your wicked ways.”
43004001	While Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple guard and the Sadducees came up to them,
43004002	greatly disturbed that they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead.
43004003	They seized Peter and John, and because it was evening, they put them in custody until the next day.
43004004	But many who heard the message believed, and the number of men grew to about five thousand.
43004005	The next day the rulers, elders, and scribes assembled in Jerusalem,
43004006	along with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and many others from the high priest’s family.
43004007	They had Peter and John brought in and began to question them: “By what power or what name did you do this?”
43004008	Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “Rulers and elders of the people!
43004009	If we are being examined today about a kind service to a man who was lame, to determine how he was healed,
43004010	then let this be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel: It is by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified but whom God raised from the dead, that this man stands before you healed.
43004011	This Jesus is ‘the stone you builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone.’
43004012	Salvation exists in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved.”
43004013	When they saw the boldness of Peter and John and realized that they were unschooled, ordinary men, they marveled and took note that these men had been with Jesus.
43004014	And seeing the man who had been healed standing there with them, they had nothing to say in response.
43004015	So they ordered them to leave the Sanhedrin and then conferred together.
43004016	“What shall we do with these men?” they asked. “It is clear to everyone living in Jerusalem that a remarkable miracle has occurred through them, and we cannot deny it.
43004017	But to keep this message from spreading any further among the people, we must warn them not to speak to anyone in this name.”
43004018	Then they called them in again and commanded them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.
43004019	But Peter and John replied, “Judge for yourselves whether it is right in God’s sight to listen to you rather than God.
43004020	For we cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard.”
43004021	After further threats they let them go. They could not find a way to punish them, because all the people were glorifying God for what had happened.
43004022	For the man who was miraculously healed was over forty years old.
43004023	On their release, Peter and John returned to their own people and reported everything that the chief priests and elders had said to them.
43004024	When the believers heard this, they lifted up their voices to God with one accord. “Sovereign Lord,” they said, “You made the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them.
43004025	You spoke by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of Your servant, our father David: ‘Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?
43004026	The kings of the earth take their stand and the rulers gather together against the Lord and against His Anointed One.’
43004027	In fact, this is the very city where Herod and Pontius Pilate conspired with the Gentiles and the people of Israel against Your holy servant Jesus, whom You anointed.
43004028	They carried out what Your hand and will had decided beforehand would happen.
43004029	And now, Lord, consider their threats, and enable Your servants to speak Your word with complete boldness,
43004030	as You stretch out Your hand to heal and perform signs and wonders through the name of Your holy servant Jesus.”
43004031	After they had prayed, their meeting place was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God boldly.
43004032	The multitude of believers was one in heart and soul. No one claimed that any of his possessions was his own, but they shared everything they owned.
43004033	With great power the apostles continued to give their testimony about the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And abundant grace was upon them all.
43004034	There were no needy ones among them, because those who owned lands or houses would sell their property, bring the proceeds from the sales,
43004035	and lay them at the apostles’ feet for distribution to anyone as he had need.
43004036	Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, whom the apostles called Barnabas (meaning Son of Encouragement),
43004037	sold a field he owned, brought the money, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
43005001	Now a man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, also sold a piece of property.
43005002	With his wife’s full knowledge, he kept back some of the proceeds for himself, but brought a portion and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
43005003	Then Peter said, “Ananias, how is it that Satan has filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and withhold some of the proceeds from the land?
43005004	Did it not belong to you before it was sold? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? How could you conceive such a deed in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God!”
43005005	On hearing these words, Ananias fell down and died. And great fear came over all who heard what had happened.
43005006	Then the young men stepped forward, wrapped up his body, and carried him out and buried him.
43005007	About three hours later his wife also came in, unaware of what had happened.
43005008	“Tell me,” said Peter, “is this the price you and your husband got for the land?” “Yes,” she answered, “that is the price.”
43005009	“How could you agree to test the Spirit of the Lord?” Peter replied. “Look, the feet of the men who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out also.”
43005010	At that instant she fell down at his feet and died. Then the young men came in and, finding her dead, carried her out and buried her beside her husband.
43005011	And great fear came over the whole church and all who heard about these events.
43005012	The apostles performed many signs and wonders among the people, and with one accord the believers gathered together in Solomon’s Colonnade.
43005013	Although the people regarded them highly, no one else dared to join them.
43005014	Yet more and more believers were brought to the Lord—large numbers of both men and women.
43005015	As a result, people brought the sick into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, so that at least Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them as he passed by.
43005016	Crowds also gathered from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, and all of them were healed.
43005017	Then the high priest and all his associates, who belonged to the party of the Sadducees, were filled with jealousy. They went out
43005018	and arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.
43005019	But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the jail and brought them out, saying,
43005020	“Go, stand in the temple courts and tell the people the full message of this new life.”
43005021	At daybreak the apostles entered the temple courts as they had been told and began to teach the people. When the high priest and his associates arrived, they convened the Sanhedrin —the full assembly of the elders of Israel—and sent to the jail for the apostles.
43005022	But on arriving at the jail, the officers did not find them there. So they returned with the report:
43005023	“We found the jail securely locked, with the guards posted at the doors; but when we opened them, we found no one inside.”
43005024	When the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests heard this account, they were perplexed as to what was happening.
43005025	Then someone came in and announced, “Look, the men you put in jail are standing in the temple courts teaching the people!”
43005026	At that point, the captain went with the officers and brought the apostles—but not by force, for fear the people would stone them.
43005027	They brought them in and made them stand before the Sanhedrin, where the high priest interrogated them.
43005028	“We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name,” he said. “Yet you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and are determined to make us responsible for this man’s blood.”
43005029	But Peter and the other apostles replied, “We must obey God rather than men.
43005030	The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you had killed by hanging Him on a tree.
43005031	God exalted Him to His right hand as Prince and Savior, in order to grant repentance and forgiveness of sins to Israel.
43005032	We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him.”
43005033	When the Council members heard this, they were enraged, and they resolved to put the apostles to death.
43005034	But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law who was honored by all the people, stood up in the Sanhedrin and ordered that the men be put outside for a short time.
43005035	“Men of Israel,” he said, “consider carefully what you are about to do to these men.
43005036	Some time ago Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and about four hundred men joined him. He was killed, all his followers were dispersed, and it all came to nothing.
43005037	After him, Judas the Galilean appeared in the days of the census and drew away people after him. He too perished, and all his followers were scattered.
43005038	So in the present case I advise you: Leave these men alone. Let them go! For if their purpose or endeavor is of human origin, it will fail.
43005039	But if it is from God, you will not be able to stop them. You may even find yourselves fighting against God.”
43005040	At this, they yielded to Gamaliel. They called the apostles in and had them flogged. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.
43005041	The apostles left the Sanhedrin, rejoicing that they had been counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name.
43005042	Every day, in the temple courts and from house to house, they did not stop teaching and proclaiming the good news that Jesus is the Christ.
43006001	In those days when the disciples were increasing in number, the Grecian Jews among them began to grumble against the Hebraic Jews because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food.
43006002	So the Twelve summoned all the disciples and said, “It is unacceptable for us to neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables.
43006003	Therefore, brothers, select from among you seven men confirmed to be full of the Spirit and wisdom. We will assign this responsibility to them
43006004	and will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word.”
43006005	This proposal pleased the whole group. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, as well as Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas from Antioch, a convert to Judaism.
43006006	They presented these seven to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
43006007	So the word of God continued to spread. The number of disciples in Jerusalem grew rapidly, and a great number of priests became obedient to the faith.
43006008	Now Stephen, who was full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people.
43006009	But resistance arose from what was called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, including Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and men from the provinces of Cilicia and Asia. They disputed with Stephen,
43006010	but they could not stand up to his wisdom or the Spirit by whom he spoke.
43006011	Then they prompted some men to say, “We heard Stephen speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God.”

43006013	where they presented false witnesses who said, “This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.

43007001	Then the high priest asked Stephen, “Are these charges true?”
43007002	And Stephen declared: “Brothers and fathers, listen to me! The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran,
43007003	and told him, ‘Leave your country and your kindred and go to the land I will show you.’
43007004	So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. After his father died, God brought him out of that place and into this land where you are now living.
43007005	He gave him no inheritance here, not even a foot of ground. But God promised to give possession of the land to Abraham and his descendants, even though he did not yet have a child.
43007006	God told him that his descendants would be foreigners in a strange land, and that they would be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.
43007007	‘But I will punish the nation that enslaves them,’ God said, ‘and afterward they will come forth and worship Me in this place.’
43007008	Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and Abraham became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day. And Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve patriarchs.
43007009	Because the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph, they sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him
43007010	and rescued him from all his troubles. He granted Joseph favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt, who appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his household.
43007011	Then famine and great suffering swept across Egypt and Canaan, and our fathers could not find food.
43007012	When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers on their first visit.
43007013	On their second visit, Joseph revealed his identity to his brothers, and his family became known to Pharaoh.
43007014	Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five in all.
43007015	So Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our fathers died.
43007016	Their bones were carried back to Shechem and placed in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor at Shechem for a price he paid in silver.
43007017	As the time drew near for God to fulfill His promise to Abraham, our people in Egypt increased greatly in number.
43007018	Then another king, who knew nothing of Joseph, arose over Egypt.
43007019	He exploited our people and oppressed our fathers, forcing them to abandon their infants so they would die.
43007020	At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful in the sight of God. For three months he was nurtured in his father’s house.
43007021	When he was set outside, Pharaoh’s daughter took him and brought him up as her own son.
43007022	So Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was powerful in speech and action.
43007023	When Moses was forty years old, he decided to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.
43007024	And when he saw one of them being mistreated, Moses went to his defense and avenged him by striking down the Egyptian who was oppressing him.
43007025	He assumed his brothers would understand that God was using him to deliver them, but they did not.
43007026	The next day he came upon two Israelites who were fighting, and he tried to reconcile them, saying, ‘Men, you are brothers. Why are you mistreating each other?’
43007027	But the man who was abusing his neighbor pushed Moses aside and said, ‘Who made you ruler and judge over us?
43007028	Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’
43007029	At this remark, Moses fled to the land of Midian, where he lived as a foreigner and had two sons.
43007030	After forty years had passed, an angel appeared to Moses in the flames of a burning bush in the desert near Mount Sinai.
43007031	When Moses saw it, he marveled at the sight. As he approached to look more closely, the voice of the Lord came to him:
43007032	‘I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’ Moses trembled with fear and did not dare to look.
43007033	Then the Lord said to him, ‘Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
43007034	I have indeed seen the oppression of My people in Egypt. I have heard their groaning and have come down to deliver them. Now come, I will send you back to Egypt.’
43007035	This Moses, whom they had rejected with the words, ‘Who made you ruler and judge?’ is the one whom God sent to be their ruler and redeemer through the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
43007036	He led them out and performed wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, at the Red Sea, and for forty years in the wilderness.
43007037	This is the same Moses who told the Israelites, ‘God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.’
43007038	He was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers. And he received living words to pass on to us.
43007039	But our fathers refused to obey him. Instead, they rejected him and in their hearts turned back to Egypt.
43007040	They said to Aaron, ‘Make us gods who will go before us! As for this Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’
43007041	At that time they made a calf and offered a sacrifice to the idol, rejoicing in the works of their hands.
43007042	But God turned away from them and gave them over to the worship of the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: ‘Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
43007043	You have taken along the tabernacle of Molech and the star of your god Rephan, the idols you made to worship. Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Babylon.’
43007044	Our fathers had the tabernacle of the Testimony with them in the wilderness. It was constructed exactly as God had directed Moses, according to the pattern he had seen.
43007045	And our fathers who received it brought it in with Joshua when they dispossessed the nations God drove out before them. It remained until the time of David,
43007046	who found favor in the sight of God and asked to provide a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
43007047	But it was Solomon who built the house for Him.
43007048	However, the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands. As the prophet says:
43007049	‘Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord, or where will My place of repose be?
43007050	Has not My hand made all these things?’
43007051	You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did.
43007052	Which of the prophets did your fathers fail to persecute? They even killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One. And now you are His betrayers and murderers—
43007053	you who received the law ordained by angels, yet have not kept it.”
43007054	On hearing this, the members of the Sanhedrin were enraged, and they gnashed their teeth at him.
43007055	But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
43007056	“Look,” he said, “I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.”
43007057	At this they covered their ears, cried out in a loud voice, and rushed together at him.
43007058	They dragged him out of the city and began to stone him. Meanwhile the witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
43007059	While they were stoning him, Stephen appealed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”
43007060	Falling on his knees, he cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” And when he had said this, he fell asleep.
43008001	And Saul was there, giving approval to Stephen’s death. On that day a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem, and all except the apostles were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.
43008002	God-fearing men buried Stephen and mourned deeply over him.

43008005	Philip went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed the Christ to them.
43008006	The crowds all paid close attention to Philip’s message and to the signs they saw him perform.
43008007	With loud shrieks, unclean spirits came out of many who were possessed, and many of the paralyzed and lame were healed.
43008008	So there was great joy in that city.
43008009	Prior to that time, a man named Simon had practiced sorcery in the city and astounded the people of Samaria. He claimed to be someone great,
43008010	and all the people, from the least to the greatest, heeded his words and said, “This man is the divine power called the Great Power.”
