43010001	At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was called the Italian Regiment.
43010002	He and all his household were devout and God-fearing. He gave generously to the people and prayed to God regularly.
43010003	One day at about the ninth hour, he had a clear vision of an angel of God who came to him and said, “Cornelius!”
43010004	Cornelius stared at him in fear and asked, “What is it, Lord?” The angel answered, “Your prayers and gifts to the poor have ascended as a memorial offering before God.
43010005	Now send men to Joppa to call for a man named Simon who is called Peter.
43010006	He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea.”
43010007	When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a devout soldier from among his attendants.
43010008	He explained what had happened and sent them to Joppa.
43010009	The next day at about the sixth hour, as the men were approaching the city on their journey, Peter went up on the roof to pray.
43010010	He became hungry and wanted something to eat, but while the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.
43010011	He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet being let down to earth by its four corners.
43010012	It contained all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth, as well as birds of the air.
43010013	Then a voice said to him: “Get up, Peter, kill and eat!”
43010014	“No, Lord!” Peter answered. “I have never eaten anything impure or unclean.”
43010015	The voice spoke to him a second time: “Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.”
43010016	This happened three times, and all at once the sheet was taken back up into heaven.
43010017	While Peter was puzzling over the meaning of the vision, the men sent by Cornelius found Simon’s house and approached the gate.
43010018	They called out to ask if Simon called Peter was staying there.
43010019	As Peter continued to reflect on the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three men are looking for you.
43010020	So get up! Go downstairs and accompany them without hesitation, because I have sent them.”
43010021	So Peter went down to the men and said, “Here am I, the one you are looking for. Why have you come?”
43010022	“Cornelius the centurion has sent us,” they said. “He is a righteous and God-fearing man with a good reputation among the whole Jewish nation. A holy angel instructed him to request your presence in his home so he could hear a message from you.”
43010023	So Peter invited them in as his guests. And the next day he got ready and went with them, accompanied by some of the brothers from Joppa.
43010024	The following day he arrived in Caesarea, where Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.
43010025	As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet to worship him.
43010026	But Peter helped him up. “Stand up,” he said, “I am only a man myself.”
43010027	As Peter talked with him, he went inside and found many people gathered together.
43010028	He said to them, “You know how unlawful it is for a Jew to associate with a foreigner or visit him. But God has shown me that I should not call any man impure or unclean.
43010029	So when I was invited, I came without objection. I ask, then, why have you sent for me?”
43010030	Cornelius answered: “Four days ago I was in my house praying at this, the ninth hour. Suddenly a man in radiant clothing stood before me
43010031	and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your gifts to the poor have been remembered before God.
43010032	Therefore send to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter. He is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea.’
43010033	So I sent for you immediately, and you were kind enough to come. Now then, we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has instructed you to tell us.”
43010034	Then Peter began to speak: “I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism,
43010035	but welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right.
43010036	He has sent this message to the people of Israel, proclaiming the gospel of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
43010037	You yourselves know what has happened throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee with the baptism that John proclaimed:
43010038	how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, and how Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him.
43010039	We are witnesses of all that He did, both in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. And although they put Him to death by hanging Him on a tree,
43010040	God raised Him up on the third day and caused Him to be seen—
43010041	not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand, by us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
43010042	And He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that He is the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead.
43010043	All the prophets testify about Him that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.”
43010044	While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard his message.
43010045	All the circumcised believers who had accompanied Peter were astounded that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles.
43010046	For they heard them speaking in tongues and exalting God. Then Peter said,
43010047	“Can anyone withhold the water to baptize these people? They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have!”
43010048	So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay for a few days.
43011001	The apostles and brothers throughout Judea soon heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
43011002	So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers took issue with him
43011003	and said, “You visited uncircumcised men and ate with them.”
43011004	But Peter began and explained to them the whole sequence of events:
43011005	“I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision of something like a large sheet being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came right down to me.
43011006	I looked at it closely and saw four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the air.
43011007	Then I heard a voice saying to me, ‘Get up, Peter, kill and eat.’
43011008	‘No, Lord,’ I said, ‘for nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’
43011009	But the voice spoke from heaven a second time, ‘Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.’
43011010	This happened three times, and everything was drawn back up into heaven.
43011011	Just then three men sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.
43011012	The Spirit told me to accompany them without hesitation. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s home.
43011013	He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter.
43011014	He will convey to you a message by which you and all your household will be saved.’
43011015	As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as He had fallen upon us at the beginning.
43011016	Then I remembered the word of the Lord, how He said, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
43011017	So if God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to hinder the work of God?”
43011018	When they heard this, they had no further objections, and they glorified God, saying, “So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life.”
43011019	Meanwhile those scattered by the persecution that began with Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the message only to Jews.
43011020	But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began speaking to the Greeks as well, proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus.
43011021	The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.
43011022	When news of this reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
43011023	When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and encouraged them all to abide in the Lord with all their hearts.
43011024	Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.
43011025	Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,
43011026	and when he found him, he brought him back to Antioch. So for a full year they met together with the church and taught large numbers of people. The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.
43011027	In those days some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
43011028	One of them named Agabus stood up and predicted through the Spirit that a great famine would sweep across the whole world. (This happened under Claudius.)
43011029	So the disciples, each according to his ability, decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea.
43011030	This they did, sending their gifts to the elders with Barnabas and Saul.
43012001	About that time, King Herod reached out to harm some who belonged to the church.
43012002	He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword.
43012003	And seeing that this pleased the Jews, Herod proceeded to seize Peter during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
43012004	He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
43012005	So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was fervently praying to God for him.
43012006	On the night before Herod was to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, with sentries standing guard at the entrance to the prison.
43012007	Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He tapped Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Get up quickly.” And the chains fell off his wrists.
43012008	“Get dressed and put on your sandals,” said the angel. Peter did so, and the angel told him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.”
43012009	So Peter followed him out, but he was unaware that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was only seeing a vision.
43012010	They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city, which opened for them by itself. When they had gone outside and walked the length of one block, the angel suddenly left him.
43012011	Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know for sure that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s grasp and from everything the Jewish people were anticipating.”
43012012	And when he had realized this, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered together and were praying.
43012013	He knocked at the outer gate, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.
43012014	When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed that she forgot to open the gate, but ran inside and announced, “Peter is standing at the gate!”
43012015	“You are out of your mind,” they told her. But when she kept insisting it was so, they said, “It must be his angel.”
43012016	But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astounded.
43012017	Peter motioned with his hand for silence, and he described how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. “Send word to James and to the brothers,” he said, and he left for another place.
43012018	At daybreak there was no small commotion among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter.
43012019	After Herod had searched for him unsuccessfully, he examined the guards and ordered that they be executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and spent some time there.
43012020	Now Herod was in a furious dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon, and they convened before him. Having secured the support of Blastus, the king’s chamberlain, they asked for peace, because their region depended on the king’s country for food.
43012021	On the appointed day, Herod donned his royal robes, sat on his throne, and addressed the people.
43012022	And they began to shout, “This is the voice of a god, not a man!”
43012023	Immediately, because Herod did not give glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down, and he was eaten by worms and died.
43012024	But the word of God continued to spread and multiply.
43012025	When Barnabas and Saul had fulfilled their mission to Jerusalem, they returned, bringing with them John, also called Mark.
43013001	Now in the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen (who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch), and Saul.
43013002	While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”
43013003	And after they had fasted and prayed, they laid their hands on them and sent them off.
43013004	So Barnabas and Saul, sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.
43013005	When they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. And John was with them as their helper.
43013006	They traveled through the whole island as far as Paphos, where they found a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus,
43013007	an attendant of the proconsul, Sergius Paulus. The proconsul, a man of intelligence, summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God.
43013008	But Elymas the sorcerer (for that is what his name means) opposed them and tried to turn the proconsul from the faith.
43013009	Then Saul, who was also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked directly at Elymas
43013010	and said, “O child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness, you are full of all kinds of deceit and trickery! Will you never stop perverting the straight ways of the Lord?
43013011	Now look, the hand of the Lord is against you, and for a time you will be blind and unable to see the light of the sun.” Immediately mist and darkness came over him, and he groped about, seeking someone to lead him by the hand.
43013012	When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, for he was astonished at the teaching about the Lord.
43013013	After setting sail from Paphos, Paul and his companions came to Perga in Pamphylia, where John left them to return to Jerusalem.
43013014	And from Perga, they traveled inland to Pisidian Antioch, where they entered the synagogue on the Sabbath and sat down.
43013015	After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them: “Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.”
43013016	Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and began to speak: “Men of Israel and you Gentiles who fear God, listen to me!
43013017	The God of the people of Israel chose our fathers. He made them into a great people during their stay in Egypt, and with an uplifted arm He led them out of that land.
43013018	He endured their conduct for about forty years in the wilderness.
43013019	And having vanquished seven nations in Canaan, He gave their land to His people as an inheritance.
43013020	All this took about 450 years. After this, God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.
43013021	Then the people asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, who ruled forty years.
43013022	After removing Saul, He raised up David as their king and testified about him: ‘I have found David son of Jesse a man after My own heart; he will carry out My will in its entirety.’
43013023	From the descendants of this man, God has brought to Israel the Savior Jesus, as He promised.
43013024	Before the arrival of Jesus, John preached a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
43013025	As John was completing his course, he said, ‘Who do you suppose I am? I am not that One. But there is One coming after me whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.’
43013026	Brothers, children of Abraham, and you Gentiles who fear God, it is to us that this message of salvation has been sent.
43013027	The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus, yet in condemning Him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.
43013028	And though they found no ground for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have Him executed.
43013029	When they had carried out all that was written about Him, they took Him down from the tree and laid Him in a tomb.
43013030	But God raised Him from the dead,
43013031	and for many days He was seen by those who had accompanied Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now His witnesses to our people.
43013032	And now we proclaim to you the good news: What God promised our fathers
43013033	He has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm: ‘You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.’
43013034	In fact, God raised Him from the dead, never to see decay. As He has said: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.’
43013035	So also, He says in another Psalm: ‘You will not let Your Holy One see decay.’
43013036	For when David had served God’s purpose in his own generation, he fell asleep. His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay.
43013037	But the One whom God raised from the dead did not see decay.
43013038	Therefore let it be known to you, brothers, that through Jesus the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you.
43013039	Through Him everyone who believes is justified from everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.
43013040	Watch out, then, that what was spoken by the prophets does not happen to you:
43013041	‘Look, you scoffers, wonder and perish! For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.’”
43013042	As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people urged them to continue this message on the next Sabbath.
43013043	After the synagogue was dismissed, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke to them and urged them to continue in the grace of God.
43013044	On the following Sabbath, nearly the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
43013045	But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy, and they blasphemously contradicted what Paul was saying.
43013046	Then Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly: “It was necessary to speak the word of God to you first. But since you reject it and do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life, we now turn to the Gentiles.
43013047	For this is what the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have made you a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’”
43013048	When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and all who were appointed for eternal life believed.
43013049	And the word of the Lord spread throughout that region.
43013050	The Jews, however, incited the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. They stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their district.
43013051	So they shook the dust off their feet in protest against them and went to Iconium.
43013052	And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
43014001	At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue, where they spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.
43014002	But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.
43014003	So Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time there, speaking boldly for the Lord, who affirmed the message of His grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.
43014004	The people of the city were divided. Some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.
43014005	But when the Gentiles and Jews, together with their rulers, set out to mistreat and stone them,
43014006	they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding region,
43014007	where they continued to preach the gospel.
43014008	In Lystra there sat a man crippled in his feet, who was lame from birth and had never walked.
43014009	This man was listening to the words of Paul, who looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.
43014010	In a loud voice Paul called out, “Stand up on your feet!” And the man jumped up and began to walk.
43014011	When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices in the Lycaonian language: “The gods have come down to us in human form!”
43014012	Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.

43014016	In past generations, He let all nations go their own way.
43014017	Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”
43014018	Even with these words, Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them.
43014019	Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, presuming he was dead.
43014020	But after the disciples had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. And the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
43014021	They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,

43014026	From Attalia they sailed to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had just completed.
43014027	When they arrived, they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
43014028	And they spent a long time there with the disciples.
43015001	Then some men came down from Judea and were teaching the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.”
43015002	And after engaging these men in sharp debate, Paul and Barnabas were appointed, along with some other believers, to go up to Jerusalem to see the apostles and elders about this question.
43015003	Sent on their way by the church, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting the conversion of the Gentiles and bringing great joy to all the brothers.
43015004	On their arrival in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and apostles and elders, to whom they reported all that God had done through them.
43015005	But some believers from the party of the Pharisees stood up and declared, “The Gentiles must be circumcised and required to obey the law of Moses.”
43015006	So the apostles and elders met to look into this matter.
43015007	After much discussion, Peter got up and said to them, “Brothers, you know that in the early days God made a choice among you that the Gentiles would hear from my lips the message of the gospel and believe.
43015008	And God, who knows the heart, showed His approval by giving the Holy Spirit to them, just as He did to us.
43015009	He made no distinction between us and them, for He cleansed their hearts by faith.
43015010	Now then, why do you test God by placing on the necks of the disciples a yoke that neither we nor our fathers have been able to bear?
43015011	On the contrary, we believe it is through the grace of the Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are.”

43015016	‘After this I will return and rebuild the fallen tent of David. Its ruins I will rebuild, and I will restore it,
43015017	so that the remnant of men may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles who are called by My name, says the Lord who does these things

43015019	It is my judgment, therefore, that we should not cause trouble for the Gentiles who are turning to God.
43015020	Instead, we should write and tell them to abstain from food polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood.
43015021	For Moses has been proclaimed in every city from ancient times and is read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.”
43015022	Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to select men from among them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, two leaders among the brothers,

43015024	It has come to our attention that some went out from us without our authorization and unsettled you, troubling your minds by what they said.
43015025	So we all agreed to choose men to send to you along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
43015026	men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

43015028	It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond these essential requirements:
43015029	You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.
43015030	So the men were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they assembled the congregation and delivered the letter.
43015031	When the people read it, they rejoiced at its encouraging message.
43015032	Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the brothers.
43015033	After spending some time there, they were sent off by the brothers in peace to return to those who had sent them.
43015035	But Paul and Barnabas remained at Antioch, along with many others, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord.
43015036	Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us go back and visit the brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”

43015038	But Paul thought it best not to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.

43015040	but Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.
43015041	And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
43016001	Paul came to Derbe and then to Lystra, where he found a disciple named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father.
43016002	The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.
43016003	Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he took him and circumcised him on account of the Jews in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
43016004	As they went from town to town, they delivered the decisions handed down by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey.
43016005	So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.
43016006	After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia, they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.
43016007	And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.
43016008	So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
43016009	During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
43016010	As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.
43016011	We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the following day on to Neapolis.
43016012	From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.
43016013	On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.
43016014	Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.
43016015	And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us.
43016016	One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.
43016017	This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”
43016018	She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.
43016019	When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.
43016020	They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil
43016021	by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”
43016022	The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.
43016023	And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.
