43023008	For the Sadducees say that there is neither a resurrection nor angels nor spirits, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.
43023009	A great clamor arose, and some scribes from the party of the Pharisees got up and contended sharply, “We find nothing wrong with this man. What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”
43023010	The dispute grew so violent that the commander was afraid they would tear Paul to pieces. He ordered the soldiers to go down and remove him by force and bring him into the barracks.
43023011	The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, “Take courage! As you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so also you must testify in Rome.”
43023012	When daylight came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
43023013	More than forty of them were involved in this plot.
43023014	They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.
43023015	Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him down to you on the pretext of examining his case more carefully. We are ready to kill him on the way.”
43023016	But when the son of Paul’s sister heard about the plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.
43023017	Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.”
43023018	So the centurion took him to the commander and said, “Paul the prisoner sent and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”
43023019	The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside, and asked, “What do you need to tell me?”
43023020	He answered, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of acquiring more information about him.
43023021	Do not let them persuade you, because more than forty men are waiting to ambush him. They have bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him; they are ready now, awaiting your consent.”
43023022	So the commander dismissed the young man and instructed him, “Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”
43023023	Then he called two of his centurions and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea in the third hour of the night.
43023024	Provide mounts for Paul to take him safely to Governor Felix.”
43023025	And he wrote the following letter:
43023026	Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings.
43023027	This man was seized by the Jews, and they were about to kill him when I came with my troops to rescue him. For I had learned that he is a Roman citizen,
43023028	and since I wanted to understand their charges against him, I brought him down to their Sanhedrin.
43023029	I found that the accusation involved questions about their own law, but there was no charge worthy of death or imprisonment.
43023030	When I was informed that there was a plot against the man, I sent him to you at once. I also instructed his accusers to present their case against him before you.
43023031	So the soldiers followed their orders and brought Paul by night to Antipatris.
43023032	The next day they returned to the barracks and let the horsemen go on with him.
43023033	When the horsemen arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and presented Paul to him.
43023034	The governor read the letter and asked what province Paul was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia,
43023035	he said, “I will hear your case when your accusers arrive.” Then he ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod’s Praetorium.
43024001	Five days later the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, who presented to the governor their case against Paul.
43024002	When Paul had been called in, Tertullus opened the prosecution: “Because of you, we have enjoyed a lasting peace, and your foresight has brought improvements to this nation.
43024003	In every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with all gratitude.
43024004	But in order not to delay you any further, I beg your indulgence to hear us briefly.
43024005	We have found this man to be a pestilence, stirring up dissension among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,
43024006	and he even tried to desecrate the temple; so we seized him.
43024008	By examining him yourself, you will be able to learn the truth about all our charges against him.”
43024009	The Jews concurred, asserting that these charges were true.
43024010	When the governor motioned for Paul to speak, he began his response: “Knowing that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I gladly make my defense.
43024011	You can verify for yourself that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
43024012	Yet my accusers did not find me debating with anyone in the temple or riling up a crowd in the synagogues or in the city.
43024013	Nor can they prove to you any of their charges against me.
43024014	I do confess to you, however, that I worship the God of our fathers according to the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything that is laid down by the Law and written in the Prophets,
43024015	and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
43024016	In this hope, I strive always to maintain a clear conscience before God and man.
43024017	After several years, then, I returned to Jerusalem to bring alms to my people and to present offerings.
43024018	At the time they found me in the temple, I was ceremonially clean and was not inciting a crowd or an uproar. But there are some Jews from the province of Asia
43024019	who ought to appear before you and bring charges, if they have anything against me.
43024020	Otherwise, let these men state for themselves any crime they found in me when I stood before the Sanhedrin,
43024021	unless it was this one thing I called out as I stood in their presence: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.’”
43024022	Then Felix, who was well informed about the Way, adjourned the hearing and said, “When Lysias the commander comes, I will decide your case.”
43024023	He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard, but to allow him some freedom and permit his friends to minister to his needs.
43024024	After several days, Felix returned with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess. He sent for Paul and listened to him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.
43024025	As Paul expounded on righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became frightened and said, “You may go for now. When I find the time, I will call for you.”
43024026	At the same time, he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe. So he sent for Paul frequently and talked with him.
43024027	After two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And wishing to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.
43025001	Three days after his arrival in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,
43025002	where the chief priests and Jewish leaders presented their case against Paul. They urged Festus
43025003	to grant them a concession against Paul by summoning him to Jerusalem, because they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.
43025004	But Festus replied, “Paul is being held in Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.
43025005	So if this man has done anything wrong, let some of your leaders come down with me and accuse him there.”
43025006	After spending no more than eight or ten days with them, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat on the judgment seat and ordered that Paul be brought in.
43025007	When Paul arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges that they could not prove.
43025008	Then Paul made his defense: “I have committed no offense against the law of the Jews or against the temple or against Caesar.”
43025009	But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me on these charges?”
43025010	Paul replied, “I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be tried. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.
43025011	If, however, I am guilty of anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is no truth to their accusations against me, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
43025012	Then Festus conferred with his council and replied, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!”
43025013	After several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.
43025014	Since they were staying several days, Festus laid out Paul’s case before the king: “There is a certain man whom Felix left in prison.
43025015	While I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews presented their case and requested a judgment against him.
43025016	I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand a man over before he has had an opportunity to face his accusers and defend himself against their charges.
43025017	So when they came here with me, I did not delay. The next day I sat on the judgment seat and ordered that the man be brought in.
43025018	But when his accusers rose to speak, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.
43025019	They only had some contentions with him regarding their own religion and a certain Jesus who had died, but whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
43025020	Since I was at a loss as to how to investigate these matters, I asked if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried there on these charges.
43025021	But when Paul appealed to be held over for the decision of the Emperor, I ordered that he be held until I could send him to Caesar.”
43025022	Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear this man myself.” “Tomorrow you will hear him,” Festus declared.
43025023	The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the auditorium, along with the commanders and leading men of the city. And Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.
43025024	Then Festus said, “King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man. The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him, both here and in Jerusalem, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.
43025025	But I found he had done nothing worthy of death, and since he has now appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.
43025026	I have nothing definite to write to our sovereign about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after this inquiry I may have something to write.
43025027	For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without specifying the charges against him.”
43026001	Agrippa said to Paul, “You have permission to speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense:
43026002	“King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today to defend myself against all the accusations of the Jews,
43026003	especially since you are acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently.
43026004	Surely all the Jews know how I have lived from my earliest childhood among my own people, and also in Jerusalem.
43026005	They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I lived as a Pharisee, adhering to the strictest sect of our religion.
43026006	And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise that God made to our fathers,
43026007	the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled as they earnestly serve God day and night. It is because of this hope, O king, that I am accused by the Jews.
43026008	Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?
43026009	So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
43026010	And that is what I did in Jerusalem. With authority from the chief priests I put many of the saints in prison, and when they were condemned to death, I cast my vote against them.
43026011	I frequently had them punished in the synagogues, and I tried to make them blaspheme. In my raging fury against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.
43026012	In this pursuit I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.
43026013	About noon, O king, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and my companions.
43026014	We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice say to me in Hebrew, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
43026015	‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’ the Lord replied.
43026016	‘But get up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen from Me and what I will show you.
43026017	I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them
43026018	to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me.’
43026019	So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.
43026020	First to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then to everyone in the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I declared that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds worthy of their repentance.
43026021	For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.
43026022	But I have had God’s help to this day, and I stand here to testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:
43026023	that the Christ would suffer, and as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles.”
43026024	At this stage of Paul’s defense, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Your great learning is driving you to madness!”
43026025	But Paul answered, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety.
43026026	For the king knows about these matters, and I can speak freely to him. I am confident that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.
43026027	King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”
43026028	Then Agrippa said to Paul, “Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?”
43026029	“Short time or long,” Paul replied, “I wish to God that not only you but all who hear me this day may become what I am, except for these chains.”
43026030	Then the king and the governor rose, along with Bernice and those seated with them.
43026031	On their way out, they said to one another, “This man has done nothing worthy of death or imprisonment.”
43026032	And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
43027001	When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
43027002	We boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail for ports along the coast of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
43027003	The next day we landed at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul with consideration, allowing him to visit his friends and receive their care.
43027004	After putting out from there, we sailed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.
43027005	And when we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.
43027006	There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.
43027007	After sailing slowly for many days, we arrived off Cnidus. When the wind impeded us, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
43027008	After we had moved along the coast with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
43027009	By now much time had passed, and the voyage had already become dangerous because it was after the Fast. So Paul advised them,
43027010	“Men, I can see that our voyage will be filled with disaster and great loss, not only to ship and cargo, but to our own lives as well.”
43027011	But contrary to Paul’s advice, the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship.
43027012	Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, hoping that somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.
43027013	When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.
43027014	But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.
43027015	Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.
43027016	Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.
43027017	After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.
43027018	We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.
43027019	On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
43027020	When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.
43027021	After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.
43027022	But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.
43027023	For just last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me
43027024	and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’
43027025	So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.
43027026	However, we must run aground on some island.”
43027027	On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.
43027028	They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.
43027029	Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.
43027030	Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.
43027031	But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”
43027032	So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.
43027033	Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.
43027034	So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”
43027035	After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.
43027036	They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.
43027037	In all, there were 276 of us on board.
43027038	After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
43027039	When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.
43027040	Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
43027041	But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.
43027042	The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.
43027043	But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
43027044	The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.
43028001	Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
43028002	The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.
43028003	Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.
43028004	When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”
43028005	But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.
43028006	The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
43028007	Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
43028008	The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.
43028009	After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.
43028010	The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.
43028011	After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.
43028012	Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
43028013	From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.
43028014	There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.
43028015	The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.
43028016	When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
43028017	After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.
43028018	They examined me and wanted to release me, because there was no basis for a death sentence against me.
43028019	But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no charge to bring against my nation.
43028020	So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”
43028021	The leaders replied, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you.
43028022	But we consider your views worth hearing, because we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect.”
43028023	So they set a day to meet with Paul, and many people came to the place he was staying. He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.
43028024	Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.
43028025	They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet:
43028026	‘Go to this people and say, “You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.”
43028027	For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’
43028028	Be advised, therefore, that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”
43028030	Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house, welcoming all who came to visit him.
43028031	Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.
44001001	Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God—
44001002	the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,
44001003	regarding His Son, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh,
44001004	and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.
44001005	Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.
44001006	And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.
44001007	To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
44001008	First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed all over the world.
44001009	God, whom I serve with my spirit in preaching the gospel of His Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you
44001010	in my prayers at all times, asking that now at last by God’s will I may succeed in coming to you.
44001011	For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,
44001012	that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.
44001013	I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.
44001014	I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.
44001015	That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
44001016	I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek.
44001017	For the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.”
44001018	The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness.
44001019	For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.
44001020	For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse.
44001021	For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.
44001022	Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools,
44001023	and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.
44001024	Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another.
44001025	They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is forever worthy of praise! Amen.
44001026	For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.
44001027	Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.
44001028	Furthermore, since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.
44001029	They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed, and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice. They are gossips,
44001030	slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, and boastful. They invent new forms of evil; they disobey their parents.
44001031	They are senseless, faithless, heartless, merciless.
44001032	Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things are worthy of death, they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them.
44002001	You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on another. For on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.
44002002	And we know that God’s judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.
44002003	So when you, O man, pass judgment on others, yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?
44002004	Or do you disregard the riches of His kindness, tolerance, and patience, not realizing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?
44002005	But because of your hard and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath, when God’s righteous judgment will be revealed.
44002006	God “will repay each one according to his deeds.”
44002007	To those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory, honor, and immortality, He will give eternal life.
44002008	But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow wickedness, there will be wrath and anger.
44002009	There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, first for the Jew, then for the Greek;
44002010	but glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first for the Jew, then for the Greek.
44002011	For God does not show favoritism.
44002012	All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.
44002013	For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but it is the doers of the law who will be declared righteous.
44002014	Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law.
44002015	So they show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts either accusing or defending them
44002016	on the day when God will judge men’s secrets through Christ Jesus, as proclaimed by my gospel.
44002017	Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and boast in God;
44002018	if you know His will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law;
44002019	if you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those in darkness,
44002020	an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth—
44002021	you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
44002022	You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
44002023	You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
44002024	As it is written: “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”
44002025	Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
44002026	If a man who is not circumcised keeps the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?
44002027	The one who is physically uncircumcised yet keeps the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.
44002028	A man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, nor is circumcision only outward and physical.
44002029	No, a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a man’s praise does not come from men, but from God.
44003001	What, then, is the advantage of being a Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision?
44003002	Much in every way. First of all, they have been entrusted with the very words of God.
44003003	What if some did not have faith? Will their lack of faith nullify God’s faithfulness?
44003004	Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar. As it is written: “So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge.”
44003005	But if our unrighteousness highlights the righteousness of God, what shall we say? That God is unjust to inflict His wrath on us? I am speaking in human terms.
44003006	Certainly not! In that case, how could God judge the world?
44003007	However, if my falsehood accentuates God’s truthfulness, to the increase of His glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?
44003008	Why not say, as some slanderously claim that we say, “Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is deserved!
44003009	What then? Are we any better? Not at all. For we have already made the charge that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin.
44003010	As it is written: “There is no one righteous, not even one.
44003011	There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.
44003012	All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.”
44003013	“Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.” “The venom of vipers is on their lips.”
44003014	“Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.”
44003015	“Their feet are swift to shed blood;
44003016	ruin and misery lie in their wake,
44003017	and the way of peace they have not known.”
44003018	“There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
44003019	Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
44003020	Therefore no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law. For the law merely brings awareness of sin.
44003021	But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, as attested by the Law and the Prophets.
44003022	And this righteousness from God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no distinction,
44003023	for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
44003024	and are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
44003025	God presented Him as an atoning sacrifice in His blood through faith, in order to demonstrate His righteousness, because in His forbearance He had passed over the sins committed beforehand.
44003026	He did this to demonstrate His righteousness at the present time, so as to be just and to justify the one who has faith in Jesus.
44003027	Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith.
44003028	For we maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law.
44003029	Is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too,
44003030	since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.
44003031	Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.
44004001	What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has discovered?
44004002	If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.
44004003	For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
44004004	Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.
44004005	However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited as righteousness.
44004006	And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
44004007	“Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
44004008	Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.”
44004009	Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.
44004010	In what context was it credited? Was it after his circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.
44004011	And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.
44004012	And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.
44004013	For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.
44004014	For if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless and the promise is worthless,
44004015	because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law, there is no transgression.
44004016	Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring—not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.
44004017	As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the presence of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist.
44004018	Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”
44004019	Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.
44004020	Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,
44004021	being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised.
44004022	This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”
44004023	Now the words “it was credited to him” were written not only for Abraham,
44004024	but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited—for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
44004025	He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.
44005001	Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
44005002	through whom we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we stand. And we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.
44005003	Not only that, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance;
44005004	perseverance, character; and character, hope.
44005005	And hope does not disappoint us, because God has poured out His love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, whom He has given us.
44005006	For at just the right time, while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.
44005007	Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die.
44005008	But God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
44005009	Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!
44005010	For if, when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!
44005011	Not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
44005012	Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned.
44005013	For sin was in the world before the law was given; but sin is not taken into account when there is no law.
44005014	Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed. He is a pattern of the One to come.
44005015	But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many!
44005016	Again, the gift is not like the result of the one man’s sin: The judgment that followed one sin brought condemnation, but the gift that followed many trespasses brought justification.
44005017	For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!
44005018	So then, just as one trespass brought condemnation for all men, so also one act of righteousness brought justification and life for all men.
44005019	For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.
44005020	The law came in so that the trespass would increase; but where sin increased, grace increased all the more,
44005021	so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
44006001	What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?
44006002	Certainly not! How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?
44006003	Or aren’t you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?
44006004	We were therefore buried with Him through baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life.
44006005	For if we have been united with Him like this in His death, we will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.
44006006	We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, that we should no longer be slaves to sin.
44006007	For anyone who has died has been freed from sin.
44006008	Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.
44006009	For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.
44006010	The death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.
44006011	So you too must count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
44006012	Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires.
44006013	Do not present the parts of your body to sin as instruments of wickedness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life; and present the parts of your body to Him as instruments of righteousness.
44006014	For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace.
44006015	What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Certainly not!
44006016	Do you not know that when you offer yourselves as obedient slaves, you are slaves to the one you obey, whether you are slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness?
44006017	But thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed.
44006018	You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.
44006019	I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness.
44006020	For when you were slaves to sin, you were free of obligation to righteousness.
44006021	What fruit did you reap at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The outcome of those things is death.
44006022	But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the fruit you reap leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life.
44006023	For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
44007001	Do you not know, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law has authority over a man only as long as he lives?
44007002	For instance, a married woman is bound by law to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is released from the law of marriage.
44007003	So then, if she is joined to another man while her husband is still alive, she is called an adulteress; but if her husband dies, she is free from that law and is not an adulteress if she marries another man.
44007004	Therefore, my brothers, you also died to the law through the body of Christ, that you might belong to another, to Him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit to God.
44007005	For when we lived according to the flesh, the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in our bodies, bearing fruit for death.
44007006	But now, having died to what bound us, we have been released from the law, so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit, and not in the old way of the written code.
44007007	What then shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Indeed, I would not have been mindful of sin if not for the law. For I would not have been aware of coveting if the law had not said, “Do not covet.”
44007008	But sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of covetous desire. For apart from the law, sin is dead.
44007009	Once I was alive apart from the law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life and I died.
44007010	So I discovered that the very commandment that was meant to bring life actually brought death.
44007011	For sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through the commandment put me to death.
44007012	So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.
44007013	Did that which is good, then, become death to me? Certainly not! But in order that sin might be exposed as sin, it produced death in me through what was good, so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful.
44007014	We know that the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.
44007015	I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do, I do not do. But what I hate, I do.
44007016	And if I do what I do not want to do, I admit that the law is good.
44007017	In that case, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.
44007018	I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my flesh; for I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out.
44007019	For I do not do the good I want to do. Instead, I keep on doing the evil I do not want to do.
44007020	And if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.
44007021	So this is the principle I have discovered: When I want to do good, evil is right there with me.
44007022	For in my inner being I delight in God’s law.
44007023	But I see another law at work in my body, warring against the law of my mind and holding me captive to the law of sin that dwells within me.
44007024	What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?
44007025	Thanks be to God, through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, with my mind I serve the law of God, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin.
44008001	Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
44008002	For in Christ Jesus the law of the Spirit of life set you free from the law of sin and death.
44008003	For what the law was powerless to do in that it was weakened by the flesh, God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin. He thus condemned sin in the flesh,
44008004	so that the righteous standard of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.
44008005	Those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh; but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.
44008006	The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace,
44008007	because the mind of the flesh is hostile to God: It does not submit to God’s law, nor can it do so.
44008008	Those controlled by the flesh cannot please God.
44008009	You, however, are controlled not by the flesh, but by the Spirit, if the Spirit of God lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.
44008010	But if Christ is in you, your body is dead because of sin, yet your spirit is alive because of righteousness.
44008011	And if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead is living in you, He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit, who lives in you.
44008012	Therefore, brothers, we have an obligation, but it is not to the flesh, to live according to it.
44008013	For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
44008014	For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.
44008015	For you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption to sonship, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
44008016	The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.
44008017	And if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ—if indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him.
44008018	I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us.
44008019	The creation waits in eager expectation for the revelation of the sons of God.
44008020	For the creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope
44008021	that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and brought into the glorious freedom of the children of God.
44008022	We know that the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until the present time.
44008023	Not only that, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies.
44008024	For in this hope we were saved; but hope that is seen is no hope at all. Who hopes for what he can already see?
44008025	But if we hope for what we do not yet see, we wait for it patiently.
44008026	In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.
44008027	And He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.
44008028	And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.
44008029	For those God foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers.
44008030	And those He predestined, He also called; those He called, He also justified; those He justified, He also glorified.
44008031	What then shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
44008032	He who did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?
44008033	Who will bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies.
44008034	Who is there to condemn us? For Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that was raised to life, is at the right hand of God—and He is interceding for us.
44008035	Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall trouble or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?
44008036	As it is written: “For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.”
44008037	No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.
44008038	For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers,
44008039	neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
44009001	I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as confirmed by my conscience in the Holy Spirit.
44009002	I have deep sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.
44009003	For I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my own flesh and blood,
44009004	the people of Israel. Theirs is the adoption as sons; theirs the divine glory and the covenants; theirs the giving of the law, the temple worship, and the promises.
44009005	Theirs are the patriarchs, and from them proceeds the human descent of Christ, who is God over all, forever worthy of praise! Amen.
44009006	It is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.
44009007	Nor because they are Abraham’s descendants are they all his children. On the contrary, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”
44009008	So it is not the children of the flesh who are God’s children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring.
44009009	For this is what the promise stated: “At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son.”
44009010	Not only that, but Rebecca’s children were conceived by one man, our father Isaac.
44009011	Yet before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad, in order that God’s plan of election might stand,
44009012	not by works but by Him who calls, she was told, “The older will serve the younger.”
44009013	So it is written: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”
44009014	What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Certainly not!
44009015	For He says to Moses: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”
44009016	So then, it does not depend on man’s desire or effort, but on God’s mercy.
44009017	For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: “I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power in you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
44009018	Therefore God has mercy on whom He wants to have mercy, and He hardens whom He wants to harden.
44009019	One of you will say to me, “Then why does God still find fault? For who can resist His will?”
44009020	But who are you, O man, to talk back to God? Shall what is formed say to Him who formed it, “Why did You make me like this?”
44009021	Does not the potter have the right to make from the same lump of clay one vessel for special occasions and another for common use?
44009022	What if God, intending to show His wrath and make His power known, bore with great patience the vessels of His wrath, prepared for destruction?
44009023	What if He did this to make the riches of His glory known to the vessels of His mercy, whom He prepared in advance for glory—
44009024	including us, whom He has called not only from the Jews, but also from the Gentiles?
44009025	As He says in Hosea: “I will call them ‘My People’ who are not My people, and I will call her ‘My Beloved’ who is not My beloved,”
44009026	and, “It will happen that in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’”
44009027	Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: “Though the number of the Israelites is like the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved.
44009028	For the Lord will carry out His sentence on the earth thoroughly and decisively.”
44009029	It is just as Isaiah foretold: “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.”
44009030	What then will we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith;
44009031	but Israel, who pursued a law of righteousness, has not attained it.
44009032	Why not? Because their pursuit was not by faith, but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone,
44009033	as it is written: “See, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
44010001	Brothers, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is for their salvation.
44010002	For I testify about them that they are zealous for God, but not on the basis of knowledge.
44010003	Because they were ignorant of God’s righteousness and sought to establish their own, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.
44010004	For Christ is the end of the law, to bring righteousness to everyone who believes.
44010005	For concerning the righteousness that is by the law, Moses writes: “The man who does these things will live by them.”
44010006	But the righteousness that is by faith says: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ (that is, to bring Christ down)
44010007	or, ‘Who will descend into the Abyss?’ (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).”
44010008	But what does it say? “The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart,” that is, the word of faith we are proclaiming:
44010009	that if you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.
44010010	For with your heart you believe and are justified, and with your mouth you confess and are saved.
44010011	It is just as the Scripture says: “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
44010012	For there is no difference between Jew and Greek: The same Lord is Lord of all, and gives richly to all who call on Him,
44010013	for, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”
44010014	How then can they call on the One in whom they have not believed? And how can they believe in the One of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone to preach?
44010015	And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
44010016	But not all of them welcomed the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
44010017	Consequently, faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.
44010018	But I ask, did they not hear? Indeed they did: “Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.”
44010019	I ask instead, did Israel not understand? First, Moses says: “I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation; I will make you angry by a nation without understanding.”
44010020	And Isaiah boldly says: “I was found by those who did not seek Me; I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me.”
44010021	But as for Israel he says: “All day long I have held out My hands to a disobedient and obstinate people.”
44011001	I ask then, did God reject His people? Certainly not! I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.
44011002	God did not reject His people, whom He foreknew. Do you not know what the Scripture says about Elijah, how he appealed to God against Israel:
44011003	“Lord, they have killed Your prophets and torn down Your altars. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well”?
44011004	And what was the divine reply to him? “I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”
44011005	In the same way, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.
44011006	And if it is by grace, then it is no longer by works. Otherwise, grace would no longer be grace.
44011007	What then? What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did. The others were hardened,
44011008	as it is written: “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear, to this very day.”
44011009	And David says: “May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution to them.
44011010	May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.”
44011011	I ask then, did they stumble so as to fall beyond recovery? Certainly not! However, because of their trespass, salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel jealous.
44011012	But if their trespass means riches for the world, and their failure means riches for the Gentiles, how much greater riches will their fullness bring!
44011013	I am speaking to you Gentiles. Inasmuch as I am the apostle to the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry
44011014	in the hope that I may provoke my own people to jealousy and save some of them.
44011015	For if their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?
44011016	If the first part of the dough is holy, so is the whole batch; if the root is holy, so are the branches.
44011017	Now if some branches have been broken off, and you, a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others to share in the nourishment of the olive root,
44011018	do not boast over those branches. If you do, remember this: You do not support the root, but the root supports you.
44011019	You will say then, “Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in.”
44011020	That is correct: They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be arrogant, but be afraid.
44011021	For if God did not spare the natural branches, He will certainly not spare you either.
44011022	Take notice, therefore, of the kindness and severity of God: severity to those who fell, but kindness to you, if you continue in His kindness. Otherwise you also will be cut off.
44011023	And if they do not persist in unbelief, they will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.
44011024	For if you were cut from a wild olive tree, and contrary to nature were grafted into one that is cultivated, how much more readily will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!
44011025	I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, brothers, so that you will not be conceited: A hardening in part has come to Israel, until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.
44011026	And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will remove godlessness from Jacob.
44011027	And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.”
44011028	Regarding the gospel, they are enemies on your account; but regarding election, they are loved on account of the patriarchs.
44011029	For God’s gifts and His call are irrevocable.
44011030	Just as you who formerly disobeyed God have now received mercy through their disobedience,
44011031	so they too have now disobeyed, in order that they too may now receive mercy through the mercy shown to you.
44011032	For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.
44011033	O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!
44011034	“Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?”
44011035	“Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?”
44011036	For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever! Amen.
44012001	Therefore I urge you, brothers, on account of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.
44012002	Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.
44012003	For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.
44012004	Just as each of us has one body with many members, and not all members have the same function,
44012005	so in Christ we who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another.
44012006	We have different gifts according to the grace given us. If one’s gift is prophecy, let him use it in proportion to his faith;
44012007	if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach;
44012008	if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.
44012009	Love must be sincere. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.
44012010	Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.
44012011	Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.
44012012	Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.
44012013	Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.
44012014	Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.
44012015	Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
44012016	Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but associate with the lowly. Do not be conceited.
44012017	Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
44012018	If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.
44012019	Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
44012020	On the contrary, “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”
44012021	Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
44013001	Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
44013002	Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.
44013003	For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.
44013004	For he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God’s servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.
44013005	Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience.
44013006	This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.
44013007	Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.
44013008	Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
44013009	The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
44013010	Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
44013011	And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.
44013012	The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.
44013013	Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.
44013014	Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.
44014001	Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.
44014002	For one person has faith to eat all things, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.
44014003	The one who eats everything must not belittle the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted him.
44014004	Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.
44014005	One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.
44014006	He who observes a special day does so to the Lord; he who eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.
44014007	For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.
44014008	If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
44014009	For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.
44014010	Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or why do you belittle your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.
44014011	It is written: “As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.”
44014012	So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.
44014013	Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.
44014014	I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.
44014015	If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.
44014016	Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.
44014017	For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
44014018	For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.
44014019	So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.
44014020	Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.
44014021	It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.
44014022	Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.
44014023	But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.
44015001	We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.
44015002	Each of us should please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.
44015003	For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”
44015004	For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.
44015005	Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus,
44015006	so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
44015007	Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.

44015009	so that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written: “Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing hymns to Your name.”
44015010	Again, it says: “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.”
44015011	And again: “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples.”

44015013	Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe in Him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
44015014	I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.

44015017	Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.
44015018	I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed,
44015019	by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.
44015020	In this way I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.
44015021	Rather, as it is written: “Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
44015022	That is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.

44015025	Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there.

44015028	So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.
44015029	I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.

44015031	Pray that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints there,
44015032	so that by God’s will I may come to you with joy and together with you be refreshed.
44015033	The God of peace be with all of you. Amen.

45001027	But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.
45001028	He chose the lowly and despised things of the world, and the things that are not, to nullify the things that are,

45001030	It is because of Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God: our righteousness, holiness, and redemption.

45002001	When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with eloquence or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony about God.
45002002	For I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified.
45002003	I came to you in weakness and fear, and with much trembling.
45002004	My message and my preaching were not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit’s power,
45002005	so that your faith would not rest on men’s wisdom, but on God’s power.
45002006	Among the mature, however, we speak a message of wisdom—but not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing.
45002007	No, we speak of the mysterious and hidden wisdom of God, which He destined for our glory before time began.
45002008	None of the rulers of this age understood it. For if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
45002009	Rather, as it is written: “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no heart has imagined, what God has prepared for those who love Him.”
45002010	But God has revealed it to us by the Spirit. The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.
45002011	For who among men knows the thoughts of man except his own spirit within him? So too, no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.
45002012	We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, that we may understand what God has freely given us.
45002013	And this is what we speak, not in words taught us by human wisdom, but in words taught by the Spirit, expressing spiritual truths in spiritual words.
45002014	The natural man does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God. For they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.
45002015	The spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is not subject to anyone’s judgment.
45002016	“For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.
45003001	Brothers, I could not address you as spiritual, but as worldly—as infants in Christ.
45003002	I gave you milk, not solid food, for you were not yet ready for solid food. In fact, you are still not ready,
45003003	for you are still worldly. For since there is jealousy and dissension among you, are you not worldly? Are you not walking in the way of man?

45006009	Do you not know that the wicked will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who submit to or perform homosexual acts,
45006010	nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor verbal abusers, nor swindlers, will inherit the kingdom of God.
45006011	And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
45006012	“Everything is permissible for me,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible for me,” but I will not be mastered by anything.
45006013	“Food for the stomach and the stomach for food,” but God will destroy them both. The body is not intended for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
45006014	By His power God raised the Lord from the dead, and He will raise us also.
45006015	Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and unite them with a prostitute? Never!
45006016	Or don’t you know that he who unites himself with a prostitute is one with her in body? For it is said, “The two will become one flesh.”
45006017	But he who unites himself with the Lord is one with Him in spirit.
45006018	Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a man can commit is outside his body, but he who sins sexually sins against his own body.
45006019	Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own;
45006020	you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body.
45007001	Now for the matters you wrote about: It is good to abstain from sexual relations.
45007002	But because there is so much sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.
45007003	The husband should fulfill his marital duty to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband.
45007004	The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband. Likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife.
45007005	Do not deprive each other, except by mutual consent and for a time, so you may devote yourselves to prayer. Then come together again, so that Satan will not tempt you through your lack of self-control.
45007006	I say this as a concession, not as a command.
45007007	I wish that all men were as I am. But each man has his own gift from God; one has this gift, another has that.
45007008	Now to the unmarried and widows I say this: It is good for them to remain unmarried, as I am.
