45007009	But if they cannot control themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn with passion.
45007010	To the married I give this command (not I, but the Lord): A wife must not separate from her husband.
45007011	But if she does, she must remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.
45007012	To the rest I say this (I, not the Lord): If a brother has an unbelieving wife and she is willing to live with him, he must not divorce her.
45007013	And if a woman has an unbelieving husband and he is willing to live with her, she must not divorce him.
45007014	For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through his believing wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified through her believing husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
45007015	But if the unbeliever leaves, let him go. The believing brother or sister is not bound in such cases. God has called you to live in peace.
45007016	How do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
45007017	Regardless, each one should lead the life that the Lord has assigned to him and to which God has called him. This is what I prescribe in all the churches.
45007018	Was a man already circumcised when he was called? He should not become uncircumcised. Was a man still uncircumcised when called? He should not be circumcised.
45007019	Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God’s commandments is what counts.
45007020	Each one should remain in the situation he was in when he was called.
45007021	Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let it concern you—but if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity.
45007022	For he who was a slave when he was called by the Lord is the Lord’s freedman. Conversely, he who was a free man when he was called is Christ’s slave.
45007023	You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men.
45007024	Brothers, each one should remain in the situation he was in when God called him.
45007025	Now about virgins, I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one who by the Lord’s mercy is trustworthy.
45007026	Because of the present crisis, I think it is good for a man to remain as he is.
45007027	Are you committed to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you free of commitment? Do not look for a wife.
45007028	But if you do marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But those who marry will face troubles in this life, and I want to spare you this.
45007029	What I am saying, brothers, is that the time is short. From now on those who have wives should live as if they had none;
45007030	those who weep, as if they did not; those who are joyful, as if they were not; those who make a purchase, as if they had nothing;
45007031	and those who use the things of this world, as if not dependent on them. For this world in its present form is passing away.
45007032	I want you to be free from concern. The unmarried man is concerned about the work of the Lord, how he can please the Lord.
45007033	But the married man is concerned about the affairs of this world, how he can please his wife,
45007034	and his interests are divided. The unmarried woman or virgin is concerned about the work of the Lord, how she can be holy in both body and spirit. But the married woman is concerned about the affairs of this world, how she can please her husband.
45007035	I am saying this for your own good, not to restrict you, but in order to promote proper decorum and undivided devotion to the Lord.
45007036	However, if someone thinks he is acting inappropriately toward his betrothed, and if she is beyond her youth and they ought to marry, let him do as he wishes; he is not sinning; they should get married.
45007037	But the man who is firmly established in his heart and under no constraint, with control over his will and resolve in his heart not to marry the virgin, he will do well.
45007038	So then, he who marries the virgin does well, but he who does not marry her does even better.
45007039	A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.
45007040	In my judgment, however, she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
45008001	Now about food sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
45008002	The one who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know.
45008003	But the one who loves God is known by God.
45008004	So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.
45008005	For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (as there are many so-called gods and lords),
45008006	yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.
45008007	But not everyone has this knowledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol. And since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.
45008008	But food does not bring us closer to God: We are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.
45008009	Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.
45008010	For if someone with a weak conscience sees you who are well informed eating in an idol’s temple, will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?
45008011	So this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.
45008012	By sinning against your brothers in this way and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
45008013	Therefore, if what I eat causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause him to stumble.
45009001	Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you yourselves not my workmanship in the Lord?
45009002	Even if I am not an apostle to others, surely I am to you. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
45009003	This is my defense to those who scrutinize me:
45009004	Have we no right to food and to drink?
45009005	Have we no right to take along a believing wife, as do the other apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas?
45009006	Or are Barnabas and I the only apostles who must work for a living?
45009007	Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of its milk?
45009008	Do I say this from a human perspective? Doesn’t the Law say the same thing?
45009009	For it is written in the Law of Moses: “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” Is it about oxen that God is concerned?
45009010	Isn’t He actually speaking on our behalf? Indeed, this was written for us, because when the plowman plows and the thresher threshes, they should also expect to share in the harvest.
45009011	If we have sown spiritual seed among you, is it too much for us to reap a material harvest from you?
45009012	If others have this right to your support, shouldn’t we have it all the more? But we did not exercise this right. Instead, we put up with anything rather than hinder the gospel of Christ.
45009013	Do you not know that those who work in the temple eat of its food, and those who serve at the altar partake of its offerings?
45009014	In the same way, the Lord has prescribed that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel.
45009015	But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this to suggest that something be done for me. Indeed, I would rather die than let anyone nullify my boast.
45009016	Yet when I preach the gospel, I have no reason to boast, because I am obligated to preach. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!
45009017	If my preaching is voluntary, I have a reward. But if it is not voluntary, I am still entrusted with a responsibility.
45009018	What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not use up my rights in preaching it.
45009019	Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.
45009020	To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law (though I myself am not under the law), to win those under the law.
45009021	To those without the law I became like one without the law (though I am not outside the law of God but am under the law of Christ), to win those without the law.
45009022	To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.
45009023	I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings.
45009024	Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to take the prize.
45009025	Everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. They do it for a crown that is perishable, but we do it for a crown that is imperishable.
45009026	Therefore I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air.
45009027	No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.
45010001	I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our forefathers were all under the cloud, and that they all passed through the sea.
45010002	They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
45010003	They all ate the same spiritual food
45010004	and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.
45010005	Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness.
45010006	These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.
45010007	Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry.”
45010008	We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.
45010009	We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.
45010010	And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.
45010011	Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.
45010012	So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.
45010013	No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.
45010014	Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
45010015	I speak to reasonable people; judge for yourselves what I say.
45010016	Is not the cup of blessing that we bless a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of Christ?
45010017	Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf.
45010018	Consider the people of Israel: Are not those who eat the sacrifices fellow partakers in the altar?
45010019	Am I suggesting, then, that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
45010020	No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to be participants with demons.
45010021	You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too.
45010022	Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?
45010023	“Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is edifying.
45010024	No one should seek his own good, but the good of others.
45010025	Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience,
45010026	for, “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.”
45010027	If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat anything set before you without raising questions of conscience.
45010028	But if someone tells you, “This food was offered to idols,” then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience—
45010029	the other one’s conscience, I mean, not your own. For why should my freedom be determined by someone else’s conscience?
45010030	If I partake in the meal with thankfulness, why am I denounced because of that for which I give thanks?
45010031	So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.
45010032	Do not become a stumbling block, whether to Jews or Greeks or the church of God—
45010033	as I also try to please everyone in all I do. For I am not seeking my own good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.
45011001	You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.
45011002	Now I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.
45011003	But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
45011004	Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.
45011005	And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is just as if her head were shaved.
45011006	If a woman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off. And if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off, she should cover her head.
45011007	A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.
45011008	For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.
45011009	Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.
45011010	For this reason a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.
45011011	In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.
45011012	For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God.
45011013	Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
45011014	Doesn’t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,
45011015	but that if a woman has long hair, it is her glory? For long hair is given to her as a covering.
45011016	If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.
45011017	In the following instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good.
45011018	First of all, I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.
45011019	And indeed, there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.
45011020	Now then, when you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat.
45011021	For as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal. While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.
45011022	Don’t you have your own homes in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What can I say to you? Shall I praise you for this? No, I will not!
45011023	For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: The Lord Jesus, on the night He was betrayed, took bread,
45011024	and when He had given thanks, He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
45011025	In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”
45011026	For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.
45011027	Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
45011028	Each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup.
45011029	For anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body eats and drinks judgment on himself.
45011030	That is why many among you are weak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep.
45011031	Now if we judged ourselves properly, we would not come under judgment.
45011032	But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined so that we will not be condemned with the world.
45011033	So, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
45011034	If anyone is hungry, he should eat at home, so that when you come together it will not result in judgment. And when I come, I will give instructions about the remaining matters.
45012001	Now about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed.
45012002	You know that when you were pagans, you were influenced and led astray to mute idols.
45012003	Therefore I inform you that no one who is speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus be cursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.
45012004	There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.
45012005	There are different ministries, but the same Lord.
45012006	There are different ways of working, but the same God works all things in all people.
45012007	Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.
45012008	To one there is given through the Spirit the message of wisdom, to another the message of knowledge by the same Spirit,
45012009	to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by that one Spirit,
45012010	to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.
45012011	All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who apportions them to each one as He determines.
45012012	The body is a unit, though it is composed of many parts. And although its parts are many, they all form one body. So it is with Christ.
45012013	For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slave or free, and we were all given one Spirit to drink.
45012014	For the body does not consist of one part, but of many.
45012015	If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.
45012016	And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.
45012017	If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?
45012018	But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.
45012019	If they were all one part, where would the body be?
45012020	As it is, there are many parts, but one body.
45012021	The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”
45012022	On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,
45012023	and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor. And our unpresentable parts are treated with special modesty,
45012024	whereas our presentable parts have no such need. But God has composed the body and has given greater honor to the parts that lacked it,
45012025	so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another.
45012026	If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it.
45012027	Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.
45012028	And in the church God has appointed first of all apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then workers of miracles, and those with gifts of healing, helping, administration, and various tongues.
45012029	Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?
45012030	Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
45012031	But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And now I will show you the most excellent way.
45013001	If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.
45013002	If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.
45013003	If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing.
45013004	Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
45013005	It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.
45013006	Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.
45013007	It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
45013008	Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.
45013009	For we know in part and we prophesy in part,
45013010	but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away.
45013011	When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.
45013012	Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.
45013013	And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.
45014001	Earnestly pursue love and eagerly desire spiritual gifts, especially the gift of prophecy.
45014002	For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God. Indeed, no one understands him; he utters mysteries in the Spirit.
45014003	But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, encouragement, and comfort.
45014004	The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.
45014005	I wish that all of you could speak in tongues, but I would rather have you prophesy. He who prophesies is greater than one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets so that the church may be edified.
45014006	Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you, unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
45014007	Even in the case of lifeless instruments, such as the flute or harp, how will anyone recognize the tune they are playing unless the notes are distinct?
45014008	Again, if the trumpet sounds a muffled call, who will prepare for battle?
45014009	So it is with you. Unless you speak intelligible words with your tongue, how will anyone know what you are saying? You will just be speaking into the air.
45014010	Assuredly, there are many different languages in the world, yet none of them is without meaning.
45014011	If, then, I do not know the meaning of someone’s language, I am a foreigner to the speaker, and he is a foreigner to me.
45014012	It is the same with you. Since you are eager to have spiritual gifts, strive to excel in gifts that build up the church.
45014013	Therefore, the one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.
45014014	For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.
45014015	What then shall I do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my mind.
45014016	Otherwise, if you speak a blessing in spirit, how can someone who is uninstructed say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
45014017	You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other one is not edified.
45014018	I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
45014019	But in the church, I would rather speak five coherent words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.
45014020	Brothers, stop thinking like children. In regard to evil be infants, but in your thinking be mature.
45014021	It is written in the Law: “By strange tongues and foreign lips I will speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to Me, says the Lord.”
45014022	Tongues, then, are a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers. Prophecy, however, is for believers, not for unbelievers.
45014023	So if the whole church comes together and everyone speaks in tongues, and some who are uninstructed or some unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are out of your minds?
45014024	But if an unbeliever or uninstructed person comes in while everyone is prophesying, he will be convicted and called to account by all,
45014025	and the secrets of his heart will be made known. So he will fall facedown and worship God, proclaiming, “God is truly among you!”
45014026	What then shall we say, brothers? When you come together, everyone has a psalm or a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. All of these must be done to build up the church.
45014027	If anyone speaks in a tongue, two, or at most three, should speak in turn, and someone must interpret.
45014028	But if there is no interpreter, he should remain silent in the church and speak only to himself and God.
45014029	Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should weigh carefully what is said.
45014030	And if a revelation comes to someone who is seated, the first speaker should stop.
45014031	For you can all prophesy in turn so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged.
45014032	The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
45014033	For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace—as in all the churches of the saints.
45014034	Women are to be silent in the churches. They are not permitted to speak, but must be in submission, as the law says.
45014035	If they wish to inquire about something, they are to ask their own husbands at home; for it is dishonorable for a woman to speak in the church.
45014036	Did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?
45014037	If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual person, let him acknowledge that what I am writing you is the Lord’s command.
45014038	But if anyone ignores this, he himself will be ignored.
45014039	So, my brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
45014040	But everything must be done in a proper and orderly manner.
45015001	Now, brothers, I want to remind you of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, and in which you stand firm.
45015002	By this gospel you are saved, if you hold firmly to the word I preached to you. Otherwise, you have believed in vain.
45015003	For what I received I passed on to you as of first importance: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
45015004	that He was buried, that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
45015005	and that He appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve.
45015006	After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep.
45015007	Then He appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
45015008	And last of all He appeared to me also, as to one of untimely birth.
45015009	For I am the least of the apostles and am unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
45015010	But by the grace of God I am what I am, and His grace to me was not in vain. No, I worked harder than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me.
45015011	Whether, then, it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
45015012	But if it is preached that Christ has been raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
45015013	If there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.
45015014	And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is worthless, and so is your faith.
45015015	In that case, we are also exposed as false witnesses about God. For we have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead, but He did not raise Him if in fact the dead are not raised.
45015016	For if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised.
45015017	And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.
45015018	Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
45015019	If our hope in Christ is for this life alone, we are to be pitied more than all men.
45015020	But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
45015021	For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead comes also through a man.
45015022	For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.
45015023	But each in his own turn: Christ the firstfruits; then at His coming, those who belong to Him.
45015024	Then the end will come, when He hands over the kingdom to God the Father after He has destroyed all dominion, authority, and power.
45015025	For He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet.
45015026	The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
45015027	For “God has put everything under His feet.” Now when it says that everything has been put under Him, this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him.
45015028	And when all things have been subjected to Him, then the Son Himself will be made subject to Him who put all things under Him, so that God may be all in all.
45015029	If these things are not so, what will those do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized for them?
45015030	And why do we endanger ourselves every hour?
45015031	I face death every day, brothers, as surely as I boast about you in Christ Jesus our Lord.
45015032	If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human motives, what did I gain? If the dead are not raised, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
45015033	Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”
45015034	Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning; for some of you are ignorant of God. I say this to your shame.
45015035	But someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? With what kind of body will they come?”
45015036	You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
45015037	And what you sow is not the body that will be, but just a seed, perhaps of wheat or something else.
45015038	But God gives it a body as He has designed, and to each kind of seed He gives its own body.
45015039	Not all flesh is the same: Men have one kind of flesh, animals have another, birds another, and fish another.
45015040	There are also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. But the splendor of the heavenly bodies is of one degree, and the splendor of the earthly bodies is of another.
45015041	The sun has one degree of splendor, the moon another, and the stars another; and star differs from star in splendor.
45015042	So will it be with the resurrection of the dead: What is sown is perishable; it is raised imperishable.
45015043	It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
45015044	It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
45015045	So it is written: “The first man Adam became a living being”; the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
45015046	The spiritual, however, was not first, but the natural, and then the spiritual.
45015047	The first man was of the dust of the earth, the second man from heaven.
45015048	As was the earthly man, so also are those who are of the earth; and as is the heavenly man, so also are those who are of heaven.
45015049	And just as we have borne the likeness of the earthly man, so also shall we bear the likeness of the heavenly man.
45015050	Now I declare to you, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
45015051	Listen, I tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed—
45015052	in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
45015053	For the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality.
45015054	When the perishable has been clothed with the imperishable and the mortal with immortality, then the saying that is written will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
45015055	“Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?”
45015056	The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
45015057	But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
45015058	Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and immovable. Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
45016001	Now about the collection for the saints, you are to do as I directed the churches of Galatia:
45016002	On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside a portion of his income, saving it up, so that when I come no collections will be needed.
45016003	Then, on my arrival, I will send letters with those you recommend to carry your gift to Jerusalem.
45016004	And if it is advisable for me to go also, they can travel with me.
45016005	After I go through Macedonia, however, I will come to you; for I will be going through Macedonia.
45016006	Perhaps I will stay with you awhile, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.
45016007	For I do not want to see you now only in passing; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.
45016008	But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,
45016009	because a great door for effective work has opened to me, even though many oppose me.
45016010	If Timothy comes, see to it that he has nothing to fear while he is with you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.
45016011	No one, then, should treat him with contempt. Send him on his way in peace so that he can return to me, for I am expecting him along with the brothers.
45016012	Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. He was not at all inclined to go now, but he will go when he has the opportunity.
45016013	Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.
45016014	Do everything in love.
45016015	You know that Stephanas and his household were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints. Now I urge you, brothers,
45016016	to submit to such as these, and to every fellow worker and laborer.
45016017	I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have arrived, because they have supplied what was lacking from you.
45016018	For they refreshed my spirit and yours as well. Show your appreciation, therefore, to such men.
45016019	The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, and so does the church that meets at their house.
45016020	All the brothers here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
45016021	This greeting is in my own hand—Paul.
45016022	If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be under a curse. Come, O Lord!
45016023	The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
45016024	My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
46001001	Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, To the church of God in Corinth, together with all the saints throughout Achaia:
46001002	Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
46001003	Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort,
46001004	who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God.
46001005	For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.
46001006	If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which accomplishes in you patient endurance of the same sufferings we experience.
46001007	And our hope for you is sure, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you will share in our comfort.
46001008	We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the hardships we encountered in the province of Asia. We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired even of life.
46001009	Indeed, we felt we were under the sentence of death, in order that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.
46001010	He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us. In Him we have placed our hope that He will yet again deliver us,
46001011	as you help us by your prayers. Then many will give thanks on our behalf for the favor shown us in answer to their prayers.
46001012	For this is our boast: Our conscience testifies that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and especially in relation to you, in the holiness and sincerity that are from God—not in worldly wisdom, but in the grace of God.
46001013	For we do not write you anything that is beyond your ability to read and understand. And I hope that you will understand us completely,
46001014	as you have already understood us in part, that you may boast of us just as we will boast of you in the day of our Lord Jesus.
46001015	Confident of this, I planned to visit you first, so that you might receive a double blessing.
46001016	I wanted to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and to return to you from Macedonia, and then to have you help me on my way to Judea.
46001017	When I planned this, did I do it carelessly? Or do I make my plans by human standards, so as to say “Yes, yes” and also “No, no”?
46001018	But as surely as God is faithful, our message to you is not “Yes” and “No.”
46001019	For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was proclaimed among you by me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not “Yes” and “No,” but in Him it has always been “Yes.”
46001020	For all the promises of God are “Yes” in Christ. And so through Him, our “Amen” is spoken to the glory of God.
46001021	Now it is God who establishes both us and you in Christ. He anointed us,
46001022	placed His seal on us, and put His Spirit in our hearts as a pledge of what is to come.
46001023	I call God as my witness that it was in order to spare you that I did not return to Corinth.
46001024	Not that we lord it over your faith, but we are fellow workers with you for your joy, because it is by faith that you stand firm.
46002001	So I made up my mind not to make another painful visit to you.
46002002	For if I grieve you, who is left to cheer me but those whom I have grieved?
46002003	I wrote as I did so that on my arrival I would not be grieved by those who ought to make me rejoice. I had confidence in all of you, that you would share my joy.
46002004	For through many tears I wrote you out of great distress and anguish of heart, not to grieve you but to let you know how much I love you.
46002005	Now if anyone has caused grief, he has not grieved me but all of you—to some degree, not to overstate it.
46002006	The punishment imposed on him by the majority is sufficient for him.
46002007	So instead, you ought to forgive and comfort him, so that he will not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
46002008	Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.
46002009	My purpose in writing you was to see if you would stand the test and be obedient in everything.
46002010	If you forgive anyone, I also forgive him. And if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven it in the presence of Christ for your sake,
46002011	in order that Satan should not outwit us. For we are not unaware of his schemes.
46002012	Now when I went to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ and a door stood open for me in the Lord,
46002013	I had no peace in my spirit, because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.
46002014	But thanks be to God, who always leads us triumphantly as captives in Christ and through us spreads everywhere the fragrance of the knowledge of Him.
46002015	For we are to God the sweet aroma of Christ among those who are being saved and those who are perishing.
46002016	To the one we are an odor that brings death, to the other a fragrance that brings life. And who is qualified for such a task?
46002017	For we are not like so many others, who peddle the word of God for profit. On the contrary, in Christ we speak before God with sincerity, as men sent from God.
46003001	Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?
46003002	You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
46003003	It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
46003004	Such confidence before God is ours through Christ.
46003005	Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.
46003006	And He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
46003007	Now if the ministry of death, which was engraved in letters on stone, came with such glory that the Israelites could not gaze at the face of Moses because of its fleeting glory,
46003008	will not the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?
46003009	For if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious is the ministry of righteousness!
46003010	Indeed, what was once glorious has no glory now in comparison to the glory that surpasses it.
46003011	For if what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of that which endures!
46003012	Therefore, since we have such a hope, we are very bold.
46003013	We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.
46003014	But their minds were closed. For to this day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant. It has not been lifted, because only in Christ can it be removed.
46003015	And even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.
46003016	But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
46003017	Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
46003018	And we, who with unveiled faces all reflect the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
46004001	Therefore, since God in His mercy has given us this ministry, we do not lose heart.
46004002	Instead, we have renounced secret and shameful ways. We do not practice deceit, nor do we distort the word of God. On the contrary, by open proclamation of the truth, we commend ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
46004003	And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.
46004004	The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so they cannot see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
46004005	For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.
46004006	For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
46004007	Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.
46004008	We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;
46004009	persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.
46004010	We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
46004011	For we who are alive are always consigned to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal body.
46004012	So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
46004013	And in keeping with what is written, “I believed, therefore I have spoken,” we who have the same spirit of faith also believe and therefore speak,
46004014	knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you in His presence.
46004015	All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is extending to more and more people may cause thanksgiving to overflow, to the glory of God.
46004016	Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.
46004017	For our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal weight of glory that is far beyond comparison.
46004018	So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.
46005001	For we know that if the earthly tent we live in is dismantled, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands.
46005002	For in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling,
46005003	because when we are clothed, we will not be found naked.
46005004	For while we are in this tent, we groan under our burdens, because we do not wish to be unclothed but clothed, so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life.
46005005	And it is God who has prepared us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come.
46005006	Therefore we are always confident, although we know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord.
46005007	For we walk by faith, not by sight.
46005008	We are confident, then, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
46005009	So we aspire to please Him, whether we are at home in this body or away from it.
46005010	For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad.
46005011	Therefore, since we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade men. What we are is clear to God, and I hope it is clear to your conscience as well.
46005012	We are not commending ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you an occasion to be proud of us, so that you can answer those who take pride in appearances rather than in the heart.
46005013	If we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.
46005014	For Christ’s love compels us, because we are convinced that One died for all, therefore all died.
46005015	And He died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again.
46005016	So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Although we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer.
46005017	Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!
46005018	All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:
46005019	that God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting men’s trespasses against them. And He has committed to us the message of reconciliation.
46005020	Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God.
46005021	God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.
46006001	As God’s fellow workers, then, we urge you not to receive God’s grace in vain.
46006002	For He says: “In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.” Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!
46006003	We put no obstacle in anyone’s way, so that no one can discredit our ministry.
46006004	Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities;
46006005	in beatings, imprisonments, and riots; in labor, sleepless nights, and hunger;
46006006	in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love;
46006007	in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;
46006008	through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine;
46006009	unknown, yet well-known; dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed;
46006010	sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
46006011	We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians. Our hearts are open wide.
46006012	It is not our affection, but yours, that is restrained.
46006013	As a fair exchange—I speak as to my children—open wide your hearts also.
46006014	Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
46006015	What harmony is there between Christ and Belial? Or what does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?
46006016	What agreement can exist between the temple of God and idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God has said: “I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.”
46006017	“Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”
46006018	And: “I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”
46007001	Therefore, beloved, since we have these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
46007002	Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have exploited no one.
46007003	I do not say this to condemn you. I have said before that you so occupy our hearts that we live and die together with you.
46007004	Great is my confidence in you; great is my pride in you; I am filled with encouragement; in all our troubles my joy overflows.
46007005	For when we arrived in Macedonia, our bodies had no rest, but we were pressed from every direction—conflicts on the outside, fears within.
46007006	But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the arrival of Titus,
46007007	and not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort he had received from you. He told us about your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced all the more.
46007008	Even if I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Although I did regret it—for I see that my letter caused you sorrow, but only for a short time—
46007009	yet now I rejoice, not because you were made sorrowful, but because your sorrow led you to repentance. For you felt the sorrow that God had intended, and so were not harmed in any way by us.
46007010	Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation without regret, but worldly sorrow brings death.
46007011	Consider what this godly sorrow has produced in you: what earnestness, what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what alarm, what longing, what zeal, what vindication! In every way you have proved yourselves to be innocent in this matter.
46007012	So even though I wrote to you, it was not on account of the one who did wrong or the one who was harmed, but rather that your earnestness on our behalf would be made clear to you in the sight of God.
46007013	On account of this, we are encouraged. In addition to our own encouragement, we were even more delighted by the joy of Titus. For his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
46007014	Indeed, I was not embarrassed by anything I had boasted to him about you. But just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting to Titus has proved to be true as well.
46007015	And his affection for you is even greater when he remembers that you were all obedient as you welcomed him with fear and trembling.
46007016	I rejoice that I can have complete confidence in you.
46008001	Now, brothers, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the churches of Macedonia.
46008002	In the terrible ordeal they suffered, their abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity.
46008003	For I testify that they gave according to their ability and even beyond it. Of their own accord,
46008004	they earnestly pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints.
46008005	And not only did they do as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, through the will of God.
46008006	So we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it.
46008007	But just as you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness, and in the love we inspired in you —see that you also excel in this grace of giving.
46008008	I am not giving a command, but I am testing the sincerity of your love through the earnestness of others.
46008009	For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich.
46008010	And this is my opinion about what is helpful for you in this matter: Last year you were the first not only to give, but even to have such a desire.
46008011	Now finish the work, so that you may complete it with the same eager desire, according to your means.
46008012	For if the eagerness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what he does not have.
46008013	It is not our intention that others may be relieved while you are burdened, but that there may be equality.
46008014	At the present time, your surplus will meet their need, so that in turn their surplus will meet your need. This way there will be equality.
46008015	As it is written: “He who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall.”
46008016	But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same devotion I have for you.
46008017	For not only did he welcome our appeal, but he is eagerly coming to you of his own volition.
46008018	Along with Titus we are sending the brother who is praised by all the churches for his work in the gospel.
46008019	More than that, this brother was chosen by the churches to accompany us with the gracious offering we administer to honor the Lord Himself and to show our eagerness to help.
46008020	We want to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this generous gift.
46008021	For we are taking great care to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men.
46008022	And we are sending along with them our brother who has proven his earnestness to us many times and in many ways, and now even more so by his great confidence in you.
46008023	As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you. As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ.
46008024	In full view of the churches, then, show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you.
46009001	Now about the service to the saints, there is no need for me to write to you.
46009002	For I know your eagerness to help, and I have been boasting to the Macedonians that since last year you in Achaia were prepared to give. And your zeal has stirred most of them to do likewise.
46009003	But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said.
46009004	Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—to say nothing of you—would be ashamed of having been so confident.
46009005	So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to visit you beforehand and make arrangements for the generous gift you had promised. This way, your gift will be prepared generously and not begrudgingly.
46009006	Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.
46009007	Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.
46009008	And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work.
46009009	As it is written: “He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.”
46009010	Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your store of seed and will increase the harvest of your righteousness.
46009011	You will be enriched in every way to be generous on every occasion, and through us your generosity will produce thanksgiving to God.
46009012	For this ministry of service is not only supplying the needs of the saints but is also overflowing in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.
46009013	Because of the proof this ministry provides, the saints will glorify God for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ, and for the generosity of your contribution to them and to all the others.
46009014	And their prayers for you will express their affection for you, because of the surpassing grace God has given you.
46009015	Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!
46010001	Now by the mildness and gentleness of Christ, I appeal to you—I, Paul, who am humble when face to face with you, but bold when away.
46010002	I beg you that when I come I may not need to be as bold as I expect toward those who presume that we live according to the flesh.
46010003	For though we live in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
46010004	The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the flesh. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.
46010005	We demolish arguments and every presumption set up against the knowledge of God; and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.
46010006	And we will be ready to punish every act of disobedience, as soon as your obedience is complete.
46010007	You are looking at outward appearances. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, he should remind himself that we belong to Christ just as much as he does.
46010008	For even if I boast somewhat excessively about the authority the Lord gave us for building you up rather than tearing you down, I will not be ashamed.
46010009	I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you by my letters.
46010010	For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.”
46010011	Such people should consider that what we are in our letters when absent, we will be in our actions when present.
46010012	We do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves. When they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they show their ignorance.
46010013	We, however, will not boast beyond our limits, but only within the field of influence that God has assigned to us—a field that reaches even to you.
46010014	We are not overstepping our bounds, as if we had not come to you. Indeed, we were the first to reach you with the gospel of Christ.
46010015	Neither do we boast beyond our limits in the labors of others. But we hope that as your faith increases, our area of influence among you will greatly increase as well,
46010016	so that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you. Then we will not be boasting in the work already done in another man’s territory.
46010017	Rather, “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”
46010018	For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
46011001	I hope you will put up with a little of my foolishness, but you are already doing that.
46011002	I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
46011003	I am afraid, however, that just as Eve was deceived by the serpent’s cunning, your minds may be led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ.
46011004	For if someone comes and proclaims a Jesus other than the One we proclaimed, or if you receive a different spirit than the One you received, or a different gospel than the one you accepted, you put up with it very easily.
46011005	I consider myself in no way inferior to those “super-apostles.”
46011006	Although I am not a polished speaker, I am certainly not lacking in knowledge. We have made this clear to you in every way possible.
46011007	Was it a sin for me to humble myself in order to exalt you, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?
46011008	I robbed other churches by accepting their support in order to serve you.
46011009	And when I was with you and in need, I was not a burden to anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my needs. I have refrained from being a burden to you in any way, and I will continue to do so.
46011010	As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
46011011	Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
46011012	But I will keep on doing what I am doing, in order to undercut those who want an opportunity to be regarded as our equals in the things of which they boast.
46011013	For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ.
46011014	And no wonder, for Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.
46011015	It is not surprising, then, if his servants masquerade as servants of righteousness. Their end will correspond to their actions.
46011016	I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool. But if you do, then receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
46011017	In this confident boasting of mine, I am not speaking as the Lord would, but as a fool.
46011018	Since many are boasting according to the flesh, I too will boast.
46011019	For you gladly put up with fools, since you are so wise.
46011020	In fact, you even put up with anyone who enslaves you or exploits you or takes advantage of you or exalts himself or strikes you in the face.
46011021	To my shame I concede that we were too weak for that! Speaking as a fool, however, I can match what anyone else dares to boast about.
46011022	Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
46011023	Are they servants of Christ? (I am speaking as if I were out of my mind.) I am so much more: in harder labor, in more imprisonments, in worse beatings, in frequent danger of death.
46011024	Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.
46011025	Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a night and a day in the open sea.
46011026	In my frequent journeys, I have been in danger from rivers and from bandits, in danger from my countrymen and from the Gentiles, in danger in the city and in the country, in danger on the sea and among false brothers,
46011027	in labor and toil and often without sleep, in hunger and thirst and often without food, in cold and exposure.
46011028	Apart from these external trials, I face daily the pressure of my concern for all the churches.
46011029	Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with grief?
46011030	If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
46011031	The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is forever worthy of praise, knows that I am not lying.
46011032	In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas secured the city of the Damascenes in order to arrest me.
46011033	But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his grasp.
46012001	I must go on boasting. Although there is nothing to gain, I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
46012002	I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven. Whether it was in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows.
46012003	And I know that this man—whether in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows—
46012004	was caught up to Paradise. The things he heard were inexpressible, things that man is not permitted to tell.
46012005	I will boast about such a man, but I will not boast about myself, except in my weaknesses.
46012006	Even if I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, because I would be speaking the truth. But I refrain, so no one will credit me with more than he sees in me or hears from me,
46012007	or because of these surpassingly great revelations. So to keep me from becoming conceited, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me.
46012008	Three times I pleaded with the Lord to take it away from me.
46012009	But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.
46012010	That is why, for the sake of Christ, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
46012011	I have become a fool, but you drove me to it. In fact, you should have commended me, since I am in no way inferior to those “super-apostles,” even though I am nothing.
46012012	The marks of a true apostle—signs, wonders, and miracles—were performed among you with great perseverance.
46012013	In what way were you inferior to the other churches, except that I was not a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!
46012014	See, I am ready to come to you a third time, and I will not be a burden, because I am not seeking your possessions, but you. For children should not have to save up for their parents, but parents for their children.
46012015	And for the sake of your souls, I will most gladly spend my money and myself. If I love you more, will you love me less?
46012016	Be that as it may, I was not a burden to you; but crafty as I am, I caught you by trickery.
46012017	Did I exploit you by anyone I sent you?
46012018	I urged Titus to visit you, and I sent our brother with him. Did Titus exploit you in any way? Did we not walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps?
46012019	Have you been thinking all along that we were making a defense to you? We speak before God in Christ, and all of this, beloved, is to build you up.
46012020	For I am afraid that when I come, I may not find you as I wish, and you may not find me as you wish. I fear that there may be quarreling, jealousy, rage, rivalry, slander, gossip, arrogance, and disorder.
46012021	I am afraid that when I come again, my God will humble me before you, and I will be grieved over many who have sinned earlier and have not repented of their acts of impurity, sexual immorality, and debauchery.
46013001	This is the third time I am coming to you. “Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”
46013002	I already warned you the second time I was with you. So now in my absence I warn those who sinned earlier and everyone else: If I return, I will not spare anyone,
46013003	since you are demanding proof that Christ is speaking through me. He is not weak in dealing with you but is powerful among you.
46013004	For He was indeed crucified in weakness, yet He lives by God’s power. For we are also weak in Him, yet by God’s power we will live with Him concerning you.
46013005	Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Do you not realize that Jesus Christ is in you—unless you fail the test?
46013006	And I hope you will realize that we have not failed the test.
46013007	Now we pray to God that you will not do anything wrong—not that we will appear to have stood the test, but that you will do what is right, even if we appear to have failed.
46013008	For we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.
46013009	In fact, we rejoice when we are weak but you are strong, and our prayer is for your perfection.
46013010	This is why I write these things while absent, so that when I am present I will not need to be severe in my use of the authority that the Lord gave me for building you up, not for tearing you down.
46013011	Finally, brothers, rejoice! Aim for perfect harmony, encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
46013012	Greet one another with a holy kiss.
46013013	All the saints send you greetings.
46013014	The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.
47001001	Paul, an apostle—sent not from men nor by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead—
47001002	and all the brothers with me, To the churches of Galatia:
47001003	Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
47001004	who gave Himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
47001005	to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
47001006	I am amazed how quickly you are deserting the One who called you by the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel—
47001007	which is not even a gospel. Evidently some people are troubling you and trying to distort the gospel of Christ.
47001008	But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be under a curse!
47001009	As we have said before, so now I say again: If anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to the one you received, let him be under a curse!
47001010	Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ.
47001011	For I want you to know, brothers, that the gospel I preached was not devised by man.
47001012	I did not receive it from any man, nor was I taught it; rather, I received it by revelation from Jesus Christ.
47001013	For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how severely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.
47001014	I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries and was extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
47001015	But when God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me by His grace, was pleased
47001016	to reveal His Son in me so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not rush to consult with flesh and blood,
47001017	nor did I go up to Jerusalem to the apostles who came before me, but I went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus.
47001018	Only after three years did I go up to Jerusalem to confer with Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
47001019	But I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord’s brother.
47001020	I assure you before God that what I am writing to you is no lie.
47001021	Later I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
47001022	I was personally unknown, however, to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.
47001023	They only heard the account: “The man who formerly persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.”
47001024	And they glorified God because of me.
47002001	Fourteen years later I went up again to Jerusalem, accompanied by Barnabas. I took Titus along also.
47002002	I went in response to a revelation and set before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. But I spoke privately to those recognized as leaders, for fear that I was running or had already run in vain.
47002003	Yet not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek.
47002004	This issue arose because some false brothers had come in under false pretenses to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us.
47002005	We did not give in to them for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you.
47002006	But as for the highly esteemed—whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism —those leaders added nothing to me.
47002007	On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted to preach the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised.
47002008	For the One who was at work in Peter’s apostleship to the circumcised was also at work in my apostleship to the Gentiles.
47002009	And recognizing the grace that I had been given, James, Cephas, and John—those reputed to be pillars—gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.
47002010	They only asked us to remember the poor, the very thing I was eager to do.
47002011	When Cephas came to Antioch, however, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.
47002012	For before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they arrived, he began to draw back and separate himself, for fear of those in the circumcision group.
47002013	The other Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, so that by their hypocrisy even Barnabas was led astray.
47002014	When I saw that they were not walking in line with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all, “If you, who are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”
47002015	We who are Jews by birth and not Gentile “sinners”
47002016	know that a man is not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ. So we, too, have believed in Christ Jesus, that we may be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no one will be justified.
47002017	But if, while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, does that make Christ a minister of sin? Certainly not!
47002018	If I rebuild what I have already torn down, I prove myself to be a lawbreaker.
47002019	For through the law I died to the law so that I might live to God.
47002020	I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself up for me.
47002021	I do not set aside the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing.
47003001	O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? Before your very eyes Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed as crucified.
47003002	I would like to learn just one thing from you: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law, or by hearing with faith?
47003003	Are you so foolish? After starting in the Spirit, are you now finishing in the flesh?
47003004	Have you suffered so much for nothing, if it really was for nothing?
47003005	Does God lavish His Spirit on you and work miracles among you because you practice the law, or because you hear and believe?
47003006	So also, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
47003007	Understand, then, that those who have faith are sons of Abraham.
47003008	The Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and foretold the gospel to Abraham: “All nations will be blessed through you.”
47003009	So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
47003010	All who rely on works of the law are under a curse. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who does not continue to do everything written in the Book of the Law.”
47003011	Now it is clear that no one is justified before God by the law, because, “The righteous will live by faith.”
47003012	The law, however, is not based on faith; on the contrary, “The man who does these things will live by them.”
47003013	Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”
47003014	He redeemed us in order that the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, so that by faith we might receive the promise of the Spirit.
47003015	Brothers, let me put this in human terms. Even a human covenant, once it is ratified, cannot be canceled or amended.
47003016	The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. The Scripture does not say, “and to seeds,” meaning many, but “and to your seed,” meaning One, who is Christ.
47003017	What I mean is this: The law that came 430 years later does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise.
47003018	For if the inheritance depends on the law, then it no longer depends on a promise; but God freely granted it to Abraham through a promise.
47003019	Why then was the law given? It was added because of transgressions, until the arrival of the seed to whom the promise referred. It was administered through angels by a mediator.
47003020	A mediator is unnecessary, however, for only one party; but God is one.
47003021	Is the law, then, opposed to the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would certainly have come from the law.
47003022	But the Scripture pronounces all things confined by sin, so that by faith in Jesus Christ the promise might be given to those who believe.
47003023	Before this faith came, we were held in custody under the law, locked up until faith should be revealed.
47003024	So the law became our guardian to lead us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.
47003025	Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.
47003026	You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
47003027	For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
47003028	There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
47003029	And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s seed and heirs according to the promise.
47004001	What I am saying is that as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, although he is the owner of everything.
47004002	He is subject to guardians and trustees until the date set by his father.
47004003	So also, when we were children, we were enslaved under the basic principles of the world.
47004004	But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
47004005	to redeem those under the law, that we might receive our adoption as sons.
47004006	And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, “Abba, Father!”
47004007	So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and since you are a son, you are also an heir through God.
47004008	Formerly, when you did not know God, you were slaves to those who by nature are not gods.
47004009	But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, how is it that you are turning back to those weak and worthless principles? Do you wish to be enslaved by them all over again?
47004010	You are observing special days and months and seasons and years!
47004011	I fear for you, that my efforts for you may have been in vain.
47004012	I beg you, brothers, become like me, for I became like you. You have done me no wrong.
47004013	You know that it was because of an illness that I first preached the gospel to you.
47004014	And although my illness was a trial to you, you did not despise or reject me. Instead, you welcomed me as if I were an angel of God, as if I were Christ Jesus Himself.
